title: Delving Into Crispness: Guided Label Refinement for Crisp Edge Detection
mechanism: Over-detect Canny edges at a very low threshold, keep the subset that agrees with the human labels and fill the gaps, then train any detector on the refined labels. A controlled study shows label offset, not the loss, causes thick predictions.
adaptation: Use a multi-scale Hessian dark-ridge detector in place of Canny (sigma about 1.5 to 2 px, since crack FWHM is about 4 px), thinned to 1 px. Snap each crack label pixel to a ridge within 2 px. Keep the original pixel where no ridge exists (the 7% of cracks with low contrast). Never snap onto gridline, busbar or ribbon label pixels. Then re-dilate to each source's label width (ARTS 1.5, CFVS/CSIR 1.75, BMRK 3.0, SDLE 3.25) so strict IoU is not lost to a width mismatch. Apply the same recipe to gridline (IoU 0.283).
min_experiment: Arm: house U-Net++ trained on ridge-snapped, width-restored crack labels, 5 seeds. Baselines: house and PF, 100% labels. Metrics: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, recall of components >= 20 px, E1 relF1@2, and also the score against ridge-snapped test GT. Kill if crack IoU falls by more than 0.012 and relF1@2 gains less than 0.01.
evidence: R: on BSDS500, crisp predictions appear only when more than about 90% of training labels are offset-free (elastic-shift study with PiDiNet). Refined labels raised Average Crispness from 17.4% to 30.6% and gave PiDiNet ODS +12.2% and OIS +12.6% on Multicue without NMS. Datasets of a few hundred images (BSDS, Multicue).
prior_overlap: BRIEF 5 Labels row: automatic label refinement is listed as not tested. Human relabelling gave +0.05 to +0.08 crack IoU, so the lever is proven. Offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) changes the loss, not the labels. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace Canny with a multi-scale dark-ridge detector (Hessian/Frangi) on 1-channel EL; snap each crack label segment to the nearest ridge within 2 px, keep unmatched px (do not delete, under-annotation hurts more); redraw at the source's width. Also produce ridge-snapped CV and test labels as a second scoring view for the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF trained on ridge-snapped crack labels vs PF; score on original and snapped CV labels; metric strict crack IoU and relF1@2; kill if CV IoU on original labels drops >0.01 with no relF1@2 gain >=0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace Canny with a multi-scale dark-ridge detector (Hessian/Frangi) on 1-channel EL; snap each crack label segment to the nearest ridge within 2 px, keep unmatched pixels. Train on snapped crack labels. Also produces ridge-snapped test labels as a second scoring view for the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm = PF trained on ridge-snapped crack labels; baseline = PF on revised labels; 5 seeds + 5-fold CV; score on original labels and on ridge-snapped labels; metrics crack IoU, relF1@2, E1 relF1@2. Kill if CV crack IoU on original labels drops > 0.01 with no relF1@2 or E1 gain.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace Canny with a multi-scale Hessian valley detector (sigma 1.5 to 2 px, crack FWHM about 4 px), thin to 1 px, snap each crack label pixel to the ridge within 2 px, keep original pixel where no ridge (low-contrast cracks), forbid snapping onto gridline/busbar/ribbon, then re-dilate to each source's label width (ARTS 1.5, CFVS/CSIR 1.75, BMRK 3.0, SDLE 3.25). Geodesic ridge path replaces the inpainting net. Same for gridline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house model trained on ridge-snapped, width-restored crack labels, 5 seeds; baseline house and PF, 5 seeds. Metrics clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, components>=20px found, E1 relF1@2, AC crispness. Kill if crack IoU < baseline - 0.012 and relF1@2 not up >= 0.01. About 12 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace Canny with a multi-scale Hessian/Frangi dark-ridge detector on inverted EL; snap each crack label pixel to the nearest ridge pixel within 2 px, keep original where no ridge (faint cracks), then re-dilate to the source's median width. CPU preprocessing only.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house on ridge-snapped crack labels. Baseline: house. Metric: relF1@2 and relP@2 primary, strict crack IoU vs original test labels secondary. Kill if relF1@2 gain < +0.01 or strict IoU drops > 0.02. About 6 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace Canny with a multi-scale dark-ridge Hessian detector (sigma 1 to 2 px, crack FWHM about 4 px) on 1-channel EL. Snap each crack label skeleton point along its normal to the ridge maximum within 2 px; keep the original point where ridge strength is below a per-source floor (7% invisible cracks, CSIR 16%); bridge gaps under 6 px (dotted labels in 22 cells); forbid snapping onto gridline/busbar/ribbon; re-dilate to each source's measured width (ARTS 1.5, CFVS/CSIR 1.75, BMRK 3.0, SDLE 3.25). CPU preprocessing only.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house U-Net++ trained on snapped + width-restored crack labels, 5 seeds, 100% labels; baseline: house (and PF pair). Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, comp>=20px recall on clean-49 against ORIGINAL test labels; E1 relF1@2. Pre-check: snapped train labels agree with 2022 labels >= 0.95 within 2 px. Kill if crack IoU < baseline - 0.012 and relF1@2 gain < 0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace Canny with a dark-ridge map (Hessian or min-intensity along the label normal, 1 to 3 px scales). Move each crack skeleton point to the darkest pixel along its normal within 2 px, reconnect, redraw at each source's median width (ARTS 1.5, CFVS/CSIR 1.75, BMRK 3.0, SDLE 3.25). Keep the original label where ridge support is weak (7% of cracks are under 2% darker) instead of deleting it.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house U-Net++ trained on ridge-snapped crack labels, 5 seeds, 100% labels. Baseline: house model. Metric: crack IoU on original clean-49 test labels and relF1@2; secondary crack IoU on snapped test labels. Kill: original-label crack IoU below baseline by more than 0.012 and relF1@2 not up by at least 0.01.

title: SAM2-UNet: segment anything 2 makes strong encoder for natural and medical image segmentation
mechanism: SAM 2 Hiera encoder kept mostly frozen with small adapters, feeding a plain U-Net decoder; Hiera has a stride-4 first stage so fine detail survives into the skips.
adaptation: 1-channel EL replicated to 3 channels; Hiera-L (and B+); one arm at 512 and one at 1024 (2x bilinear upscale); replace binary head with 24-class head, house CE + soft Dice on crack/inactive, label-safe aug only, val-chosen crack logit bias; also ensemble with the house U-Net++ (heterogeneous ensembles untested here).
evidence: R: beats specialised SOTA on camouflage, salient, mirror, marine, polyp segmentation (abstract only); 242 citations. No thin-structure numbers in abstract.
min_experiment: Arms SAM2-UNet Hiera-L @512 and @1024, 3 seeds, 20k steps vs house U-Net++ and PF. Metrics clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob; E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU; 5-fold CV. Also SAM2-UNet+house ensemble vs house 5-seed ensemble. Kill if crack IoU < 0.465 and relF1@2 < 0.875 and E1 relF1@2 < 0.43 and ensemble adds < +0.01 crack IoU.
prior_overlap: Foundation encoders row: only a frozen linear probe of SAM2 Hiera-T was run. Adapter fine-tuning of Hiera-L with a U-Net decoder and 1024 input is listed as not closed.

alt_notes.adaptation: Gray to 3 channels, 512 px, Hiera-B+ or L. Hiera stage 1 is stride 4, so add a full-resolution conv skip from the raw image or 1-2 px cracks vanish. 24-class head, house CE plus Dice on crack and inactive.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: SAM2-UNet Hiera-B+ with adapters and extra full-res skip; baseline PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU, E1 crack relF1@2, mIoU_rob. Kill if CV crack IoU < PF minus 0.01 and E1 n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Gray replicated to 3 channels, 512 px, Hiera-B+ or L. Hiera stage 1 is stride 4, so add a full or half resolution conv skip from the raw image, or 1 to 2 px cracks are lost. 24-class head, house CE + Dice. SECrackSeg (doi:10.3390/s25092642) shows the same design used for cracks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: SAM2-UNet with full-res skip, 24 classes; baseline: PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU, E1 crack relF1@2, mIoU_rob. Kill if CV crack IoU < PF minus 0.01 and E1 n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: 1-ch EL replicated to 3 ch, 512 upscaled to 1024; Hiera-B+ or L; 24-class head; add stride-2 conv stem skip so 1-2 px cracks reach the decoder; house CE + Dice on crack/inactive, label-safe aug, 20k steps, encoder lr 0.1x (PF-style).
alt_notes.min_experiment: SAM2-UNet Hiera-B+ at 1024 vs house PF; module-grouped 5-fold CV (1 seed/fold) then 3 seeds on clean-49 and E1. Kill if CV crack relF1@2 > 0.005 below PF AND E1 crack relF1@2 not >= PF+0.03 AND E1 inactive IoU not > 0.24.

alt_notes.adaptation: Hierarchical stride-4 encoder avoids the stride-16 crack dilution (70.7% of crack signal below 1/4 at stride 16 vs 8.5% at stride 4, idea08 file). Hiera-B+ or L at 1024, add a stride-2 stem skip, 24-class head, house loss, 20k steps. Overlaps D14 item 1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: SAM2-UNet Hiera-B+ at 1024. Baseline: house PF. Metric: CV crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, then 3 seeds clean-49 and E1. Kill: default line.

alt_notes.adaptation: Hiera-B+ / L at 512 and 1024 px, add a stride-2 image skip, 24-class head, house loss. Hiera is stride 4, so no ViT stride problem.
alt_notes.min_experiment: SAM2-UNet Hiera-B+ vs house PF, CV then 3 seeds; default kill line.

title: ERM++: An Improved Baseline for Domain Generalization
mechanism: A tuned plain-ERM recipe: average all weight iterates (MPA), warm-start the new head on a frozen backbone, set training length on val then retrain on train+val, stronger init, unfrozen BN.
adaptation: MPA as a running mean of all U-Net++ weights from step 2k to 20k with BN stats recomputed on train; warm start = PF's 1k frozen steps; fix the schedule (plateau lr drops, cap 80k) on the module-grouped 5-fold CV, then retrain the final model on all 532 train+val cells.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + MPA (same run, paired raw vs averaged), then PF + MPA + full-data retrain. Baseline: SUP100-PF, seeds 5-9. Metric: val/CV crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, then test clean crack relF1@2, E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU. Kill: MPA minus raw < +0.005 val relF1@2 paired over 5 seeds and E1 inactive not better.
evidence: R (full text, Table 2a, ResNet-50, 5 DomainBed datasets): ERM++ 68.9 avg; without MPA 65.9 (-3.0, largest), without full data 67.7, without strong init 67.6, without unfrozen BN 68.3, without Auto-LR 68.4, without warm start 68.7.
prior_overlap: BRIEF section 5 optimizer row: EMA/SWA and longer schedules never varied; PF covers only the warm-start part. Open.

title: Rethinking Generalization: The Impact of Annotation Style on Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Conditional instance norm: per-dataset scale and shift in norm layers on a shared network, so the model learns each dataset's annotation style instead of averaging conflicting styles.
evidence: 6 MS lesion trials (~390 patients each): naive pooling worse than single-trial models (0.766 vs 0.784 Dice); trial-conditioned 0.787 to 0.789, matching or beating every single-trial model; can output any style; few-shot fine-tune to a new style.
adaptation: Per-source affine params (ARTS, CFVS, CSIR, BMRK, SDLE, plus UCF, MSS, PV-Vision) in U-Net++ decoder BN; encoder BN shared. Condition on known source at test; E1 as CSIR. Absorbs measured label-width differences (1.5 to 3.25 px) and lets wider external crack labels join training without widening BenchmarkEL predictions.
min_experiment: Arm: house model + per-source decoder affine, BenchmarkEL only, 20k steps, 5 seeds. Baseline: house 5-seed. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and per-source crack IoU (BMRK, CFVS). Kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and BMRK/CFVS crack IoU not up by 0.02. ~6 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: none; source-conditional prediction listed as never tried in BRIEF section 5

alt_notes.adaptation: 5-way source ID drives FiLM / conditional-BN scale and shift in U-Net++ decoder blocks only (encoder shared, PF schedule), init gamma 1 beta 0; 10% source dropout to a consensus ID for source-blind use. At test condition on filename source; E1 uses CSIR / BMRK. Targets the per-source crack width convention (ARTS 1.5 to SDLE 3.25 px).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house PF + source-FiLM decoder, 5 seeds. Baseline: house PF, 5 seeds. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, per-source crack IoU in module-grouped 5-fold CV, BMRK inactive IoU. Kill if 5-seed mean crack IoU gain < +0.012 and no source gains >= +0.03 in CV. Run only after zero-GPU check that predicted widths are flat across sources.

alt_notes.adaptation: A 5-way source embedding drives FiLM / conditional-norm scale and shift in the U-Net++ decoder only (encoder shared, kept by PF). Condition on the filename source at test (CSIR / BMRK on E1). Use 10% source dropout to get a consensus ID for source-blind use. Targets the per-source crack width differences (1.5 to 3.25 px).
alt_notes.min_experiment: First a zero-GPU check: per-source predicted crack width versus label width on CV out-of-fold predictions. Then arm = house PF + source-FiLM decoder (5 seeds) versus house PF (5 seeds). Metrics: crack IoU on clean-49 and per-source CV crack IoU. Kill if the mean gain is < +0.012 and no source gains >= +0.03 in CV. Zero-training control: skeleton redraw at source width, or a per-source logit bias.

title: Naive-Student: Leveraging Semi-Supervised Learning in Video Sequences for Urban Scene Segmentation
mechanism: An offline teacher with multi-scale and flip TTA pseudo-labels a large pool (hard labels, no threshold). The student trains on the pseudo-labels only, is then fine-tuned on the human labels, and the loop is repeated.
adaptation: Teacher = 5-seed PF ensemble with 8 dihedral TTA (flips and rot90 are label-safe), labelling the 11.9k CSIR/ARTS pool and later 159k. Store soft p(crack) and p(inactive); use argmax plus the val-chosen crack bias for the other classes. Student = house U-Net++ R34 (and a wider encoder): 40k steps on the pseudo-labelled pool with strong aug, then 20k PF fine-tune on the 478 labelled cells. It differs from our Mean Teacher in the offline, stronger teacher, the pseudo-only pretraining and the larger pool.
min_experiment: Arm NS-12k vs house PF (5 seeds each). Metrics: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if crack IoU gains less than 0.012 and E1 relF1@2 gains less than 0.03. If it survives, rerun with the 159k pool.
evidence: R: full Cityscapes labels (2,975), 89k video frames + 20k extra unlabelled. Student 82.5 -> 85.7 mIoU (+3.2) at iteration 1, +0.8 at iteration 2. Teacher used multi-scale + flip TTA.
prior_overlap: BRIEF row 'Pseudo-label SSL' tested an online EMA Mean Teacher (same R34) with hard/tolerant pseudo-labels at 100% labels and the 11.9k pool: n.d. Not tested: an offline ensemble+TTA teacher, pseudo-only pretraining then fine-tune, the 159k pool, or model distillation (listed as never tried). Still open.

title: nnU-Net: a self-configuring method for deep learning-based biomedical image segmentation
mechanism: Rule-based self-configuration from a dataset fingerprint plus a fixed recipe: 1000x250 iterations, SGD 0.01 Nesterov 0.99 poly lr, CE+Dice, deep supervision, foreground oversampling, heavy on-the-fly augmentation (rotation, scaling, noise, blur, brightness, contrast, low-res simulation, gamma, mirroring), 5-fold CV, fold ensemble, CV-chosen component post-processing.
adaptation: 2D config, 1 channel, 512 full-image patch; splits_final.json = our module-grouped 5-fold roots over 532 cells. Change two defaults: 2D rotation U(-180,180) and scaling U(0.7,1.4) resample 1-2 px crack labels (shrink below 1 px, shift), so run a label-safe variant (rot90/flips only, intensity aug kept); nnU-Net trains from scratch with instance norm, while PF showed preserved pretrained features matter for E1, so add an ImageNet R34 encoder arm. Disable largest-component post-processing for crack (many components per cell), let CV decide for inactive.
min_experiment: 3 arms (default aug, label-safe aug, label-safe + R34 ImageNet encoder), 5 folds each, fold ensemble, scored once on test clean-49 and E1. Baseline: house U-Net++ R34 5-seed ensemble (relF1@2 0.897, inactive IoU 0.456, E1 relF1@2 ~0.43-0.47). Kill if best arm is below house on test crack relF1@2 by >0.01 and on inactive IoU, and E1 relF1@2 not up by >=0.03. Cheaper companion: recipe ladder inside house trainer (100k-step SGD poly, deep supervision, noise/blur/gamma/low-res aug, 5-fold v 5-seed ensemble, CV component removal), 3 seeds each on CV, keep a step if crack relF1@2 or inactive IoU +0.01.
evidence: R: state of the art on 23 public datasets / challenges at release; paper states shorter trainings than 1000 epochs diminish performance; 5 fold models ensembled for test. OmniCrack30k reports nnU-Net best for cracks (clIoU@4px 64%, >=10 points ahead).
prior_overlap: Partial. BRIEF section 5 never varied schedule length, optimizer (beyond Adam), deep supervision, noise/blur/gamma/low-res augmentation, CV fold ensembles or component post-processing; nnU-Net style auto-configuration is listed as never tried. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: 2D config, 1-channel z-scored EL, 512 px whole-cell patch, 24 labels. Use the existing module-grouped 5 fold roots over the 532 train+val cells as the splits file. Arm A uses default augmentation. Arm B uses label-safe augmentation (flips, rot90, brightness/contrast; no rotation, scaling or low-res simulation, because a 1 px shift costs 0.44 crack IoU). Arm C uses CE + Dice on crack/inactive only, because Dice on 12 classes hurt here.
alt_notes.min_experiment: nnU-Net 2d, arms A and B, 5 module-grouped folds; ensemble the 5 fold models on test-49 and E1. Baseline: house 5-seed ensemble (crack IoU 0.485 to 0.488 argmax, relF1@2 0.897, inactive 0.456, mIoU_rob 0.583; E1 relF1@2 about 0.45). Kill: both arms more than 0.012 crack IoU below the house ensemble with no gain in relF1@2, inactive IoU or E1 relF1@2.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use the existing module-grouped 5-fold roots over the 532 train+val cells. Train the house recipe (and a PF copy) once per fold and ensemble the 5. Pick the crack logit bias on the 532 OOF predictions instead of 54 val cells. Report OOF CV metrics as the benchmark's development score.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: 5-fold module-grouped fold ensemble on 532 cells, bias from OOF. Baseline: house 5-seed ensemble on 478 cells (crack IoU 0.485-0.488 argmax, 0.492 with bias; inactive 0.456). Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: argmax crack IoU < 0.488 AND inactive IoU < 0.456.

title: Crossing the Validation Crisis: Cross-Validation Reduces Benchmarking Variance Surprisingly Well
mechanism: Repeated cross-validation splits act as a virtual enlargement of the test set (sample gain); gains keep growing past K=5 and an early-stop rule from split redundancy says when to stop.
adaptation: Module-grouped repeated CV over the 532 train+val cells using the existing fold roots (2 groupings x 5 folds), paired per split and seed; pooled out-of-fold crack/inactive IoU as the decision instrument; test-49 and E1 kept untouched for confirmation. Also lets logit bias / checkpoint be chosen on 532 OOF cells instead of 54 val cells.
min_experiment: Arm: house and PF on 10 grouped splits, 1 seed each, paired. Baseline: 5v5 seeds on clean test-49. Metric: SE of paired delta in pooled OOF crack IoU and minimum detectable effect (2.8 x SE). Kill: CV MDE not <= 0.008 (vs ~0.012 now).
evidence: R: MCCV at K=200 gave test-sample gain ~14 (Ridge) and ~15 (MLP) on synthetic data; real data (PCam histopathology CNNs/ViT, Yelp BERT) gains of about 5 to 20 at K=20, not converged at K=5; repeated K-fold comparable.
prior_overlap: BRIEF 4.5 notes grouped 5-fold roots exist; section 5 'never tried' lists k-fold cross-validated selection. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Make module-grouped 5-fold CV over 532 cells the primary comparison, clean-49 test and E1 as held-out reports; OOF predictions double as label-audit input.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Compare seed-pair standard error of crack IoU difference on CV vs clean-49 for house vs PF. Kill: none (measurement design).

title: MatchED: Crisp Edge Detection Using End-to-End, Matching-based Supervision
mechanism: A plug-in head of about 21K params. At each step it does one-to-one Hungarian matching, within distance tau_d, between confident predicted pixels and GT pixels. Matched GT moves to the matched prediction, unmatched GT is kept, and the crisp head is trained with BCE on this target.
adaptation: Crack and gridline only, tau_d = 2 px to match relF1@2. Candidate predictions are pixels with p > tau_c inside a 3 px dilation of GT, which keeps the cost matrix to a few thousand by a few hundred per cell, so scipy assignment on CPU is cheap. The head sits on top of the U-Net++ logits. Its 1 px output is dilated to the source's label width for strict IoU.
min_experiment: Arm: house + MatchED head (tau_d 2, tau_c 0.05), 5 seeds. Baseline: house at 100% labels. Metrics: relF1@2, relP@2/relR@2, recall of components >= 20 px, crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if relF1@2 and component recall are both within noise (< 0.01) or crack IoU drops by more than 0.012.
evidence: R: Average Crispness up 2 to 4x and ODS up 20 to 35% under crispness-emphasized evaluation on BSDS, NYUD, BIPED and Multi-cue, applied to PiDiNet, RankED, DiffusionEdge and SAUGE. Robust to tau_c (0.01 to 0.1) and tau_d (2 to 8). GPU memory reaches 28 GB at 320 px when tau_c = 0.01.
prior_overlap: Partly overlaps offset-tolerant CE (n.d.), which also tolerates shifts but allows many-to-one matches and so rewards thick output. One-to-one matching with a separate crisp head was not tested. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: tau_d = 2 px on the crack class only, on top of PF; one fixed jittered label per cell; tau_d = 0 control to separate the matching from the new sigmoid decision rule.
alt_notes.min_experiment: As T3 matched_crack_head after the corrected P-M4 pre-check: arm vs tau_d=0 control and PF; metric relF1@1 and strict IoU vs jittered CV labels, width 0.8-1.2; kill if arm minus control <0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: tau_d = 2 px, crack only, appended to the PF house decoder. One-to-one constraint stops the width blow-up seen with Skeleton Recall w 1.0.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm = PF + MatchED crack head; baseline = PF; 5 seeds + CV; metrics relF1@2, crack IoU, mean predicted width. Kill if relF1@2 gain < 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack and gridline only; tau_d = 2 px to equal relF1@2; restrict candidates to a 3 px dilation of GT plus confident pixels so per-cell scipy assignment is cheap (crack is 0.19% of pixels); re-dilate the crisp output to source width for strict IoU.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + MatchED head (tau_d 2, tau_c 0.05), 5 seeds; baseline house 5 seeds. Metrics relF1@2, components>=20px found, strict crack IoU. Kill if relF1@2 and component recall both n.d. and strict IoU drops. About 15 GPU-h.

title: Data-centric benchmark for label noise estimation and ranking in remote sensing Binary building segmentation
mechanism: Rank training images by label noise with an augmented or cross-validated ensemble: noise score = 1 - IoU(prediction, given label), optionally variance-weighted; train on the least-noisy part.
adaptation: Use module-grouped 5-fold roots to get out-of-fold 3-5 seed predictions for all 532 cells; crack noise = 1 - relF1@2 plus missed-component count (tolerant so 1 px jitter does not dominate), inactive noise = 1 - IoU. Do not drop cells (209 crack, 42 inactive): ignore crack loss on worst-ranked cells/components, keep all other classes. First check overlap with the 24 audit-flagged cells.
min_experiment: Arm: house model with crack loss ignored near label segments and on predicted-unlabelled components in worst 10% of cells by OOF crack noise. Baseline: house and PF, 5 seeds. Metric: clean-49 crack relF1@2 and IoU, 5-fold CV crack IoU, F51 AP. Kill: audit-cell overlap no better than random, or < +0.01 relF1@2 on CV and < +0.012 test crack IoU.
evidence: R: Kendall tau 0.61 / Spearman 0.77 vs CleanLab 0.17 / 0.24; U-Net on top-ranked 50% F1 80.34 vs 78.26 on all noisy data (oracle 80.98); boundary shrink/expand noise hardest for all methods. SpaceNet8-derived building set.
prior_overlap: BRIEF Labels row: audit flagged 24/239 cells, nothing fixed; automatic label refinement never run. Open.

title: Adaptive Early-Learning Correction for Segmentation from Noisy Annotations (ADELE)
mechanism: Detects per class the onset of memorisation from the train IoU curve against noisy labels, then from that point replaces labels with confident, multi-scale-consistent model predictions.
adaptation: Per-class curves for crack, inactive, gridline and splice on the 478 train cells. Correction is allowed only (a) within 3 px of an existing crack label, to re-centre it on the ridge while keeping that source's width, and (b) for new components with p>0.9 at every scale, to recover missing cracks. Padding, frame and structural classes are never corrected. Flips and rot90 only as consistency views (label-safe).
min_experiment: Arm: PF + ADELE on crack and inactive, 5 seeds, 20k steps. Baseline: PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: relF1@2 and relR@2 at relP@2>=0.90, components >=20 px found, crack IoU, inactive IoU on test-clean-49 and E1. Kill if relF1@2 gain <0.01 and component-recall gain <0.02, or if crack IoU drops by more than 0.012.
evidence: R (abstract): beats standard noisy-label methods on a medical segmentation task with noisy annotations, and is SOTA for weakly supervised segmentation on PASCAL VOC 2012. Thin-structure numbers were not read because the full text was unavailable.
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF section 5 lists noisy-label methods and automatic label refinement as never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Separate triggers for crack, inactive, gridline, splice, edge_dark; corrections allowed only within 2 px of existing crack labels (no new components) to protect recall.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + ADELE, 3 seeds on 5-fold CV. Baseline: house folds. Metric: fold-mean crack IoU, mIoU_rob. Promote only if gain >= +0.01. About 15 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Log per-class train IoU curves over the 20k steps; apply correction to crack only within 2 px of the original label, and to gridline, splice, edge_dark, material where labels look incomplete. Keep inactive uncorrected (well labelled).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + ADELE correction, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, gridline IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: crack IoU and mIoU_rob both within noise (under 0.012 and under 0.01).

title: MultiTalent: A Multi-Dataset Approach to Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Keep every dataset's classes distinct with one sigmoid head per class on a shared backbone; BCE + batch Dice only on classes a dataset annotates; losses summed; dataset sampling ~ 1/sqrt(n).
evidence: 13 CT datasets: +1.26 Dice average over datasets, largest gains on difficult/cancer classes; as pretraining beat SSL baselines.
adaptation: Keep 24-class softmax head for BenchmarkEL; add sigmoid heads for UCF crack_region/contact/interconnect/corrosion, MSS crack/dark/busbar/noncell, PV-Vision crack. Batches 50% BenchmarkEL; loss per head only on its dataset's cells. Joint from step 0 so no later fine-tune erases the shared encoder.
min_experiment: Arm: joint training with extra heads, 30k steps, 5 seeds, with source conditioning if D36 exp 1 passed. Baseline: house 5-seed. Metrics: clean-49 crack IoU, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if crack IoU < +0.012 AND E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 AND inactive IoU not up. ~15 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: BRIEF 5 'UCF-EL supervised pretraining of the encoder' was sequential pretrain then house fine-tune that erased the encoder; joint training is explicitly not closed

alt_notes.adaptation: Same run family as the partial-label loss. BenchmarkEL, MultiSolSegment (independent crack, busbar, dark) and UCF-EL in one model, with per-dataset loss masks on independent outputs.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Variant of the UCF joint run that adds MultiSolSegment with masked sigmoid losses. Baseline: PF. Metrics: E1 relF1@2, crack IoU. Kill if no gain over the UCF-only joint arm of >= 0.01 relF1@2.

alt_notes.adaptation: UCF-EL, MultiSolSegment, BenchmarkEL in one run with sigmoid outputs and dataset-specific loss masks; union-class loss for UCF from the Bevandic row.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Extension of the UCF joint run adding MultiSolSegment with masked channels; same baseline (PF) and kill line as the Bevandic arm.

alt_notes.adaptation: Add 5 per-source crack sigmoid channels (optionally per-source inactive) beside the 24-class softmax; each cell trains only its source channel; at test read the image's source channel. The same head admits UCF-EL 'crack' (a crack+inactive region class) and MultiSolSegment classes as their own channels for joint training without overwriting the thin-crack convention.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm A: per-source crack channels on house PF, 5 seeds vs house PF 5 seeds; clean-49 crack IoU and per-source CV crack IoU; kill if gain < +0.012. Arm B: + UCF-EL joint training with its own channel; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and recall; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03.

title: Causality-Inspired Single-Source Domain Generalization for Medical Image Segmentation (GIN + IPA)
mechanism: Random shallow conv nets re-map intensity and texture each step (GIN); two GIN views are blended with a smooth random spatial map (IPA) so neighbouring regions get independent appearance, removing confounder-to-label shortcuts; KL consistency between views.
adaptation: 1-channel EL fits directly (built for gray MRI/CT). Use 1x1 or 3x3 kernels and cap blend alpha so 1-2 px cracks are not blurred. IPA lattice of 8 to 16 cells per 512 px so streak-sized regions (scuff analogue) get their own appearance. No geometric change, so jittered crack labels stay aligned. Stack on house label-safe aug.
min_experiment: PF + GIN/IPA (p=0.5) vs PF, 3 seeds. Metric E1 crack relF1@2 and recall; guard test-clean-49 crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 or test crack IoU drops > 0.01. Selection on val/F51 only.
evidence: R: consistent Dice gains over ERM, RandConv, AdvBias, MixStyle on CT->MRI abdominal, bSSFP->LGE cardiac and cross-site prostate; ablation 4 layers / 2 hidden channels best (86.04 avg Dice abdominal without IPA). Small medical training sets.
prior_overlap: none: BRIEF s5 aug was flips/rot90/brightness/contrast only; intensity normalisation at inference failed but that is test-time, not train-time randomisation.

alt_notes.adaptation: 1-channel GIN with 1x1/3x3 kernels keeps 1-2 px crack geometry so labels stay valid; IPA masks use structural classes (ribbons, border, frame_edge, sp_multi grain) so their appearance cannot serve as a crack/inactive cue; aimed at E1 and weak BMRK/CSIR sources.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + GIN (p=0.5) + IPA on structural classes, also on PF. Baselines: house and PF. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, test mIoU_rob. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 and E1 inactive IoU < +0.03 on PF arm, or test mIoU_rob drop > 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: 1-channel GIN with 4 layers and 2 hidden channels; at least 2 layers with 1x1 kernels so 1 to 2 px cracks survive; renormalise intensity. The IPA blend map gives low-frequency, spatially varying contrast that looks like scuff streaks and uneven EL. Labels unchanged. Replaces brightness/contrast-only augmentation.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+GIN-IPA (p 0.5) vs PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 and relR@2, E1 inactive IoU; guard test clean-49 crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 or test crack IoU drop > 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply GIN (3x3 kernels, 1 channel) with p=0.5 on top of label-safe augmentation; geometry is untouched so 1 to 2 px labels stay valid. IPA regions = structural classes (busbar, ribbon, border, padding) so their appearance cannot act as a crack or source cue. Aims at E1 and weak sources (BMRK, CSIR).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + GIN-IPA, 5 seeds; also PF + GIN-IPA. Baseline: house and PF. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, test mIoU_rob. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 and E1 inactive IoU < +0.03 vs PF.

title: Component-Adaptive and Lesion-Level Supervision for Improved Small Structure Segmentation in Brain MRI (CATMIL)
mechanism: Adds a lesion-level multiple-instance term (per lesion, -log of the max probability inside it) and a component-adaptive Tversky term (voxel weight 1/(size+5)) to DiceCE, so every lesion gets a detection signal independent of size.
adaptation: Bags = crack instances after merging fragments (closing r 2-3 px, drop specks < 3 px), dilated by 2 px so one pixel anywhere on the 4 px dark line satisfies the bag (jitter tolerant); same for inactive components. lambda_MIL 0.2, MIL-only first. Targets the E1 failure where 70% of crack pixels get p < 0.001.
min_experiment: Arm: house + MIL on merged dilated crack/inactive instances (also PF variant), 5 seeds. Baseline: house and PF 5-seed. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 / relR@2; test clean-49 component recall <20 and >=20 px at relP@2 >= 0.90; crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02, or test crack IoU drop > 0.012 without relF1@2 gain.
evidence: MSLesSeg (nnU-Net): small-lesion recall 0.873 vs 0.796 DiceCE, missed lesions -48%, DSC comparable; ablation: MIL alone 0.871 (all of the gain), CAT alone 0.823 n.s.; more small FPs removed by a size filter; second dataset 3D-MR-MS same direction with more FPs.
prior_overlap: Skeleton Recall (w 1.0 / 0.1) shares the aim (thin-structure recall) but is a different mechanism; it widened predictions. MIL acts on one pixel per instance. No MIL or instance loss was run.

title: Knowledge distillation with ensembles of convolutional neural networks for medical image segmentation
mechanism: Train one CNN on the soft class probabilities of a seed or architecture ensemble. The distilled network keeps the ensemble's accuracy and beats the same network trained on reference labels.
adaptation: Teacher = our 5-seed PF ensemble with dihedral TTA. Save soft probabilities for the 478 train cells (mixed with or replacing the 1-2 px hard crack labels, whose soft band absorbs label jitter) and for the 11.9k CSIR/ARTS pool. Student = house U-Net++ R34 under PF, 1-channel, 512 px.
min_experiment: Arm A: PF student on train soft targets. Arm B: A + pool soft targets with strong aug. Baseline: PF single model (5 seeds) and the 5-seed ensemble. Metrics: clean-49 crack IoU and relF1@2, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob, E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU. Kill: B below PF single mean + 0.010 crack IoU and no E1 gain. Success: a single model reaches the ensemble's 0.485 crack IoU at argmax.
evidence: R: on 3 public datasets (chest CT 4 organs, brain MRI 6 structures, cardiac cine-MRI 3 structures), the distilled networks matched the uniform and diverse ensembles and significantly beat the same network trained on reference segmentations. E: our 5-seed ensemble gives +0.014 to +0.018 crack IoU, the only clear win so far.
prior_overlap: Partial. The BRIEF section 5 SSL row used an online Mean Teacher (an EMA of itself) with hard or tolerant pseudo-labels, and distillation is listed as never tried. An offline ensemble teacher with soft targets on labelled and pool cells has not been run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Same FINAL 5-seed teacher as the JML-KD arm, plain KL/CE on soft maps over train + pool cells; acts as the control that shows whether JML adds anything over classic KD.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: KL-KD student from FINAL ensemble, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Metric crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill: crack IoU < SUP100 + 0.009.

alt_notes.adaptation: Cache 5-seed house (and PF) softmax under the D4 group on the 478 train cells; student = house U-Net++ RN34, CE(GT) + crack/inactive Dice + KL to teacher (T 1-2). Soft targets carry the ensemble's 2-4 px crack band and per-source width that 1-2 px jittered hard labels lack.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: KD student, house recipe 20k steps, 5 seeds. Baseline: house single (0.474 crack IoU, 0.881 relF1@2) with 5-seed ensemble as upper reference. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2 on clean 49 and 5-fold module-grouped CV. Kill: student mean crack IoU < 0.481 and relF1@2 < 0.889.

title: Application of Decision Rules for Handling Class Imbalance in Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Replace argmax-of-posterior by a prior-corrected decision rule (posterior divided by class prior, globally or per pixel position) so rare classes are not ignored at inference.
adaptation: Zero training. Fit one logit bias per class (13 mIoU_rob classes plus splice) on out-of-fold logits from the existing module-grouped 5-fold roots, apply to the 5-seed ensemble. Position priors only for edge classes (edge_dark, frame_edge, border), not crack. Main target: splice (0.000, 4 test cells, worth +0.023 mIoU_rob at IoU 0.3).
min_experiment: Arm: per-class bias vector fitted by coordinate ascent on OOF mIoU_rob, applied to 5-seed ensemble; baseline: same ensemble with crack-only bias; metric test clean-49 mIoU_rob and splice IoU; kill if mIoU_rob gain < +0.01 or splice IoU < 0.05. Precede with per-class AP diagnostic on OOF logits.
evidence: R: street scenes, 20k frames: pedestrian instance recall +25%, info signs +23.4%, non-detection -61% / -38%.
prior_overlap: Partial: crack-only val-chosen logit bias already used in best ensemble; per-module thresholds failed. Per-class bias for all classes, chosen on OOF folds, never tested.

title: Coarse-to-fine crack cue for robust crack detection (CrackCue)
mechanism: Max-pool (k=8) plus upsample erases thin dark cracks; a skip-free encoder-decoder trained only on non-crack pixels refines this into a crack-free background; abs(image minus background) is concatenated as an extra input channel to any segmenter.
evidence: R: cross-dataset (train CrackTree, test 3 sets) ODS +5.7% U-Net, +7.6% CrackFormer, +4.2% DeepCrack; under defocus blur U-Net+CrackCue avg ODS 0.795 vs 0.739 (LIOT 0.723); under contrast perturbation 0.842 vs 0.668. Ablation: median and black-hat cues help moderately, Canny hurts.
adaptation: Learned golden cell for EL: mask crack (dilated to 5 px to cover the 4 px FWHM) and inactive from the reconstruction loss; keep k=8 at 512 px (also try 12); fingers, busbars and grain texture stay in the loss so the cue learns to suppress them; 2-channel input with conv1 channel 2 initialised from the mean ImageNet filter. Risk: scuff streaks on E1 are dark and unseen, so the cue may fire on them.
min_experiment: Arm: house U-Net++ + background net + cue channel, 5 seeds. Baseline: house (PF for E1 inactive). Metrics: test-clean crack IoU and relF1@2; E1 crack relF1@2 and recall in half-cut cells. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 and test crack IoU gain < +0.012.
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF 5 tried intensity normalisation and BN adaptation at inference, not a learned background-difference input channel.

alt_notes.adaptation: Mask crack and inactive (crack dilated to about 5 px, matching the 4 px dark-line FWHM) from the reconstruction loss so fingers, busbars and grain are learned as background; k=8 at 512 px (try 12); 2-channel input with conv1 channel 2 initialised from the mean ImageNet filter; watch E1 precision because scuff streaks are absent from training and may light up the cue.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + background net + |I-B| channel, joint loss weight 1, 5 seeds. Baseline: house U-Net++. Metrics: test-clean crack IoU and relF1@2, E1 crack relF1@2 and recall in the 20 scuff half-cut cells. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 AND test crack IoU gain < +0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: EL cracks are thin and darker, matching the prior. Dilate crack labels to about 5 px (4 px FWHM) and also mask inactive in the recon loss. Fingers and busbars are thin dark lines too, so the recon net must learn to rebuild them; inspect cue maps on mono vs multi and half-cut cells before training. Feed (EL, cue) as 2 channels to U-Net++ PF.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF U-Net++ with 2-channel (EL, cue) input, recon net trained per fold; plus a LIOT-input arm. Baseline: PF. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and recall, module-grouped 5-fold CV crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 or CV crack IoU drops > 0.01. 3 seeds per arm.

alt_notes.adaptation: EL cracks are thin and darker than context, so the prior fits. Dilate crack labels to about 5 px (FWHM 4 px) and also mask inactive in the recon loss. Fingers and busbars are thin dark lines too, so the recon net must rebuild them; inspect cue maps on mono, multi and half-cut scuffed pool cells first. Cue becomes a second input channel to U-Net++ PF.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: 2-channel (EL, cue) U-Net++ PF, recon net trained per fold; baseline PF; 3 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and recall, CV crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 or CV crack IoU drops > 0.01. Add a LIOT input arm in the same batch.

alt_notes.adaptation: 1-ch EL + cue as 2-ch input to house U-Net++ (conv1 widened, weights copied). Mask crack and gridline (dilated to 5 px) in the reconstruction loss. Start with the zero-parameter coarse cue, pool k in {4,6,8} since crack FWHM is about 4 px and fingers 2-3 px. Expect the cue to also fire on fingers and E1 scuff streaks: a chance for gridline recall and a risk for crack precision.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + coarse cue channel, 5 seeds, 20k steps; baseline: house 5 seeds (PF variant as second pair for E1). Select on val+F51, score test clean-49 and E1. Metrics: crack relF1@2, crack IoU, gridline IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03 and test relF1@2 not up, or test crack IoU drop > 0.012.

title: Jaccard Metric Losses: Optimizing the Jaccard Index with Soft Labels
mechanism: An IoU loss that is a true metric on [0,1], so it is minimised at prediction = soft target; this lets label smoothing and knowledge distillation be combined with an IoU loss, which the L1 soft Jaccard / soft Dice cannot do (they push soft-label predictions to 0/1).
adaptation: Distil the 5-seed FINAL (or PF) ensemble into one U-Net++ R34: CE + JML on hard labels plus CE + JML on teacher soft maps, over the 478 train cells and the 11.9k pool. JML only on crack and inactive (paper warns class-wise JML amplifies extreme minority classes), computed over the whole batch so it matches our pooled IoU (paper warns per-GPU small batches optimise per-image IoU), active classes PRESENT. House soft Dice must be replaced, since it breaks on soft targets.
min_experiment: Arm JML-KD student (5 seeds) vs SUP100 single (and SUP100-PF). Metrics clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU; E1 secondary. Kill if 5-seed mean crack IoU < SUP100 + 0.009 (half the ensemble gap) and relF1@2 n.d.
evidence: R: CE+JML beats CE alone by typically > 2% mIoU on Cityscapes, VOC, ADE20K over 13 models; JML-KD beats SOTA segmentation KD (e.g. DL3-R18 VOC 74.42 hard JML vs 75.89 JML-KD); BLS best at k=3, eps 0.5; with soft labels L1 soft Jaccard underperforms hard labels on VOC (74.13 vs 74.42).
prior_overlap: Partial: pseudo-label SSL at 100% with the 11.9k pool was n.d., but it used an EMA teacher of the same model, hard / tolerant labels and the old Dice. A 5-model ensemble teacher with soft targets and a soft-compatible IoU loss is untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Distil the 5-seed FINAL (or PF) ensemble into one U-Net++ R34 with CE + JML on teacher soft maps over the 478 train cells plus the 11.9k pool; JML only on crack + inactive, computed per batch to match pooled IoU; active classes filtered by teacher confidence (LABEL). House soft Dice must be replaced, since it breaks on soft targets.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: CE+JML hard + (CE+JML) on FINAL ensemble soft maps, train+pool, 5 seeds; control: same teacher with plain KL; baseline SUP100 single (repeat on PF). Metric crack IoU (clean 49, val bias), relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 inactive. Kill: crack IoU < SUP100 + 0.009 (half the ensemble gap) and relF1@2 n.d.

title: Rethinking Weight Decay for Robust Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models (Selective Projection Decay, SPD)
mechanism: Adam with an L2-SP style pull toward pretrained weights, applied per layer only when the layer's gradient opposes its drift from init (c_t < 0), scaled by a deviation ratio; strong pull on some layers, free movement on others.
adaptation: Apply SPD to the ResNet-34 encoder only (decoder is random init, no reference); conv1 reference = ImageNet RGB kernel summed to 1 channel as the house does. lambda grid {0.5,1,2.2}, house lr, 20k steps, CE + Dice. Replaces PF's freeze + 0.1x lr. Log per-layer cosine to init to confirm layer3/4 are kept.
evidence: PASCAL semantic seg, Swin-T IN21k, 60 epochs (read in full text, Table 4): mIoU ID / OOD-corruption avg: vanilla FT 66.03/44.00, L2-SP 73.47/56.70, LLRD 72.09/54.47, TPGM 72.56/56.96, FTP 73.79/58.45, Adam-SPD 74.27/60.06. Also DomainNet, ImageNet, LLaMA PEFT, VQA.
min_experiment: Arm SPD (encoder) vs SUP100-PF, seeds 5-9, 20k steps. Co-primaries: test clean crack relF1@2, test inactive IoU, E1 inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2; screen first on module-grouped 5-fold CV. Kill if no co-primary improves over PF and layer3/4 cosine to init is not higher than PF's.
prior_overlap: Partial: PF (freeze 1k + 0.1x encoder lr, no encoder wd) is a crude form of the same idea and helped E1 inactive. A per-layer selective pull toward init was never run; BRIEF section 5 lists the optimizer as never varied.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply SPD to the ResNet-34 encoder only (decoder has no pretrained reference); lambda in {0.5, 1, 2.2}; keep 20k steps, CE + Dice; replaces PF's freeze + 0.1x lr; log per-layer cosine to init to confirm layer3/4 are no longer erased.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house lr schedule + encoder SPD (3 lambdas, 5 seeds best lambda). Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metric: test clean crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU. Kill: no co-primary better than PF and layer3/4 cosine to init not above PF's.

title: Study Group Learning: Improving Retinal Vessel Segmentation Trained with Noisy Labels
mechanism: Uses K-fold study groups: each model predicts the fold it did not train on, and these out-of-fold predictions refine the labels, which are then distilled into the final model. Training also simulates erased thin vessels.
adaptation: Reuse the existing module-grouped 5-fold roots over the 532 train+val cells. The out-of-fold ensemble gives soft crack targets max(label, OOF p), restricted to the dark-ridge mask so the model does not learn scuff or gridline. Short crack segments are randomly erased from the labels as augmentation, which teaches robustness to missing annotations. Distil into PF.
min_experiment: Arm: OOF soft targets from 5 fold models (5 x 1.1 GPU-h), then PF retrain with 5 seeds. Baseline: PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: relR@2 at equal relP@2, component recall, crack IoU. Kill if relR@2 rises by less than 0.015 at equal relP@2.
evidence: R (from web abstract): improves vessel segmentation on DRIVE and CHASE_DB1, mainly when labels are noisy; small datasets (tens of images); thin structures. Verified through WebSearch only; Research MCP was down.
prior_overlap: none. Pseudo-label SSL (section 5) used unlabelled pool cells; it did not refine labels on the labelled cells with out-of-fold predictions.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use the existing module-grouped 5-fold roots over 532 train+val cells; fold models emit out-of-fold soft crack/inactive maps; final U-Net++ trained on 0.5 hard + 0.5 soft targets. Also distils part of the 5-seed ensemble gain into one model.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: SGL distillation single model. Baseline: house single model and house 5-seed ensemble. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU. Kill if single-model crack IoU gain < +0.008. About 12 GPU-h.

title: nnU-Net Revisited: A Call for Rigorous Validation in 3D Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Residual-encoder U-Net presets (ResEnc M/L/XL) scaled to a VRAM budget inside nnU-Net, plus validation rules: isolate confounders, equal compute, 5-fold CV, and keep only datasets whose inter-method SD exceeds their intra-method SD.
adaptation: Run ResEnc M and L (XL fits in 48 GB) in the 2D configuration at 512 px with label-safe augmentation on the module-grouped folds. For the benchmark, compute the inter/intra SD ratio for strict crack IoU, relF1@2 and inactive IoU on test-49, E1 and CV folds to pick headline metrics that separate methods beyond seed noise.
min_experiment: ResEnc L against ResEnc M against nnU-Net org, same folds and recipe (label-safe), CV-mean crack relF1@2, inactive IoU and E1 relF1@2; best preset also ensembled on test-49 against the house 5-seed ensemble. Kill: L not above M by 0.01 crack IoU or 0.02 inactive IoU in CV mean.
evidence: R (3D, from scratch, 6 datasets): KiTS DSC 86.04 org, 86.79 ResEnc M, 88.17 L, 88.67 XL; MedNeXt best on 5/6; transformers below original nnU-Net; U-Mamba Bot 91.79 against No-Mamba Base 91.89 on ACDC, so the Mamba layers had no effect. BTCV noise exceeded method signal.
prior_overlap: ResNet-50 U-Net++ was worse on inactive, but that was an ImageNet encoder, a U-Net++ decoder, the 20k-step Adam recipe and a fine-tune that erases layers 3 and 4. A residual encoder trained under the nnU-Net recipe is untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Every transformer arm must beat the tuned house U-Net++ under the same schedule on module-grouped 5-fold CV, not only the 50-cell test; nnU-Net 2D as a suite entry.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Protocol rule, not a run: apply 5-fold CV + 5 seeds and paired tests to all D23 arms; include nnU-Net 2D once.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark rule: each transformer arm must beat a tuned house U-Net++ at matched compute on module-grouped 5-fold CV, not only on the 50-cell test; include nnU-Net 2D in the suite.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Protocol only; plus one nnU-Net 2D run on the 5 folds as a suite entry.

alt_notes.adaptation: nnUNetPlannerResEncL (and XL, A6000 has 48 GB) in 2D on our 1-channel 512 px data with label-safe aug and module-grouped folds. Its validation rules (5-fold CV with rotating val plus independent test pool, size-matched baselines, no cherry-picked classes) define our benchmark protocol: CV over 532 cells + frozen test + E1, all 24 classes reported.
alt_notes.min_experiment: ResEnc-L 2D v the nnU-Net default 2D winner (arm A), same 5 folds; baseline also house 5-seed ensemble. Metric: CV crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if within 0.012 crack IoU and inactive IoU on CV and E1 relF1@2 not up 0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Run nnU-Net v2 2D ResEnc-M on 1-channel 512 px PNGs with all 24 labels, using splits_final.json = our module-grouped folds. One arm with nnU-Net default augmentation (it resamples 1-2 px cracks through rotation, scaling and elastic deformation) and one with label-safe augmentation. In the benchmark, every method is compared at matched compute, without ensembles, and the ensemble/TTA results go in a separate table.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: nnU-Net 2D ResEnc-M 5-fold ensemble (default aug and label-safe aug). Baseline: house fold ensemble on the same folds. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob, E1 relF1@2. Kill: crack IoU more than 0.01 below the baseline AND inactive more than 0.02 below (it stays as a benchmark baseline regardless). Needs the user's OK to install nnunetv2.

title: MultiSolSegment: Multi-channel segmentation of overlapping features in electroluminescence images of photovoltaic cells
mechanism: Per-channel sigmoid multi-label U-Net so one pixel can be crack and busbar, or crack and dark area, at the same time; trained with BCE on multi-hot masks.
adaptation: Keep the 24-class softmax head of the house U-Net++ and add 2 sigmoid channels (crack, inactive). The crack target keeps the 20% of train crack pixels that single-label masks assign to inactive. Per-channel thresholds chosen on val; final crack map from the sigmoid channel.
min_experiment: Arm: house PF + 2 sigmoid channels (BCE + Dice). Baseline: PF, 5 seeds each. Metric: test clean-49 crack IoU, inactive IoU, relF1@2. Kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and inactive IoU < +0.02.
evidence: R: 2,340 augmented images, 4 classes; mean-over-class IoU 0.384, Dice 0.503; crack count per image 4.34 v GT 5.29 v PV-Vision 6.03 (PV-Vision fragments cracks at busbars). Nested 5-fold CV. No crack-only IoU reported.
prior_overlap: none; multi-label heads are listed as never tried in BRIEF section 5

alt_notes.adaptation: Keep softmax for the 22 structural / other classes, add independent sigmoid channels for crack and inactive. Build overlap targets from our single-label masks: inactive channel = inactive label morphologically closed over the crack pixels it encloses (20% of train crack pixels lie in or at inactive), crack channel unchanged. Per-channel thresholds chosen on val. Optionally add the 585 MultiSolSegment cells with loss masked to the shared crack / dark channels and resampled to our crack width.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house U-Net++ + sigmoid crack and inactive heads (BCE + Dice). Baseline: house, 5 v 5 seeds. Metrics: test clean-49 inactive IoU, crack IoU, crack relF1@2. Kill if inactive IoU gain < 0.02 and relF1@2 gain < 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Keep house U-Net++ R34; add sigmoid crack and inactive channels (BCE + soft Dice) next to the softmax head for the other 22 classes. Build multi-label targets: inactive = hole-filled inactive region including crack pixels inside it; crack = crack label even inside inactive. Thresholds chosen on val. Targets the 20% of train crack pixels in/at inactive regions that argmax must split.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house + multi-label crack/inactive heads vs house and PF, 5 seeds each; inactive IoU (clean 49, E1), crack IoU, relF1@2; kill if inactive IoU gain < 0.02 on both test and E1 and crack IoU not >= house.

alt_notes.adaptation: Independent crack and inactive channels (shared run with the region head). Also let crack overlap busbar and ribbons, where crack labels are now broken. Optionally add its 585 cells with the loss masked to the shared channels (crack, busbar, dark ~ inactive).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Same arm as the region-head run, plus a variant that adds MultiSolSegment cells with masked loss. Baseline: PF. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, crack components >= 20 px found, inactive IoU. Kill if crack IoU gain < 0.012 and inactive CV IoU gain < 0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: EL precedent for the region head: independent crack and inactive channels, and let crack overlap busbar/ribbon. Optionally add its 585 cells with loss masked to shared channels (crack; dark area as weak inactive).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Shared with the region-head run: PF + independent sigmoid crack/inactive (+ crack over busbar) vs PF; crack components >=20 px found and relF1@2 on clean 49; kill if relF1@2 gain < 0.01 and component recall gain < 0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: (a) 585 extra crack-labelled cells for joint runs, with own source flag. (b) Add crack and inactive sigmoid channels on top of the softmax head, since 20% of our train crack pixels lie in or at inactive regions where argmax drops one.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + 2 sigmoid channels, 20k steps, 5 seeds. Baseline: house 5-seed. Metric: clean-49 relR@2 at equal relP@2, inactive IoU. Kill if relR@2 < +0.02 and inactive IoU not up. ~6 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Three sigmoid channels (crack, inactive, dark) on PF, so the 20% of crack pixels lying in or at inactive regions are no longer lost to argmax. Its outputs are also the clean inputs for the isolated-area rules. The paper says the code is in the sandialabs/pvcracks repo; the repo was not opened.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Shared with D27 experiment 1. Arm: PF + 3 sigmoid channels with BCE + soft Dice. Baseline: PF. Metrics: CV inactive IoU, crack IoU, relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU. Kill if inactive gain < 0.02 and crack IoU drop > 0.012. About 12 GPU-h.

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Canonical Knowledge Distillation for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: At matched compute and long schedules, plain logit / feature KD beats segmentation-specific KD; pure logit KD keeps scaling with unlabelled images while feature KD does not.
adaptation: Pure logit KD from the frozen 5-seed ensemble (full 24-class soft targets) over 478 labelled + 11.9k pool cells (incl. 1,152 half-cells), 60k-100k steps; keep the teacher architecture-aligned (U-Net++ family).
min_experiment: Arm: student on GT + pool KD, 60k steps, 3 seeds. Baseline: labelled-only KD student (Noothout arm) and house single. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU on CV / clean 49; E1 relF1@2 secondary. Kill: < +0.012 crack IoU over labelled-only KD and < +0.02 E1 relF1@2.
evidence: R: Cityscapes PSPNet-R18 student 79.0 vs R101 teacher 79.8 mIoU (feature KD, 55 GPU-h); pure logit KD + 20k unlabelled images also 79.0; Mask2Former teacher gave 77.8 vs 77.7 at 3x compute.
prior_overlap: partial: Mean Teacher with hard/tolerant pseudo-labels on the 11.9k pool at 100% labels was n.d.; that closes single EMA teachers with thresholded labels, not a frozen 5-seed ensemble with soft full-distribution targets and long schedules

title: Analyzing Overfitting Under Class Imbalance in Neural Networks for Image Segmentation
mechanism: With small data, test-time logits of rare classes shift toward the decision boundary while the majority class does not; asymmetric margin / focal losses applied only to the rare class counter the shift.
adaptation: Asymmetric large margin on the true-class logit of crack, inactive, gridline, splice, edge_dark, material only. First verify the logit shift on our checkpoints (train vs val vs E1 crack-logit histograms); E1 shows 70% of crack pixels at p<0.001, consistent with the claim.
min_experiment: Arm: margin m in {0.5, 1.0}, 3 seeds each on house config; baselines SUP100 and PF; metric test crack recall and mIoU_rob, E1 crack recall secondary; kill if test crack recall gain < 0.02 and E1 recall gain < 0.03.
evidence: R (full text): KiTS kidney tumor, 100% data, post-processed: DSC 79.2 -> 82.3, sensitivity 77.0 -> 81.4 with asymmetric large margin; consistent sensitivity gains on BRATS, ATLAS, KiTS at 10-100% data.
prior_overlap: none: offset-tolerant CE and Dice variants tested, margin / asymmetric focal never tested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Our symptoms match: inactive recall 0.61, and on E1 70% of crack pixels get p<0.001. Apply stronger photometric augmentation only to crack and inactive cells or pixels: contrast, gamma, noise, and a simulated downscale-and-pad for the BMRK style. Add an asymmetric margin on classes 11 and 14. This acts at training time, unlike the inference logit bias already in use.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+asymmetric rare-class augmentation vs PF, 5 seeds plus CV. Metrics: CV inactive IoU, BMRK inactive IoU, E1 crack recall@2. Kill if CV inactive gain < +0.015 and E1 recall@2 gain < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Strong photometric augmentation (contrast, gamma, noise, simulated downscale for BMRK) only inside dilated crack and inactive masks; asymmetric margin on classes 11 and 14. Training-time, unlike the inference logit bias already used.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+ASYM vs PF; CV inactive IoU, BMRK inactive IoU, E1 crack recall@2. Kill: CV inactive < +0.015 and E1 recall@2 < +0.02.

title: Controllable flow matching synthesis for generalizable crack segmentation with a 50k image-mask benchmark (CrackSegFlow)
mechanism: Pixel-space flow-matching mask-to-image renderer with topology-preserving mask injection and boundary-gated modulation, plus a class-conditional mask generator and rectified-flow injection of a crack mask onto any crack-free background.
adaptation: 1-channel renderer trained on 256 px crops at native 512 scale from the 478 train cells only; condition on the crack mask (dilated to 3 px) plus a 5-source one-hot so it learns each source's line width and contrast; masks sampled from train crack masks with rotation/elastic/width changes; inject onto the 1,152 unlabelled multi half-cut pool cells and scuff-bearing cells so scuffs become hard negatives for E1.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + rendered pairs on half-cut pool cells (<=30% of batch), 5 seeds. Baseline: PF 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and recall@2; guard test crack IoU clean 49. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 or test crack IoU drop > 0.01.
evidence: R: +5.37 mIoU / +5.13 F1 in-domain averaged over 5 crack sets with 16x synthetic pairs; CrackTree260 (1 px centreline labels, 400 train crops at 256 px) 38.2 -> 49.5 mIoU; target-guided cross-domain +13 mIoU / +14.7 F1; latent diffusion conditioning blurs or misaligns hairline cracks (qualitative). Trained on 2 A100.
prior_overlap: Partly overlaps CP100 (real crack components pasted onto pool cells, house model, n.d. on test). Still open: CP100 moved real crack pixels without adapting appearance, used no new shapes or widths, did not select half-cut/scuff backgrounds, was not scored for E1 as the primary metric, and used the house fine-tune, not PF.

alt_notes.adaptation: Train the renderer on our 209 crack cells; inject sampled crack masks into pool half-cells with scuff streaks, producing labelled half-cut + scuff crack cells, the exact E1 condition that training lacks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + 2,000 injected half-cells (+ real) vs PF, 3 seeds. Kill if E1 crack recall in scuff cells gains < +0.10 or test crack precision drops > 0.03.

title: Disentangling Human Error from the Ground Truth in Segmentation of Medical Images
mechanism: Two coupled CNNs: a true-label segmentation head and per-annotator pixel-wise confusion matrices, with a trace regulariser that pushes annotator matrices to be maximally unreliable so the clean head stays clean.
adaptation: Treat the 5 image sources (ARTS, CFVS, CSIR, BMRK, SDLE) as annotators with confusion heads over {bg, crack, inactive, other}; source id is known at test, so score both the clean head and the source-specific head (learns BMRK/SDLE 3 px width vs ARTS 1.5 px).
min_experiment: Arm: house + 5 source confusion heads. Baseline: house 5 seeds. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, per-source crack IoU (BMRK, CFVS). Kill if clean-head IoU < house - 0.005 and source-head IoU < house + 0.012. About 6 GPU-h.
evidence: R: MSLSC, BraTS, LIDC-IDRI with real and simulated multi-annotator labels; beats baselines most when annotations are few and disagreement large (abstract).
prior_overlap: none; annotator / source-style modelling and source-conditional prediction are listed as never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Per-source pixel confusion matrices over a reduced 4-class space (bg, crack, inactive, other) conditioned on source id. They can absorb BMRK widening and the crack/inactive overlap that a single-label argmax must resolve. The true head is used at test.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Run only if PADL shows any gain. Arm: house + CM head per source, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, inactive IoU, BMRK. Kill if there is no detectable difference versus house.

alt_notes.adaptation: Treat each of the 5 sources as one annotator. The per-source spatial confusion head learns how each source widens or shifts crack labels. Source is known from the filename for test and E1, so score both the latent output and the source-styled output.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + per-source confusion head (crack and inactive channels), 5 seeds; report source-styled output. Baseline: house. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU per source (BMRK, CFVS), overall crack IoU. Kill: overall crack IoU gain under 0.012 and no source gains more than 0.03. First run a no-GPU check: predicted vs label crack width per source on val.

alt_notes.adaptation: Annotator = source, with 5 confusion matrices restricted to crack / inactive / background to save memory. Score the source-specific output on strict IoU and the latent output on relF1@2 and E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm = house PF + CM head (5 seeds) versus house PF. Metrics: crack IoU (source output) and relF1@2 / E1 relF1@2 (latent output). Kill if both are under the +0.012 IoU / +0.01 relF1 line.

alt_notes.adaptation: Annotator = source; CMs over {background, crack, inactive, other} only to keep memory low. Score the source-CM output with strict IoU against source labels and the latent output with relF1@2 and on E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: CM model on house backbone, 5 seeds. Baseline: house PF. Metrics: clean-49 crack IoU (source output), relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2 (latent output). Kill if neither beats the baseline by +0.012 IoU or +0.02 relF1@2.

alt_notes.adaptation: Each source and external dataset is an 'annotator'; restrict confusion to crack/inactive/background (3x3); score the clean head.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + annotator branch, BenchmarkEL only then with external data, 20k steps, 5 seeds. Baseline: house 5-seed and source-conditioned arm. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and relF1@2. Kill if crack IoU < +0.012. ~8 GPU-h.

title: Full-Resolution Network and Dual-Threshold Iteration for Retinal Vessel and Coronary Angiograph Segmentation
mechanism: Keeps a full-resolution stream so 1 px structures never pass through a stride. Dual-threshold iteration (DTI) then grows low-confidence pixels that connect to high-confidence ones, a hysteresis step.
adaptation: Two arms. (a) DTI needs no training: apply hysteresis growth (high seed threshold, low growth threshold, 8-connected) to the existing 5-seed ensemble crack probabilities, with thresholds chosen on val and F51. (b) smp U-Net++ drops the full-resolution feature (its finest skip is conv1 at 1/2). Add a 3-layer stride-1 conv branch (32 ch) on the 1-channel input and concatenate it into the last decoder block.
min_experiment: (a) DTI on house ensemble outputs vs the same ensemble at argmax and with the val-chosen logit bias. Metric: test-clean crack relR@2 at relP@2 >= 0.90, plus E1 recall. Kill if the relR@2 gain is < 0.01 at matched relP@2. (b) Detail branch vs house, 5 v 5 seeds. Kill if crack IoU gains < 0.012 and relF1@2 gains < 0.01.
evidence: R: the abstract reports the best Sen, AUC, F1 and IoU on most of DRIVE (20 train images), CHASE_DB1, STARE, DCA1 and CHUAC, with fewer parameters, and says DTI greatly improves sensitivity and connectivity. Ablation numbers not retrieved.
prior_overlap: Partial. A val-chosen logit bias (a global threshold) was run in section 5. A connectivity-conditional threshold was not, and no full-resolution branch was ever tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: DTI as pure post-processing on saved crack probabilities of the house and PF ensembles (t_high, t_low chosen on val). FR-UNet trained from scratch on 1-ch 512 px cells, 24 classes, as a heterogeneous ensemble member.
alt_notes.min_experiment: A (0 GPU-h): DTI on 5-seed house and PF ensemble logits vs current val-chosen logit-bias operating point; metric test relR@2 at matched relP@2, components >=20 px found. Kill: relR@2 gain < 0.01 at equal relP@2. B: FR-UNet 5 seeds vs house 5 seeds; kill if single model crack relF1@2 < house - 0.02 and adding it to the ensemble does not raise ensemble relF1@2.

title: nnU-Net for Brain Tumor Segmentation (region-based training)
mechanism: Replace the softmax over exclusive labels with per-region sigmoid outputs and BCE + Dice on nested, overlapping regions that match the evaluation regions.
adaptation: Keep the 24-class softmax for the other classes. Add 3 sigmoid channels. D = crack OR inactive (the damaged area). I = inactive, hole-filled, so it includes crack pixels inside it. C = crack, kept even inside inactive. Inference: softmax argmax, then overwrite with I > t_I, then C > t_C, with thresholds chosen on val or fold CV. D is a large, easy target that shares features between the two rare classes. This frees the 20% of crack pixels that argmax currently gives to inactive.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + D/I/C sigmoid channels with overlap targets. Baseline: PF (5 seeds). Metrics: inactive IoU on module-grouped 5-fold CV and on clean 49, crack IoU, relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU. Kill if the CV inactive IoU gain is < 0.02 and crack IoU falls by more than 0.012.
evidence: R (tables 1 and 2 of the PDF): 5-fold CV mean Dice 86.09 -> 86.73 with region training (tumour core +1.0, enhancing +2.0). Validation 83.76 -> 84.13. 369 training cases, 3D MRI.
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF section 5 lists multi-label heads as never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Keep 24-class softmax; add 3 sigmoid channels D = crack OR inactive, I = inactive hole-filled, C = crack kept inside inactive (recover crack layer under inactive from 2022 correction layers or mask the loss there). Final map: argmax, then write I, then C (outer to inner) with val/CV thresholds.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + D/I/C sigmoid heads (BCE+Dice), 5 seeds + module-grouped 5-fold CV; baseline PF; metrics inactive IoU (CV and clean 49), crack IoU, relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU; kill if inactive CV IoU gain < 0.02 and crack IoU drop > 0.012.

title: Focal Inverse Distance Transform Maps for Crowd Localization
mechanism: Regress a focal inverse distance transform map (sharp peak at each label, smooth fall-off) instead of a binary or Gaussian map, then read out by local-maximum detection.
adaptation: Crack-only extra regression head on the U-Net++ decoder with target 1/(d^(a d+b)+c), d = distance to nearest crack label skeleton pixel, so a 1 px label shift changes the target smoothly. Read-out: ridge NMS along predicted normal, draw at per-source width chosen on val (ARTS 1.5, CFVS/CSIR 1.75, BMRK 3, SDLE 3.25 px). 24-class CE head kept for all other classes.
min_experiment: E0 first (no GPU): skeletonise house-ensemble crack predictions on CV folds and redraw at width 1-4 px per source to measure IoU headroom. Then arm = PF + FIDT crack head (MSE + I-SSIM), two read-outs (ridge-drawn vs CE logit with FIDT as auxiliary); baseline = PF house, 5 seeds, clean-49 test + module-grouped 5-fold CV; metrics relF1@2, components >=20 px, crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if CV relF1@2 gain < 0.01 and E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03.
evidence: R: SOTA crowd localisation on six crowd datasets and one vehicle set; more robust on negative and very dense scenes. No thin-line test.
prior_overlap: Partial: offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) and Skeleton Recall (wider, IoU worse) also tolerate shift, but neither changed the output to a regressed distance field with a ridge read-out. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack-only auxiliary head on the U-Net++ decoder; target from distance to the crack label skeleton (1.0 at 0 px, 0.5 at 1 px, 0 beyond 20 px), computed after augmentation; 24-class CE head unchanged. Team CPU pre-check: FIDT of a mask and its 1 px shift correlate at median 0.919 vs binary IoU 0.548. Optional read-out: ridge NMS then draw at per-source width.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + FIDT aux (stacked with orientation, as T5 arm 4) vs PF, cv5v2 2 seeds x 5 folds; metric crack components >=20 px found and relF1@2, width ratio guard; kill if components +<0.02 and relF1@2 +<0.01, or strict crack IoU down >0.01.

title: BiCC: Bidirectional Connected-Component Loss for Instance-Aware Segmentation
mechanism: DiceCE on Voronoi cells of each GT component plus a branch on Voronoi cells of predicted components that penalises pure false-positive components with a size-independent mass score; alpha trades lesion precision vs recall.
adaptation: 2D 8-connectivity on merged crack instances and inactive components; GT Voronoi cells precomputed in the loader, prediction cells per step via GPU connected components on 8 x 512 px. Replaces soft Dice on crack/inactive; CE on 24 classes kept. FP branch penalises decoys (scuff streaks, gridline look-alikes) per component.
min_experiment: Arms: alpha 0 (CC-DiceCE) and 0.5, 5 seeds each vs house 5 seeds. Metrics: component F1 on merged instances (test clean-49, E1), relF1@2, crack and inactive IoU. Kill: component F1 not above house by 0.02 on both sets.
evidence: 5 datasets (AutoPET III, ISLES, BraTS-METS, LiTS, CMB), 5-fold nnU-Net: lesion F1 significantly above DiceCE on 3, tie on 2; CC-DiceCE loses up to 0.363 precision; post-hoc thresholding of DiceCE cannot reproduce the alpha sweep; +17-23% training time on A6000.
prior_overlap: Global logit bias was tried (ensemble); BiCC shows threshold shifts cannot reproduce its precision-recall shift. No component-wise loss run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack: GT branch for small missed cracks, prediction branch for decoys (scuff streaks on half-cut E1 cells, busbar edges); alpha tuned on val relP@2/relR@2.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house loss + BiCC on crack, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100 and the CC-DiceCE arm. Metric components found, relP@2, E1 false-alarm components. Kill: components found < +0.02 at relP@2 drop <= 0.02.

title: Do Vision Foundation Models Enhance Domain Generalization in Medical Image Segmentation?
mechanism: Frozen VFM (DINOv2, SAM, MAE) tuned with Rein / Rein-LoRA / Ladder plus a strong decoder head; VFMs match CNNs in-domain but generalise much better to unseen scanners.
evidence: R (full text): 10 to 198 training volumes, greyscale MRI/CT. DINOv2 + Rein-LoRA DG Dice: brain 52-55 vs 44 for ResNet101-UNet; lumbar spine 31-41 vs 1-6 for U-Nets; in-domain about equal. Larger VFMs help DG slightly, not ID.
adaptation: Use as a side branch on the house PF U-Net++ R34 (VFM-H): frozen DINOv2-L at 1024 px (grey to 3 channels) with Rein-LoRA, features added at stride 16/32 decoder inputs; house keeps the 1-2 px crack path. Target E1 (half-cut, scuff), plus leave-BMRK-out as a source-shift probe.
min_experiment: Arm VFM-H (DINOv2-L + Rein-LoRA) vs house PF; module-grouped 5-fold CV + one E1 opening; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU, CV crack relF1@2; kill if CV relF1@2 drops >0.005 AND E1 relF1@2 not +0.03 over about 0.42 AND E1 inactive IoU not above 0.24.
prior_overlap: Section 5 foundation row tested only linear probes and a 4k-step ConvNeXt-T PF screen; no PEFT, no ViT-L, never judged on E1. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use its ranking of VFM + PEFT pairs to pick VFM-H's backbone and tuning method before spending GPU time; the 5-source plus E1 split is our analogue of multi-site DG.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No own arm: read the full text (open access) and choose the two VFM + PEFT pairs it ranks best for VFM-H; kill this item if its best pair is not one we already plan.

alt_notes.adaptation: Template for our E1 study: same PEFT x head grid, our 5 sources as domains (leave-one-source-out), E1 as the external domain.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Leave-one-source-out CV over the 5 sources for house vs best FM arm; metric held-out-source crack relF1@2; kill if mean gain < 0.02.

title: Image-Level Regression for Uncertainty-Aware Retinal Image Segmentation (SAUNA)
mechanism: Convert hard thin-structure masks to soft targets from distance to the annotation boundary and local thickness, then train as regression with a generalised JML plus a stable Focal-L1 loss.
adaptation: Crack only: SAUNA transform of the 1-2 px crack labels, thickness term normalises source width (ARTS 1.5 px to SDLE 3.25 px); separate sigmoid crack head with GJML + SF-L1 next to the 24-class softmax trained with house CE; crack threshold re-picked on val. BMRK (downscaled ELPV) is the aliasing case where the paper's evidence is strongest.
min_experiment: Arm: SAUNA crack targets + GJML + SF-L1, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Metric crack IoU at val-chosen threshold, relP@2, relR@2, BMRK crack IoU. Kill: crack IoU < SUP100 + 0.012 or relP@2 drop > 0.05.
evidence: R: FIVES, low-res input, UNet++ BCE+Dice hard 74.05 IoU; JML+BLS 81.77; SAUNA+GJML+SF-L1 84.75; UNet++ high-res hard 81.70. +0.4 to +2.3 IoU over BLS on STARE, DRIVE, CHASEDB1, HRF.
prior_overlap: none: soft-label regression targets never run; offset-tolerant CE and Skeleton Recall are different mechanisms.

title: Pixel-accurate road crack detection in presence of inaccurate annotations
mechanism: Measures the cost of inaccurate crack annotations under tolerance-free scoring using the Syncrack synthetic set with controlled label noise, and corrects crack labels with weakly supervised label-noise-correction before retraining.
adaptation: Train house model, replace crack labels by its confident predictions only inside a 2 px band around the original label, retrain. For the benchmark: synthesize EL cracks with exact labels plus controlled 1 to 2 px jitter to quantify what jitter costs strict IoU.
min_experiment: Arm: house model retrained on self-corrected crack labels (band-limited to 2 px), 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and relF1@2. Kill: crack IoU change under +0.012 and relF1@2 change under +0.01.
evidence: R: inaccurate annotations reduce F by up to 20%; corrected labels improve Syncrack results by up to 12%; gains also reported on CrackForest and Aigle-RN (real data).
prior_overlap: none. Pseudo-label SSL in section 5 added pool data; it never replaced the labelled crack masks.

alt_notes.adaptation: Our crack labels sit off the dark ridge (half the points over 1 px away). Fold-held-out models propose a re-placement of each crack label pixel onto the predicted ridge within 2 px; retrain on corrected train labels only, 2 rounds.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF trained on ridge-snapped crack labels; baseline PF on original labels; 3 seeds. Metric: strict test crack IoU against original labels, relF1@2. Kill if strict IoU drops > 0.01 and relF1@2 n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: build EL images with exact crack masks (copy-paste or a physics generator) plus jittered label copies at the measured 1 px / source-width noise. This shows how much of the strict-IoU gap each method recovers, and justifies relF1@2 alongside strict IoU.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training arm at first. Build jittered copies of 30 train cells with clear ridges; check that the generator reproduces the measured 1 px-shift IoU of 0.56; then score arms 1 to 8 on it. Kill the track if the noise model cannot match the measured inter-annotation IoU of 0.21 to 0.26.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use its protocol as an EL synthetic-jitter probe: add known 1 px / 2 px offsets and width changes to train crack labels, measure strict IoU vs relF1@2 sensitivity; decides whether label-noise arms can move strict IoU at all.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house on train labels with +1 px and +2 px synthetic jitter (2 levels x 5 seeds). Baseline: house. Metric: strict crack IoU and relF1@2. Decision: if +1 px jitter costs < 0.01 strict IoU, judge label-noise arms on relF1@2 only. About 11 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Our crack labels are 1 to 2 px lines, half of points more than 1 px off the dark ridge, widths differ by source. Fold-held-out models propose a snap of each label pixel onto the predicted ridge within 2 px; 2 rounds; crack class only; inactive labels untouched.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF trained on corrected crack labels; baseline: PF on original labels; 3 seeds. Metric: strict test crack IoU vs original labels, relF1@2, and IoU vs corrected held-out labels. Kill if strict IoU drops > 0.01 and relF1@2 n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Build a synthetic-EL crack test bed (pasted synthetic cracks with exact GT) and simulate each source's labelling convention (width 1.5-3.25 px, 1-2 px offset); test which metric ranks models by true accuracy.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: 300 synthetic cells, 3 existing models. Metric: Kendall tau between ranking under exact GT and jittered labels for strict IoU, NSD@2, relF1@2. Kill: strict IoU tau within 0.1 of NSD@2.

title: Local Intensity Order Transformation for Robust Curvilinear Object Segmentation
