mechanism: Encodes each pixel as 4 channels of 8-bit codes: is the pixel darker than each of its 8 neighbours (1 to 8 px away) to the left, right, top and bottom. The code is invariant to any monotone contrast change.
adaptation: EL cracks are dark lines about 4 px FWHM, which is exactly the LIOT prior. Use a 5-channel input (raw + 4 LIOT) under PF, with the ResNet-34 stem weights extended to the new channels. This targets contrast differences across the 5 sources and the E1 CSIR half-cuts. Risk: gridlines, busbars, cell edges and scuff streaks are also darker than their context, so false positives may rise.
min_experiment: LIOT+raw PF vs PF house, 5 seeds. Primary metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and recall. Guard: test-clean crack relF1@2. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains < 0.03 or test relF1@2 drops by > 0.01.
evidence: R (full text): in-dataset results are about equal to baseline (slightly worse on retina, competitive on CrackTree). Cross-retinal (DRIVE/STARE/CHASE, 3 random splits) gives a better mean and smaller standard error on Se, Acc, AUC, F1 and connectivity. Retina-to-CrackTree transfer is also reported.
prior_overlap: Partial. Inference-time intensity normalisation failed in section 5. LIOT is a different mechanism: a contrast-invariant representation used during training.

alt_notes.adaptation: Feed [EL, LIOT x4] (5 channels) rather than LIOT alone to keep in-distribution signal; neighbour range about 8 px to span a 4 px crack; per-source check on BMRK because LIOT degraded under blur in the CrackCue tables.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with [EL, LIOT x4] input, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: test crack IoU, relF1@2, per-source crack IoU (BMRK, CFVS), E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.03, or test crack IoU drop > 0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Input-side, not output-side. Stack LIOT channels with raw 1-channel EL (5 channels, re-init the 4 extra first-conv channels). Aimed at E1 contrast shift and half-cut scuff streaks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm = PF with LIOT+raw input; baseline = PF; 5 seeds; metrics E1 crack relF1@2 and recall, test crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03 or test IoU drops > 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Input [EL, LIOT x4] (5 channels) so in-distribution signal is kept; order window about 8 px to cover 4 px dark lines. Targets source contrast differences (5 sources) and CSIR E1. BMRK (downscaled, blurry) and the noisy CSIR cell are the risk cases.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with [EL, LIOT] input, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, per-source test crack IoU (BMRK, CFVS), test crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 and test crack IoU drop > 0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Compute LIOT on the 1-ch EL cell; input [EL, LIOT] (5 ch) or LIOT only; run on house and PF since E1 inactive depends on PF. Aimed at E1 contrast / source shift; watch for extra finger and scuff false alarms.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house and PF with [EL, LIOT] input, 5 seeds each; baseline: house / PF 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and recall, test crack IoU as guard. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03 or test crack IoU drop > 0.015.

title: MIC: Masked Image Consistency for Context-Enhanced Domain Adaptation
mechanism: On target images, the student sees a patch-masked input and must match confidence-weighted pseudo-labels that the EMA teacher made from the full image. This forces the student to use context.
adaptation: Target = the 1,152 multi half-cells + CSIR pool cells, which look like E1 (half-cut, scuff streaks). Source = the 478 labelled cells. Patch 32 to 64 px at 512, mask ratio 0.5 to 0.7, EMA 0.999, weight 1, pixel confidence weighting. Implement as masking added to the existing Mean Teacher code.
min_experiment: Arm MIC-E1 vs house PF, 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU, plus a clean-49 crack IoU guard. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains less than 0.03, or if test crack IoU drops by more than 0.01.
evidence: R: GTA->Cityscapes +2.1 mIoU on HRDA (73.8 -> 75.9), +4.3 on CS->DarkZurich. DeepLabV2 R101 gains +1.2 to +4.5. Largest gains on low-baseline classes (fence +5.4, pole +2.6). Removing confidence weighting costs 1.6. Training time +24%.
prior_overlap: BRIEF row 'Pseudo-label SSL' explicitly leaves open 'UDA-style methods aimed at E1 with target-like data'. Masked consistency with a half-cut target pool was never run. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Target domain = the 1,152 multi half-cells (plus multi cells) in the unlabelled pool, never E1 itself. Use 32 px mask patches. Drop the crack-class loss inside masked patches, since a thin crack under a mask cannot be inferred, and keep it for inactive, busbar/ribbon and background. Aimed at the half-cut layout and scuff false alarms.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house PF + MIC loss on half-cell pool as target, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, half-cut false alarms on H36/F51, clean-49 crack IoU non-inferiority (max -0.01). Kill: E1 crack relF1@2 gain < +0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Target = unlabelled pool cells like E1 (the 1,152 multi half-cells plus CSIR cells), never E1. Patch 32 px, ratio 0.5. E1 cracks get p<0.001, so crack pseudo-labels will be missing; the useful signal is DACS pasting true-labelled source cracks into half-cut, scuffed target context. Use class-wise thresholds and do not force uncertain crack pixels to background.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+DACS+MIC on half-cell+CSIR pool vs PF and the best augmentation arm, 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, recall@2 in the 20 scuffed half-cut cells; guard test crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 or test crack IoU drop > 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Target = 1,152 unlabelled pool half-cells (never E1). Patch 32 to 64 px, mask ratio 0.5 to 0.7. Keep confidence weighting; use a lower threshold or tolerant pseudo-labels for crack (<1% pixels). Risk: teacher gives p<0.001 to 70% of E1-like cracks, so MIC helps only if context, not local contrast, is the failure.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + MIC on pool half-cells vs PF and vs PF + EMA self-training without masking (isolates masking), 3 seeds. Kill if E1 crack relF1@2 gain over the no-mask arm < +0.03.

title: SelectSeg: Uncertainty-based selective training and prediction for accurate crack segmentation under limited data and noisy annotations
mechanism: A deep-ensemble uncertainty flags likely-wrong crack annotations, training uses only trusted pixels, and the model abstains on uncertain test regions.
adaptation: The 5-seed house and PF ensembles already exist, so uncertainty maps cost no extra training. Ignore a train pixel when all 5 seeds disagree with its label beyond 2 px: label says crack but ensemble p<0.02 within 2 px, or label says background but ensemble p>0.9 on a dark ridge. Retrain. The abstention map becomes a reliability output for the benchmark.
min_experiment: Arm: house model with the ensemble-disagreement ignore mask, 5 seeds. Baseline: house, 5 seeds. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, BMRK crack IoU. Kill if both crack IoU and relF1@2 show no detectable difference. Sanity check on train only: share of the 24 audited cells that get flagged.
evidence: R (from web listing): on real crack datasets with noisy annotations it beats existing methods, and both selective training and selective prediction help. A noisy CRACK500 mask set (10 to 100% of masks noised) is on Mendeley. Exact numbers not retrieved.
prior_overlap: none. The 5-seed ensemble was used only at inference, never to filter training labels.

alt_notes.adaptation: Rank train cells by 5-seed ensemble disagreement with the crack label; unlabel the crack channel of the top 10% (about 24 cells, the audit count) and train them through the existing MT consistency branch. Report coverage vs crack F curve.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: filtered cells as unlabelled + MT. Baseline: house. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and relF1@2. Kill if crack IoU < house + 0.008. About 8 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use the existing 5-seed ensembles to rank train cells and crack components by disagreement with the label; demote the worst 5 to 10% (the audit flagged 24 of 239 cells) to ignore regions or unlabeled; retrain.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house trained with ensemble-flagged components set to ignore, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, relR@2 and E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: crack IoU under +0.012 and E1 relF1@2 under +0.02.

title: DAFormer: Improving Network Architectures and Training Strategies for Domain-Adaptive Semantic Segmentation (Rare Class Sampling)
mechanism: Rare Class Sampling: draw a class c with P(c)=softmax((1-f_c)/T), T=0.01, then draw a uniform image containing c, so images with rare classes are seen far more often.
evidence: Table 5 ablation, GTA to Cityscapes, SegFormer: no RCS 58.2, class-balanced (T=inf) 62.0, RCS T=0.01 64.0 mIoU (+5.8). Largest gains on rare classes rider, train, motorcycle, bicycle. Source set is about 25k synthetic images.
adaptation: Compute f_c from the 478 train masks over the 24 classes, using only classes present in at least 3 cells. Cap any single cell at 10x its uniform draw rate so the 42 inactive cells do not overfit. Keep label-safe augmentation and the 20k steps. This should mainly lift inactive, splice, gridline, edge_dark and material, plus the BMRK cells that carry inactive.
min_experiment: PF+RCS vs PF, 5 seeds each. Metrics: module-grouped 5-fold CV inactive IoU, test mIoU_rob, splice and gridline IoU, with test crack IoU as a guard. Kill if CV inactive gain < +0.02 and mIoU_rob gain < +0.005, or if crack IoU drops by more than 0.012. About 31 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: none. The handbook records no oversampling or class-aware sampling run; the house sampler is uniform.

alt_notes.adaptation: f_c = fraction of the 478 train cells containing class c (splice 53, inactive 42, edge_dark 41). T in {0.1, 0.01}. Fixed 20k steps so the iteration budget is matched. Also usable later to oversample half-cut synthetic views for E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: RCS T=0.01, 5 seeds, 20k steps; baseline SUP100; metric mIoU_rob and inactive IoU; kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01 and inactive n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: f_c over 24 classes from the 478 train masks; candidates only classes in >= 3 train cells; cap any cell's draw rate at 10x uniform so the 42 inactive cells are not memorised; same 20k steps, label-safe augmentation unchanged.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+RCS vs PF, 5 seeds; metrics module-grouped CV inactive IoU, test mIoU_rob, splice/gridline IoU, crack IoU guard. Kill: CV inactive < +0.02 and mIoU_rob < +0.005, or crack IoU drop > 0.012.

title: Marginal loss and exclusion loss for partially supervised multi-organ segmentation
mechanism: Marginal loss sums predicted probabilities over the classes a partially labelled dataset merges into one label; exclusion loss pushes labelled pixels away from mutually exclusive classes.
evidence: Multi-organ CT from several partially labelled datasets; marginal + exclusion beat naive merging (numbers not re-read in this pass).
adaptation: UCF crack polygon supervised as log(p_crack + p_inactive); UCF background as marginal over all 24-class structural classes UCF does not label; UCF contact/corrosion/interconnect pixels excluded from crack. Single house softmax head, no new heads.
min_experiment: Arm B of joint run: single softmax + marginal/exclusion on UCF and MSS, 30k steps, 5 seeds. Baseline: house 5-seed. Metrics and kill line as MultiTalent arm. ~15 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: none; cross-dataset joint training never tried

title: SUPER Module for Detail-Sensitive and Cost-Efficient U-Net Variant Decoders
mechanism: Wavelet-domain decoder block: DWT of decoder features, a learned per-channel bounded suppression (tanh(CBAM) x learnable scale) subtracted from all subbands, and an inverse DWT that replaces spatial upsample + refine.
adaptation: Replace the U-Net++ upsample + conv refine at the 256 and 512 px decoder levels with Haar IDWT + suppression. Implement Haar as fixed 2x2 convs; keep the ResNet-34 encoder and the PF schedule; 1-channel input unchanged.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + SUPER at decoder levels 0 and 1, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, components >= 20 px found. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012 and relF1@2 < +0.01.
evidence: R: CrackVision12K with a FACS-Net baseline. IoU on 0 to 2 px cracks 0.356 -> 0.451, 2 to 4 px 0.398 -> 0.415, average 0.629 -> 0.646; CTS also up.
prior_overlap: none in BRIEF section 5 (2x resolution n.d. is a different mechanism). Also listed by D09.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace U-Net++ decoder upsampling and refinement blocks with SUPER blocks; ResNet-34 encoder and head unchanged; report crack IoU binned by component size.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF with SUPER decoder; baseline PF; 3 seeds. Metric: crack recall on components under 20 px, CV crack IoU. Kill if small-component recall gain < +0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace U-Net++ decoder upsampling blocks with SUPER blocks, encoder unchanged; report crack metrics binned by component size since 76 to 88% of crack components are under 20 px.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF with SUPER decoder; baseline: PF; 3 seeds. Metric: recall on crack components < 20 px, CV crack IoU. Kill if small-component recall gain < +0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace the U-Net++ upsample + conv at the top two decoder levels (256, 512 px) with Haar IDWT + suppression, Haar implemented as fixed 2x2 convs; keep the ResNet-34 encoder and PF schedule.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + SUPER at decoder levels 0 and 1; baseline PF; 5 seeds; crack IoU, relF1@2, components >= 20 px found; kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and relF1@2 < +0.01. About 8 GPU-h.

title: SWAD: Domain Generalization by Seeking Flat Minima
mechanism: Dense stochastic weight averaging over a loss-plateau window of training gives flatter minima and better unseen-domain accuracy.
adaptation: Average weights every 100 steps from about 8k to 20k in house and PF runs; window chosen on F51 / val loss, never on test. Recompute BN stats on train after averaging. Targets E1 (new modules, half-cut, scuff).
evidence: +1.6 points average out-of-domain accuracy over prior SOTA on PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita, DomainNet (classification).
min_experiment: In-run arm: same PF runs s5-9 save raw and SWAD weights (paired within run). Metric: val relF1@2 and F51 crack AP, then E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU at an opening. Kill if SWAD - raw < +0.005 val relF1@2 paired and E1 not better.
prior_overlap: none. Ensembling 5 seeds was tested (only clear win); weight averaging within a run was never run (BRIEF section 5 lists EMA / SWA as never varied).

alt_notes.adaptation: Average PF weights every 200 steps from 10k to 20k, recompute BN on train. Near-free; may also reduce the 1-in-6 wrecked-run variance.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + SWAD vs PF final checkpoint, same 3 seeds. Kill if test crack IoU gain < +0.01 and E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: PF recipe + dense averaging every step from ~8k to 20k at constant or cyclic lr; window chosen on F51 / H36, never on E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + SWAD, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF single. Metric: E1 relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU; test crack IoU guard. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.02 or test crack IoU loss > 0.005.

alt_notes.adaptation: Average weights every 100 steps from about 8k to 20k, window chosen on F51/CV val loss; recompute BN on train after averaging. E1 (new modules, half-cut, scuff) is the DG target.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + SWAD (same run, raw vs averaged, 5 seeds). Baseline: SUP100-PF raw weights. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU, test crack relF1@2. Kill: averaged minus raw < +0.005 val relF1@2 and E1 not better.

title: TopoMortar: A dataset to evaluate image segmentation methods focused on topology accuracy
mechanism: Controlled benchmark of 8 topology losses under small data, noisy labels and OOD. Self-distillation (3 rounds of retraining on the model's own soft labels) raises both Dice and topology accuracy under noisy labels.
adaptation: Use self-distillation as a noisy-label arm for 1-2 px jittered crack labels: split the house 20k steps into 3 rounds of about 6.7k, each trained on the previous round's softmax for crack and inactive (hard labels for the other 22 classes). Adopt its protocol (10 seeds, paired permutation test, Betti or component errors reported next to overlap) for our benchmark.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + 3-round self-distillation, 5 seeds, 20k total steps. Baseline: PF 5 seeds. Metrics: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, predicted crack width. Kill if crack IoU gain < 0.012 and relF1@2 gain < 0.01.
evidence: R: nnU-Net, 10 seeds. CrackTree Dice: CEDice 0.78, cbDice 0.76, Warping 0.77, clDice 0.54, SkelRecall 0.32, TopoLoss 0.52. clDice / SkelRecall cut beta0 error (22 / 14 vs 84). Noisy labels: SkelRecall best topology. Self-distillation improved Dice and Betti errors with pseudo and noisy labels.
prior_overlap: Losses overlap the clDice and Skeleton Recall rows. Self-distillation on the labelled set is untested here: SSL used the external pool, and noisy-label methods and distillation are listed as never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Self-distillation on PF: 3 x 6.7k steps inside the 20k budget, rounds 2 and 3 trained on the previous round's softmax for all 24 classes (soft crack targets spread around jittered 1 to 2 px traces). Its protocol (10 seeds, paired permutation tests, Betti errors only next to overlap, reported augmentation) is a template for the EL benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + 3-round self-distillation vs PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, width, inactive IoU. Kill if crack IoU gain < 0.012 and relF1@2 gain < 0.01.

title: SAM3-UNet: Simplified Adaptation of Segment Anything Model 3
mechanism: SAM3 image encoder with a simple adapter and a light U-Net decoder; under 6 GB at batch 12.
adaptation: 1008 input (2x of 512), 3-ch replicated EL, 24-class head, house loss and schedule; run in parallel with SAM2-UNet and keep the better for ensembles.
min_experiment: SAM3-UNet vs house PF and vs SAM2-UNet; 5-fold CV then 3 seeds clean-49 + E1; same kill line as SAM2-UNet.
evidence: R (from CoRe-SAM3 Table 2): SAM3-UNet 68.6% mean crack IoU over 5 crack sets (84-2,357 train images) vs native SAM3 62.3%, crack specialists 67.8-70.0%.
prior_overlap: none; SAM3 never tried here.

alt_notes.adaptation: Same recipe as SAM2-UNet on the SAM3 encoder at 1008 px (2x upscale of 512); 24-class head; house loss and aug. Provides the SAM3 encoder arm.
alt_notes.min_experiment: SAM3-UNet @1008, 3 seeds vs house and vs SAM2-UNet; same metrics; kill as SAM2-UNet. Run only after weights licence OK.

title: Bridging the Data Gap: Spatially Conditioned Diffusion Model for Anomaly Generation in Photovoltaic Electroluminescence Images (E-SCDD, PV-DDPM)
mechanism: Mask-conditioned DDPM generates EL cells of four types (mono, multi, half-cut multi, IBC) from feature and defect masks, allowing controlled single- or multi-defect synthesis.
adaptation: Train PV-DDPM on the 478 train cells only (exclude E-SCDD F51/H36, which are our val). Generate half-cut multi cells carrying real train crack and inactive masks to cover the E1 gap (0 half-cut train cells) and the 42-cell inactive shortage; add at about 20% sampling.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + 500 PV-DDPM half-cut cells. Baseline: PF, 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU; guard: test crack IoU may not fall more than 0.012. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 and E1 inactive IoU < +0.03.
evidence: R: FID 4.10, KID 0.0023; E-SCDD = 805 real + 195 synthetic annotated cells, 30 classes, new sp_multi_halfcut class, 43 new half-cut cells; AA-CLIP pixel AP +8.34. Never evaluated with a segmenter.
prior_overlap: Partial: synthetic half-cut views (geometric, not generative) n.d.; +107 real E-SCDD cells n.d. Generative synthesis is open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Arm A: add the 195 labelled synthetic cells (30 half-cut) to training, no generator work. Arm B: train the generator on train cells plus E-SCDD half-cut cells not in H36 val (avoid leakage), render half-cut cells from train crack masks, add scuff-like streaks with no crack label as hard negatives.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm A and B vs house, 5 seeds; E1 crack recall and relF1@2 on half-cut subset, clean-49 crack IoU; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03 and test crack IoU drops > 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Retrain on our 478 train cells only (its training data, SCDD 20221008, was reshuffled against our split and may contain our test/E1 cells). Condition on the 24-class one-hot plus source id instead of binary masks. Use for inactive and other blobby classes, not 1 px cracks. Feed it physics-edited layouts: add isolated inactive regions to train cells that have crack but no inactive (167 cells).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + 500 synthetic inactive cells (FreeMask-filtered), 5 seeds. Baseline: PF 5 seeds. Metric: module-grouped 5-fold CV inactive IoU over 532 cells, plus E1 inactive IoU. Kill: CV inactive IoU gain < +0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Rerun AA-CLIP under our split and metrics as the VLM AD baseline; for scores, use generated half-cut cells with defects (E1-like) as training data via the generative-data directions.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark: AA-CLIP binary map on clean-49 and E1 with pixel AP and relF1@2; for scores, arm house + PV-DDPM half-cut synthetic cells vs baseline PF, metric E1 crack relF1@2 on CV-equivalent half-cells (H36), kill if gain < +0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Retrain on our 478 train cells only, since the released model may have seen test or E1 cells (see D06). Use it as an inpainter (with the SARD row) for inactive regions, and to generate half-cut multi cells from edited crack masks for E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + retrained PV-DDPM inactive insertions vs PF + inactive copy-paste (Soft-CP arm). Metric: CV inactive IoU. Kill if not above the copy-paste arm.

alt_notes.adaptation: Retrain on our train cells only (leakage), use as a PV-aware inpainter for defect removal (GDI's own stated limitation) and for half-cut layouts with edited crack masks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+GDI(DDPM inpainter) vs PF+GDI(LaMa). Kill: not above LaMa arm.

title: Dino U-Net: Exploiting High-Fidelity Dense Features from Foundation Models for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Frozen DINOv3 ViT with an adapter that fuses ViT semantics with a conv low-level spatial branch, plus a fidelity-aware projection into a U-Net decoder; accuracy rises with backbone size up to 7B.
adaptation: DINOv3 ViT-L/16 at 1024 input (and one frozen ViT-7B run on 48 GB A6000), 24-class head, house loss; the conv spatial branch is what must carry the 1-2 px cracks; 1-ch to 3-ch.
evidence: R: SOTA on 7 public medical segmentation datasets; scaling gains to 7B (abstract).
min_experiment: Dino U-Net ViT-L @1024, 3 seeds vs house U-Net++ and PF; same read-outs as SAM2-UNet; kill if crack IoU < 0.465, relF1@2 < 0.875 and E1 relF1@2 < 0.43.
prior_overlap: Frozen DINOv3 ViT-S linear probe and DINOv3 ConvNeXt-T PF screen (4k steps, judged on F51 crack AP) showed no gain. Large ViT, adapter with spatial branch, 1024 input not tested; open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Repeat 1-ch EL to 3 ch; DINOv3 ViT-L/16 at 512 px gives 32x32 tokens, so a conv-stem skip path at 1/2 and 1/4 resolution must carry the 1-2 px cracks; keep CE + soft Dice on crack/inactive, 24 classes, label-safe augmentation.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm Dino U-Net (ViT-L) vs baseline PF, 5 seeds; metrics CV crack IoU / relF1@2 then E1 relF1@2; kill if below PF by > 0.01 crack IoU and < +0.03 E1 relF1@2. About 30 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Repeat 1-ch EL to 3 ch; DINOv3 ViT-L/16 at 512 gives 32x32 tokens, so the conv skip path at 1/2 and 1/4 resolution must carry 1-2 px cracks; keep CE + soft Dice on crack/inactive and the 24-class head; compare ViT-S/B/L to test scaling.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm Dino U-Net (frozen DINOv3 ViT-L) vs PF baseline, 5 seeds; metrics test crack IoU and relF1@2, E1 crack relF1@2, mIoU_rob; kill if test crack IoU is > 0.01 below PF and E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: DINOv3 ViT-L/16 or H+ frozen at 1024 input; spatial branch at stride 2 and 4 from raw EL; 24 classes; house loss. DINOv3 weights are gated (user OK needed).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Dino U-Net ViT-L vs house PF, 5-fold CV then 3 seeds clean-49 + E1; default kill line.

alt_notes.adaptation: Run as a stand-alone benchmark arm (1-channel replicated, 512 and 1024 px, 24 classes) and borrow its projection module for VFM-H.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Dino U-Net (ViT-L) vs house PF and vs VFM-H; CV crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 relF1@2; kill if more than 0.01 CV relF1@2 below VFM-H and no E1 gain.

title: Foreground Sampling and Spatial Support in Pavement Crack Segmentation
mechanism: Controlled study at 2 px tolerance AP: crack-biased crop sampling hurts because it makes background area unreachable; GroupNorm instead of BatchNorm lifts a random-crop U-Net.
adaptation: (a) Swap every decoder BatchNorm2d in U-Net++ for GroupNorm(16) while the pretrained encoder keeps BN, batch 8 of mixed sources. (b) Any crack/inactive oversampling or cropping we add must keep the whole cell reachable. Their paired-seed, prespecified-contrast protocol with a practical floor is a template for the benchmark.
min_experiment: Arm: PF with GroupNorm decoder, 5 seeds. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metric: test clean crack relF1@2, crack IoU, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU both within 0.012 of PF.
evidence: R (full text): Crack500 full-res, U-Net from scratch, AdamW 3e-4, 20k updates, batch 16, BCE+Dice, flips+rot90, 3 paired seeds. AP2 random crops 0.812 (BN), positive-only 0.789, 10% positive 0.730; positive-only made 47% of area unreachable. GroupNorm random 0.844 vs BN 0.812 (+0.032).
prior_overlap: none; normalisation and sampling never varied here.

title: Long-tail learning via logit adjustment
mechanism: Add tau*log(class prior) to logits inside the CE during training (or subtract post hoc), a Fisher-consistent loss for balanced error.
adaptation: Priors from train pixel frequencies over the 17 present classes; apply to the CE term only, keep crack + inactive Dice. tau in {0.5, 1.0}. Watch crack width (prior 0.19%) and re-tune the crack bias after.
min_experiment: Arm: LA-CE tau 0.5 and 1.0, 3 seeds each; baseline SUP100 5 seeds; metric mIoU_rob plus splice/gridline/edge_dark IoU on OOF folds then test once; kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01 or crack IoU drop > 0.01 after crack bias re-tune.
evidence: R: classification long-tail benchmarks (CIFAR-LT, ImageNet-LT, iNaturalist); BLV paper also uses it as a fully supervised segmentation baseline.
prior_overlap: none for training-time LA; only post-hoc crack bias exists.

title: Towards High-Quality Image Segmentation: Improving Topology Accuracy by Penalizing Neighbor Pixels (SCNP)
mechanism: Before the loss, each foreground logit is replaced by the worst value among its same-class foreground neighbours and each background logit by the worst among background neighbours, so the model must fix neighbours first. Three lines of code, no inference cost, wraps CE, Dice, clDice or Skeleton Recall.
adaptation: Wrap the house CE + Dice over all 24 channels, window 3 (best window is about structure width; ours is 1 to 2 px). Thin classes crack, gridline (recall 0.33) and splice should gain most. Because it is symmetric it penalises false positives beside the line as hard as misses on it, so it should not widen predictions like Skeleton Recall did. Jitter risk: background pixels 1 px off a drawn crack get the max off-line crack logit, so run a second arm with SCNP on all classes except crack.
min_experiment: PF + SCNP (all classes) and PF + SCNP (all but crack) vs PF, 5 seeds each. Metrics: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, gridline IoU, E1 relF1@2, predicted crack width. Kill if crack IoU < PF - 0.012 and gridline IoU gain < +0.02 and E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02.
evidence: R: 13 datasets, 5 runs each. Lowest beta0 error on TopoMortar and Crack500 without lowering Dice or clDice. FIVES: CEDice beta0 10.82 to 6.94 at equal Dice 0.92; SkelRecall 12.45 to 5.07 with SCNP; clDice 36.55 to 5.44. Binary closing only reached 8.79. clCE on FIVES beta0 10.62. DeepGlobe roads: topology up but Dice down slightly.
prior_overlap: none. Section 5 ran clDice, Skeleton Recall and offset-tolerant CE; neighbour-worst logit penalisation was never run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply to the CE term over all 24 classes with a 3x3 neighbourhood. Crack and gridline (recall 0.33) and splice are thin lines that should gain continuity. With 1-2 px jittered crack labels the worst neighbour is often a mislabelled pixel, so also try crack + gridline only or a capped penalty.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + SCNP on CE, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF 5 seeds. Metrics: clean-49 crack IoU, gridline IoU, E1 crack relF1@2, predicted width. Kill if crack IoU < baseline - 0.012 and gridline gain < 0.02 and E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.02.

title: Better Aggregation in Test-Time Augmentation
mechanism: Simple-mean TTA can turn correct predictions wrong; learn per-augmentation aggregation weights instead.
adaptation: D4 group (flips x rot90, label-safe, already in training aug) mean TTA on singles and ensemble first; then per-class per-transform weights fitted in 5-fold CV (val too small alone).
min_experiment: Arm: D4 mean TTA on 5 singles and the ensemble. Baseline: same checkpoints without TTA (paired). Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2, components >= 20 px, inactive IoU on clean 49 / CV. Kill: paired gain < 0.005 crack IoU on singles.
evidence: R: consistent gains over mean TTA across models, datasets and augmentations (classification).
prior_overlap: none; per-panel BN adaptation (failed) is test-time adaptation, not TTA; flip/rot/multi-scale TTA listed as open

title: Segment Any Crack: Deep Semantic Segmentation Adaptation for Crack Detection
venue: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering
mechanism: Fine-tune only the normalization parameters (LayerNorm gain and bias) of a foundation model and the head; this beats full fine-tuning and other PEFT in accuracy and in generalization to unseen datasets.
adaptation: Arm (a): house ResNet-34 U-Net++ with all encoder conv weights frozen, BN affine plus decoder trained (a stricter PF). Arm (b): a large frozen encoder (SAM or DINOv3 ViT-L) with LN-only tuning and a U-Net++ style decoder, 24-class head, gray replicated to 3 channels. Aimed at E1 where encoder preservation already moved inactive IoU 0.05 to 0.24.
min_experiment: Arms (a) and (b) vs baseline PF, 3 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, CV crack IoU. Kill if neither arm beats PF by +0.03 E1 relF1@2 or +0.05 E1 inactive IoU while CV crack IoU stays within 0.01.
evidence: R: SAC reaches F1 61.22% and IoU 44.13% on OmniCrack30k test, best mean on three zero-shot datasets with lowest std; norm-only beat full fine-tuning across SAM and five other segmentation models.
prior_overlap: Partial: PF (frozen 1k steps then 0.1x lr) tested encoder preservation; norm-only tuning and large frozen ViT with norm tuning are untested (section 5 lists large ViT, adapters as open).

alt_notes.adaptation: (a) House ResNet-34 U-Net++: freeze conv weights, train BN affine plus decoder (a stricter PF). (b) Frozen DINOv3 ViT-L or SAM encoder, LayerNorm-only tuning, U-Net++ style decoder, 24-class head, 1-channel EL replicated to 3. Aimed at E1, where PF already moved inactive IoU 0.05 to 0.24.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arms (a) and (b), 3 seeds each, vs house PF. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU, module-grouped 5-fold CV crack IoU. Kill if neither arm beats PF by +0.03 E1 relF1@2 or +0.05 E1 inactive IoU with CV crack IoU within 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: (a) Norm-only tuning of the SAM2 / DINOv3 encoder inside the FM arms; (b) house U-Net++ R34 with encoder convs frozen, only BN + decoder trained (stricter than PF), aimed at E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: House norm-only encoder vs PF, 5 seeds; success = E1 crack relF1@2 +0.03 or E1 inactive IoU > 0.28 with CV crack relF1@2 drop <= 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: SAM ViT or SAM2 Hiera encoder LN-only plus a trainable multi-class conv decoder at 1024; tests whether minimal encoder drift helps E1 the way PF helped E1 inactive.
alt_notes.min_experiment: LN-only arm inside the PEFT grid vs house PF; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU, plus clean-49 crack IoU; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03 and test crack IoU drops > 0.01.

title: Exponential Moving Average of Weights in Deep Learning: Dynamics and Benefits
mechanism: EMA of weights as a plug-in gives solutions that generalise better, are more robust to noisy labels, more consistent and better calibrated, with less need for lr decay.
adaptation: Add EMA (decay 0.999 and 0.9998, BN recomputed) to house and PF runs; evaluate EMA vs last iterate from the same runs; targets positional noise in crack labels.
min_experiment: Arm: EMA weights of 5 runs. Baseline: last iterate of the same 5 runs (paired). Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU on clean 49 / CV; E1 relF1@2. Kill: paired diff < 0.005 crack IoU and < 0.01 E1 relF1@2.
evidence: R: systematic study on image classification; EMA improves generalisation, noisy-label robustness, prediction consistency, calibration and transfer.
prior_overlap: partial: EMA teacher in Mean Teacher runs was within +-0.005 of the student, under SSL losses; supervised EMA on house/PF never varied (BRIEF optimizer row)

alt_notes.adaptation: Add EMA (decay 0.999 and 0.9998) to house and PF; recompute or EMA BN stats. Crack labels are 1-2 px jittered, i.e. label noise, which is where the paper reports EMA helps. Paired raw vs EMA from the same run reduces seed noise (problem 5).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF+EMA vs PF raw weights of the same runs, seeds 5-9. Metric: test clean crack IoU and relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if EMA - raw < +0.005 relF1@2 paired over 5 seeds and inactive not better.

alt_notes.adaptation: EMA decay 0.999 and 0.9998 on house and PF runs; EMA BN buffers or recompute them; raw vs EMA is paired within a run, which removes seed variance. Crack label jitter is the label noise case.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + EMA (0.999, 0.9998), 5 seeds. Baseline: same runs' raw weights and SUP100-PF. Metric: val relF1@2, then test clean crack relF1@2, crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill: EMA minus raw < +0.005 val relF1@2 paired over 5 seeds.

title: MuGE: Multiple Granularity Edge Detection
mechanism: A small network estimates a granularity scalar from each annotation. The scalar is injected into the multi-scale and high-frequency features, so one model can output edges at any requested granularity or annotator style.
adaptation: Condition on label style, not granularity: a per-cell scalar for measured crack label width and mean offset to the dark ridge, or a source one-hot. Implement as FiLM in the U-Net++ decoder. At test time give the known source, or the value that is best on val. This targets the BRIEF point that strict IoU near 0.5 is a ceiling unless the model learns each source's convention.
min_experiment: Arm: house + FiLM style conditioning, 5 seeds. Baseline: house at 100% labels. Metrics: per-source crack IoU (BMRK 0.379, CFVS without train twin 0.397), overall crack IoU, E1 relF1@2 using the CSIR style. Kill if no source gains >= 0.02 and overall crack IoU is n.d.
evidence: R: one model produces multiple controllable edge maps and is competitive on BSDS500 and Multicue. Per-number detail not read (snippets were rate-limited).
prior_overlap: BRIEF 5 lists source-conditional prediction as never tried. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Condition on label style instead: per-cell scalar of measured crack label width and mean offset to the dark ridge, or a source one-hot, via FiLM in the U-Net++ decoder; at test feed the known source or the val-optimal value, so the model reproduces each source's convention.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + FiLM source/label-width conditioning, 5 seeds; baseline house 5 seeds. Key metric per-source crack IoU (BMRK 0.379, CFVS-no-twin 0.397) and overall crack IoU. Kill if no source gains >= 0.02 and overall n.d. About 8 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace discrete source ID with a continuous per-cell label width w (crack area / skeleton length of that cell's label, about 1 to 3.5 px) fed through FiLM to the decoder; captures within-source annotator variation. At test set w to the source median width, or tune w per source on CV folds.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house PF + width-FiLM, 5 seeds, w = source median at test; second readout with CV-tuned w. Baseline: house PF 5 seeds. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and relF1@2. Kill if crack IoU gain < +0.012.

title: Rethinking Pre-training and Self-training
mechanism: A fixed teacher pseudo-labels extra data, and the student is trained on labels plus pseudo-labels under strong augmentation. Self-training helps at every label size, including 100%, when the augmentation is strong.
adaptation: Our house uses weak label-safe augmentation because hard 1-2 px labels break under resampling. Soft teacher probabilities can be resampled bilinearly, so pool images can take scale jitter 0.75-1.5, small rotation, blur and gamma. Labelled cells keep label-safe aug. Teacher = the ensemble of paper 1.
min_experiment: Arm B of the ensemble-distillation experiment, run with and without strong aug on pool images (aug ablation). Baseline: PF single model. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and relF1@2, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: strong-aug arm not better than weak-aug arm by +0.005 crack IoU or +0.02 E1 relF1@2.
evidence: R: COCO detection, self-training +1.3 to +3.4 AP at every data size including 100% labels, while ImageNet pretraining hurt at full COCO. PASCAL segmentation +1.5 mIoU over the previous SOTA (90.5 mIoU), on top of a pretrained model.
prior_overlap: Partial. The BRIEF SSL row (Mean Teacher with CutMix, 11.9k pool, 100% labels) was n.d. That run used an online EMA teacher and weak label-safe geometry. An offline stronger teacher with soft labels and strong scale augmentation on the pool is open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use strong geometric and photometric aug (scale jitter 0.5 to 2, elastic, blur, gamma) only on pseudo-labelled pool cells: the pseudo mask is warped with the image, so the label-safe rule for jittered GT does not apply. Use the L_h/L_p EMA normalisation (decay 0.9997). Can be combined with the Naive-Student arm.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Within the NS-12k arm, compare student aug = label-safe vs strong (5 seeds each). Metric: crack relF1@2 and IoU on clean-49, E1 relF1@2. Kill if strong aug is n.d. vs label-safe.

title: Devil Is in the Edges: Learning Semantic Boundaries From Noisy Annotations (STEAL)
mechanism: A thinning loss forces a single response peak along the edge normal, and active alignment moves noisy 1-2 px edge labels toward the true boundary by level-set evolution during training.
adaptation: Treat crack as an edge class. Every N steps, snap each crack label polyline to the ridge of the current crack logit within +/-2 px, keeping the source's width convention, and add the normal-direction NMS loss on the crack channel only. The released code is old inference code (PyTorch 0.4), so we would reimplement it.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + periodic label snapping + NMS loss, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, crack pixel precision. Kill if crack IoU falls more than 0.012 below baseline, or if relF1@2 shows no detectable difference.
evidence: R (abstract): edge datasets carry label noise that pushes detectors toward thick predictions; STEAL improves on a CASENet backbone and can refine coarse labels. Its edges are 1-2 px wide, the closest structural analogue to our crack labels.
prior_overlap: Partial. Offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) took a per-pixel min over shifts. STEAL instead re-aligns labels persistently to the image or model ridge and adds a thinning loss, which was not tested. Soft clDice and Skeleton Recall are different mechanisms.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply the normal-NMS loss to crack only, normal from the orientation target; replace level sets with a +-2 px 1D search along the normal for the best-scoring label position.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + normal-NMS loss + 1D alignment vs PF; metric relF1@2, width ratio, strict IoU; kill if relF1@2 +<0.01 or width ratio <0.8.

alt_notes.adaptation: Take the normal direction from the orientation of the label skeleton and apply the NMS loss to crack logits. Replace the level set with a simple snake: every k steps, move each crack label curve to the model's ridge within 2 px. This is the canonical align-while-training baseline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + NMS loss + periodic label alignment, 5 seeds. Baseline: house at 100% labels. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, component recall. Kill if all are n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Normals from label skeleton orientation; NMS loss on crack logits; every k steps move each crack label curve to the model ridge within 2 px using a simple snake instead of the level set.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + NMS loss + periodic label alignment, 5 seeds; baseline house. Metrics crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if both n.d. About 12 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply the NMS loss across the crack normal (orientation from label polyline) so the model gives one peak per crack; replace level sets with a 1D search of +-2 px along the normal for the best-scoring label position.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm = PF + normal-NMS loss + 1D alignment on crack; baseline = PF; 5 seeds + CV; metrics relF1@2, crack IoU, predicted width. Kill if relF1@2 gain < 0.01 and IoU drops.

alt_notes.adaptation: Every 2k steps move each crack label pixel to the argmax of p(crack) within 2 px along the local normal, preserving connectivity, and keep the updated label. SEAL bipartite matching (ECCV 2018) is a simpler implementation.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + active alignment on crack labels. Baseline: house. Metric: relF1@2 primary, strict IoU secondary. Kill if relF1@2 gain < +0.01 or strict IoU drop > 0.02. About 6 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Model-in-the-loop snapping: every 2k steps move each crack polyline along its normal within 2 px to the argmax of p(crack) blended with ridge strength, re-dilate to source width. Compare with fixed filter snapping.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Only if the ridge-snap arm passes. Arm: model-in-the-loop snap; baseline: ridge-snap arm. Kill if n.d. vs ridge-snap.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use the normal-direction max-response loss as an auxiliary crack loss: along each label skeleton normal (5 px profile) the predicted crack probability should peak once. Skip level-set alignment (covered by the snake arm).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + normal-max auxiliary loss on crack, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and pixel precision. Kill: crack IoU under +0.012 with no precision gain.

alt_notes.adaptation: Align jittered 1-2 px crack labels toward the dark ridge during training (half of label points are > 1 px off the ridge), keep each source's width; NMS loss to control predicted width. Test labels stay jittered, so judge on relF1@2 and width, not only strict IoU.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house training with label alignment step every k iterations. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack relF1@2, crack IoU, predicted width per source on 5-fold CV. Kill: relF1@2 < +0.005 and IoU drop > 0.01.

title: Explicit Inductive Bias for Transfer Learning with Convolutional Networks (L2-SP)
mechanism: Replace weight decay toward zero with an L2 penalty toward the pretrained weights, keeping the fine-tuned model near the source solution.
adaptation: Encoder only, alpha grid {1e-3,1e-2,1e-1}; decoder keeps wd 1e-4. Simplest feature-preserving arm; the baseline that SPD improves on.
evidence: Recommends L2-SP as the baseline penalty for transfer. In SPD's PASCAL seg table: L2-SP 73.47 ID / 56.70 OOD mIoU vs vanilla FT 66.03 / 44.00.
min_experiment: Arm L2-SP vs SUP100-PF and vs house, seeds 5-9. Co-primaries as for SPD. Kill if no gain over PF on E1 inactive IoU or test relF1@2 and no gain over house on test.
prior_overlap: Partial: PF removes encoder weight decay and lowers lr but has no pull toward init. L2-SP itself never run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Encoder L2-SP alpha in {1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1} with the house lr; decoder plain wd 1e-4; conv1 reference = the summed 1-channel ImageNet kernel. Separates PF's freeze, low lr and no-wd components.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + encoder L2-SP (best alpha on val, 5 seeds). Baseline: SUP100-PF and house. Metric: E1 inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2, test crack relF1@2. Kill: not better than PF on any co-primary.

title: Knowledge Distillation for Semantic Segmentation: A Label Space Unification Approach
mechanism: A teacher in the target taxonomy pseudo-labels other datasets, with each dataset's own GT (mapped) constraining which classes are allowed per pixel; students trained on the union beat the teacher.
evidence: 12 urban and 7 off-road datasets; students outperform teachers (exact numbers not read).
adaptation: Teacher = house 5-seed ensemble. Pseudo-label UCF, MSS, PV-Vision cells in 24 classes: inside UCF crack polygon only crack/inactive allowed; inside MSS/PV-Vision crack mask crack forced; outside any defect GT crack and inactive forbidden.
min_experiment: Arm: student on BenchmarkEL + constrained pseudo-labels, 30k steps, 5 seeds. Baseline: house 5-seed (and ensemble teacher). Kill if crack IoU < +0.012 AND E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 AND inactive not up. ~15 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: BRIEF 5 pseudo-label SSL used unconstrained pseudo-labels on unlabelled pool cells (n.d. at 100%); GT-constrained labels on external labelled sets are a different mechanism

title: Adjusting the Ground Truth Annotations for Connectivity-Based Learning to Delineate
mechanism: The annotated centerline is a snake (graph of vertices) that deforms during training toward the network's predicted distance map, regularized by elasticity and spring terms so it stays smooth and keeps its topology; the net trains on the distance map of the adjusted snake.
adaptation: 2D version: skeletonize crack labels to polylines, add a truncated-distance regression head to U-Net++, update snakes every N steps (SnakeFast) with displacement capped at 2 px, train the crack class on the adjusted snake redrawn at the source width.
min_experiment: Arm: house + distance head with snake-adjusted crack targets, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, components >= 20 px found. Kill: crack IoU below baseline by more than 0.012 and relF1@2 not up by 0.01.
evidence: R: on Brain, Neurons, MRA (10, 1, 31 training volumes) SnakeFast beats training on original annotations in APLS and TLTS, pixel quality about equal; degrades much more slowly as synthetic annotation deformation grows; beats NR-Dice, QAM, DS6 on topology metrics.
prior_overlap: none. Snakes listed as never tried; offset-tolerant CE did not move the labels.

alt_notes.adaptation: Skeletonise each crack label into a polyline graph, snake it toward the model's crack ridge (or the image's dark ridge) within 2 px every N steps, then redraw at each source's convention width (ARTS 1.5, CSIR/CFVS 1.75, BMRK 3.0, SDLE 3.25 px). Test labels stay unchanged, so gains may show in relF1@2 before strict IoU.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF trained on snake-adjusted crack labels vs PF, 5 seeds. Kill if relF1@2 gain < 0.01 and crack IoU change < +0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Skeletonise crack labels to polylines, run a snake toward the dark EL ridge or the model's ridge every N steps (max 2 px displacement), redraw at each source's convention width (ARTS 1.5, CFVS/CSIR 1.75, BMRK 3.0). Test labels stay unchanged, so relF1 may rise more than strict IoU. Doubles as a label-refinement tool for the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF trained on snake-adjusted crack labels, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF on revised labels. Metrics: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, width. Kill if crack IoU < baseline - 0.012 and relF1@2 gain < 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack mask -> skeleton -> polylines; each epoch move polylines up to 2 px toward the network's ridge (snake energy = network output + smoothness), rasterise at source width as the new target. Code is 3D; port to 2D.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF with snake-adjusted crack labels from epoch 25% onward vs PF; metric relF1@2 and strict IoU against original CV labels; kill if relF1@2 +<0.01 and strict IoU down >0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Convert crack masks to polylines, allow each to move within 2 px toward the network's predicted ridge each epoch, rasterise at source width. Model-driven version of ridge snapping.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm = PF with per-epoch polyline snapping (limit 2 px, start after 5k steps); baseline = PF; 5 seeds + 5-fold CV; metrics crack IoU on original labels, relF1@2, E1. Kill as for ridge snapping: IoU drop > 0.01 with no relF1@2 gain.

title: When Semantic Segmentation Meets Frequency Aliasing
mechanism: De-aliasing filter zeroes feature-map frequencies above the equivalent Nyquist frequency before each downsampling (parameter free); FreqMix learns channel x spatial weights for below/above-Nyquist bands inside encoder blocks.
adaptation: Put DAF before the ResNet-34 max-pool and the stride-2 convs of layer2/3/4 (not before conv1, so stride-2 skips keep crack detail); FreqMix in layer1/2. EL fingers (pitch likely 4 to 6 px at 512, unverified) alias into moire from stride 4 onward; moire depends on source rescaling, a plausible cause of BMRK and E1 weakness. Keeps ImageNet weights.
min_experiment: Arm: house + DAF + FreqMix; baseline house and PF; 5 seeds, CV then test/E1; metrics crack IoU, relF1@2, per-source crack IoU, E1 relF1@2; kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.02. Precede with a 1 h CPU diagnostic of finger pitch and encoder aliasing score.
evidence: R: UPerNet-R50 Cityscapes 78.1 to 79.7 mIoU, boundary IoU 61.8 to 63.2; PASCAL VOC 74.3 to 76.1; ADE20K 38.9 to 40.4. Large datasets, not thin structures.
prior_overlap: none; section 5 never varied downsampling or anti-aliasing. 2x resolution n.d. is a different mechanism (compute, not aliasing).

title: Rethinking Data Augmentation for Single-Source Domain Generalization in Medical Image Segmentation (SLAug)
mechanism: Global plus class-wise random Bezier intensity curves (location-scale per class region), fused via a gradient saliency map so augmentation targets regions the model relies on.
adaptation: Apply class-wise curves only to structural classes (busbar, ribbon, gridline, border, background, padding, frame); never to crack or inactive, because a class-wise transform on 1 px jittered labels paints a line at the label rather than the dark ridge and creates a shortcut. Forces crack detection under any busbar/background contrast, which CSIR half-cuts change.
min_experiment: PF + SLAug (crack/inactive excluded) vs PF, 3 seeds. E1 crack relF1@2 primary, test crack IoU and mIoU_rob guard. Kill if E1 gain < +0.03 or test crack IoU drops > 0.01.
evidence: R: exceeds prior SDG methods by a large margin on two medical SDG tasks (abstract; numbers not read). Code public.
prior_overlap: none: no class-wise or non-linear intensity augmentation was run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Class-wise curves only on structural classes (busbar, ribbons, border, frame_edge, gridline, sp_mono/sp_multi, background); keep crack and inactive darker than their neighbours. Mimics source contrast conventions and new module types.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+SLAug vs PF+GIN-IPA and PF, 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU. Kill: < +0.02 E1 relF1@2 over GIN-IPA.

title: Domain Adaptive and Generalizable Network Architectures and Training Strategies for Semantic Image Segmentation (DAFormer / HRDA)
mechanism: Training strategies against source overfitting in segmentation: Rare Class Sampling, Thing-Class ImageNet Feature Distance (L2 between bottleneck features and a frozen ImageNet copy on selected classes), lr warmup; plus multi-resolution crops.
adaptation: FD: frozen ImageNet ResNet-34 copy, L2 on layer4 features masked to crack and inactive pixels. RCS: sample cells by rarest class present (temperature 0.01-0.1) so the 42 inactive cells and BMRK crack cells appear more. Multi-res crops left to D22.
evidence: DAFormer and HRDA improve UDA and DG segmentation SOTA by more than 10 mIoU on 5 benchmarks (abstract); per-strategy ablation numbers not retrieved.
min_experiment: Arms FD and FD+RCS vs SUP100-PF, seeds 5-9. Metric: test inactive IoU, E1 inactive IoU, test crack relF1@2. Kill if inactive IoU gain < +0.02 on test and E1 not better.
prior_overlap: none. Feature-space preservation and class-frequency sampling never run (long-tail methods listed as never tried).

alt_notes.adaptation: FD: frozen ImageNet ResNet-34, L2 on layer4 features masked to crack + inactive pixels. RCS: sample whole cells by class frequency (temperature 0.01 to 0.1) over 42 inactive and 209 crack cells; whole-cell input keeps all area reachable.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + FD, PF + RCS, PF + both, 5 seeds. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metric: inactive IoU (test, E1), BMRK inactive IoU, crack relF1@2. Kill: inactive IoU gain < 0.02 on test and E1.

title: Modeling annotator preference and stochastic annotation error for medical image segmentation (PADL)
mechanism: A shared network with one head per annotator models each annotator's systematic preference and stochastic error (Gaussian) separately from a consensus segmentation.
adaptation: The 5 sources play the role of 5 annotators: a shared U-Net++ decoder, one 1x1 head per source, plus a consensus head. At test, use the cell's source head (source is known for every cell), which reproduces that source's crack width and placement, the only route BRIEF names to strict IoU above 0.5. The consensus head serves E1 and the benchmark.
min_experiment: Arm: source heads + consensus head, 5 seeds. Baseline: house, 5 seeds. Metrics: crack IoU overall and per source (BMRK, CFVS without twin), relF1@2. Kill if the source-head crack IoU gain is below 0.012.
evidence: R: multi-annotator medical segmentation; it models preference and error separately. Abstract not retrieved by the tool; numbers not read.
prior_overlap: none. Source-conditional prediction and annotator / source-style modelling are on BRIEF's never-tried list.

alt_notes.adaptation: An ablation of the TAB arm that splits source width preference from trace jitter. Run only if the TAB or FiLM arm shows a gain.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm = house PF + preference/error heads versus the TAB arm. Metric: crack IoU clean-49. Kill if it does not beat TAB.

title: Disconnect to Connect: A Data Augmentation Method for Improving Topology Accuracy in Image Segmentation (CoLeTra)
mechanism: Augmentation that paints background-like patches over parts of thin structures and keeps the original label, so the model learns that structures that look broken are connected.
adaptation: Paste local background texture (same cell, same source) over 3 to 10 px stretches of crack and gridline labels, label unchanged. Aims at faint cracks (7% under 2% contrast) and E1 misses. No width bias because labels are untouched. Do not cover inactive regions or busbars.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + CoLeTra on crack and gridline, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, test crack component recall (>= 20 px), relP@2. Kill if E1 relF1@2 and component recall both gain < 0.02, or relP@2 falls > 0.02.
evidence: R (abstract): across architectures, losses and datasets, more accurate topology, often better Dice and HD, robust to its hyperparameters, works with topologically inaccurate labels.
prior_overlap: Crack copy-paste onto pool cells (n.d.) added cracks. CoLeTra removes image evidence under a kept label, a different mechanism. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Paste same-cell, same-source local background over 3 to 10 px stretches of crack and gridline only, never over inactive. Targets faint cracks (7% under 2% contrast) and E1 misses where 70% of crack pixels get p < 0.001. Labels untouched, so no width bias. Otherwise keep label-safe augmentation.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + CoLeTra (crack + gridline) vs PF, 5 seeds. Kill if E1 crack relF1@2 and test component recall (>= 20 px) both gain < +0.02, or relP@2 falls > 0.02.

title: Knowledge distillation: A good teacher is patient and consistent
mechanism: Function matching: teacher and student see the identical augmented view, with aggressive mixup and very long schedules.
adaptation: Online ensemble teacher on the same rot90/flip/crop/brightness view as the student, CutMix or mixup across labelled and pool cells (label-free since the teacher labels the mix), 100k steps on A6000s.
min_experiment: Arm: online function-matching KD, 100k steps, 3 seeds. Baseline: cached fixed-view KD student (Noothout arm). Metric: crack IoU / relF1@2 on CV and clean 49. Kill: below baseline or < +0.01 crack IoU.
evidence: R: ImageNet ResNet-50 student 82.8% top-1; implicit design choices (consistent views, long training) drive KD success across many vision datasets.
prior_overlap: none; CutMix only used inside Mean Teacher SSL

alt_notes.adaptation: Distil the 5-seed ensemble, our only clear win (+0.014 to +0.018 crack IoU), into one U-Net++ R34. Per-pixel KL on the same augmented view of labelled + pool cells, mixup/CutMix between cells, about 100k steps. Gives single-model deployment.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm KD-ens vs house PF single model and the 5-seed ensemble. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and relF1@2. Kill if less than 50% of the single-to-ensemble gap is closed.

title: Improved Road Connectivity by Joint Learning of Orientation and Segmentation
mechanism: Add an auxiliary task predicting binned road orientation along the label skeleton, sharing features with segmentation, plus a refinement step that closes small gaps.
adaptation: Orientation bins (16) computed from the crack label skeleton via PCA in a 7 px window; a 1 px jitter barely changes orientation, so the target is jitter-robust. Also apply to gridline/busbar/ribbon (layout-fixed directions) to help gridline recall 0.33.
min_experiment: Arm = PF + 16-bin orientation CE on crack and gridline skeleton pixels; baseline = PF; 5 seeds + 5-fold CV; metrics crack components >=20 px found, relF1@2, gridline IoU. Kill if components gain < 0.02 and gridline IoU gain < 0.02.
evidence: R: SpaceNet and DeepGlobe roads, better connectivity (APLS) with the orientation task; exact numbers not read.
prior_overlap: None; no orientation or direction target has been trained here.

alt_notes.adaptation: 16 orientation bins from crack skeleton second moments in a 7x7 window (95.8% of px stay within +-1 bin under 1 px label shift, team E); also apply to gridline and busbar whose orientation is fixed by cell layout (gridline IoU 0.283). Refinement net optional, trained on our own corrupted crack masks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Within T5 arm 4 (stacked); if it passes, decomposition arm PF + orientation only vs PF; metric components >=20 px found, gridline IoU; kill if components +<0.02 and gridline IoU +<0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: (a) Orientation head: 16 angle bins from the crack skeleton tangent, dilated 2 px, CE on crack pixels only. Orientation stays stable under 1-2 px label jitter. (b) Train a mask-to-mask refiner on the 478 train crack masks with random breaks, gaps and shifts. This needs no new labels and adds the refinement stage that has never been tried here.
alt_notes.min_experiment: (a) Orientation aux vs house, 5 seeds. (b) Refiner on the house ensemble output vs the ensemble alone. Metrics: crack relR@2 at fixed relP@2, components found, E1 recall. Kill if relR@2 gains < 0.01.

title: Weakly-Supervised Crack Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
mechanism: Refine coarse crack annotations by removing annotated pixels whose local visual features resemble the background (data-driven), replacing an earlier brightness-threshold refinement.
adaptation: Deliberately coarsen our crack labels to a 5 px band (covers 4 px FWHM plus 1 to 2 px jitter), then apply the data-driven refinement per cell so it adapts to each source's contrast; thin and re-dilate to source width. A second snapper to compare with the ridge snapper, expected to do better on low-contrast CSIR cracks.
min_experiment: Arm: house trained on coarsen-then-refine labels; baseline: house and the ridge-snap arm. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2, CSIR crack relR@2. Kill if CSIR relR@2 not above the ridge-snap arm by 0.02 and pooled metrics n.d. vs house.
evidence: R: three crack segmentation datasets and one vessel dataset; annotation 10 to 30x faster at comparable detection accuracy (abstract).
prior_overlap: none: no label refinement was run (BRIEF section 5, Labels row).

title: Haar Wavelet Downsampling: A Simple but Effective Downsampling Module for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Haar DWT plus 1x1 conv as the downsampling operator, so stride-2 steps keep high-frequency detail in subband channels instead of aliasing it away.
adaptation: Swap the ResNet-34 stem max-pool for HWD (all ImageNet weights kept), and optionally the layer2 entry stride. A 1 to 2 px crack is partly lost at the first max-pool on a 512 px cell.
min_experiment: Arm: house and PF with an HWD stem, 5 seeds. Baseline: house / PF. Metric: crack components >= 20 px found, crack recall at relP@2 >= 0.90. Kill: components found < +0.02 and crack IoU not up.
evidence: R: segmentation gains across modalities and backbones and a lower feature-entropy index, as stated in the abstract and README. I saw no thin-structure numbers.
prior_overlap: none. D09 proposes a similar wavelet stem through NWG-DETR.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace the ResNet-34 stem max-pool (optionally the stride-2 entry of layer2); a 1 to 2 px crack is half lost at the first max-pool. Combine with Seg-Aliasing if both pass.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with HWD stem; baselines house and PF; 5 seeds; crack components found, recall at relP@2 >= 0.90, crack IoU; kill if components found < +0.02 and crack IoU not up. About 6 GPU-h.

title: RankED: Addressing Imbalance and Uncertainty in Edge Detection Using Ranking-based Losses
mechanism: Ranking loss that ranks positive over negative pixels (AP-style, handles extreme imbalance) plus a second ranking term that orders positive pixels by label certainty.
adaptation: Crack is 0.19% of pixels: replace soft Dice on crack with the ranking term. Certainty from agreement between the 2021 and 2022 crack label versions, or from distance to the label skeleton.
min_experiment: Arm = PF with RankED crack loss in place of crack Dice; baseline = PF; 5 seeds + 5-fold CV; metrics crack AP, relP/relR@2, IoU. Kill if CV crack AP not up and IoU drops > 0.01.
evidence: R: new SOTA on NYUD-v2, BSDS500 and Multicue edge detection.
prior_overlap: None; ranking/AP losses never tried (BRIEF loss row lists Lovasz and others as open).

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack is 0.19% of pixels, so the ranking term fits. Build the certainty map from the two label versions we already have, the BenchmarkEL 2021 original and 2022 revised crack masks, with d = 2 px. Cells with only one version get c = 1. Add L_Rank + L_Sort on the crack logit alongside CE + Dice.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + RankED losses on crack, 5 seeds, with a sub-arm using UAED-style weighting. Baseline: house at 100% labels. Metrics: crack AP, relF1@2, crack IoU. Kill if AP and relF1@2 are both n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply L_Rank + L_Sort on the crack logit next to CE + Dice. Certainty from the two label versions on the same cells (BenchmarkEL 2021 original vs 2022 revised) with 2 px tolerance; single-version cells get certainty 1. AP is threshold-free, replacing the val-tuned crack logit bias.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + L_Rank (+ L_Sort; UAED weighting as sub-arm), 5 seeds; baseline house 5 seeds. Metrics crack AP, relF1@2 at val-chosen threshold, strict IoU at argmax. Kill if crack AP and relF1@2 both n.d. About 15 GPU-h.

title: Spatially Varying Label Smoothing: Capturing Uncertainty from Expert Annotations
mechanism: Convolve one-hot labels with a Gaussian so boundary pixels get soft targets and interiors stay hard, encoding annotation position uncertainty.
adaptation: For a 1.75 px crack every pixel is boundary, so SVLS becomes a soft crack band covering the 1-2 px jitter. Sigma per source from label width (ARTS 1.5 px to SDLE 3.25 px) as a second arm. Train with JML or DML instead of house soft Dice; re-pick the crack logit bias on val because soft targets shift the argmax width.
min_experiment: Arm SVLS (sigma 0.7 px) + JML vs SUP100, 5 v 5 seeds. Metric clean-49 crack IoU at val-chosen bias, relF1@2, relP@2. Kill if crack IoU < +0.012 or relP@2 drop > 0.05.
evidence: R: better boundary prediction and calibration on 4 clinical segmentation tasks, single and multi-rater (abstract).
prior_overlap: Related but not the same: offset-tolerant CE (P14, 10% labels, min over shifts) was n.d.; soft Gaussian targets with an IoU loss at 100% labels never run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply SVLS (sigma 0.7 to 1.0) only to the crack channel in CE, giving a soft 3 to 4 px band matching the 4 px FWHM line; keep Dice on the hard crack label; structural classes unchanged.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + SVLS on crack CE. Baseline: house. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if both < house + 0.005. About 6 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Soft crack band with sigma 0.7 px, second arm with per-source sigma from measured label width; must pair with JML/DML instead of house soft Dice; crack bias re-picked on val.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: SVLS crack targets + CE + JML, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Metric crack IoU (val bias), relP@2. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012 or relP@2 drop > 0.05.

title: Your ViT is Secretly an Image Segmentation Model (EoMT)
mechanism: Plain ViT with learnable queries injected for the last blocks predicts class + mask directly; mask annealing removes masked attention at inference, so no adapter or pixel decoder.
evidence: R: COCO PQ gap to ViT-Adapter+M2F shrinks with scale and pretraining (-5.8 ViT-S, -3.8 B, -1.1 L, -0.7 g; -6.1 with IN1K pretraining); ADE20K 58.4 mIoU at 512 with ViT-L DINOv2; small-object AP drops most (23.4 to 20.3); up to 4x faster. DINOv3 EoMT-L 59.5 ADE20K per README.
adaptation: ViT-L/16 DINOv2-reg (DINOv3 if user OKs gated weights) from ADE20K semantic ckpt with class head reset; grey replicated to 3 ch; 1024 px input so tokens cover 32 px of original; add a 2-layer full-res conv refinement head on upsampled mask logits + raw image for 1-2 px cracks; dense CE + Dice on crack/inactive on the final semantic map; layer-wise lr decay (PF-like); ~50 queries for 24 classes; also used as a heterogeneous-ensemble member with the house 5-seed ensemble.
min_experiment: Arm EoMT-L 1024 + refinement + dense aux, 20k steps, module-grouped 5-fold CV then 5 seeds on test/E1; baseline house PF; metrics inactive IoU, mIoU_rob, E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, plus ensemble arm (softmax average with house ensemble, weight from val). Kill alone if inactive IoU < 0.449 and mIoU_rob < 0.570 and E1 relF1@2 < 0.43; kill as ensemble member if no metric beats the paired noise floor (crack IoU 0.012).
prior_overlap: Foundation encoders row: frozen ViT-S/ConvNeXt-T probes and one ConvNeXt-T 4k-step screen. ViT-L, mask decoders, 1024 input and long schedules are explicitly listed as not closed. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark baseline for modern ViT mask classification; run at 1024 for 64 x 64 tokens; expect crack weakness, possible gains on inactive, material and other blob classes.
alt_notes.min_experiment: EoMT DINOv2-L @1024, 3 seeds; mIoU_rob and inactive IoU vs house; kill if mIoU_rob < 0.57 and inactive < 0.44.

alt_notes.adaptation: ViT-L DINOv2-reg (DINOv3 if user OKs gated weights) from ADE20K semantic checkpoint without class head; grey replicated to 3 ch; 1024 px input; full-res path (LoftUp-style upsampler or conv head on upsampled mask logits + raw EL image); dense CE + Dice on crack/inactive on final semantic map; layer-wise lr decay 0.8 as PF analogue; 24 classes, 2 queries per class.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm EoMT-L DINOv2 1024 px + full-res head + dense aux, 20k steps vs house PF on module-grouped 5-fold CV then 5 seeds; metrics inactive IoU, mIoU_rob, E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU; kill if inactive IoU < 0.449 and mIoU_rob < 0.570 and E1 relF1@2 < 0.43; also test as ensemble member with house 5-seed ensemble, kill if no metric beats noise floor (crack IoU 0.012).

title: DAFormer: Improving Network Architectures and Training Strategies for Domain-Adaptive Semantic Segmentation (RCS + ImageNet feature distance)
mechanism: Rare-class sampling of source images plus an L2 distance that keeps bottleneck features close to the frozen ImageNet encoder (thing-class pixels), with lr warmup; protects pretrained features during adaptation.
evidence: GTA to Cityscapes: self-training 58.2, +FD 61.7, +RCS 64.0, both 66.2 mIoU; with no target data (pure DG) RCS+FD add +5.1 mIoU (supp. Table S3); also helps DeepLabV2.
adaptation: FD as a soft alternative to PF: L2 between layer4 features of the training ResNet-34 and a frozen ImageNet ResNet-34 (weight 0.005 to 0.05, all pixels or crack/inactive/defect pixels). This targets the found erasure of layer3/4 that PF fixes (E1 inactive 0.05 to 0.24). RCS: sample training cells by rarity of inactive, splice, gridline and material.
min_experiment: Arms house+FD, house+FD+RCS, PF+RCS vs house and PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2, test inactive IoU, splice/gridline IoU. Kill: house+FD not within 0.03 of PF on E1 inactive and no other gain; RCS killed if inactive and splice gain < +0.03.
prior_overlap: Partial: PF already tests encoder preservation by freezing and low lr; the FD loss and rare-class sampling were never run. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: The feature distance directly counters our finding that the house fine-tune erases ResNet layer3/layer4. Add an L2 loss to frozen ImageNet R34 layer4 on crack, inactive and splice pixels (weight 0.005 to 0.05), as an alternative or complement to PF. RCS: sample training cells by rarity of crack, inactive, splice and gridline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm FD-RCS vs house PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 inactive IoU, clean-49 crack IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill if no metric beats PF beyond the seed noise.

alt_notes.adaptation: Rare class sampling over cells with crack, inactive (42 cells), splice, gridline. Feature-distance regulariser as a soft form of PF encoder preservation. MiT-B5 at 512 px with 1-ch replicated to 3 as a benchmark entry.
alt_notes.min_experiment: (a) house + RCS vs house; kill if test and E1 inactive IoU gains < +0.02. (b) house + FD vs PF; kill if not better than PF on E1. 3 seeds each.

title: Stronger, Fewer, & Superior: Harnessing Vision Foundation Models for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation (Rein)
mechanism: Learnable tokens refine every layer's features of a frozen VFM (<1% params); beat full fine-tuning on unseen domains.
evidence: R: DGSS benchmarks (GTA to Cityscapes etc.) above full fine-tune; 182 citations, standard DGSS baseline.
adaptation: Port only the token module into our trainer; use in VFM-H side branch with DINOv2-L / DINOv3-L / C-RADIOv4; 24-class head unchanged; train on all 5 sources.
min_experiment: Rein vs Rein-LoRA vs frozen-only vs LoRA in VFM-H, house PF baseline; CV crack relF1@2 + E1 relF1@2 / inactive IoU; keep only the best PEFT on E1, drop all if none passes the default kill line.
prior_overlap: Section 5 lists adapters / LoRA / Rein as not tested. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: DINOv2/v3 ViT-L at 1024 with Rein, our U-Net or Mask2Former head, 24 classes; train on 478 cells, primary read-out E1 (half-cut, scuff, new modules) and leave-one-source-out folds.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Rein vs full FT vs LN-only vs LoRA on the best encoder, 3 seeds; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU; kill if no arm beats house PF on E1 relF1@2 by +0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Same VFM-H harness: frozen DINOv2-L/14 or DINOv3-L/16 at 1024 px (64x64 tokens), Rein tokens, CNN detail branch for the 1-2 px crack scale, 24 classes; repo configs cover DINOv2, ConvNeXt, CLIP, SAM so the backbone is a switch. Overlaps D14 item 11.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: VFM-H + Rein vs VFM-H full fine-tune at 0.1x lr. Baseline: house PF. Metric: CV crack relF1@2, CV inactive IoU, then E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU once. Kill: default line (CV relF1@2 down > 0.005 and E1 relF1@2 not +0.03 and E1 inactive not > 0.24).

alt_notes.adaptation: DINOv2-L or DINOv3-L/16 at 1024 + Rein + Mask2Former/UPerNet head, 24 classes; train on the 5 sources, judge mainly on E1 (unseen modules, half-cut).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Rein-DINOv2-L vs house PF: E1 crack relF1@2 (+0.03 to pass), E1 inactive IoU (> 0.24), clean-49 crack IoU not below 0.46; 3 seeds.

alt_notes.adaptation: ViT patch 14 at 512 px gives 37x37 tokens, too coarse for 1-2 px cracks: run at about 1024 px or fuse with the U-Net++ detail decoder. Rein-A target = pool half-cells. 1-ch replicated to 3.
alt_notes.min_experiment: DINOv2-L (or DINOv3-L) + Rein + Mask2Former at ~1024 px vs PF U-Net++, 3 seeds. Kill if test crack IoU < 0.45 or E1 relF1@2 not above PF.

title: DINOv3 Beats Specialized Detectors: A Simple Foundation Model Baseline for Image Forensics
mechanism: Frozen DINOv3 ViT backbone with LoRA plus a lightweight convolutional decoder for pixel-level localisation of small manipulated regions. LoRA beats full fine-tuning, which is unstable on scarce data.
adaptation: Repeat 1-channel EL to 3 channels; 512 or 1024 px input; add a stride-2 CNN stem skip into the conv decoder so 1-2 px cracks survive the patch-16 grid; 24-class CE plus Dice on crack and inactive as in the house recipe. DINOv3 is gated (user OK needed); fallback DINOv2-L or C-RADIOv4.
min_experiment: Arm: frozen DINOv3 ViT-L/16 + LoRA r16 + conv decoder + stem skip, 1024 px, 20k steps, 5 seeds. Baseline: house PF 5-seed. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, test crack relF1@2 and IoU. Kill: after 2 seeds, E1 relF1@2 below PF + 0.02 and test relF1@2 below PF.
evidence: R: +17.0 average pixel F1 over previous SOTA on 4 benchmarks (CAT-Net protocol) with 9.1M trainable params on frozen ViT-L; data-scarce MVSS protocol F1 0.774 vs 0.530; LoRA > full FT at all backbone scales. E: our house fine-tune erases the encoder and PF keeps it, the same pattern.
prior_overlap: Partial. BRIEF section 5 ran frozen linear probes of small VFMs and one DINOv3 ConvNeXt-T PF screen; ViT-L with LoRA and a conv decoder is listed as open. D24 covers VFM PEFT in general but not this paper.

title: Directional Connectivity-based Segmentation of Medical Images
mechanism: Predict 8-neighbour pixel connectivity maps per class, with a decoder that disentangles and tracks directional sub-spaces; the mask is recovered from connectivity votes.
adaptation: Connectivity output only for crack and inactive (2 x 8 channels) on the ResNet-34 encoder, keep the 24-class CE head. Hoped effect: fewer fragmented crack pieces, more components found, cleaner inactive borders.
min_experiment: Arm = PF + DconnNet connectivity heads for crack/inactive; baseline = PF; 5 seeds + 5-fold CV; metrics components >=20 px found, relF1@2, inactive IoU. Kill if components gain < 0.02 and inactive IoU flat.
evidence: R: beats SOTA on several public medical segmentation benchmarks; third-party listings show DRIVE and CRACK500 results (not read).
prior_overlap: None; connectivity outputs never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Add an 8-channel connectivity head for crack and gridline to U-Net++ (BCE), fused at inference. Build connectivity targets from labels dilated by 1 px, because 1-2 px jittered traces give noisy direction targets.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + connectivity head (crack, gridline), 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: gridline IoU, crack component recall, crack IoU. Kill if gridline gain < 0.02 and component recall gain < 0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Connectivity output for crack and inactive only (2 x 8 channels) on the ResNet-34 U-Net++ encoder, 24-class CE head kept. Binary connectivity flips under 1 px jitter, so pair with a 1 px tube target or use TMAL instead.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + DconnNet crack/inactive heads vs PF; metric components >=20 px found and inactive IoU; kill if components +<0.02 and inactive IoU flat (within 0.01).

alt_notes.adaptation: Use a multi-class connectivity head on crack, inactive and gridline on top of the U-Net++ decoder. Inactive touches crack in 99% of regions, so crack-inactive connectivity is a natural constraint.
alt_notes.min_experiment: DconnNet head vs house, 5 seeds. Metrics: inactive IoU on 5-fold CV (test inactive rests on 3 cells) and crack relF1@2. Kill if inactive CV IoU gains < 0.02 and crack is flat.

alt_notes.adaptation: Extra connectivity head only for crack, inactive and gridline (24x8 channels is wasteful); connectivity targets built from labels dilated by 1 px to absorb jitter; keep the CE+Dice mask head.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + 3-class connectivity head, 5 seeds; baseline house. Metrics: components >=20 px found, crack relF1@2, inactive IoU. Kill: components found and relF1@2 gains both < 0.01.

title: TMAL: Topology-preserving Multi-offset Affinity Learning for Curvilinear Structure Segmentation
mechanism: Predict soft directional affinities at several pixel offsets, fuse them with decoder-derived spatial weights, decode to an inverted distance map and threshold; auxiliary mask branch keeps overlap accuracy.
adaptation: Published target (inverted EDT) is degenerate on 1-2 px cracks (every crack px has EDT 1). Replace with a Gaussian tube around the label skeleton (sigma about 1 px, the measured jitter) and build affinities as products of tube values at offsets s in {1,2}, so links bridge a 1 px gap. Crack channels only on the house encoder; 24-class CE head kept; crack read-out = TMAL map as crack logit or threshold chosen on val. Code link from abstract (github.com/suho-han/TMAL) not found by web search.
min_experiment: Arm PF + TMAL crack branch vs PF, cv5v2 2 seeds x 5 folds then 5 seeds test; control with s={1} only (DconnNet-like); metric components >=20 px found and relF1@2, width ratio and strict IoU guards; kill if components +<0.02 and relF1@2 +<0.01, or strict IoU down >0.01.
evidence: Full text read. Own 512 px protocol, baselines retrained: DeepCrack (300 train) IoU 0.743 vs DconnNet 0.713 vs U-Net 0.681, clDice 0.907 vs 0.893 vs 0.859, component error 1.98 vs 4.51 vs 4.93. DRIVE (20 train) IoU 0.709 vs 0.635, component error 24.5 vs 452.8. HD95 not best.
prior_overlap: none; connectivity outputs never run (DconnNet parked in T2 for cost)

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack-only affinity head on U-Net++ (offsets 1, 2, 4 px, 8 directions) fused with the seg branch; weight larger offsets more because 1 px offsets are dominated by label jitter.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + multi-offset affinity head; baseline PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV components >= 20 px found, relF1@2, strict crack IoU. Kill if components found gain < +0.02 and IoU n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Affinity head for crack and gridline on U-Net++, offsets 1, 2 and 4 px so a 1 px jitter does not break the target; segmentation branch kept as is. Held by D09 / D12.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + TMAL head vs PF, 5 seeds. Kill if crack relF1@2 gain < 0.01 and component recall gain < 0.02.
