alt_notes.adaptation: Crack-only affinity head on U-Net++ with offsets 1, 2, 4 px and 8 directions; weight larger offsets more because 1 px affinities inherit label jitter; fuse with the seg branch for the crack map.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + affinity head; baseline: PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack components >= 20 px found, relF1@2, strict IoU. Kill if components-found gain < +0.02 and IoU n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack-only affinity head at offsets 1, 2, 4 px; larger offsets link pixels along the crack and should tolerate 1-2 px label jitter better than 1-px connectivity.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + multi-offset affinity head, 5 seeds; baseline house. Metrics: components found, crack relF1@2, E1 relF1@2. Kill: gains < 0.01 in-distribution and < 0.02 on E1.

title: Beyond prompt-only segmentation: Foundation model-guided trust-region label refinement for single-stage bone fracture instance segmentation
mechanism: Foundation-model masks are used only inside a narrow trust region around expert labels, gated by instance IoU, with minimal closing; the original annotation anchors everything.
adaptation: For crack labels: inside a 2 px band, move each label line onto the FM (or SERD / dark-ridge) crack response, reject cells with large shifts, keep source width conventions (ARTS 1.5 px, BMRK 3 px).
min_experiment: Refine train crack labels only; retrain house 5 seeds; score on original test labels. Kill if test crack IoU and relF1@2 both fall > 0.005; pass if crack IoU +0.01.
evidence: R: 5-fold CV, constrained refinement modest gain in sample-matched ablations; unconstrained MedSAM pseudo-labels degraded; mAP@0.5 0.63. E: 2022 relabelling gave +0.05 to +0.08 crack IoU.
prior_overlap: Section 5 Labels row: automatic label refinement never run; offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) is a loss, not label editing.

alt_notes.adaptation: Proposal = 5-seed ensemble or SAM2 prompted from label skeleton points; accept refinements only within 2 px of each crack label, per-component gate IoU >= 0.3. Skeleton metric becomes a candidate benchmark metric next to relF1@2.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house on trust-region refined crack labels. Baseline: house. Metric: relF1@2, strict IoU, skeleton coverage. Kill if relF1@2 gain < +0.01. About 6 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Proposal = 5-seed house ensemble or a SAM2 / DINOv3 refiner; accept a refined crack component only inside the 2 px band of the label and if IoU with the dilated label passes a gate; otherwise keep the original component.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house trained on trust-region-refined crack labels, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill: crack IoU change under +0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Convert UCF region-crack polygons and wide external crack masks to thin lines only within 2 px of the given label, gated by agreement with the EL dark ridge; never train on raw SAM crack masks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: joint run where external crack labels are trust-region-thinned vs used raw; 5 seeds each, 30k steps. Baseline: joint run with raw labels and house 5-seed. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and relP@2. Kill if thinning gives < +0.012 crack IoU over raw. ~15 GPU-h.

title: Learning to Segment from Noisy Annotations: A Spatial Correction Approach
mechanism: A Markov model treats label noise as spatially correlated and biased, so boundaries grow or shrink as a chain, and boundary pixels are corrected progressively with theoretical guarantees.
adaptation: Fit the noise bias per source: dilation for BMRK and SDLE (3 px), jitter for ARTS, CFVS and CSIR. Correct only the crack and inactive boundary band. The same Markov noise model can also generate controlled label-noise copies for a benchmark stress track.
min_experiment: Arm: house + spatial correction on crack and inactive bands, 5 seeds. Baseline: house, 5 seeds. Metrics: crack IoU, inactive IoU, per-source crack IoU (BMRK). Kill if neither crack IoU nor inactive IoU shows a detectable difference.
evidence: R (abstract): beats state-of-the-art methods on synthetic and real noisy annotations. Per the repo README, it was evaluated on JSRT among others. Blobby organs, not thin structures.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Fit the noise model on our real pairs: 265 cells with both 2021 and 2022 crack labels, plus ridge-snapped labels as a third version. Correct crack labels once after the early-learning point of a house run (val crack AP plateau, about 4k to 6k steps), retrain from scratch. Extend to gridline (recall 0.33) and material.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house -> correct at early-learning point -> retrain, 5 seeds; baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, gridline IoU. Kill if crack IoU and relF1@2 both n.d. (< 0.012) and gridline gain < 0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: No clean set exists: estimate the offset per source relative to ridge-snapped val labels or a reference source. Use it to correct train labels per source and as a per-source inference-time width offset to match each source's label convention on test.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: per-source signed-distance offset applied to house model crack logits at inference (no retraining), then a retrain on SC-corrected labels. Baseline: house 5-seed. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and per-source crack IoU. Kill: inference-only arm under +0.008 crack IoU and retrain arm under +0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply only to crack (and possibly gridline) labels. Treat the 1-2 px trace jitter and source width as spatial noise and correct toward the dark ridge; leave the structural classes untouched.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm = house PF trained with spatially corrected crack labels (5 seeds) versus house PF. Metrics: crack IoU clean-49 and relF1@2. Kill if crack IoU gain < +0.012.

title: A generative approach for improving multi-label defect classification in photovoltaic modules (Generative Defect Isolation)
mechanism: Remove selected defects from EL images with LaMa inpainting guided by the annotation masks, producing single-defect and defect-free training samples (subtractive rather than additive augmentation).
adaptation: For labelled crack cells, inpaint chosen crack components (mask dilated to cover the ~4 px dark line + 3 px) and relabel background, keeping other defects; also remove inactive while keeping its crack. Never remove a crack while keeping its inactive. Creates exact-location hard negatives, the counter to CP100's decoys.
min_experiment: Pre-check: 30 inpainted cells inspected, house ensemble p(crack) on inpainted spots < 0.1. Then PF+GDI vs PF, 5 seeds; test crack relP@2 and IoU, false crack px on val, E1 relF1@2. Kill: relP@2 < +0.01 and crack IoU < +0.012.
evidence: UCF-EL multi-label classification: beat mask-exact random copy-paste on 3 backbones; copy-paste dropped EfficientNetV2-L F1 0.767 to 0.746, GDI raised it to 0.774; rare-class F1 up to +63.6%.
prior_overlap: none; defect removal never tried. CP100 (additive paste onto pool cells) is the opposite operation.

alt_notes.adaptation: Fine-tune LaMa on pool cells, then (a) inpaint inactive regions to normal brightness to make crack-only twins, breaking the 'inactive never without crack' coupling, and (b) inpaint cracks out to make clean negatives with identical context; masks edited accordingly.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + inpainted twins (1:1). Baseline: house, 5 v 5 seeds. Metrics: test inactive IoU, crack precision. Kill if inactive IoU < +0.02 and crack pixel precision flat.

alt_notes.adaptation: Erase 3 to 5 px dilated crack masks (and, separately, inactive regions) in the 209 crack train cells to make paired clean twins with relabelled masks; train on originals plus twins to sharpen crack v decoy decisions and decouple crack from inactive.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + paired LaMa twins. Baseline: house, 5 seeds. Metric: crack relP@2 and crack IoU. Kill if relP@2 < +0.01 and IoU < +0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Inpaint the crack label dilated 3 px on the 209 crack cells (and inactive on 42) to make crack-free twins: paired hard negatives sharing every decoy, clean canvases for procedural or generated cracks drawn at a known place (labels aligned by construction), and crack-only / inactive-only variants for the argmax conflict. Verify no dark residue (house p(crack) < 0.01 inside old mask).
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + 209 twins as in-batch paired negatives vs PF. Metric test crack relP@2 and E1 false-positive px per cell; guard relR@2. Kill: relP@2 gain < +0.01 with relR@2 drop > 0.01. Second arm: procedural crack on twins, kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Inpaint dilated crack labels on the 209 crack cells (inactive on 42) to make crack-free twins: paired hard negatives with identical decoys, clean canvases for procedural cracks at known places (aligned by construction), and crack-only / inactive-only variants for the argmax conflict. Check no dark residue.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + 209 twins paired in batch vs PF. Metric test crack relP@2 and E1 crack FP px per cell, guard relR@2. Kill: relP@2 < +0.01 with relR@2 drop > 0.01. Second arm procedural cracks on twins, kill E1 relF1@2 < +0.02. About 8 GPU-h.

title: HyperSORT: Self-organising Robust Training with Hyper-networks
mechanism: Hypernetwork maps a learned per-sample latent (L1-pulled to 0) to U-Net weights; systematic label styles and errors become outlying latents, latent 0 models the majority style.
adaptation: FiLM on the U-Net++ decoder driven by a 2-4 D learned latent per train cell instead of a full hypernetwork (repo needs ImFusion SDK key). Check whether latents cluster by source (label width 1.5 to 3.25 px) and outliers match audit cells; infer at latent 0 or per-source centroid (source-conditional prediction).
min_experiment: Arm: FiLM-latent U-Net++, 2 L1 weights, inference at 0 and source centroid. Baseline: house, 5 seeds. Metric: per-source crack IoU (BMRK, CFVS), clean-49 crack IoU / relF1@2, mIoU_rob. Kill: no centroid gain on BMRK/CFVS and no gain at latent 0.
evidence: R: AMOS with synthetic erosion/dilation styles formed separate latent clusters; on TotalSegmentator surfaced systematic biases and erroneous cases. Qualitative, 3D CT.
prior_overlap: none; source-conditional prediction and annotator modelling listed as never tried.

title: Multi-domain semantic segmentation with overlapping labels
mechanism: Universal taxonomy where each dataset class is a union of universal classes; one softmax over universal classes trained with a partial-label NLL (log of summed probability over the union).
evidence: Competitive within- and cross-dataset, state of the art on WildDash 2; learns concepts never labelled separately in any training dataset.
adaptation: Universal classes = our 24 plus UCF/MSS classes with no BenchmarkEL counterpart (contact, interconnect). Hand-written dataset-to-universal map (UCF crack = {crack, inactive}). Use as the formal version of the marginal-loss arm.
min_experiment: Same as marginal-loss arm (Arm B) but with the universal-taxonomy NLL; 5 seeds, 30k steps vs house 5-seed; kill line as MultiTalent arm. Shares GPU budget with Arm B.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Joint training with UCF-EL 9,562 cells: UCF crack -> log(p_crack + p_inactive); contact/interconnect mapped to ribbon/busbar groups after an eyeball check on ~20 cells; BenchmarkEL loss unchanged.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + UCF-EL 1:1 batches under union loss; baseline PF; metrics E1 crack recall and relF1@2, inactive IoU; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.02 or test crack IoU drop > 0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Joint training with UCF-EL's 9,562 cells. UCF 'crack' is trained as log(p_crack + p_inactive). UCF contact and interconnect map to the busbar and ribbon groups; check this mapping by eye on 20 cells, with no relabelling. The BenchmarkEL loss is unchanged. This keeps UCF information in the model, unlike the old pretraining that the fine-tune erased.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF jointly trained with UCF-EL (1:1 batches) under the union loss. Baseline: PF. Metrics: E1 crack recall and relF1@2, inactive IoU, test crack IoU. Kill if the E1 relF1@2 gain is < 0.02 or test crack IoU drops by more than 0.012.

title: That Label's Got Style: Handling Label Style Bias for Uncertain Image Segmentation
mechanism: Condition stochastic segmentation models (Probabilistic U-Net, SSN) on a discrete label-style variable, modelling p(annotation | image, style) instead of p(annotation | image), which removes style-induced area bias.
adaptation: Style = source. Cheapest form is a one-hot source code into the decoder (shares the arm of the CIN paper); the stochastic variant adds per-source crack sample distributions for calibrated uncertainty and severity flags. Use as small-data evidence and as the probabilistic follow-up.
min_experiment: Arm: c-SSN crack head conditioned on source on house PF, 5 seeds vs house PF; metric clean-49 crack IoU (mean prediction) and crack ECE; kill if IoU gain < +0.012 and ECE not reduced by >= 20%.
evidence: R: ISIC subset, 179 train image-mask pairs over 3 styles; c-Prob.U-Net IoU 0.77/0.78/0.76 vs pooled 0.65/0.65/0.69; PhC-U373 0.92 vs 0.89-0.90. Small data, blob objects.
prior_overlap: none

title: Mixed supervision for surface-defect detection: from weakly to fully supervised learning
mechanism: Segmentation + image-level classification network trained on any mix of pixel-level and image-level labels.
evidence: KolektorSDD2, DAGM, Severstal: few pixel labels plus many weak labels approach full supervision.
adaptation: ELPV 2,624 cells (BMRK source): cell-level defect head; p=0 cells give full-image negatives for crack/inactive; p=1 cells MIL positives. De-duplicate ELPV against BenchmarkEL val/test BMRK cells and modules first.
min_experiment: Arm: house + cell head + ELPV weak labels, 20k steps, 5 seeds. Baseline: house 5-seed. Metric: BMRK inactive IoU on module-grouped 5-fold CV, crack pixel precision. Kill if BMRK inactive IoU < +0.05 and crack precision not up. ~8 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: none; ELPV image labels listed as unused

alt_notes.adaptation: Image-level crack-present / inactive-present heads on U-Net++ bottleneck + pooled seg logits; train on 478 masks plus ELPV 2,624 image labels (BMRK source) and PVEL-AD boxes as image labels; seg loss only where masks exist.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + presence heads + ELPV image labels; baseline PF; metrics BMRK crack IoU, inactive CV IoU, E1 inactive IoU; kill if BMRK crack IoU gain < 0.02 and inactive CV IoU gain < 0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Add an image-level head (crack present, inactive present) on the U-Net++ bottleneck and the seg logits. Train it on mask-derived labels from the 478 cells, on ELPV's 2,624 cells with defect-probability labels (ELPV is the BMRK source, our weakest), and on PVEL-AD boxes reduced to image labels. The seg loss applies only to masked cells.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + presence heads + ELPV image labels. Baseline: PF. Metrics: BMRK crack and inactive IoU, inactive precision, E1 inactive IoU. Kill if the BMRK crack IoU gain is < 0.02 and the CV inactive IoU gain is < 0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Dilate 1-2 px crack labels to the 4-5 px dark-line FWHM and weight by distance to the label centreline (p=1 or 2), negatives weight 1; add crack-present / inactive-present cell heads so ELPV image labels (2,624 cells) can enter as weak data.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + dilated crack label with DT weights (p=1, p=2); baseline: house; metric: 5-fold CV crack relF1@2 and strict IoU; kill if relF1@2 < +0.01 or IoU drops > 0.01. Arm 1b adds stop-grad cls head, kill if cell-level crack recall < +0.02.

title: Depth Anything: Unleashing the Power of Large-Scale Unlabeled Data
mechanism: With many labels, plain self-training gives nothing. It helps only with strong perturbation of the student's unlabelled inputs plus a 1-minus-cosine feature-alignment loss to a frozen DINOv2 (tolerance margin 0.85), applied to unlabelled images only, with the student re-initialised.
adaptation: House U-Net++ R34 student. Align layer3 output through a 1x1 projector (weight warmed up from 0 to 0.1) to frozen DINOv3 ViT-L or ConvNeXt-L stride-16 features of the same pool cell (1-channel image replicated to 3 channels). Margin 0.85, applied only to pool cells, plus colour/blur/CutMix on the student view.
min_experiment: Arm DA-feat (PF + pool pseudo-labels + strong perturbation + feature alignment) vs house PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if all are n.d.
evidence: R: 1.5M labelled + 62M unlabelled. Table 9 (ViT-L AbsRel): unlabelled without perturbation, no gain (KITTI 0.085 -> 0.085). With perturbation 0.081. Adding the feature loss 0.076. Gains on all 6 sets. Feature loss helps on unlabelled data, not on labelled. Margin 0.85 beats 1.0 (0.175 vs 0.188).
prior_overlap: Our Mean Teacher had no feature anchor and the same architecture as its teacher, which is exactly the failure case the paper describes. D24 #16 proposes feature alignment on labelled data; this version is on pool data with a margin. Open.

title: PNT-Edge: Towards Robust Edge Detection with Noisy Labels by Learning Pixel-level Noise Transitions
mechanism: Models label corruption as a smooth displacement field. A 4-layer FCN takes the image, confident predictions and the noisy label, and warps the detector output onto the noisy label, so the detector itself fits the clean, aligned edges.
adaptation: Warm up the house model only until the val crack metric saturates (the memorization point). Then train jointly with the warp module on the crack channel, max shift 3 px. Drop or replace the local-edge-density prior with ridge strength, because cracks are sparse. The warp absorbs per-source and per-annotator offsets, and the detector learns ridge-centred cracks.
min_experiment: Arm: house warm-up + PSL joint training, 5 seeds. Baseline: house at 100% labels. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, E1 relF1@2. Kill if crack IoU and relF1@2 are both n.d. (< 0.012 and < 0.01).
evidence: R: gains over CASENet-S and SEAL on SBD and Cityscapes, scored on a re-annotated clean SBD subset. Shows the memorization effect: clean-label metrics saturate early, then the model memorizes noise. Losses: MSE on confident shifts, warp similarity, smoothness, unmatched-pixel suppression.
prior_overlap: Partly overlaps offset-tolerant CE (n.d.). A learned smooth displacement field with suppression of unmatched pixels is a different mechanism. Noisy-label methods are listed as never tried. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Warm up the house model until val crack metric on revised labels saturates, then joint training with a crack-only warp (max shift 3 px), ridge strength replacing the edge-density prior. Detector learns ridge-centred cracks; warp absorbs per-source offsets.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: warm-up + PSL joint training, 5 seeds; baseline house 5 seeds. Metrics crack IoU, relF1@2, E1 relF1@2. Kill if crack IoU and relF1@2 both n.d. About 15 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Add a 2-channel flow head on the U-Net++ decoder bounded to +/-3 px, applied only to crack (and inactive boundary) channels, with smoothness along the crack in place of the edge-density term; infer with the unwarped head.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + bounded flow head on crack. Baseline: house. Metric: strict crack IoU, relF1@2, component recall >= 20 px. Kill if strict IoU < house and relF1@2 not up by >= 0.01. About 6 GPU-h plus 2 days code.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack only, max shift 3 px, after warm-up on the house recipe; condition the shift network on a source one-hot so it learns per-source bias (BMRK worst, 38% within 1 px). Report mean learned shift per source as a label-quality number for the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house warm-up + PSL warp training, 5 seeds; baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2 on clean-49, E1 relF1@2. Kill if both n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Add a 2-channel shift head conditioned on source ID, displacement capped at 2 px with smoothness, applied to the crack channel before CE + Dice; predict unwarped. The source conditioning lets it learn each source's offset and width.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + source-conditioned shift head, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and relF1@2. Kill: crack IoU under +0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Make the shift head source-conditioned (FiLM on source ID) and apply it to the crack channel only. Use the warped output for strict IoU against source labels and the unwarped output for relF1@2 and severity length estimates. Run only if per-source label-to-ridge offset is systematic.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Pre-check (no GPU): per-source signed offset of label skeleton to darkest ridge in x and y on train labels; proceed only if any source mean > 0.3 px. Arm: house PF + source-conditioned shift head, 5 seeds vs house PF; metric clean-49 crack IoU; kill if < +0.012.

title: rNCA: Self-Repairing Segmentation Masks
mechanism: A 12k-parameter neural cellular automaton runs 64 local update steps on [mask state, image features] and learns to grow and prune a coarse mask; trained on the base model's real predictions paired with ground truth.
evidence: R: DRIVE (20 images, about 4,000 64x64 patches), U-Net base Dice 0.761 / clDice 0.802 / dBeta0 0.965 -> rNCA 0.777 / 0.820 / 0.532. SegFix 0.759, SegRefiner 0.760, DenseCRF 0.760 Dice in the same table. Unseen Swin base 0.767 -> 0.776. Myocardium zero-shot repairs 61.5% of broken cases.
adaptation: Input 1-ch EL + out-of-fold house-ensemble p(crack), p(inactive), plus source id as a constant channel so it can learn per-source label width (ARTS 1.5 px vs BMRK 3.0 px). 64x64 patches centred on predicted and GT crack components plus random patches. Train per CV fold on OOF predictions from the module-grouped 5-fold roots, never on in-sample train predictions. Apply to the test 5-seed ensemble probabilities.
min_experiment: Arm: rNCA on house 5-seed ensemble output. Baseline: house 5-seed ensemble (relF1@2 0.897, relR@2 0.866 at relP@2 0.930, components>=20 px 0.834). Metrics: relR@2 at relP@2>=0.93, component recall, strict crack IoU, OOF-CV relF1@2 for power. Kill: relR@2 gain < +0.01 at fixed relP@2 on both test and OOF CV, or crack IoU drop > 0.01.
prior_overlap: none run. BRIEF section 5 lists learned refinement stages as never tried. D12 item 7 proposes a corrupted-mask refiner on ensemble output (same family, not run); coordinate.

alt_notes.adaptation: Train on out-of-fold crack probability maps from the existing module-grouped 5-fold roots (532 cells; in-fold train predictions are near-perfect and useless) plus synthetic skeleton breaks and faint-segment deletions on GT; 64 px patches around predicted or GT cracks of the 1-channel EL; refine only the crack channel of the 5-seed ensemble, keep argmax for the other 23 classes. Expected to help fragments and component recall, not the 2 px jitter loss.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house 5-seed ensemble + rNCA on crack probabilities. Baseline: same ensemble without refiner (also PF ensemble). Metrics: 5-fold CV and clean-49 crack relF1@2, components >= 20 px found, crack IoU; E1 relR@2. Kill: relF1@2 gain < +0.005 and components-found gain < +0.02 on 5-fold CV.

title: Align and Segment: Unsupervised Learning for Building Segmentation From Misaligned Labels
mechanism: A spatial transformer warps the misaligned label during training so the warped label is the target, with a self-supervised regulariser plus augmentation that stops the segmenter from learning the misalignment; no clean labels needed.
adaptation: Replace the affine warp with a learned per-source label renderer: the net predicts a 1 px crack centreline; a differentiable renderer (Gaussian blur with learnable width and learnable sub-pixel shift per source, 5 sources x 3 numbers) maps it to what that source's annotator draws; loss against the human label. Test: render with the cell's source parameters for strict IoU, or output the centreline for relF1@2. E1 labels are about 1.5x wider than train, so the E1 render width is a stated val-free choice.
min_experiment: Arm: centreline head + per-source renderer on house U-Net++, 5 seeds; baseline: house. Metrics: pooled crack IoU and per-source crack IoU (BMRK 0.379, CFVS-no-twin 0.397). Kill if pooled crack IoU gain < 0.012 and no source gains >= 0.02.
evidence: R: synthetic and real misaligned building labels from several cities; numbers not read (abstract-level via web listing). Code link from the same listing, not opened.
prior_overlap: none: source-conditional prediction and learned label offsets are listed as never tried in BRIEF section 5. D13 rejected AnS as affine-only; this adaptation changes the transform to per-source width and shift.

alt_notes.adaptation: Learn a small per-cell deformation field (+/-3 px, smooth) that warps crack labels to agree with the segmenter under flips and rot90; train the segmenter on the warped labels. Inactive labels are kept fixed (well labelled).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Try only after STEAL. Arm: learned warp field + house, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if there is no detectable difference.

title: Enhanced Crack Segmentation (eCS): A Reference Algorithm for Segmenting Cracks in Multicrystalline Silicon Solar Cells
mechanism: Classical EL crack pipeline that, per a search summary, zeroes the gridline frequencies in the Fourier domain before crack segmentation, which cuts false positives from finger edges.
adaptation: On the fly per image: 2D FFT, detect the finger and busbar peaks on each axis, notch them, inverse FFT, and use the residual as input channel 2 next to raw (conv1 channel-2 weights zero-initialised). Per-image peaks adapt to half-cut E1 layouts. Also aims at the gridline class (a local break of finger periodicity).
min_experiment: Arm: house with the 2-channel [raw, notch residual], 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: gridline IoU/recall, crack precision at fixed recall, E1 relF1@2. Kill: gridline < +0.03 and crack IoU < +0.012 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.02.
evidence: R (search summary only, full text not read): Fourier zeroing smooths the gridlines and reduces false positives. The code zip is on the FAU page (Python 3.5, skimage, OpenCV).
prior_overlap: none. Intensity normalisation (fail) is a different mechanism.

alt_notes.adaptation: Per image 2D FFT, auto-detect finger and busbar peaks per axis, notch, IFFT; feed raw minus de-gridded residual as channel 2 with zero-initialised conv1 weights. Computed per image so half-cut E1 cells get their own notch. Also a classical benchmark row.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: 2-channel [raw, notch residual]; baseline house; 5 seeds; gridline IoU/recall, crack precision at fixed recall, E1 relF1@2; kill if gridline IoU < +0.03 and crack IoU < +0.012 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.02. About 6 GPU-h.

title: Multi-teacher based knowledge distillation for retinal vessel segmentation
mechanism: Specialist teachers trained on modified ground truth (original, thin-only, thick-only); student distils all of them.
adaptation: Teacher A house (native labels), teacher B crack labels dilated 3-5 px (recall teacher), teacher C inactive specialist (oversample 42 inactive cells), teacher D PF (E1 inactive 0.24); student CE(GT) + per-class teacher mix (crack from A+B, inactive from C+D).
min_experiment: Arm: 4-specialist KD student, 3 seeds. Baseline: house single and Noothout KD arm. Metric: relR@2 at relP@2 >= 0.90, inactive IoU, E1 inactive IoU. Kill: relR@2 < +0.015 and inactive IoU < +0.02.
evidence: R: two fundus and two angiography sets; up to +8.44 F1 and +10.42 IoU over baseline U-Net.
prior_overlap: none; dilated labels never used as a teacher (Skeleton Recall / offset-tolerant CE are different mechanisms)

title: UniMatch V2: Pushing the Limit of Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Uses a DINOv2 ViT encoder with a DPT head and single-stream weak-to-strong consistency. Complementary channel-wise dropout gives two disjoint feature streams, with an EMA teacher. The gains persist at full labels when the encoder is a large pretrained ViT.
adaptation: Replicate the 1-channel EL image to 3 channels. 518 px gives 37x37 tokens, far too coarse for 1-2 px cracks, so fuse the DPT output with a stride-2 CNN stem or decoder (U-Net++ R34 branch), or run at 1036 px. Fine-tune the encoder at 0.1x lr following the PF finding. Unlabelled pool = 11.9k CSIR/ARTS cells, including the 1,152 half-cells.
min_experiment: Arm A: DINOv2-B + DPT + CNN skip, supervised on 478 cells. Arm B: A + UniMatch V2 on the 11.9k pool. 3 seeds, 40k steps. Compare B vs A and B vs the house model on clean-49 crack relF1@2 and IoU, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: B-A < +0.01 crack relF1@2 and < +0.02 inactive IoU, and B more than 0.02 below house crack IoU.
evidence: R: Pascal full split (1,464 labels): DINOv2-S 85.6 -> 87.8 (+2.2), DINOv2-B 88.3 -> 90.8 (+2.5), DINOv2-L 90.7 -> 91.2 (+0.5) mIoU. Real-world full-label setting with extra unlabelled data: COCO +0.7, ADE20K +0.8 to +1.6, Cityscapes +0.3. A frozen DINOv2-S beats a fine-tuned ResNet-101. SAM encoders do much worse than DINOv2 in their framework.
prior_overlap: Partial. The SSL row was ResNet-34 only, and the foundation-encoder row covered frozen linear probes plus one 4k-step ConvNeXt-T screen. A fine-tuned ViT-B/L, with or without SSL, was never run, and BRIEF lists it as open.

alt_notes.adaptation: VFM-H as the student; 478 labelled + 11.9k pool; keep label-safe augmentation for strong views of thin cracks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: UniMatch V2 VFM-H vs supervised VFM-H; CV crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 relF1@2; kill if all n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: VFM-H as student on 478 labelled + 11.9k pool (or E1-like half-cells), house label-safe strong augmentation only.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: VFM-H + UniMatch V2. Baseline: VFM-H supervised only, and house PF. Metric: CV crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill: both CV metrics n.d. and E1 not +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: DINOv2/v3 ViT-B or ViT-L at 1024 px input, since the 37-token grid at 512 px is too coarse for 1 to 2 px cracks. 1-channel input replicated to 3. Pool 11.9k. tau 0.95 for non-crack classes and a tolerance band for crack pseudo-labels. Best used as a VFM SSL baseline in the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm UMv2-VFM (DINOv3 ViT-B, 1024 px, 478 labelled + 11.9k pool) vs the same encoder supervised-only, 3 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob, E1 relF1@2. Kill if all are n.d. vs supervised-only.

title: Omni-Crack30k: A Benchmark for Crack Segmentation and the Reasonable Effectiveness of Transfer Learning
mechanism: 30k crack images from 20+ datasets as one benchmark; nnU-Net transfer learning beats all other approaches; tolerance metric clIoU@4px because strict IoU favours wide cracks.
adaptation: Use as the direct thin-crack evidence that the nnU-Net recipe should be run on EL, and adopt clIoU@k (k=2 for our 1-2 px labels) beside relF1@2 as a benchmark crack metric. OmniCrack30k pretraining of the crack head is D09's arm; do not duplicate.
min_experiment: Covered by the nnU-Net arm A; metric work: compute clIoU@2 and @4 for the house 5-seed ensemble and arm A on CV and E1; keep the metric if it ranks runs consistently with relF1@2 and has lower seed variance than strict IoU.
evidence: R: 30k samples, 9 billion pixels, asphalt / ceramic / concrete / masonry / steel; nnU-Net mean clIoU4px 64%, at least 10 points above all other approaches.
prior_overlap: none in BRIEF section 5; also listed in D09 (pretraining arm)

alt_notes.adaptation: (a) Crack-binary pretraining of the ResNet-34 U-Net++ on OmniCrack30k in grayscale at 512 px, then PF fine-tune on EL so the pretraining survives. (b) nnU-Net v2 auto-configured on our 24 classes as a benchmark row. (c) Adopt clIoU@k as a benchmark metric next to relF1@2.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: OmniCrack30k pretrain (20k steps) then PF; baseline PF from ImageNet; 3 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, CV crack IoU, CV components >= 20 px found. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.02 and CV crack IoU n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Add a tolerant centerline IoU at 2 px next to relF1@2 in our benchmark; include nnU-Net 2D as a required baseline; optional crack pretraining corpus.
alt_notes.min_experiment: CPU: compute clIoU@2px on existing predictions; GPU: nnU-Net 2D on the 5 folds vs house PF on crack relF1@2.

alt_notes.adaptation: (a) Pretrain the crack channel of the house model on OmniCrack30k in grayscale (512 crops), then PF fine-tune on EL so the pretraining survives. (b) Run nnU-Net v2 auto-configured on our 24 classes as a benchmark row. (c) Adopt clIoU@k next to relF1@2 in the benchmark protocol.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: OmniCrack30k crack pretraining then PF; baseline: PF from ImageNet; 3 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, CV crack IoU, CV components >= 20 px found. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.02 and CV crack IoU n.d. nnU-Net 5-fold as separate benchmark row.

alt_notes.adaptation: (a) Metric: add tolerance clIoU at 1, 2 and 4 px next to relF1@2, because EL crack labels jitter 1-2 px. (b) Score arm: convert OmniCrack30k to grayscale 512 crops, pretrain U-Net++/ResNet-34 as binary crack, then fine-tune on EL with PF so the encoder is kept.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: OmniCrack30k-pretrained U-Net++ R34, then PF fine-tune, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF 5-seed mean from ImageNet init. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: crack IoU gain < +0.01 AND E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02.

title: Automatic Crack Segmentation and Feature Extraction in Electroluminescence Images of Solar Modules (PV-Vision)
mechanism: From segmented cracks and busbars, compute the crack-isolated area (region cut off from all busbars) as worst-case inactive area, plus crack length and brightness inside the isolated area.
adaptation: Build an isolated-region map from our predicted crack plus ribbon/busbar classes and feed it as an extra input to a second-stage inactive head (inactive touches a crack in 99% of cases). Same map gives a severity output. Public DuraMAT crack set (1,272/206/359) usable as an external cross-dataset test.
min_experiment: Step 0 (CPU): on val compute isolated area from GT crack + ribbon masks; kill if it covers < 50% of GT inactive pixels. Step 1: arm PF + isolated map into stage-2 inactive head v PF, 5 seeds; metric inactive IoU; kill if < +0.02.
evidence: R: UNet-VGG16 crack F1 0.875, IoU 0.782 on their own test set (359 cells, includes busbar class); companion PVSC 2022 paper predicts maximum inactive area from detected cracks.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Same per-dataset-head joint training as MSPS; map its dark area class to a second inactive head to attack the 42-cell inactive shortage; resample 400 px to our scale. Hold out its test split as an external crack test set for the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + LBNL joint with own head. Baseline: PF, 5 v 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, test inactive IoU (BMRK cells), test crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03 and inactive IoU gain < 0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Physics prior for inactive (99% of our inactive regions touch a crack label): build crack-bounded regions from predicted crack + busbar + border masks and relabel a region inactive if its mean EL is below a source-wise fraction of the cell median; union / vote with the network's inactive map. Also an open baseline for the benchmark suite.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house 5-seed ensemble + region rule (threshold tuned on CV folds only); baseline: same ensemble. Metric: CV inactive IoU and relR. Kill if inactive IoU < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Run its released model under our protocol as a published EL baseline; use its crack features for severity; its crack set is possible extra data (D02 / D03).
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training arm: inference of PV-Vision model on our test-clean and E1 under our metrics (crack IoU, relF1@2). Then optional joint training with its crack set vs house; kill if test crack IoU < +0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Run the released model under our protocol as a published EL baseline; its features feed the severity track; its dataset is extra data for D02/D03.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training arm: evaluate released PV-Vision weights on test-clean and E1 crack relF1@2 and IoU under our protocol (benchmark row). Kill not applicable.

alt_notes.adaptation: Third pixel-labelled EL crack source for joint training; its high IoU suggests wide crack labels (unverified), so it must enter through source conditioning or a separate head. Crack-isolated-area features give a severity baseline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Measure its median crack label width first. Then add it as a source in the joint run (MultiTalent arm) vs joint run without it; 5 seeds each. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, E1 crack recall. Kill if no gain >= 0.012 crack IoU or +0.03 E1 recall. ~15 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use our predicted crack + ribbons (+ busbars) + border masks. Interior components touching no ribbon are isolated. If an isolated part is darker than a per-source threshold fitted on train, label it inactive and OR it with the model's inactive. For half-cut E1 cells, add the cut edge as a barrier.
alt_notes.min_experiment: CPU post-processing on PF and PF-ensemble predictions; thresholds fitted on module-grouped 5-fold CV (532 cells). Metrics: inactive IoU, P / R, BMRK inactive IoU on CV and E1. Kill if CV inactive IoU gain < +0.02 or precision drop > 0.05. <2 GPU-h.

title: Evaluating SAM-based and Convolutional Architectures in Thin Retinal Vessel Segmentation: Model Capacity, Computational Cost and Foundation Pre-training
mechanism: Evidence that a pretrained plain ViT (MedSAM, patch 16) matches the best CNN on thin-vessel centerline recall only when the image is upscaled to its 1024 window; padding loses the thin structures.
adaptation: Fixed rule for every ViT arm: upscale 512 EL to 1024; one ablation inside the SAM2-UNet arm at 512 vs 1024. Explains why our native-resolution probes may have under-read FMs.
min_experiment: SAM2-UNet at 512 vs 1024 input, 5-fold CV; if 1024 is not >= +0.01 crack relF1@2, drop upscaling for all arms.
evidence: R: DRIVE, HRF, FIVES, VessMap; MedSAM thin recall within 0.6 to 2.5 pp of best CNN; padding vs upscaling cut thin recall by 17.9 and 41.3 points; pretraining raised thin recall 17.6 / 12.4 points on two sets.
prior_overlap: Section 5 linear probes ran at native resolution; input upscaling for ViTs not tested (2x input run was on the house CNN).

alt_notes.adaptation: Design rule for every ViT arm here: upscale 512 to 1024, fine-tune (full or PEFT), never frozen probe; report crack recall binned by label width (per source widths 1.5 to 3.25 px).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Within SAM2-UNet or Dino U-Net: 512 vs 1024 input, 3 seeds; metric crack recall on components < 20 px and relF1@2; kill the 1024 arm if gain < 0.012 crack IoU and < 0.01 relF1@2.

title: Balancing Logit Variation for Long-Tailed Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Add class-scaled Gaussian noise to logits during training (larger for rare classes) so tail features occupy a region rather than a point; removed at test.
adaptation: Sigma from log inverse pixel frequency over 17 present classes; cap crack sigma at the inactive value (or exclude crack in a second arm) because crack labels are already jittered. One-line head change on U-Net++.
min_experiment: Arm: BLV with crack capped, 3 seeds; baseline SUP100; metric mIoU_rob, splice/edge_dark IoU, crack IoU guard; kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01 or crack IoU drop > 0.01.
evidence: R: gains mostly on tail classes; fully supervised ViT-B UperHead 77.7 mIoU, tail 66.2, ahead of logit adjustment and Lovasz in their comparison table.
prior_overlap: none

title: Adaptive Post-Processing Drives Instance-Level Detection in Stroke Lesion Segmentation (VCAP)
mechanism: Component-size thresholds adapted per case to the predicted lesion burden, fitted cross-fold.
adaptation: Per-cell predicted crack burden sets min component length and peak-probability cut for crack components; fitted on val + F51 or module-grouped CV out-of-fold maps of the existing 5-seed ensemble; no retraining.
min_experiment: Arm: VCAP rule on ensemble maps. Baseline: ensemble with val-chosen logit bias. Metric: test and E1 crack relF1@2 and component F1. Kill: relF1@2 gain < 0.005 and component F1 gain < 0.01.
evidence: ISLES'26 training set 1,453 cases, 5-fold: lesion F1 +0.032 from VCAP, about 6x any architecture change tested; post-processed ensemble Dice 0.651 / lesion F1 0.614 vs 0.644 / 0.573.
prior_overlap: Per-module thresholds and global logit bias were tried; per-component, burden-conditioned rules were not.

title: Fracture-Informed CNN-Transformer Ensemble for Multiclass Photovoltaic Defect Segmentation in Electroluminescence Images
mechanism: SegFormer-B0 with an edge-guided residual-logit refiner (probability, uncertainty, Sobel cues) soft-fused with a compact U-Net++ branch (weights 0.55/0.45).
adaptation: Heterogeneous ensemble: house 5-seed U-Net++ ensemble plus a SegFormer-B2 (1024 px) or EoMT member; fusion weight chosen on val per class group (crack, inactive, rest); refiner idea optional.
min_experiment: Arm house 5-seed ensemble + SegFormer-B2 member vs house 5-seed ensemble; metrics crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob, E1 relF1@2; kill if no metric improves beyond its noise floor fold-paired (crack IoU 0.012).
evidence: R: 5-class EL set (dataset unverified), ensemble mIoU 0.840, non-background mIoU 0.804, defect mIoU 0.779 internal test; gains over refined SegFormer confirmed by paired bootstrap.
prior_overlap: none: BRIEF lists heterogeneous ensembles as never tried; only same-architecture 5-seed ensembles were run (the one clear win).

alt_notes.adaptation: Train a tiny refiner on out-of-fold 5-seed ensemble probabilities, entropy, Sobel magnitude and the image, using the existing module-grouped 5-fold roots so the refiner never sees in-fold predictions.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: 5-seed ensemble + OOF-trained refiner. Baseline: 5-seed ensemble at argmax (crack IoU 0.485 to 0.488). Metric: crack IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill if crack IoU < +0.01 or mIoU_rob drops.

alt_notes.adaptation: Add one non-RN34 member (SegFormer / ConvNeXt / DINOv3 from D23-D24) to the 5-seed ensemble with per-class fusion weights fitted in CV; diversity by architecture since more RN34 seeds saturate (E1 +0.001 when doubled).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: 5 house + 5 transformer (or 3+3 at equal compute), CV-fitted per-class weights. Baseline: 10-seed RN34 ensemble. Metric: crack IoU, E1 relF1@2, inactive IoU. Kill: < +0.008 crack IoU and < +0.02 E1 relF1@2.

title: AnyUp: Universal Feature Upsampling
mechanism: Encoder-agnostic, image-guided local-window attention upsampler that lifts any feature map to any resolution without retraining per encoder.
adaptation: Upsample frozen or LoRA DINOv3 ViT-S/L patch-16 tokens (32x32 at 512 px) to 512x512 using the 1-channel EL cell (replicated to 3) as guidance, then a light conv head plus a full-res conv stem; no upsampler training, so a probe costs hours. Targets the E1 context gap by making ViTs usable for 1-2 px cracks and gridline.
min_experiment: Frozen DINOv3 ViT-S/16 and ViT-L/16 1x1 probe over 24 classes: bilinear-512 vs bilinear-1024-input (existing ViT-S crack AP 0.212) vs AnyUp-512; metric F51 + module-grouped CV crack AP and gridline AP. Kill if AnyUp at 512 does not beat bilinear at 1024 input on crack AP. Pass leads to a fine-tuned ViT-L + AnyUp arm vs house PF, kill if E1 crack relF1@2 gain < +0.03.
evidence: R: linear probe on DINOv2 ViT-S, 448 px: ADE20k mIoU 40.54 bilinear -> 42.43; COCO 59.48 -> 62.16; VOC 81.43 -> 84.00; best feature-space preservation (ADE20k 40.83 with pre-trained probes vs LoftUp 4.27). E: our DINOv3 ViT-S/16 probe crack AP 0.147 at 512 vs 0.212 at 1024 px, so token resolution limits ViTs here.
prior_overlap: Foundation-encoder row tested frozen linear probes with bilinear upsampling only and no ViT fine-tune; upsamplers untested. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Second zero-shot arm beside NAF on frozen DINOv3 features of 512 px EL cells (1-ch replicated); output feeds a conv head plus a full-resolution conv stem for 1 to 2 px cracks and gridline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Same probe as NAF: AnyUp 512 vs bilinear 512 / 1024 on frozen DINOv3 ViT-S and ViT-L; metric F51 + CV crack AP and gridline AP; kill if not above bilinear-1024 crack AP. About 2 GPU-h.

title: Cut to the Mix: Simple Data Augmentation Outperforms Elaborate Ones in Limited Organ Segmentation Datasets
mechanism: Supervised CutMix between labelled images (box ~ Beta(0.5,0.5)) with labels copied, compared with CarveMix, AnatoMix and ObjectAug on small data.
adaptation: CutMix between two labelled train cells of the same cell type, box aligned to the cell grid; labels follow the box; 50% of batches; no mixing across BMRK and others at first (label width differs). Seams are labelled from both sides, teaching that discontinuities are not cracks.
min_experiment: PF+CM vs PF, 5 seeds; mIoU_rob, splice/gridline/edge_dark/material IoU, crack IoU and false crack px on 31 crack-free val cells. Kill: mIoU_rob < +0.005 and crack IoU change within +-0.012.
evidence: 20 training CT volumes (AMOS), 16 organs, nnU-Net: CutMix +4.8 macro Dice with TDA (78.2 to 83.0), CarveMix +2.5, AnatoMix +3.2, ObjectAug collapsed to 22.6 macro.
prior_overlap: Partial: CutMix was run inside Mean Teacher on the unlabelled stream (n.d. at 100%). Supervised CutMix of labelled cells never run.

title: FreeMask: Synthetic Images with Dense Annotations Make Stronger Segmentation Models
mechanism: Generate images from semantic masks, drop synthetic pixels whose loss under a real-trained model exceeds a per-class threshold, and generate more samples for harder masks.
adaptation: Filter synthetic EL pairs with the house ensemble's per-class loss (crack threshold set on train-cell loss, allowing 2 px jitter); hardness per mask = per-cell crack/inactive loss of the house model on train; applies to every synthetic arm in this direction.
min_experiment: Arm: synthetic stream (row 1 or 2) with filtering + hardness resampling. Baseline: same stream unfiltered, PF, 5 seeds. Metric: the arm's main metric (E1 relF1@2 or CV inactive IoU). Kill: gain < +0.01.
evidence: R (from web summary of the paper): ADE20K 48.7 -> 52.0 mIoU with filtered synthetic data jointly or as pretraining; synthetic-only 48.3 vs real 48.5.
prior_overlap: None.

title: NAF: Zero-Shot Feature Upsampling via Neighborhood Attention Filtering
mechanism: Encoder-agnostic zero-shot upsampler: cross-scale neighbourhood attention with RoPE guided only by the high-res image, a learned joint bilateral filter that lifts any VFM's patch features to pixel resolution.
adaptation: Lift frozen DINOv3 ViT-L/16 (or 7B) 32x32 tokens to 512x512 using the 1-channel EL cell replicated to 3 channels as guidance; light conv head over 24 classes. Check that sub-2%-contrast cracks are not smoothed by the bilateral weighting along finger and busbar edges.
min_experiment: Frozen DINOv3 ViT-S and ViT-L 1x1 probe: NAF at 512 vs bilinear at 512 vs bilinear at 1024 input (existing 0.212 crack AP for ViT-S). Metric F51 + 5-fold CV crack AP and gridline AP. Kill: NAF at 512 does not beat bilinear at 1024 on crack AP. About 3 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: Partial: frozen linear probes of DINOv3 / DINOv2 / SAM2 used bilinear upsampling only. No learned upsampler was tested, so open.
evidence: R: Pascal VOC probe with DINOv3-B 87.85 mIoU vs JAFAR 87.10; runs on DINOv3-7B where VFM-specific upsamplers run out of memory; 2K feature maps at 18 FPS. Object-scale benchmarks only.

title: Boosting Semantic Segmentation by Conditioning the Backbone with Semantic Boundaries (SBCB)
mechanism: Auxiliary semantic-boundary-detection head on multi-scale backbone features, dropped at inference (no cost).
evidence: R: Cityscapes average +1.2 IoU and +2.6 boundary F over several heads and backbones; improves over- and under-segmentation.
adaptation: Boundary targets (2 px) from the 24-class mask, excluding crack (its boundary is itself) or using a 3 px band; aimed at gridline, edge_dark, border, material, inactive edges; attach to ResNet-34 stages 1-4.
min_experiment: Arm house + SBCB head; baseline house; metrics gridline/edge_dark/material IoU and mIoU_rob; kill if mIoU_rob gain < 0.01 and no weak class up >= 0.03.
prior_overlap: none; edge formulations never tried

title: Boosting Semantic Segmentation with Semantic Boundaries (SBCB)
mechanism: An auxiliary semantic-boundary-detection head on multi-scale backbone features. It conditions the backbone during training and is dropped at inference.
adaptation: Boundary targets come from the 24-class mask (2 px class edges), with crack excluded or replaced by a 3 px dilated crack band because a crack is all boundary. Attach to ResNet-34 layers 1 to 4. Aimed at gridline, edge_dark, border, material and inactive edges.
min_experiment: Arm: house + SBCB head. Baseline: house (5 seeds). Metrics: mIoU_rob, gridline, edge_dark and material IoU. Kill if the mIoU_rob gain is < 0.01 and no weak class rises by >= 0.03.
evidence: R: Cityscapes +0.5 to +3.0 IoU and boundary F +1.6 to +4.1, across several heads and backbones including ViTs.
prior_overlap: none. Edge formulations are listed as never tried.

title: GeoLS: an Intensity-based, Geodesic Soft Labeling for Image Segmentation
mechanism: Soft labels from a geodesic distance transform on image intensity, so label mass spreads along similar intensities and not across edges.
adaptation: Geodesic distance on the EL image from each crack label pixel: soft crack mass flows along the dark crack ridge and not over bright silicon, recentring labels that sit > 1 px off the darkest ridge (half of label points). Same for inactive borders. Combine with JML/DML.
min_experiment: Pre-check without training: on train cells, measure distance of GeoLS soft-label peak vs raw label to the darkest ridge; stop if not closer in most cells. Then arm GeoLS + JML vs SUP100, 5 v 5; kill if crack IoU < +0.012 or relP@2 drop > 0.05.
evidence: R: consistent Dice and Hausdorff gains over other soft-labelling methods on three public medical datasets (abstract).
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Geodesic distance on the EL image from each crack label pixel so soft crack mass flows along the dark ridge, not across bright silicon; recentres labels that sit > 1 px off the ridge; same for inactive edges.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Pre-check without training: on train cells, compare distance of GeoLS soft-label peak vs raw label to the darkest ridge; stop if no shift toward ridge in most cells. Then arm GeoLS crack targets + CE + JML vs SUP100; kill crack IoU < +0.012 or relP@2 drop > 0.05.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Retinal Vessel Segmentation via Ensemble Distillation
mechanism: Distil a 5-model ensemble into one FR-UNet (KL or contrastive representation distillation) to keep ensemble Dice and calibration for thin vessels.
adaptation: Same arm as Noothout; also report ECE on crack pixels and student uncertainty over the crack band as input to severity post-evaluation.
min_experiment: Within the Noothout arm: add crack-pixel ECE and relF1@2 at matched precision. Kill as Noothout arm.
evidence: R: DRIVE (40 imgs) and FIVES (800); distilled model comparable to 5-model deep ensemble on DSC / MCC and calibration (ECE, Brier, NLL); beats MC dropout and Layer Ensembles on cost.
prior_overlap: none

title: Vision Transformer-Conditioned UNet for Domain-Adaptive Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: A full UNet with local inductive bias and full-res decoding is conditioned on frozen pretrained ViT representations through learnable tokens and a two-way attention decoder, aimed at sparse, fine, low-SNR targets.
adaptation: Keep the house U-Net++/ResNet-34 detail path; add cross-attention from its bottleneck and decoder nodes to frozen DINOv3 ViT-L tokens of the same cell. The ViT supplies context for half-cut layout and scuff streaks (E1); 1-2 px localisation stays with the CNN. PF schedule for the CNN.
min_experiment: Arm: house PF + ViT-L token conditioning; baseline: house PF; 5-fold module-grouped CV crack IoU and inactive IoU, then E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU. Kill if E1 crack relF1@2 < +0.03 or CV crack IoU drops > 0.012.
evidence: R: abstract reports gains over baselines on MRI and CT semantic segmentation with frozen ViT; no numbers retrieved, no thin-line data.
prior_overlap: none; no ViT-conditioned CNN run exists.

alt_notes.adaptation: Keep the house U-Net++ / ResNet-34 as the pixel path for 1 to 2 px localisation; add cross-attention from its bottleneck and decoder stages to frozen DINOv3 ViT-L tokens of the same cell so half-cut layout and scuff context come from the ViT. About 200 lines of our own code (official code not released).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house PF + frozen DINOv3 ViT-L conditioning; baseline house PF; 5-fold CV crack IoU / relF1@2 / inactive IoU, then E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU. Kill: E1 crack relF1@2 gain < +0.03 or CV crack IoU drop > 0.012. About 20 GPU-h.

title: Multi-Period Texture Contrast Enhancement for Low-Contrast Wafer Defect Detection and Segmentation
mechanism: MPTCE: reconstruct the dominant periodic component of a feature map in the frequency domain, take abs(F - F_periodic) as a disturbance map, turn its gradient into attention, and output F + alpha*A*F.
adaptation: Insert after ResNet-34 layer1 (128 px) and layer2 (64 px), where the finger pitch is still resolvable. Pick the top-k spectral peaks per channel per image so half-cut layouts adapt. Optionally supervise the disturbance map weakly with crack + gridline masks.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + MPTCE at layer1/2, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metric: gridline IoU, crack pixel precision, crack IoU. Kill: gridline < +0.03 and crack IoU < +0.012.
evidence: R: wafer data, 4,531 RGB images, 7 classes, YOLOv8-seg base. MPTCE alone: recall 71.2 -> 73.7, mAP50 72.7 -> 76.2, mAP50-95 47.9 -> 51.1. Full model +8.3 mAP50-95, false positives -8.6%.
prior_overlap: none in BRIEF section 5. D08 also lists it.

alt_notes.adaptation: Fingers and busbars are periodic, cracks and inactive are not: add the periodic-suppressed image as channel 2 only, never replace the input (gridline and busbar are classes).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + periodic-suppressed channel, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack precision and IoU, gridline IoU. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012 or gridline IoU drop > 0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Insert after encoder layer1 (128 px) and layer2 (64 px), top-k spectral peaks per channel per image; expose D as auxiliary map. Targets gridline recall and crack precision near fingers.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + MPTCE at layer1/2; baseline PF; 5 seeds; gridline IoU, crack pixel precision; kill if gridline < +0.03 and crack IoU < +0.012.

title: MedNeXt: Transformer-Driven Scaling of ConvNets for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Fully ConvNeXt encoder-decoder with residual ConvNeXt up/down blocks and large depthwise kernels; UpKern initialises a large-kernel net from a trained small-kernel net, which avoids saturation on small data.
adaptation: 2D MedNeXt in nnU-Net at 512 px, 1 channel, label-safe augmentation. Train k3 first, then UpKern to k5/k7 to widen context along crack direction while keeping 1 px detail in the full-resolution stage.
min_experiment: MedNeXt-B k3 then UpKern k5 on the module-grouped folds, against the ResEnc M arm on the same folds; metric CV-mean crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2. Kill: no fold-mean gain above 1 fold SD on either.
evidence: R: best on 5 of 6 3D datasets in nnU-Net Revisited (for example ACDC 92.65, BTCV 85.04 against 83.08 org), at 68 to 233 A100 h in 3D. Part of the gain was explained by target spacing choice.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: 2D MedNeXt-B/L k3 at 512 px, 1 channel, label-safe aug, then UpKern to k5. Large kernels give context for E1 (scuff v crack) without attention. 2D support in repo unverified; a 2D port of the block is small.
alt_notes.min_experiment: MedNeXt-B k3 and k5 (UpKern) 2D, 5 folds v nnU-Net arm A. Metric: CV crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if no metric improves by >=0.01 (CV) or 0.03 (E1).

title: Dynamic Snake Convolution based on Topological Geometric Constraints for Tubular Structure Segmentation
mechanism: Deformable offsets constrained to a continuous chain along x or y, so the kernel follows a thin curved line. x, y and standard kernels are fused across views, with a persistent-homology loss (TCLoss).
adaptation: Put DSConv (x, y, standard, fused) in the two finest U-Net++ decoder stages only and keep the ResNet-34 encoder. Leave TCLoss out of the first arm. 76 to 88% of EL crack components are under 20 px, so expect gains mainly on long cracks and E1 long cracks.
min_experiment: DSConv decoder vs house, 5 v 5 seeds. Metrics: test-clean crack relF1@2, components >= 20 px found, E1 relF1@2. Kill if no metric improves by >= 0.012.
evidence: R (full text): DRIVE Dice 82.06, clDice 82.07. Massachusetts Roads Dice 78.21, clDice 87.64, at most +1.31 Dice and +0.77 clDice over U-Net. 3D coronary +3.40 Dice.
prior_overlap: None. BRIEF lists snake and deformable convolutions as never tried. Topology losses (clDice, Skeleton Recall) were run, but TCLoss was not.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace the two highest-resolution U-Net++ decoder blocks (optionally encoder layer1) with DSConv-x + DSConv-y + 3x3 fused, 1-ch 512 px, 24 classes. Drop TCLoss initially (topology losses already run). Judge on detection and E1, not strict IoU, because labels are jittered.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: U-Net++ with DSConv decoder blocks, house and PF, 5 seeds; baseline house / PF 5 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2, components >=20 px found, E1 relF1@2, test crack IoU. Kill: relF1@2 and components-found gains both < 0.01 and E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.02.

title: An End-to-End Automated Pipeline for Controllable Crack Data Synthesis
mechanism: Procedural Bezier skeletons turned into crack masks by a GAN, rendered by dual-ControlNet Stable Diffusion; an ensemble of real-trained segmenters assigns pixel-wise label confidence that weights the synthetic loss instead of hard filtering; detectors evaluated by probability of detection (POD) vs crack width.
adaptation: Use the existing 5-seed house ensemble as the confidence model for any synthetic crack pair (it already sits at relF1@2 0.897); weight synthetic pixels by agreement with the inherited mask. Add POD vs crack width and contrast (a90/95) to the benchmark, computed on test and E1 crack components.
min_experiment: Arm: row-1 synthetic stream with confidence-weighted loss. Baseline: same stream unweighted, both on PF, 5 seeds. Metric: E1 relF1@2 and test crack relP@2. Kill: gain < +0.01 on both.
evidence: R: improves five segmentation networks over conventional, diffusion and flow-matching augmentation on CRACK500 and CrackTree200; confidence weighting beats threshold filtering at every threshold; U-Net width detected at 90% POD / 95% confidence 8.0 -> 4.3 px; ECE 14.2% -> 9.6%.
prior_overlap: None.

alt_notes.adaptation: Take only the confidence weighting: the house 5-seed ensemble scores every pasted or rendered pixel, and that score weights the loss in the copy-paste, ObjectAug and procedural arms. For the benchmark, report POD against crack contrast and length on test and E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Any synthetic arm with vs without ensemble-confidence weights, 5 seeds. Metric: that arm's main metric. Kill if gain < +0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use only the confidence weighting: house 5-seed ensemble scores every pasted, carved or rendered pixel in the CarveMix, Soft-CP, Synth4Seg and procedural arms. For the benchmark, report POD vs crack contrast and length on test and E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Best synthetic arm with vs without ensemble-confidence weights; that arm's main metric. Kill: < +0.01.

title: Rein++: Efficient Generalization and Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation With Vision Foundation Models
mechanism: Rein-style learnable tokens on a frozen VFM for generalisation (Rein-G), plus an adaptation stage (Rein-A) that uses unlabelled target-domain images.
adaptation: 1024 px input (EL grey to 3 channels), frozen DINOv2-L or DINOv3-L, ResNet-34 stem as a stride-2/4 detail branch, 24-class head, house loss. Rein-G trained on the 5 labelled sources; Rein-A run on the 1,152 unlabelled multi half-cells from the pool (target-like for E1), never on E1 cells.
min_experiment: Arm: VFM-H + Rein-G, then + Rein-A. Baseline: house PF. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU (one pre-registered opening), module-grouped 5-fold CV crack relF1@2. Kill: CV crack relF1@2 more than 0.005 below PF and E1 relF1@2 not at least +0.03 over PF (about 0.42) and E1 inactive IoU not above 0.24; Rein-A killed if it adds less than +0.02 E1 relF1@2 over Rein-G.
evidence: R: abstract only (TPAMI 2026, 5 citations); Rein-A / Rein-G split stated in abstract; numbers not read.
prior_overlap: none: no adapter, no target-domain adaptation and no ViT-L was ever tested (BRIEF section 5 lists UDA aimed at E1 as open).

alt_notes.adaptation: Rein-G on the 5 labelled sources; Rein-A on unlabelled pool cells resembling E1 (1,152 multi half-cells, CSIR), never E1 itself; drop the SAM boundary module for cracks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Add Rein-A to the winning Rein arm; baseline Rein-G alone and house PF; metric E1 crack relF1@2; kill if not +0.02 over Rein-G.

alt_notes.adaptation: Rein-G on DINOv2-L or DINOv3 with a high-resolution CNN skip for cracks, trained on 478 cells. Rein-A with the half-cell pool as the unlabelled target. Overlaps the adapters direction; included for its UDA part.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: Rein-G (+ Rein-A) with CNN skip, 3 seeds. Baseline: PF house. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, clean-49 crack IoU and mIoU_rob. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < PF + 0.03 and test crack IoU more than 0.02 below PF.

title: The Centerline-Cross Entropy Loss for Vessel-Like Structure Segmentation: Better Topology Consistency Without Sacrificing Accuracy
mechanism: CE restricted to the label skeleton (recall) and to the predicted skeleton (precision), added to CE. This keeps CE's robustness to noisy annotations, which Dice-based clDice lacks.
adaptation: Crack class only, weight 0.1 to 0.5. The label skeleton is about the 1-2 px trace itself. The predicted-skeleton precision term penalises thin false lines (E1 scuff streaks, gridline confusion) and so counters the widening Skeleton Recall caused.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + clCE (crack, w 0.25), 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, predicted width, E1 relF1@2. Kill if crack IoU < baseline - 0.012, or width rises > 15% with no relF1@2 gain.
evidence: R (abstract): 2D/3D retinal and coronary data, better overlap than other losses and better connectivity. Exact numbers not read (S2 snippets rate-limited).
prior_overlap: Partial. Soft clDice (Dice-based) failed and Skeleton Recall (recall only) widened predictions. CE-based skeleton terms with a predicted-skeleton precision term are untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack class only, weight 0.25. The predicted-skeleton term penalises thin false lines (E1 scuff streaks, gridline confusions), which should counter the widening seen with Skeleton Recall. Follow the released code; a reviewer flagged sign errors in the paper equations.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + clCE (w 0.25) vs PF, 5 seeds. Kill if crack IoU < PF - 0.012 or predicted width rises > 15% with no relF1@2 gain. Run only if SCNP and TRACE fail.

title: Automatic Crack Segmentation in Electroluminescence Images of Solar Modules and Maximum Inactive Area Prediction
mechanism: After segmenting cracks and busbars, compute the worst-case inactive area: cell regions that cracks cut off from every busbar (a circuit prior on where inactive can occur).
adaptation: From house/PF predictions of crack + ribbons + border, close crack gaps, then mark cell components not connected to any ribbon as 'isolatable'. Use as a post-hoc gate on inactive (suppress outside, lower threshold inside) and, if it helps, as input to a small second-stage inactive head. Fits E: 99% of inactive regions touch a crack. Half-cut E1 ribbon geometry handled natively.
min_experiment: Step 1, no training: apply the gate to existing PF 5-seed ensemble predictions on val and the module-grouped 5-fold CV roots; metric inactive IoU/precision/recall; kill if CV inactive IoU gain < +0.02; read E1 inactive IoU once at the end. Step 2: second-stage head with the isolatable map as input vs PF baseline, same kill line on top of step 1.
evidence: R: UNet on 1,272 train / 206 val / 359 test cells, test F1 0.875, IoU 0.782 for crack lines, cross cracks, busbars, dark areas; isolated-area algorithm given, no accuracy figure for it in the abstract.
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF lists refinement networks and physics priors as never tried; no circuit-consistency rule on inactive was tested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Post-evaluation layer on our crack + ribbon/busbar predictions; compare predicted isolated area with labelled inactive fraction per cell on test and E1 to define power-loss bands.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Zero training: run on existing predictions; Spearman correlation of isolated area vs labelled inactive fraction; keep as a severity metric if rho > 0.6.

alt_notes.adaptation: Severity output for the benchmark: per-cell potential inactive fraction from predicted crack + busbar masks, reported next to measured inactive fraction; also the region generator for the crack-bounded inactive prior.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Same arm as the PV-Vision inactive prior (post-processing, CV inactive IoU, kill < +0.02); for the benchmark, report correlation of potential vs labelled inactive fraction on CV.

title: FMS2: Unified Flow Matching for Segmentation and Synthesis of Thin Structures
mechanism: SynFlow renders pixel-aligned image-mask pairs with multi-scale mask injection, Lite-SPADE GroupNorm and a boundary-gating module, driven by a mask generator that controls sparsity, width and branching; SegFlow casts segmentation as image-to-mask flow transport.
adaptation: Use SynFlow blocks inside the row-1 renderer; sample crack widths per source (ARTS 1.5, CFVS/CSIR 1.75, BMRK 3.0, SDLE 3.25 px) so synthetic labels follow each source's convention; SegFlow is a thin-structure method for the benchmark suite (outside D06 scope).
min_experiment: Arm: renderer with LSGN + boundary gate + width-controlled masks. Baseline: plain mask-concat renderer at matched steps. Metric: house-ensemble crack IoU on rendered pairs (mask adherence), then E1 relF1@2 of PF trained with each. Kill: adherence gain < 0.05 IoU.
evidence: R: 0.25 of real labels + SynFlow pairs largely closes the gap to full labels on CRACK500, CrackTree260, CrackLS315; cross-domain IoU +0.11 average; SegFlow mIoU 0.511 -> 0.599 over best baseline on 5 crack/vessel sets; 256 px, about 400 train crops; SynFlow 150k iterations on 2 A100.
prior_overlap: None.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack-only binary SegFlow head on our encoder (2.96M-param model in paper); later the synthesis module for half-cut / scuff-like EL pairs.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm = SegFlow crack head; baseline = PF; 3 seeds first; metrics crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if IoU below PF by > 0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack-only binary SegFlow head conditioned on house encoder features; or use the synthesis half to make crack training images from E1-like half-cut backgrounds.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm SegFlow crack head vs PF on cv5v2 2 seeds; metric relF1@2 and components found; kill if relF1@2 +<0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Put a SegFlow crack head on our encoder. Train SynFlow on the 478 cells to render cracks on EL backgrounds, varying width to match each source's labelling convention, and add the pairs to training.
alt_notes.min_experiment: SegFlow crack head vs house, 2 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2 and components found. Kill if below house. The SynFlow arm runs only if SegFlow passes.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack-only SegFlow head on the house encoder, ODE integration 10-20 steps; SynFlow overlaps with the generative-data direction.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house encoder + SegFlow crack head, 3 seeds screen then 5; baseline house. Metric crack relF1@2, components found, E1 relF1@2. Kill: relF1@2 gain < 0.015.

alt_notes.adaptation: Bold use as a refiner: start the flow at house logits instead of noise (coarse-to-fine transport), condition on 1-ch EL, crack and inactive channels only, 4 to 8 Euler steps, trained on OOF predictions. Also a standalone thin-structure baseline for the benchmark at 512 px.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: flow-matching refiner on house ensemble output. Baseline: house ensemble, and rNCA if it passes. Metrics: relR@2 at relP@2>=0.93, component recall, crack IoU. Kill: relR@2 < +0.01 or no gain over rNCA.

title: Generalizing Deep Learning for Medical Image Segmentation to Unseen Domains via Deep Stacked Transformation (BigAug)
mechanism: Nine stacked random transforms (blur, sharpen, noise, brightness, contrast, gamma, elastic, rotation, scale) on a single source simulate unseen-domain shift.
evidence: Trained on 10 to 32 volumes: unseen-domain Dice drop 11% vs 39% with conventional augmentation and 25% with CycleGAN DA; with 465 volumes it matches in-domain models.
adaptation: Widen the label-safe policy: blur sigma <= 0.7 px, sharpen, Gaussian noise, gamma 0.7 to 1.5, scale 0.85 to 1.15 with nearest-neighbour labels, small elastic. No large blur (it would erase 1 px cracks).
min_experiment: PF+BigAug-lite vs PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU; guard test crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 or test crack IoU drop > 0.01.
prior_overlap: None: only flips, rot90 and brightness/contrast were ever used.

title: Robust T-Loss for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Negative log-likelihood of a Student-t on the per-pixel residual. A learnable degrees-of-freedom parameter sets how far large residuals (likely label errors) are down-weighted.
adaptation: Drop-in on the crack channel (one-vs-rest), replacing or adding to CE + Dice, with nu learnt per class. Keep CE for the 22 structural classes. Check that it does not down-weight genuine low-contrast cracks (7% of components).
min_experiment: Arm: house with T-Loss on crack, a 2-seed screen, then 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, components found. Kill if both crack IoU and relF1@2 show no detectable difference after 5 v 5.
evidence: R (abstract): beats traditional losses on Dice for ISIC skin lesions and the Shenzhen lung set under simulated mask noise. Blobby targets, not thin ones.
prior_overlap: none. Robust-loss families are not in section 5; offset-tolerant CE and Dice variants are different mechanisms.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace CE on crack and inactive with T-Loss (separate learnable nu per class), keep soft Dice.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with T-Loss, 3 seeds on 5-fold CV. Baseline: house folds. Metric: fold-mean crack IoU. Promote if >= +0.01. About 15 GPU-h.

title: Accurate Industrial Anomaly Detection and Localization Using Weakly-Supervised Residual Transformers (WeakREST)
mechanism: Residual between each test patch feature and its nearest normal patch feature (PosFAR) is fed to a supervised Swin segmenter; works with pixel, box or image labels.
adaptation: Memory banks from house-clean pool cells per source x layout (mono, multi, multi half-cut from 1,152 pool half-cells). Features from house ResNet-34 layer1/layer2 (stride 4/8) so residuals align with U-Net++ skips; residual 1x1-projected to 16 ch and added to decoder at 1/4 and 1/8. 24-class labels unchanged. Half-cut banks make scuff 'normal' in the residual, so the prior targets cracks on E1.
evidence: R: MVTec AD supervised AP 87.6 (prior best 86.0); box-only labels AP 87.1; also MVTec 3D, KSDD2, Real-IAD. No thin-label evidence.
min_experiment: Offline: fraction of crack components >=20 px missed by PF ensemble (p<0.001) that fall in top 1% residual norm on F51 + CV val; kill if <30%. Then arm PF + residual injection vs PF, 5 seeds, module-grouped 5-fold CV then E1 once. Metrics: CV crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2 and recall in 20 scuff half-cut cells. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 and CV inactive gain < +0.02, or CV crack IoU drop > 0.01. Extra arm: bank without half-cells.
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF section 5 lists anomaly-detection priors as never tried; pool feature learning (MIM, DDeP) is a different mechanism.

title: Automated Detection of Label Errors in Semantic Segmentation Datasets via Deep Learning and Uncertainty Quantification
mechanism: Component-level uncertainty meta-classifier flags predicted connected components without labels (missing labels) and unsupported labels.
adaptation: Component features for tiny crack segments: size, mean p(crack), ridge contrast, distance to nearest label, source, inactive adjacency; train meta-classifier on val, apply out-of-fold on train to find under-annotated crack segments that 1-IoU confuses with jitter.
min_experiment: Arm: ignore (or soft 0.5) flagged unlabelled crack components in train. Baseline: house, 5 seeds. Metric: crack relR@2, components >= 20 px found, strict IoU. Kill: flagged-set precision < 30% on an automatic ridge-darkness check, or no relR@2 gain.
evidence: R: detects most dropped labels on Cityscapes and CARLA while controlling false detections; collection of real label errors released.
prior_overlap: none (no label-error detection run in BRIEF section 5).

alt_notes.adaptation: Run on out-of-fold predictions over train+val and the test set to rank suspected crack/inactive label errors per source; defines the 'clean' test subset objectively for the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: label-error ranking; relabel nothing, drop top-ranked cells' crack loss. Baseline: house. Metric: crack IoU; for benchmark, per-source estimated label error rate. Kill (model use) if crack IoU < house + 0.008.

alt_notes.adaptation: Run with the existing ensemble on train, val and the benchmark test set to rank missing / spurious crack and inactive components; output an audit list, auto-flag cells like CSIR_00070_r8_c4 for a clean benchmark subset.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: audit list on train + val; drop or ignore top-ranked components and retrain house, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: crack IoU and recall of the 24 audit-flagged cells among the top-50 ranked. Kill: fewer than 10 of 24 flagged cells recovered.

alt_notes.adaptation: Score every train crack and inactive component with out-of-fold models and drop or down-weight the flagged ones, with no manual labelling. For the benchmark, audit the test and E1 labels in a later phase and publish clean subsets with the reasons.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: drop the top 5% error-scored train crack components, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if there is no detectable difference. The benchmark audit is separate.

title: Does Your ViT Still Need U-Net for Segmentation? (EoSeg)
mechanism: Encoder-only query segmenter for small medical sets: queries refined through the last 3 DINOv2-L blocks, a learned gate fuses per-block predictions, 2 queries per class.
adaptation: Use as the small-data recipe for the EoMT arm: 2 queries per class (48), block-fusion gate, AdamW 5e-4 with layer decay, about 12k steps at batch 8 on 478 cells; add 1024 input and full-res head for cracks; judge on inactive and E1, not strict crack IoU.
min_experiment: Fold into EoMT arm as variant: EoMT-L vs EoMT-L + EoSeg block fusion + 2 queries/class, 5-fold CV; metric inactive IoU and mIoU_rob; kill the variant if it does not beat plain EoMT by > 0.01 mIoU_rob fold-paired.
evidence: R: Synapse (18 train volumes) 85.50 DSC vs TransUNet 77.48, SwinUNet 79.13; ablation 82.40 linear head -> 83.70 query masks -> 84.34 multi-level -> 84.78 fusion -> 85.50 two queries per class; DINOv2-L 81.86 vs DINOv3-L 81.60; GlaS Dice 93.27 (5-fold). No nnU-Net comparison. Code stated as github.com/Retinal-Research/EoSeg (not opened).
prior_overlap: none

title: Learning to Look Closer: A New Instance-Wise Loss for Small Cerebral Lesion Segmentation (CC-DiceCE)
mechanism: DiceCE computed per connected-component region (CC-Metrics), so each small object contributes its own term instead of being swamped by large ones.
adaptation: Per-component Dice + CE on crack (76-88% of crack components are < 20 px); optionally inactive. Targets the components-found metric and E1 crack recall.
min_experiment: Arm CE+Dice+CC-DiceCE(crack) vs SUP100, 5 v 5. Metric components >= 20 px found, crack IoU, relP@2; E1 relF1@2 secondary. Kill if components found < +0.02 or crack IoU drop > 0.012.
evidence: R: nnU-Net multi-dataset study; increases detection recall with minimal to no segmentation loss, dataset-dependent precision trade-off; generally beats blob loss (abstract).
prior_overlap: none (component-wise losses listed as untested in BRIEF section 5)

alt_notes.adaptation: Per-component Dice on crack (76-88% of components < 20 px) and inactive; component regions from the train labels with a 2 px dilation to absorb jitter.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house loss + CC-DiceCE on crack, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Metric components >= 20 px found, crack IoU, E1 recall. Kill: components found < +0.02 or crack IoU drop > 0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Equal to BiCC alpha = 0 on merged crack and inactive instances; run as that arm. Recall bias suits E1; watch precision on test.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Run as BiCC alpha = 0 arm (see BiCC). Kill: component F1 below house or relP@2 drop > 0.03.

title: SADL: A Size-Adaptive Decision Layer for Chronic Stroke Lesion Segmentation in ISLES 2026
mechanism: A decision layer fitted on out-of-fold predictions: per-size-bucket thresholds, pruning components by size and peak probability, and a never-empty rescue.
adaptation: Hysteresis-like crack rule: keep a weak component if its peak probability passes its size-bucket threshold; rescue rule for cells where the model outputs nothing (E1 half-cut cells). Fit on CV folds or val + F51 only.
min_experiment: Arm: SADL-style layer on 5-seed ensemble maps. Baseline: ensemble at argmax and with logit bias. Metric: test / E1 relF1@2 and component recall < 20 px. Kill: no gain >= 0.005 relF1@2 on both sets.
evidence: Site-disjoint 91-case holdout: Dice 0.732, lesion F1 0.746, PR-AUC 0.843; bootstrap p = 0.024 vs a single member; gain largest for small lesions.
prior_overlap: Overlaps logit bias and per-module thresholds only in spirit; component-level peak-prob pruning and rescue untested.

title: TRACE: Topology-Aware Reconnection via Prediction-Adaptive Connectivity Enforcement for Thin-Structure Segmentation
mechanism: For each skeleton point whose removal splits the local target skeleton, find the easiest valid reconnection under the current prediction among nearby target pixels and supervise its bottleneck pixel with a centred logit margin, so supervision follows the prediction rather than a fixed centreline.
adaptation: Implement in-house (3x3 local search, about 150 lines). As published the candidates are only label pixels, so on 1 to 2 px labels it stays on the drawn line; widen the candidate support to the crack label dilated by 1 px for this term only so the reconnection can follow the true dark ridge. Crack class only, weight 0.1 or 0.3 chosen on val.
