min_experiment: PF + TRACE (dilated support) vs PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: relF1@2, components >= 20 px found, crack IoU, predicted width. Kill if relF1@2 gain < 0.01 or predicted width rises > 15%.
evidence: R: nnU-Net style training, 6 benchmarks. DeepCrack (270 train, CS2-Net backbone): Dice 82.78 to 85.20, beta error 6.16 to 3.69, clDice 89.03 to 91.10; SkelRecall 84.26 / 4.74; clDice 84.58 / 5.06. Stacks with SCNP on DRIVE and DSCA. Low memory and time overhead vs clDice / Betti matching.
prior_overlap: Partial: Skeleton Recall (fixed skeleton recall) and offset-tolerant CE were run; prediction-adaptive bottleneck supervision was not.

alt_notes.adaptation: Suits jittered labels: the model must connect the crack, not sit on the drawn line. In-house: build a graph from each crack component's label skeleton, run a min-cost path in a 3 px band on -log p(crack), and add CE on the bottleneck pixels. Cheap at 512 px with 0.19% crack pixels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + TRACE-style bottleneck CE (crack), 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: component recall (>= 20 px), relF1@2, crack IoU, width. Kill if component recall gain < 0.02 and relF1@2 gain < 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: 2D re-implementation for crack only; addresses why fixed-skeleton losses misbehave under 1-2 px jitter.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm = PF + TRACE crack loss; baseline = PF and PF + Skeleton Recall w 0.1; 5 seeds; metrics components found, E1 relF1@2, IoU. Kill if no gain over Skeleton Recall w 0.1.

title: Efficient unsupervised domain adaptation for crack segmentation with interpretable Fourier-Morphology blending and Uncertainty-guided self-training
mechanism: Fourier low-frequency style transfer plus morphological operators that align crack width/geometry between domains (two parameters), then dual-network uncertainty-guided self-training on target.
adaptation: Morphology half matches our source-dependent label width (ARTS 1.5 px, CSIR 1.75, BMRK 3.0, SDLE 3.25): erode/dilate source labels toward the CSIR convention while swapping low-frequency amplitude from pool half-cells. Test the blending half first; self-training half overlaps SSL nulls.
min_experiment: PF + FDA(pool half-cells) + label width matching to 1.75 px vs PF + FDA, 3 seeds. Kill if E1 crack IoU gain < +0.02 at equal relF1@2.
evidence: R: up to +18.5% F1 over competitive baselines in cross-domain crack segmentation on public and industrial sets (abstract only; full text unavailable).
prior_overlap: Self-training part overlaps BRIEF s5 pseudo-label SSL (n.d. at 100%); Fourier plus label-width alignment untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Target = CSIR half-cell pool (1,152 multi half-cells look like E1); the morphology half can also align label width across sources (BMRK 3.0 / SDLE 3.25 vs ARTS 1.5 px). Run blending without self-training first.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + Fourier-Morphology blending with CSIR half-cell pool as target, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: < +0.03. Add self-training only if it passes.

alt_notes.adaptation: Target = E1-like pool cells (1,152 multi half-cells, CSIR). Fourier-swap labelled cells toward half-cut scuffed pool cells; morph crack label width to the CSIR convention (1.75 px); dual-network self-training with uncertainty masks on the 11.9k pool. Freeze the recipe on F51 / H36 val before scoring E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: Fourier-morphology blending + uncertainty-gated dual-network self-training; baseline PF; 3 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and recall, E1 inactive IoU; CV crack IoU within 0.01. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Morphology step: thin or thicken source crack masks and dark lines to match each source's label width (ARTS 1.5 px to SDLE 3.25 px). Fourier step towards half-cell pool cells. Dual-network self-training on the pool.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Morphology step alone first: house+width-matching vs house, 5 seeds; metric per-source test crack IoU (BMRK, SDLE) and E1 relF1@2. Kill: < +0.01 test crack IoU and < +0.02 E1 relF1@2.

alt_notes.adaptation: Target = unlabelled CSIR half-cell pool (1,152 multi half-cells) as an E1 proxy. Morphology part can also harmonise label width conventions across sources (BMRK 3.0, SDLE 3.25 vs ARTS 1.5 px). Run blending first without self-training.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + FM blending toward CSIR half-cell pool, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, test crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.03. Add self-training only if it passes.

title: Learning Semantic Segmentation from Multiple Datasets with Label Shifts (UniSeg)
mechanism: Class-independent BCE removes gradient conflict between mismatched label spaces; an extra loss exploits cross-dataset class relationships.
evidence: Road scenes: more than +8 IoU on unseen KITTI, 39.4 IoU on WildDash2 zero-shot.
adaptation: Replace softmax CE with per-class BCE in the joint run; encode UCF crack_region as parent of {crack, inactive}. Judge on E1, since R gain is on unseen domains.
min_experiment: Arm: joint UCF+MSS run with per-class BCE, 30k steps, 5 seeds. Baseline: house 5-seed and the softmax joint arm. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and recall. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 and clean-49 crack IoU drops > 0.012. ~15 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: none

title: Striking the Right Balance: Recall Loss for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Weight CE per class by (1 - running recall), interpolating between plain CE and inverse-frequency CE, so under-called classes get more weight only while they are under-called.
adaptation: EMA recall per class across batches (splice absent from most batches of 8). Targets gridline recall 0.33 and splice recall 0. Follow with per-class post-hoc bias to recover precision lost.
min_experiment: Arm: recall-weighted CE + Dice(crack, inactive), 3 seeds, then OOF bias; baseline SUP100 and R2c; metric gridline IoU and mIoU_rob; kill if gridline IoU not above 0.357 (R2c) or mIoU_rob < +0.01.
evidence: R: Synthia, DeepLab-ResNet18: +9% relative mean accuracy with competitive mIoU.
prior_overlap: Partial: Dice on gridline (R2c) already showed recall gain at precision cost (gridline 0.283 -> 0.357, mIoU_rob n.d.). Recall-weighted CE across all classes not tested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Targets gridline (recall 0.33) and splice (never predicted); monitor crack precision.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: recall loss, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Kill: gridline IoU < +0.03 and splice still 0.

alt_notes.adaptation: Targets gridline (recall 0.33) and splice (never predicted) on the 24-class head; crack precision must be checked.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm recall loss + house Dice vs SUP100, 5 v 5. Kill if gridline IoU < +0.03 and splice IoU still 0, or crack IoU < -0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: All 24 classes with EMA recall over batches; aims at gridline (recall 0.33) and splice (never predicted) without fixed inverse-frequency weights that flood FPs.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: recall-weighted CE + house Dice, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: mIoU_rob, gridline / splice / edge_dark IoU, crack IoU. Kill: mIoU_rob < house + 0.005.

title: FDA: Fourier Domain Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation
venue: CVPR 2020 (from memory; the arXiv page lists no venue)
mechanism: Replace the low-frequency Fourier amplitude of a labelled source image with that of an unlabelled target image; the alignment needs no training.
adaptation: Targets: the pool's 1,152 multi half-cells and CSIR cells (E1 is 101 CSIR, 58 half-cut). Small beta 0.005 to 0.02 so only illumination profile and contrast move; masks unchanged. Training time only.
min_experiment: Arm: house + FDA (beta 0.01, p 0.5), 5 seeds. Baseline: house and PF. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU; test crack IoU must not fall by more than 0.01. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.03.
evidence: R: state of the art on synthetic-to-real segmentation benchmarks at the time (abstract). No EL evidence.
prior_overlap: Not closed: section 5 lists UDA-style methods aimed at E1 as open. Inference-time intensity normalisation (fail) is a different mechanism.

alt_notes.adaptation: Target styles from the CSIR half-cell pool; beta 0.01 to 0.05 so finger periodicity is untouched; expected small effect because the E1 gap is mostly content (half-cut, scuff).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + FDA (beta 0.01 / 0.05), 3-seed screen. Baseline: house. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Targets drawn from the CSIR half-cell pool; small beta (0.01 to 0.05) so finger periodicity and crack frequencies stay untouched. S: E1 gap is mostly content (half-cut layout, scuffs), so expect a small effect.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + FDA (beta 0.01 and 0.05), 3-seed screen then 5. Baseline: house. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Targets: 1,152 pool half-cut multi cells and CSIR pool cells (E1 is 101 CSIR); beta 0.005 to 0.02 so only illumination profile and contrast transfer; labels unchanged.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + FDA (beta 0.01, p 0.5); baselines house and PF; 5 seeds; E1 relF1@2 and inactive IoU, test crack IoU drop <= 0.01; kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Beta 0.01 to 0.05; target spectra from pool half-cells and CSIR cells. Cracks are high-frequency so labels stay valid. Handles illumination, vignetting, global contrast; does not model scuff streaks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + FDA (beta 0.01, 0.03) vs PF, 3 seeds. Kill if E1 inactive IoU and crack relF1@2 gains are both < +0.02.

title: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time
mechanism: Average weights of models fine-tuned from one shared init with different hyperparameters; greedy soup chosen on held-out data.
adaptation: Our seeds share only the ImageNet encoder; decoders are random per seed, so fork 5 continuations from one checkpoint at 2k-5k steps (different seeds, aug order, Dice weights), uniform and greedy soup on F51 + val, recompute BN.
min_experiment: Step 0 (free): average 5 existing PF seeds, eval on val (expected collapse). Arm: forked soup (k=4k), 2 replicates. Baseline: same forks as output ensemble and as singles. Metric: crack IoU on CV / clean 49. Kill: soup below mean single of its members.
evidence: R: ImageNet, WILDS and text classification gains without inference cost; no segmentation results.
prior_overlap: none run; a soup of 5 PF seeds was proposed 30 Oct and not run

title: Robust fine-tuning of zero-shot models (WiSE-FT)
mechanism: Linearly interpolate pretrained and fine-tuned weights; large OOD gains at small or no ID cost.
adaptation: Post hoc, zero training: interpolate encoder only between ImageNet and fine-tuned weights (a in 0.3..0.9), keep the decoder, recompute BN stats on train. Also interpolate house and PF checkpoints of the same seed.
evidence: +4 to 6 pp under distribution shift on ImageNet shifts, +2 to 23 pp on six other shifts, +0.8 to 3.3 pp on seven transfer datasets (CLIP classification).
min_experiment: Existing checkpoints house s5-9, PF s5-9: pick a on val relF1@2, then read E1 at an opening. Kill if no a beats both endpoints by +0.005 val relF1@2.
prior_overlap: none. Weight interpolation never tested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Post hoc on existing checkpoints: encoder theta = (1-a) ImageNet + a fine-tuned, a in 0.3 to 0.9, decoder kept, BN recomputed on train; also house-to-PF interpolation of the same seed and LiNeS (arxiv:2410.17146) depth scaling. Choose a on val/CV only.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: interpolated house s5-9 and PF s5-9. Baseline: the endpoints. Metric: val relF1@2 and F51 crack AP, then E1 at an opening. Kill: no coefficient beats both endpoints on val by +0.005 relF1@2.

title: Soft-CP: A Credible and Effective Data Augmentation for Semantic Segmentation of Medical Lesions
mechanism: Copy-paste of lesions with an object-blend that keeps edge information, applied offline at a 3:1 real to synthetic ratio.
evidence: Abstract: +26.5% DSC with 10% of the data and +10.2% DSC with all data on KiTS19 and other modalities. Beats other lesion-synthesis methods on KiTS19.
adaptation: Build a library of the inactive regions from the 42 train cells, each cut together with the crack pixels that bound it. Paste onto labelled train cells of the same source and cell type, at a spot where the region touches the cell edge or a crack-free busbar side. Match intensity to the per-source inactive/active ratio and use a soft 3 px edge. The target cell keeps its full labels and the pasted region overrides them. Inactive is blobby and well labelled, so pastes avoid the label-jitter problem that 1.75 px crack pastes have.
min_experiment: PF+inactive copy-paste vs PF, 5 seeds plus 5-fold CV. Metrics: CV inactive IoU, false inactive pixels on crack-only cells, test crack IoU as a guard. Kill if CV inactive gain < +0.02 or if inactive false positives on the 167 crack-only train-fold cells rise by more than 50%.
prior_overlap: none. CP100 pasted only crack, onto unlabelled pool cells; inactive copy-paste has never been run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Inactive library from the 42 train cells, each cut with its bounding crack; paste onto labelled cells of the same source/cell type where the region meets a cell edge or busbar; intensity matched by per-source inactive/active ratio; 3 px soft edge. TumorCP (arxiv:2107.09843, code github.com/YaoZhang93/TumorCP) is the same family.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+ICP vs PF, module-grouped CV; CV inactive IoU, false inactive px on crack-only cells, crack IoU guard. Kill: CV inactive < +0.02 or false inactive px up > 50%. Pre-check 32 composites.

title: CarveMix: A simple data augmentation method for brain lesion segmentation
mechanism: Carve an ROI around a lesion with random context margin from one labelled image and place it at the same coordinates in another labelled image, labels following, with harmonisation across sources.
adaptation: Same-location transfer works because cells of one type share geometry. ROI = crack or inactive component dilated by 8 to 40 px, source and target same source and cell type, both labelled; seam lies in labelled background, so seams are not tied to defects.
min_experiment: PF+CVM vs PF, 5 seeds + module-grouped CV; CV inactive IoU, test crack IoU, CP100 decoy rate. Kill: CV inactive < +0.02 and crack IoU < +0.012, or decoy rate > 2x PF.
evidence: Improves brain lesion Dice on several datasets (abstract); in Cut to the Mix +2.5 macro Dice on 20 CT volumes.
prior_overlap: CP100 pasted crack masks only (no context) onto unlabelled pool cells at random places; same-location ROI transfer between labelled cells is untested.

title: Deep Nets with Subsampling Layers Unwittingly Discard Useful Activations at Test-Time
mechanism: Stride-2 layers drop 3 of 4 phases; search and aggregate the discarded activations at test time.
adaptation: A 1-2 px crack falls on one stride phase in the RN34 stem and maxpool; cheap version is 1 px shift TTA (0,1),(1,0),(1,1) with exact un-shift; full version is their phase search on stem and maxpool.
min_experiment: Arm: shift/phase TTA on 5 singles. Baseline: D4 TTA arm. Metric: crack IoU, components >= 20 px. Kill: < +0.003 over D4 TTA.
evidence: R: consistent test-time gains for classification and semantic segmentation over nine architectures, complementary to standard TTA.
prior_overlap: none

title: IterNet: Retinal Image Segmentation Utilizing Structural Redundancy in Vessel Networks
mechanism: A shared-weight mini-UNet is applied repeatedly to the segmentation output itself (with skip connections from earlier iterations), with supervision at each iteration, so the network learns to complete broken thin structures.
evidence: R: DRIVE AUC 0.9816, CHASE-DB1 0.9851, STARE 0.9881; trained from 10 to 20 labelled images, no pretraining.
adaptation: Bolt 3 shared-weight mini-UNets onto the U-Net++ full-resolution output; each takes [1-ch EL, softmax of crack / inactive / gridline / splice, last decoder features]; house loss (CE + Dice on crack and inactive) on every iteration; end to end, no OOF data needed. Gridline (recall 0.33) is a periodic thin line and is a second target.
min_experiment: Arm: U-Net++ + 3-iteration IterNet head, 5 seeds, 20k steps. Baseline: house 5-seed (and PF variant if adopted). Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, gridline IoU and recall, mIoU_rob. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012 and relF1@2 < +0.01 and gridline IoU < +0.03.
prior_overlap: none. No iterative or stacked head was run; architecture changes tried were ResNet-50 encoder and 2x input only.

alt_notes.adaptation: Append 3 weight-shared mini-U-Nets after U-Net++ that read the softmax output (and last decoder features); loss CE + crack/inactive Dice at each stage; same label-safe augmentation, 20k steps; test on house and PF fine-tunes.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: U-Net++ + 3 IterNet stages, 5 seeds. Baseline: house and PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: clean-49 and 5-fold CV crack IoU, relF1@2, components found, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012 and no relF1@2 gain.

title: Frangi-Net: A Neural Network Approach to Vessel Segmentation
mechanism: The multi-scale Frangi vesselness filter rewritten as a network with preset weights, so it starts as Frangi and can then be trained end to end.
adaptation: Dark-ridge variant with sigmas 0.7 to 2.5 px, matched to the 4 px FWHM crack line. Used as a trainable input branch concatenated to the raw channel before the ResNet-34 stem.
min_experiment: Arm: house with [raw, learnable dark-ridge Frangi], 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: test relF1@2, E1 crack recall. Kill: E1 recall < +0.03 and relF1@2 < +0.01.
evidence: R: 45 high-resolution fundus images; F1 up to +17% after fine-tuning compared with the fixed filter.
prior_overlap: none in BRIEF section 5. D12 notes that HarmonySeg found vesselness at the input gave no notable gain on 3D hepatic vessels (other domain).

alt_notes.adaptation: Dark-ridge variant, sigma 0.7 to 2.5 px to match the 4 px FWHM crack line; extra input channel or parallel stem branch trained jointly.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: 2-channel [raw, learnable dark-ridge Frangi]; baseline house; 5 seeds; relF1@2, E1 crack recall; kill if E1 recall < +0.03 and test relF1@2 < +0.01.

title: Instance Awareness of Multi-class Semantic Segmentation Loss Functions
mechanism: One-vs-rest extension of blob / CC losses so each class and each instance contributes equally, with inverse-size weighting confined inside each component.
adaptation: Apply the multi-class CC loss over crack, inactive, splice, gridline, edge_dark, material so the rare and weak classes get equal signal on 478 cells.
min_experiment: Arm house + multi-class CC loss vs SUP100, 5 v 5. Metric mIoU_rob, inactive IoU, crack IoU. Kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01 and inactive < +0.03, or crack IoU < -0.012.
evidence: R: BraTS-METS 2025, 260 test cases: foreground Dice 0.64 vs 0.59 baseline; inverse-size weighting raises rare-class Dice to 0.44 at a detection cost.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply jointly to rare and weak classes (crack, inactive, splice, gridline, edge_dark, material) so each instance gets equal signal.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house loss + multi-class CC loss, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Metric mIoU_rob, inactive IoU, crack IoU. Kill: mIoU_rob < +0.01 and inactive IoU < +0.03, crack not worse than -0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply to small-component defect classes (crack, inactive, gridline, splice, edge_dark, material) only; structural classes keep CE.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + multi-class CC loss over 6 defect classes, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: mIoU_rob, gridline and splice IoU, crack IoU. Kill: mIoU_rob < house + 0.005 or crack IoU drop > 0.012.

title: Self-Correction for Human Parsing
mechanism: Cyclic learning rate; at each cycle end, model weights are averaged into a running average and labels are replaced by a running average of label and model prediction, so model and labels improve together on ambiguous boundaries.
adaptation: All 24 classes: gridline (recall 0.33), splice (never predicted), edge_dark, material have boundary and missing-label noise. Five cosine cycles of 4k steps inside the 20k budget; label update only within 2 px of crack labels and on class boundaries so rare inactive is not erased. The weight averaging doubles as an EMA/SWA test.
min_experiment: Arm: 5-cycle self-correction, 5 seeds; baseline: house. Metrics: mIoU_rob, gridline IoU, crack relF1@2. Kill if mIoU_rob gain < 0.01 and gridline gain < 0.03.
evidence: R: human parsing benchmarks (LIP etc.); numbers not read here (abstract-level).
prior_overlap: partial: Mean Teacher pseudo-labels on unlabelled pools were run, but never correction of the labelled set's own labels; EMA/SWA never varied (BRIEF section 5).

title: Domain generalization for retinal vessel segmentation via Hessian-based vector field
mechanism: Represent thin vessels by the scaled minor eigenvector field of the Hessian, which is stable across imaging styles, plus a structure-preserving style augmentation.
adaptation: Bold bet for E1: add multi-scale dark-ridge Hessian eigenvector field channels (sigma 0.7 to 2.5 px) to the raw image; contrast invariance should help where 70% of E1 crack pixels get p < 0.001. Scuffs are also ridge-like but wider, so restrict sigma.
min_experiment: Arm: 3-channel [raw, vx, vy]; baseline house; 5 seeds; E1 crack recall and relF1@2; kill if E1 recall < +0.03. Run after the cheaper Frangi channel.
evidence: R (WebSearch summary, paper not read): train on fundus, test on OCT-A; extends MIDL 2022 Vector Field Transformer.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Feed multi-scale Hessian orientation and eigenvalue channels to the house CNN (not their ViT) and add strong intensity-style augmentation; aimed at E1 (CSIR half-cut, scuff).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + Hessian channels + style aug, 5 seeds; baseline PF. Metric E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, test crack IoU guard. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03.

title: U-Bench: A Comprehensive Understanding of U-Net through 100-Variant Benchmarking
mechanism: One protocol for 100 U-Net variants on 28 2D datasets, with paired t-tests against U-Net, a zero-shot axis (train on one dataset, test on an unseen same-modality dataset) and an accuracy-efficiency U-Score.
adaptation: Use the harness and model zoo to run 10 to 15 variants at 512 px, 1 channel, on our module-grouped folds. Test-49 is the in-domain axis and E1 the zero-shot axis. FLOPs/FPS go in as the deployment axis for WattCycle.
min_experiment: U-Net, Swin-UMamba, RWKV-UNet, MEGANet, UTANet, U-KAN and VM-UNet under one recipe, one seed per fold; rank by test crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2 against the house model. Kill for the score line: no variant beats the house model on E1 relF1@2 by more than 0.03.
evidence: R: over 80% of variants not significantly better than U-Net in-domain; average in-domain top-1 gain 1 to 2% IoU, zero-shot more than 3% and more often significant; fundus/nuclei (thin, local) stagnate; RWKV-UNet top-1 IoU in-domain and zero-shot, Swin-UMamba #3 zero-shot; Mamba family weaker on fine detail; blurry boundaries are the main difficulty factor.
prior_overlap: none (BRIEF: no transformer or Mamba segmenter tried)

alt_notes.adaptation: Template for the EL benchmark: paired significance tests across seeds and folds, a zero-shot column (E1 and F51), an efficiency column; pick 5-8 suite members from its families via its 2D trainers.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark design, not a score arm: run U-Bench's statistical test on existing house v PF seed results; adopt if it reproduces the BRIEF minimum detectable difference (~0.012 crack IoU).

title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks
mechanism: Randomise all sources of variation (data split, init, order, augmentation, hyperparameters) in every run; this cheap estimator approaches the ideal one (51x less compute) and comparisons use P(A>B).
adaptation: Each benchmark run draws a fresh grouped split and seed; methods compared by P(A>B) over paired runs instead of mean of 5 seeds on one fixed split.
min_experiment: Arm: 10 runs per method with new split+seed. Baseline: 10 seed-only runs on fixed split. Metric: share of delta variance from data split vs seed. Kill: split variance < 25% of seed variance means seed-only protocol is enough.
evidence: R: data sampling, init and hyperparameter choice all mark results; error rates of detecting improvements studied on five deep-learning tasks.
prior_overlap: none; current protocol is seed-only on a fixed split.

title: Revisiting Evaluation Metrics for Semantic Segmentation: Optimization and Evaluation of Fine-grained Intersection over Union
mechanism: Per-image and per-class-per-image mIoU plus worst-case (lowest k%) variants reduce bias to large objects and expose failure cases.
adaptation: Report per-cell crack and inactive IoU means and worst-10% next to dataset-level IoU so the 3 cells with 59% of inactive pixels cannot decide inactive; worst-case crack metric matches the 'almost all cracks' goal; mIoU over 24 classes computed per image ignores classes absent in a cell.
min_experiment: Arm: per-cell mean and worst-10% IoU on OOF predictions of house vs PF. Baseline: dataset-level IoU. Metric: paired-delta SE/|delta|. Kill: neither cuts that ratio by >= 20%.
evidence: R: 15 networks on 12 natural and aerial datasets; fine-grained mIoUs reduce large-object bias; architecture and loss choices change fine-grained ranking.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark: report pooled IoU plus per-cell IoU and worst-k cells per source; loss arm JML per-image vs per-batch.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training: rescore val predictions of SUP100, PF, FINAL with per-cell and worst-k IoU; keep as secondary benchmark metrics if they reorder models or narrow CIs.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark: report pooled IoU plus per-cell IoU and worst-k cells per source; loss arm JML per-image vs per-batch.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training: rescore existing val predictions of SUP100, PF and FINAL with fine-grained and worst-case IoU; adopt as benchmark secondaries if model ranking changes or CIs narrow.

title: Swin-UMamba: Mamba-Based UNet with ImageNet-Based Pretraining
mechanism: An ImageNet-pretrained VMamba (visual state space) encoder with a U-Net decoder inside the nnU-Net pipeline. Pretraining is what makes the Mamba U-Net beat CNN, ViT and from-scratch Mamba models.
adaptation: Average the 3-channel stem weights to 1 channel; 512 px (16 x 16 at the deepest stage). Use the PF fine-tune (frozen encoder 1k steps, then 0.1x lr), because the house fine-tune erases pretrained layers. Aim at E1, where half-cut layout and scuff streaks need cell-scale context. Needs the mamba-ssm CUDA build on cv02.
min_experiment: Swin-UMamba PF against house PF, 3 seeds each, 20k steps; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU, with test-49 crack IoU as a guard. Kill: under +0.03 E1 relF1@2, or test crack IoU worse by more than 0.01.
evidence: R: beats U-Mamba_Enc by 2.72% on average over AbdomenMRI, Endoscopy and Microscopy (2D). In U-Bench it ranks #3 zero-shot and #5 in-domain IoU over 28 2D datasets. In GP-VMxSMA it is on par with general-purpose models.
prior_overlap: The foundation-encoder screens (DINOv3/ConvNeXt linear probes, one 4k-step ConvNeXt-T PF fine-tune) did not test a pretrained SSM encoder under a full schedule, so this is open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Gray replicated to 3 channels, 512 px, 24 classes, label-safe aug, PF-style schedule (frozen encoder 1k steps, 0.1x lr) so the pretraining is not erased as in the house fine-tune.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Swin-UMamba (PF) v its scratch trainer v house PF, 5 folds. Metric: E1 relF1@2 and inactive IoU, CV crack relF1@2. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 over house PF.

title: MSPS: Monocrystalline Silicon Photovoltaic Cell Defect Segmentation Dataset
mechanism: 1,500 production-line mono EL cells (640x590, 1,000 train / 500 test) with pixel masks for crack, busbar break and black spot, each annotated by two experts and adjudicated by a third.
adaptation: Joint training with a separate output head per dataset (MSPS 4-class head, BenchmarkEL 24-class head) on a shared U-Net++ encoder-decoder, so label conventions never mix; rescale MSPS so crack line width in px matches ours (about 1.75 px), 1-channel input as is. Its double annotation also gives an inter-annotator reference for the benchmark's tolerant crack metric.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + MSPS joint (own head, 1:1 batch mix). Baseline: PF, 5 v 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 and recall, test crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03 or test crack IoU drops > 0.012.
evidence: R: dataset record only; associated paper (DACN) not found, no model numbers seen.
prior_overlap: Partial: +107 E-SCDD cells n.d. and UCF-EL pretraining erased by fine-tune. Joint multi-dataset training with separate heads, and a new source, are untested.

title: CSWinUNETR: Segmentation of Thin Anatomical Structures in Medical Images
mechanism: Thin-structure backbone with cross-shaped stripe self-attention and cyclic shift for long principal-axis context, detail-enhanced multi-scale attention, and sparse-control dynamic snake convolution.
adaptation: 2D variant, 1-channel input, 512 px, house CE+Dice loss and schedule, trained from scratch on 478 cells. Stripe attention suits busbar-aligned and diagonal cracks and long scuff streaks on E1.
min_experiment: Arm: 2D CSWinUNETR, 20k and 40k steps, 5 seeds. Baseline: house U-Net++ R34. Metrics: test crack IoU, relF1@2, mIoU_rob, gridline IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill: 2-seed mean crack IoU or mIoU_rob more than 0.02 below house.
evidence: R: FIVES (500 train) Dice 90.71 vs nnUNetv2 89.26; FFHQ-Wrinkle (800 train, thin low-contrast lines) Dice 64.75 vs 63.27; TopCoW 3D clDice gains; 31M params (2D); Dice+CE only, no topology loss; paired t-test with BH correction.
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF section 5 lists transformer segmenters as never tried.

title: Region Rebalance for Long-Tailed Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Pool pixel features per class per image into region features and train an auxiliary rebalanced region classifier; region-level counts are far less imbalanced than pixel counts.
adaptation: Region imbalance in our data is mild (splice 53/478 cells) while pixel imbalance is extreme, matching the premise. Pool full-res U-Net++ decoder features per class per cell; auxiliary balanced linear classifier; drop at test. About 50 lines.
min_experiment: Arm: RR auxiliary branch weight 0.5, 3 seeds; baseline SUP100 (or best loss/sampling arm); metric mIoU_rob and splice/edge_dark IoU; kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01.
evidence: R: consistent gains on ADE20K and COCO-Stuff; BEiT +0.7 mIoU on ADE20K val.
prior_overlap: none

title: CoANet: Connectivity Attention Network for Road Extraction From Satellite Imagery
mechanism: Decoder built from strip convolutions in 4 directions (horizontal, vertical, two diagonals) plus a connectivity attention module predicting 8-neighbour links, for long thin occluded roads.
adaptation: Replace U-Net++ decoder blocks with 4-direction strip-conv blocks. EL cells are axis-aligned, so h/v strips match fingers (gridline), busbars, ribbons, splice, borders; diagonals serve cracks.
min_experiment: Arm: strip-conv decoder, 5 seeds; baseline house. Metrics: gridline IoU, splice IoU, mIoU_rob, crack relF1@2. Kill: gridline IoU gain < 0.03 and mIoU_rob gain < 0.005.
evidence: Improved road connectivity on DeepGlobe and SpaceNet (abstract; numbers not read; snippet search rate-limited).
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Add strip blocks to the U-Net++ decoder for gridline, splice and crack. Add an auxiliary 8-channel connectivity target derived from the crack and gridline masks. Connectivity of a 1-2 px line is unchanged by a 1 px shift.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Strip blocks + connectivity head vs house, 5 seeds. Metrics: gridline IoU (CV), crack components found, crack relF1@2. Kill if gridline gains < 0.03 and crack is flat.

title: Convolution Meets LoRA: Parameter Efficient Finetuning for Segment Anything Model
mechanism: LoRA bottleneck with lightweight convolution experts gated per scale (MoE), injecting a local image prior into SAM's plain ViT.
adaptation: Conv-LoRA rank 8-32 in SAM ViT-B/L at 1024, prompt-free multi-class decoder; local conv prior targets the 16 px patch blind spot for 2 px cracks.
evidence: R: beats LoRA and adapters across medical, natural, agriculture, remote sensing segmentation (ICLR 2024).
min_experiment: Conv-LoRA vs plain LoRA on SAM ViT-L @1024, 3 seeds; metric crack IoU and recall on components < 20 px; kill if gain over LoRA < 0.012 crack IoU.
prior_overlap: none; LoRA/adapters listed as not closed.

alt_notes.adaptation: Same harness as TopoLoRA-SAM arm; swap LoRA for Conv-LoRA; local prior is what 1-2 px cracks on a 4 px dark line need.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Conv-LoRA SAM vs LoRA SAM vs house PF, 5-fold CV; default kill line.

title: Disentangling Sampling from Training Budget in Class-Imbalanced CT Body Composition Segmentation
mechanism: Episodic (class-balanced) batch construction in fully supervised segmentation, with the warning that sampling gains are often a training-iteration confound.
adaptation: Batch of 8: force at least one cell with inactive and one with splice/edge_dark/material, rest random; keep 20k steps. Benchmark rule: report iteration budgets when comparing samplers.
min_experiment: Arm: episodic batches, 5 seeds, 20k steps; baseline SUP100; metric mIoU_rob and inactive IoU; kill if both n.d. Run only if RCS arm is unclear.
evidence: R: 210 CT scans, 9 tissues: full data Dice 0.882 vs 0.878 (equal); low data 0.787 vs 0.758/0.762 mostly from 12x iteration difference; under matched budgets random sampling overfits about 3x earlier.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Batches of 8 with at least 2 crack, 2 inactive and 1 rare-structure cell; compare at matched 20k steps (already our protocol) and report val overfitting curves.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+EP vs PF+RCS vs PF in one sweep; same metrics and kill as RCS.

alt_notes.adaptation: Each batch of 8 holds at least 1 of the 42 inactive cells and spans at least 3 of the 5 sources; compare at matched 20k steps and at 40k; keep it moderate given the crack sampling result.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + episodic batches, 5 seeds. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metric: inactive IoU (test, E1), BMRK crack/inactive IoU. Kill: inactive IoU gain < 0.02 and BMRK not better.

title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficiently Improving Generalization
mechanism: Minimise the worst-case loss in a weight neighbourhood of radius rho; seeks flat minima and is robust to label noise.
adaptation: rho {0.02,0.05} on Adam (or ASAM), BN stats from the first pass only; 2x step cost. Crack label jitter is treated as label noise.
evidence: Better generalisation on CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet and fine-tuning tasks; label-noise robustness comparable to dedicated noisy-label methods (abstract).
min_experiment: Arm PF+SAM vs SUP100-PF, seeds 5-9, 20k steps. Metric: test clean crack relF1@2 and IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if test relF1@2 gain < +0.01 and E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02; also check 10k / 15k checkpoints (early-stopping effect).
prior_overlap: none. Noisy-label methods and SAM never run.

alt_notes.adaptation: rho in {0.02, 0.05} on the house Adam (or ASAM), 2x step cost; crack label jitter treated as label noise; also score 10k and 15k checkpoints because SAM's label-noise gain is largest with early stopping (arxiv:2405.03676). arxiv:2408.04065 found plain SAM the only sharpness optimizer that consistently helped on medical data.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + SAM, 5 seeds. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metric: test clean crack relF1@2 and crack IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: test crack relF1@2 gain < +0.01 and E1 crack relF1@2 gain < +0.02.

title: XNet v2: Fewer Limitations, Better Results and Greater Universality
mechanism: A Haar wavelet split gives low- and high-frequency images, remixed with random weights (x_L = I_L + a I_H, x_H = I_H + b I_L). Three sub-networks (raw, LF, HF) are trained with consistency and feature-level LF/HF fusion.
adaptation: 1-channel Haar of the 512 px cell. HF carries cracks and fingers, LF carries inactive and dark regions. Two uses: (a) supervised XNet v2 as a benchmark arm; (b) the random LF/HF remix as a label-safe augmentation on U-Net++.
min_experiment: Arm: house + LF/HF remix augmentation (a, b in [0, 0.5]), 5-fold CV. Baseline: house. Metric: inactive IoU, BMRK crack IoU. Kill: no gain larger than 1 SE on CV. Separately run official XNet v2 supervised as a benchmark entry.
evidence: R with full supervision: CREMI Jaccard 75.47 (UNet) -> 79.80, GlaS 81.54 -> 84.03, ISIC-2017 74.49 -> 76.04. XNet (ICCV 2023) repo verified at github.com/Yanfeng-Zhou/XNet.
prior_overlap: Pseudo-label SSL at 100% was n.d., but XNet's frequency-split consistency and LF/HF remix augmentation were never run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark arm on 1-channel 512 px; for our model, use the random LF/HF remix as a label-safe augmentation on U-Net++ (HF carries cracks and fingers, LF carries inactive).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark run of supervised XNet v2 (about 10 GPU-h); separate arm house + LF/HF remix vs house, kill if CV gain below 1 SE on inactive and BMRK crack IoU.

title: Advancing metallic surface defect detection via anomaly-guided pretraining on a large industrial dataset (AGSSP)
mechanism: Label-free anomaly maps on a large unlabelled pool are distilled into the backbone and, more importantly, used as pseudo-defect targets to pretrain the localisation head before fine-tuning.
adaptation: Compute AD maps (AnomalyDINO / INP-Former, references from the same source and layout) on the 11.9k pool then 159k; pretrain the whole U-Net++ (encoder + decoder) with a 1-channel soft anomaly head (soft BCE) jointly with the 24-class head on the 478 labelled cells; fine-tune with PF so the decoder is kept.
min_experiment: Arm AGSSP-EL pretrain + PF fine-tune vs baseline PF, 5 seeds, module-grouped 5-fold CV; metrics CV inactive IoU and crack relF1@2, then E1 relF1@2 / inactive IoU; kill if CV inactive gain < +0.02 and crack relF1@2 gain < +0.01. About 45 GPU-h.
evidence: R: in-domain MoCo v3 / classification pretraining about 0 or negative (-3.6 to +2.9 mAP@.5:.95); backbone anomaly-map distillation -1.5 to +4.0; full AGSSP +2.0 to +11.4 mAP@.5:.95 on four metal defect sets, +21.6 to +24.5 on Casting Billet-Mini50; 120k unlabelled images. COCO detection pretraining close on several sets.
prior_overlap: Partial: section 5 MIM and DDeP on the 11.9k pool were n.d., but those were backbone/decoder-denoising objectives without anomaly pseudo-targets; dense pseudo-defect head pretraining kept by PF is untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Run a normal-reference AD (AnomalyDINO-style, references = clean pool cells of same source and layout incl. the 1,152 half-cells) on the 11.9k then 159k pool; pretrain the full U-Net++ (encoder + decoder) with a 1-channel soft anomaly head (soft BCE) alongside the 24-class head on the 478 labelled cells; fine-tune with PF so the pretrained decoder survives.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm AGSSP-EL pretrain + PF fine-tune vs PF baseline, 5 seeds; metrics E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, test clean-49 crack IoU; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 and test crack IoU drops > 0.01.

title: DINOv3-PEFT: A Dual-Branch Collaborative Network with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Precise Road Segmentation in SAR Imagery
mechanism: PEFT-tuned DINOv3 branch for context paired with a second branch for fine spatial detail, fused for thin road segmentation in speckled greyscale SAR.
adaptation: Thin lines in greyscale non-natural images is the closest domain match found. Use its dual-branch fusion as the template for the CNN detail branch of VFM-H: ResNet-34 stride-2/4 features fused with DINOv3 tokens upsampled from 1024 px input.
min_experiment: Arm: VFM-H with the detail branch vs without it, same PEFT. Baseline: house PF and the no-branch arm. Metric: CV crack relF1@2 and crack IoU. Kill: branch adds less than 0.01 relF1@2 over no-branch AND the arm is below PF.
evidence: R: abstract fragment only; SAR road extraction; numbers not read.
prior_overlap: none: Om's A1 (DINOv3 + HR CNN branch) was dropped on the A8 KILL, not tested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Fusion pattern only: house ResNet-34 stream plus DINOv3 ViT adapter stream fused at stride 4 and 8 inside U-Net++; fallback for ViTC-UNet if its cross-attention is unstable on 478 cells.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Run as the fusion variant of the ViTC-UNet arm; same baseline (house PF), metrics and kill line (E1 crack relF1@2 < +0.03 or CV crack IoU drop > 0.012). About 20 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Closest domain found (thin lines in noisy greyscale). CNN branch = house R34 under PF; implement its fusion module from the paper in VFM-H.
alt_notes.min_experiment: VFM-H with its fusion vs plain additive fusion; CV crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2; kill if below plain fusion on both.

title: From SAM to DINOv2: Towards Distilling Foundation Models to Lightweight Baselines for Generalized Polyp Segmentation (PolypDiFoM)
mechanism: Distil semantic priors of SAM / DINOv2 into U-Net / U-Net++ encoders with frequency-domain encoding, keeping the cheap model for deployment.
adaptation: House U-Net++ R34 + cosine feature-alignment loss at layer3/layer4 to frozen DINOv3-L or SAM2 features computed at 1024 and pooled to encoder stride; labelled + 11.9k pool cells.
min_experiment: House PF + distillation (weights 0.1 and 1.0) vs house PF, 5 seeds; pass if E1 crack relF1@2 +0.03 with CV loss <= 0.005.
evidence: R: beats U-Net / U-Net++ baselines and SOTA on 5 polyp sets with about 9x less compute.
prior_overlap: SSL with foundation-model teachers listed as not closed; distillation never tried.

title: Generative AI enables medical image segmentation in ultra low-data regimes (GenSeg)
mechanism: Pixel-space mask-to-image GAN fed with augmented real masks; generator architecture learned by multi-level optimisation so the segmenter's validation loss steers generation.
adaptation: Pixel space keeps cracks. Train on 478 cells at 512 px or 256 crops; mask augmentations = flips, rot90, crack evolution, inactive region edits; validation = module-grouped CV fold or F51, never test. Snap crack labels to the ridge first. Target inactive and weak sources (BMRK, CFVS without twin).
min_experiment: PF + GenSeg pairs (2x train size) vs PF, 5 seeds. Metric CV inactive IoU, BMRK crack/inactive IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: CV inactive < +0.02 and mIoU_rob < +0.01. About 36 GPU-h.
evidence: R: 11 tasks, 19 datasets, 8 to 480 training images per task, +10 to 20% absolute Dice/IoU in- and out-of-domain; 8 to 20x less data needed. Code stated as github importZL/semantic_segmentation (not opened).
prior_overlap: none; generative synthesis never tried

title: SPDCN: Strip-based Deformable Convolutional Network for Steel Surface Defect Segmentation
mechanism: Deformable convolution whose offsets come from decoupled horizontal and vertical strip convolutions, so the sampling grid aligns with elongated, anisotropic defects.
adaptation: Gridline (IoU 0.283, recall 0.33) and splice (never predicted) are axis-aligned in rectified cells, and rot90 augmentation keeps them axis-aligned. Use strip-offset deformable blocks in the U-Net++ decoder with the 24-class head.
min_experiment: SPDCN-style decoder blocks vs house. Metrics: gridline IoU and recall, plus mIoU_rob on test and module-grouped 5-fold CV; crack IoU as a guard. Kill if gridline CV IoU gains < 0.03.
evidence: R: 89.60 mIoU on NEU-Seg with 3.54M params (abstract). The author page github.com/DWlzm is named; the repository itself is unverified.
prior_overlap: None. Never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Closest domain here: grey industrial surfaces with cracks and scratches. Insert ADADC blocks at 1/2 and 1/4 resolution in the U-Net++ decoder; 1-ch, 24 classes.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: ADADC decoder, 5 seeds; baseline house. Metrics: crack relF1@2, components found, gridline IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill: all gains < 0.01 and E1 < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Cells are axis-aligned, so strips fit gridline fingers (IoU 0.283, recall 0.33), busbars, ribbons, splice; learned offsets cover diagonal cracks. Replace 3x3 convs in the last two U-Net++ decoder stages, keep the ImageNet encoder.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with ADADC in last two decoder stages; baseline: house; metric: CV gridline IoU and crack relF1@2; kill if gridline IoU gain < +0.03 and crack n.d.

title: A Fourier-based Framework for Domain Generalization (FACT); see also arxiv:2108.08487 Amplitude-Phase Recombination
mechanism: Amplitude-spectrum mixing between images plus a co-teacher consistency between original and mixed views, so the model relies on phase (structure) rather than amplitude (style).
adaptation: Treat the 5 sources as domains: mix amplitudes across ARTS / CFVS / CSIR / BMRK / SDLE and with pool cells; keep masks. Aimed at E1 and at the weak BMRK and CFVS sources.
min_experiment: Arm: house + cross-source amplitude mix + consistency, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, BMRK crack IoU. Kill: E1 < +0.02 and BMRK < +0.03.
evidence: R: state of the art on three domain-generalisation classification benchmarks. APR (ICCV 2021): gains in corruption robustness and OOD. No segmentation or EL numbers.
prior_overlap: none. Section 5 used brightness / contrast augmentation only.

title: ExPLoRA: Parameter-Efficient Extended Pre-Training to Adapt Vision Transformers under Domain Shifts
mechanism: Continue the VFM's own self-supervised objective (DINOv2) on unlabelled target-domain images, unfreezing 1-2 blocks and LoRA on the rest, then LoRA fine-tune.
evidence: R (abstract): SOTA on satellite imagery, beats full pretraining + fine-tune, up to +8% linear-probe top-1 with <10% of parameters.
adaptation: Continued DINO pretraining of DINOv2-L (or DINOv3-L) on the 11.9k server pool including 1,152 multi half-cells, so the encoder sees half-cut and scuff cells before supervision; then the VFM-H Rein-LoRA arm.
min_experiment: VFM-H with ExPLoRA-adapted backbone vs VFM-H with original backbone; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and CV crack relF1@2; kill if E1 not +0.02 over the original backbone.
prior_overlap: MIM and DDeP pretraining on ResNet-34 with the 11.9k pool were n.d.; continued VFM-objective pretraining of a ViT is a different mechanism and untested. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Continue DINOv2/v3 ViT-L SSL on the 159k CSIR/ARTS pool (crops 224-448, 1-ch to 3-ch, include the 1,152 multi half-cells so E1-like layouts are seen), then use as the Dino U-Net backbone.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm ExPLoRA-adapted ViT-L in Dino U-Net vs Dino U-Net with stock weights and vs PF, 5 seeds; metric CV crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2; kill if < +0.01 CV relF1@2 over stock and < +0.03 on E1. About 150 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Continue DINOv2 or DINOv3 ViT-L SSL on the 159k CSIR/ARTS pool (1-ch to 3-ch, crops 224 to 448 from 512 or native 1200 px), then use as the frozen backbone of the Dino U-Net arm.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm ExPLoRA-EL ViT-L in Dino U-Net vs the same with off-the-shelf DINOv3 vs PF, 5 seeds; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and test crack IoU; kill if ExPLoRA arm gains < +0.02 E1 relF1@2 over the off-the-shelf arm.

alt_notes.adaptation: Cheaper route to ViT-L continued pretraining on the pool on 8 A6000; feed into D24's VFM fine-tune.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Run only if MedDINOv3 or DINOCell arm shows a sign; same arm vs non-adapted VFM; kill if E1 crack recall < +0.02.

title: Frequency-aware Feature Fusion for Dense Image Prediction
mechanism: Decoder feature fusion with an adaptive low-pass filter (consistent interiors), offset resampling, and an adaptive high-pass filter (restores boundary detail lost in downsampling).
adaptation: Replace the upsample + concat at each U-Net++ decoder node with FreqFusion on 1-channel EL features. The low-pass is meant for blobby inactive regions, the high-pass for 1 to 2 px crack edges.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + FreqFusion decoder, 5-fold CV. Baseline: PF. Metric: inactive IoU and crack IoU. Kill: both < 1 SE.
evidence: R: gains on semantic, instance and panoptic segmentation and detection (abstract). No thin-structure numbers seen.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace upsample + concat at each U-Net++ node; low-pass should help blobby inactive regions, high-pass crack edges.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + FreqFusion decoder; baseline PF; 5 seeds; inactive IoU (CV) and crack IoU; kill if both below 1 SE.

title: Generalised Balanced Softmax: A Finite-Data Perspective on Logit Adjustment for Long-Tailed Recognition
mechanism: Training-time logit adjustment z + beta*log N_c with beta treated as a finite-data hyperparameter; beta = 1 (balanced softmax) is often not optimal.
adaptation: Supplies the beta grid for the logit-adjusted CE arm; with 478 cells beta below 1 is likely best; select on OOF folds.
min_experiment: Run as the beta arm of the LA-CE experiment: beta in {0.25, 0.5, 1.0}, 3 seeds, vs SUP100; metric mIoU_rob; kill as LA-CE.
evidence: R: across long-tailed classification benchmarks, beta = 1 does not attain the best average recall on most datasets; tuned beta lowers the model imbalance metric.
prior_overlap: none

title: MS-Net: Multi-Site Network for Improving Prostate Segmentation With Heterogeneous MRI Data
mechanism: Train one segmentation network on several heterogeneous sites with shared conv kernels, site-specific batch normalisation and site-specific auxiliary branches plus multi-site knowledge transfer.
adaptation: Treat the 5 EL sources (ARTS, CFVS, CSIR, BMRK, SDLE) as sites in the house U-Net++: per-source BN (PyTorch re-implementation of the BN part only), source id known for every cell; E1 (101 CSIR + 5 BMRK) uses the CSIR / BMRK branches. Optional 6th site UCF-EL for joint (not sequential) training.
min_experiment: Arm: PF with per-source BN; baseline: PF. Module-grouped 5-fold CV, 2 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, BMRK crack IoU, then E1 crack recall. Kill if relF1@2 and inactive IoU both < +0.01 and BMRK crack IoU < +0.02.
evidence: R: consistent gains across 3 heterogeneous prostate MRI sites over joint training and single-site baselines (numbers not read).
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF per-panel BN adaptation was test-time BN; the SSL 'separate BN' split labelled vs unlabelled batches. Training-time per-source BN and joint multi-dataset training are listed as never tried.

title: RRWNet: Recursive Refinement Network for effective retinal artery/vein segmentation and classification
mechanism: A base subnetwork plus a recursive refinement subnetwork that iteratively corrects manifest class confusions in multi-class thin-structure maps; the refinement module also works as a post-processor for other models.
adaptation: Run the recursive module on the 24-class probabilities to fix crack vs inactive (20% of train crack pixels sit in or at inactive) and crack vs gridline / ribbon confusions; train on out-of-fold maps from the 5 fold models.
min_experiment: Arm: house + recursive refinement module. Baseline: house / PF. Metrics: crack-inactive-gridline confusion, inactive IoU, gridline IoU, mIoU_rob, crack IoU on 5-fold CV and clean-49. Kill: mIoU_rob < +0.005 and inactive IoU < +0.01.
evidence: R: state of the art A/V segmentation on three public fundus datasets with fewer manifest classification errors; module improves other methods' maps as post-processing (numbers not read).
prior_overlap: none.

title: Uncertainty-Aware ControlNet: Bridging Domain Gaps with Synthetic Image Generation
mechanism: A semantic ControlNet trained on labelled masks and an uncertainty ControlNet trained on labelled + unlabelled images (conditioned on the segmenter's mean entropy) are fused at sampling, giving labelled images in the unlabelled domain's style.
adaptation: LDM fine-tuned on the 11.9k pool (1-ch to 3); semantic ControlNet on 478 train masks; uncertainty = house 5-seed ensemble mean entropy per cell (high on half-cut/scuff CSIR); sample entropy from the half-cut pool; feed half-cut-cropped train masks so layout and style move toward E1. Use for inactive, scuff context, layout; latent 64x64 means crack pixels must pass an adherence check.
min_experiment: PF + 2,000 generated half-cut-style cells vs PF, 5 seeds. Metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU; guard test crack IoU clean 49. Kill: both E1 gains < +0.03 or test crack IoU drop > 0.01.
evidence: R: retinal OCT Spectralis (labelled) to Home-OCT (unlabelled), about 10k B-scans per domain at 256 px; abstract reports significantly improved segmentation without target labels; also Cityscapes to ACDC. Numbers not read.
prior_overlap: Synthetic half-cut views (geometry only) were n.d.; generated target appearance never tried. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: LDM fine-tuned on the 11.9k pool; semantic ControlNet on 478 train masks (24-class one-hot); uncertainty = house 5-seed mean entropy, high on half-cut/scuff CSIR cells; feed half-cut-cropped train masks. Use for inactive, scuff, layout; crack pixels only after the adherence gate.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + 2,000 generated half-cut-style cells vs PF. Metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU, guard test crack IoU. Kill: both E1 gains < +0.03 or test crack drop > 0.01. About 90 GPU-h.

title: Universal Loss Reweighting to Balance Lesion Size Inequality in 3D Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Reweights voxel loss by inverse lesion size so each lesion carries equal total weight.
adaptation: Precomputed per-pixel weight map on merged crack instances, (median size / size)^gamma with gamma 0.5 or 1, capped at 10, applied on CE only; zero runtime cost.
min_experiment: Arm: house with inverse-size CE weights, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: component recall <20 px and >=20 px, relF1@2, crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill: component F1 not above house by 0.02.
evidence: Abstract not in index; mechanism from title and session-1 notes; numbers unverified.
prior_overlap: none; no size reweighting was run.

title: Data Distillation: Towards Omni-Supervised Learning
mechanism: Omni-supervised learning: all labelled data plus unlabelled data. Labels for the unlabelled data come from ensembling one model's predictions over multiple input transforms, and a student is retrained on the union.
adaptation: Single-model teacher = one PF model with 8-way dihedral TTA (rot90 x flip; EL cracks have no orientation prior), applied to the 11.9k pool. A cheaper alternative to a 5-seed ensemble teacher and easy to refresh for later rounds.
min_experiment: Same as the ensemble-distillation arm B, but with a single-model TTA teacher. Baseline: PF single model. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: no gain >= +0.008 crack IoU over PF and no E1 gain.
evidence: R: CVPR 2018, keypoint and box detection on COCO, with gains over the fully supervised baseline when internet-scale unlabelled images are added (numbers not retrieved).
prior_overlap: Partial. The SSL row used an online EMA teacher without TTA ensembling. Offline TTA teacher labels have not been tested.

title: FreeCOS: Self-Supervised Learning from Fractals and Unlabeled Images for Curvilinear Object Segmentation
mechanism: Fractal L-system curvilinear structures blended into unlabelled images via Fourier domain adaptation, with intensity-order (geometric) alignment between synthetic and real images.
adaptation: Procedural crack skeletons (L-system or Bezier, branching typical of cell cracks) drawn as dark lines with a measured profile (about 4 px FWHM, per-source contrast from train crack statistics, including the 7% at < 2% contrast) and finger interruptions; FDA-blend onto pool half-cut cells; labels at each source's width. No generator training.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + procedural cracks on half-cut pool cells, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: gain < +0.02. Run first; it prices the row-1 renderer.
evidence: R: outperforms unsupervised and self-supervised methods on XCAD, DRIVE, STARE, CrackTree without labels (abstract; numbers not read).
prior_overlap: Partly overlaps CP100 (real crack pixels pasted on pool cells, n.d. on test). Differs in new procedural shapes, physically modelled intensity, FDA appearance matching and half-cut target backgrounds scored on E1.

alt_notes.adaptation: Render L-system cracks as dark Gaussian dips (FWHM 3-5 px, 2-20% contrast, per-source) into crack-free pool cells with a 1.75 px centreline label; use as a pretraining stage for the crack branch, then house fine-tune.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm FreeCOS-style crack pretraining + house fine-tune vs house, 5 seeds; metric test relR@2 at matched relP@2 and E1 relF1@2; kill if relR@2 gain < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Render L-system cracks as dark Gaussian dips (FWHM 3-5 px, 2-20% contrast, per source) into crack-free pool cells with a 1.75 px centreline label; use as a crack-branch pretraining stage before house fine-tune, not mixed training data.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm FreeCOS-style crack pretraining + house fine-tune vs baseline house, 5 seeds; metric CV crack relR@2 at equal relP@2; kill if gain < +0.02. About 15 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Composite procedural thin dark curves into pool half-cells (including scuff cells) as a pretext stage, then PF fine-tune. Differs from the closed crack copy-paste (real crack patches) by procedural shapes and order-based alignment. Overlaps D06.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: FreeCOS-style pretrain on half-cell pool then PF fine-tune, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: E1 relF1@2, E1 crack false-positive px per half-cut cell. Kill: < +0.03 relF1@2.

alt_notes.adaptation: Pretext stage on pool half-cells (scuff-bearing) so the model sees thin dark curves on half-cut backgrounds, then PF fine-tune on 478 cells.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: FreeCOS pretext then PF fine-tune, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: E1 relF1@2 and crack false-positive px per half-cut cell. Kill: < +0.03 relF1@2.

alt_notes.adaptation: Render fractal dark lines with a 4 px Gaussian profile on CSIR half-cut pool cells; use as a pretext / 10% minibatch share for crack, aimed at E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + fractal synthetic share, 5 seeds; baseline PF. Metric E1 relF1@2 and E1 false alarms on scuff cells. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03 or more scuff false alarms.

title: GOOSE-M2F: Adapting Mask2Former for High-Fidelity, Long-Tailed Fine-Grained Semantic Segmentation in Unstructured Outdoor Terrain
mechanism: Auxiliary per-pixel CE head (weight 0.4, removed at inference) beside the Mask2Former matching loss so rare/tiny classes get dense gradient; plus 200 queries, distribution-balanced loss, rare-class copy-paste.
evidence: R: ablation on GOOSE val 54.6 -> 57.1 (+200 queries) -> 60.4 (+refinement) -> 63.8 (+3.4 aux head) -> 67.5 (balanced loss + rare copy-paste); 3rd place 70.08 composite mIoU; Swin-L; ablation table has internal inconsistencies.
adaptation: Bolt the dense head onto any mask classifier we run (EoMT/M2F) at full resolution, not 1/4, supervised with our CE + soft Dice on crack and inactive; class-balanced weights only on weak other classes (gridline, splice, edge_dark, material). S: in semantic mode each present class is one target so the 'zero gradient' claim is shaky; the head is cheap insurance for 0.19%-pixel crack.
min_experiment: Within the M2F/EoMT runs: arm with dense aux head vs same model without; metrics crack IoU, relF1@2, splice IoU, mIoU_rob; kill if crack IoU gain < 0.012 and splice stays 0.
prior_overlap: none; long-tail and auxiliary losses on mask classifiers untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Add a full-res dense head with our CE + Dice on crack and inactive to any mask classifier (EoMT, M2F); copy-paste inactive regions together with their bounding cracks rather than cracks alone.
alt_notes.min_experiment: M2F Swin-B 512 arm A (plain) vs arm B (+dense aux head + high-res conv branch), baseline house; metrics crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, splice/material/edge_dark IoU, mIoU_rob; kill B if mIoU_rob < house - 0.01 and inactive IoU not above house.

title: JAFAR: Jack up Any Feature at Any Resolution
mechanism: Attention upsampler with high-res queries from low-level image features and SFT-modulated low-res semantic keys; trained only at low ratios without high-res supervision, generalises to large upsampling.
adaptation: Train JAFAR label-free on the 11.9k EL pool for the chosen DINOv3 encoder so it learns busbar, finger and crack texture; compare with off-the-shelf AnyUp in the same probe.
min_experiment: Same probe as AnyUp (X1): JAFAR-pool-trained arm vs AnyUp vs bilinear-1024; metric CV crack AP and gridline AP. Kill if it does not beat AnyUp by >= 0.01 crack AP.
evidence: R: AnyUp's comparison: VOC linear probe 84.36 mIoU (best), COCO 61.82, ADE20k 42.06 vs bilinear 81.43/59.48/40.54.
prior_overlap: none; label-free pool training of an upsampler was never run (pool MIM/DDeP trained the encoder, not an upsampler).

alt_notes.adaptation: Upsample frozen DINOv3 ViT-L features to 512 x 512 and concatenate them into the house U-Net++ decoder as a side branch; keeps the house encoder that already works.
alt_notes.min_experiment: House + JAFAR-DINOv3 side branch, 3 seeds; crack IoU, inactive IoU, E1 relF1@2; kill if all within 0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Train label-free on the 11.9k EL pool for the chosen DINOv3 encoder (its training command takes any timm backbone) so the upsampler learns EL texture (fingers, busbars, grain, cracks) before any labels are used.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Pool-trained JAFAR vs zero-shot NAF / AnyUp in the same frozen probe; metric CV crack AP, gridline AP; kill if it does not beat the better zero-shot upsampler by +0.01 AP. About 8 GPU-h including training.

title: One-Step Image Translation with Text-to-Image Models (CycleGAN-Turbo)
mechanism: One-step SD-Turbo generator with LoRA and encoder-decoder skip connections trained with cycle and adversarial losses on unpaired domains; skips keep the input structure.
adaptation: Domain A = 478 train cells plus existing synthetic half-cut views; domain B = 1,152 half-cut multi pool cells plus scuffed CSIR cells. Translate train cells to B style and keep real labels; 1-ch replicated to 3. Latent 64x64 may erase low-contrast cracks, so drop samples where house-ensemble crack relF1@2 on the translated cell falls below 0.9 of the source value.
min_experiment: PF + 478 translated cells vs PF, 5 seeds. Metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU, guard clean-49 crack IoU. Kill: both E1 gains < +0.03 or test crack IoU drop > 0.01. About 25 GPU-h.
evidence: R: beats GAN and diffusion translators on day/night and weather translation (FID, structure preservation); 193 citations; no segmentation-on-translated numbers.
prior_overlap: Synthetic half-cut views (geometry only) were n.d.; appearance translation toward half-cut/scuff style never run. Open.

title: Pasta: Proportional Amplitude Spectrum Training Augmentation for Syn-to-Real Domain Generalization
mechanism: Perturb the Fourier amplitude spectrum with jitter that grows with frequency, keeping phase, to generate augmented views.
adaptation: Source-free counterpart of FDA: phase kept so crack positions are unchanged; cap the high-frequency jitter so faint cracks (7% are under 2% darker) survive. Aimed at E1 and weak sources BMRK/CFVS.
min_experiment: Arm: house + PASTA; baseline house; 5 seeds; E1 relF1@2, per-source crack IoU; kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03; run beside FDA with shared code.
evidence: R: beats more complex DG methods on 5 syn-to-real shifts incl. GTAV-to-real segmentation; complementary to them.
prior_overlap: none; house augmentation is brightness/contrast only

title: Quality Sentinel: Estimating Label Quality and Errors in Medical Segmentation Datasets
mechanism: Regressor on (image, label) predicts the label's Dice against a correct label, trained on synthetic corruptions; used to pick high-quality labels and pseudo-labels.
adaptation: Train on 532 labelled cells with EL-specific corruptions (1-3 px shifts, width 1-4 px, dropped/spurious segments, inactive boundary errors), target relF1@2 and inactive IoU; use to rank train labels and to select pool pseudo-labels image by image.
min_experiment: Arm: house + top 1,000 pool cells by predicted pseudo-label quality (5-seed teacher). Baseline: house and earlier pool SSL. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, clean-49 crack IoU. Kill: predicted-vs-true quality Spearman < 0.5 on real val labels, or no gain over earlier pool run.
evidence: R: r = 0.902 between predicted and true label Dice over 142 structures; 4M training pairs; quality-selected pseudo-labels gave 33-88% gain over entropy selection; 1/3 annotation cost cut on TotalSegmentator.
prior_overlap: Pseudo-label SSL row: per-pixel hard/tolerant thresholds with 11.9k pool at 100% labels n.d.; image-level learned quality selection not run. Partly open.

title: A principled representation of elongated structures using heatmaps
mechanism: Encode a curve's nominal position and positional uncertainty as a heatmap by convolving the curve distribution with a filter, approximated in linear time by a distance-dependent function.
adaptation: Filter width per source set from measured label-to-ridge offsets (team E: 48% of label points within 1 px of the ridge); regression head separate from the CE head so it cannot widen the argmax; read out by ridge NMS and draw at per-source width.
min_experiment: Arm PF + heatmap regression head (MSE), two read-outs (aux only; heatmap-NMS drawn at source width) vs PF; metric relF1@2 and strict IoU on CV; kill if relF1@2 +<0.01 in both read-outs.
evidence: Approximation error analysed vs curve type and SNR; applied to surgical 2D/3D data, semantic boundaries, skeletonisation. No crack test; numbers not read.
prior_overlap: none in BRIEF 5; related to T2 soft_band_jml (soft band inside the CE target) but different head and loss

title: Label refinement network from synthetic error augmentation for medical image segmentation
mechanism: A generator of synthetic structural errors plus a label-appearance simulation network makes corrupted masks that look like real network outputs; a refiner trained on image + these masks learns to fix breaks and missing branches.
adaptation: 2D version; error model = skeleton breaks, deletion of the lowest-contrast crack segments, 1 px shifts off the dark ridge, width changes between source conventions (1.5 to 3.25 px), gridline-like false fragments; appearance net mimics out-of-fold crack probability maps; pool cells give extra base-model predictions to correct.
min_experiment: Arm: U-Net refiner on image + 24-class probabilities trained on out-of-fold + synthetic errors. Control: identical refiner trained on out-of-fold maps only. Metric: 5-fold CV crack relF1@2 and IoU, components found. Kill: arm beats control by < 0.01 relF1@2.
evidence: R: airway (chest CT) and brain vessel (CTA) segmentation; beat a 3D U-Net, four earlier label refinement methods and a tubular-structure loss; larger gains with extra unlabeled data (exact numbers not read).
prior_overlap: Crack copy-paste and synthetic half-cut views were data augmentation for the segmenter, not a refiner; mechanism not tested.

title: Surgical Fine-Tuning Improves Adaptation to Distribution Shifts
mechanism: Tuning only a subset of layers matches or beats full fine-tuning; the best block depends on shift type (input-level shifts favour early layers); tuning more parameters on small data forgets pretrained information.
adaptation: Arms: train stem+layer1-2 with layer3-4 frozen at ImageNet; and the reverse. Decoder always trained. E1 shift (scuff streaks, half-cut layout, contrast) is input-level, so early-layer tuning is predicted to help E1.
evidence: Seven real-world tasks, three shift types; first-layer tuning best for image corruptions (abstract).
min_experiment: Two arms vs SUP100-PF on module-grouped 5-fold CV, 2 seeds, then 5 seeds for the winner. Metric: CV inactive IoU and crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU. Kill if neither arm beats PF on CV by +0.01 inactive IoU or +0.005 relF1@2.
prior_overlap: Partial: PF freezes the whole encoder for 1k steps only. Block-wise permanent freezing never run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Arms: tune stem + layer1-2 with layer3-4 frozen at ImageNet, and the reverse; decoder always trained. E1's shifts (scuff, half-cut, contrast) are input-level, so early-layer tuning is the prediction.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: two surgical freezes, 5-fold CV x 2 seeds, then 5 seeds on full train. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, test crack relF1@2. Kill: neither freeze beats PF on E1 by +0.02 relF1@2 or +0.03 inactive IoU.

title: Deep Distance Transform for Tubular Structure Segmentation in CT Scans
mechanism: A multi-task head predicts the mask and a per-pixel distance map to the structure surface. The mask is then refined with a shape prior rebuilt from that map.
adaptation: An auxiliary head regresses truncated distance to the crack label centerline, capped at 4 px (the dark-line FWHM). This target degrades smoothly under 1 to 2 px label jitter. Use it as an extra crack cue and for ridge-following refinement.
min_experiment: Arm: house + distance head (L1, weight 0.5). Baseline: house. Metrics: crack relF1@2 and IoU on test and E1. Kill if the relF1@2 gain is < 0.01 on both test and E1.
evidence: R: six CT datasets, more than 13% DSC gain on pancreatic duct.
prior_overlap: none. Offset-tolerant CE and Skeleton Recall are different mechanisms. D11 (centerline regression) overlaps as a formulation, but here the distance map is an auxiliary head next to CE.

alt_notes.adaptation: For crack use distance-to-skeleton bins 0..4 px; for inactive true distance to boundary; radius head yields crack width per source and inactive area fraction for severity.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + DDT distance head (crack + inactive) vs PF; metric inactive IoU and relF1@2; kill if both move <0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: For 1-2 px cracks distance-to-surface is near 0, so use distance-to-label-skeleton bins (0..4 px) for crack and true distance for inactive; radius head also gives crack width for severity.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm = PF + quantised distance head (crack, inactive) with DDT refinement; baseline = PF; 5 seeds + CV; metrics inactive IoU, crack relF1@2. Kill if both flat (< 0.01).

alt_notes.adaptation: Regress truncated distance to crack label centerline capped at 4 px (dark-line FWHM); target degrades smoothly under 1-2 px jitter; auxiliary head next to CE, optional ridge-following fusion at inference.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house + distance head (L1, w 0.5); baseline house; metrics crack relF1@2, IoU, E1 relF1@2; kill if relF1@2 gain < 0.01 on test and E1.

title: Deep Vessel Segmentation Based on a New Combination of Vesselness Filters
mechanism: Train the segmentation net on stacked multi-scale vesselness filter responses instead of (or with) the raw image; helps small vessels.
adaptation: Add Frangi / Sato / Jerman responses for dark ridges at sigma 1, 1.5, 2, 3 px as extra input channels to house U-Net++ (no training of the filters). Fingers and busbar edges will respond too.
min_experiment: Arm: house with [EL, 4 ridge maps], 5 seeds; baseline house 5 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2, E1 relF1@2, gridline IoU. Kill: crack and E1 relF1@2 gains both < 0.01. Note HarmonySeg found plain concatenation gave no notable gain, so a null here then points to attention fusion.
evidence: U-Net on vesselness hyper-volumes improved segmentation, mainly small vessels, on two vascular datasets (abstract). HarmonySeg ablation: simple CT+vesselness concatenation gave no notable gain.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Input stack: raw, Sato dark-ridge sigma 1 and 2, Frangi dark-ridge, FFT residual. Use 4 to 5 channels, with the conv1 extra-channel weights zero-initialised.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with the 4-channel stack, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: test relF1@2, E1 crack recall. Kill: E1 recall < +0.03 and relF1@2 < +0.01.

title: IMWA: Iterative Model Weight Averaging benefits class-imbalanced learning
mechanism: Split training into episodes; several models trained from the same start are averaged and the average starts the next episode; complements EMA on imbalanced tasks.
adaptation: 4 parallel copies on 4 A6000s, average every 1k-2k steps across the 20k house schedule; aims at rare crack pixels and the 42 inactive cells.
min_experiment: Arm: IMWA (4 copies, 10 episodes), 3 replicates. Baseline: house single. Metric: inactive IoU and crack IoU on CV. Kill: < +0.01 on both.
evidence: R: long-tailed classification, imbalanced SSL and SSOD; +0.8 to +1.8 top-1 over strong bases vs about +0.2 for end-of-training averaging; additive with EMA; Pascal VOC SSOD AP50:95 +1.8 for Unbiased Teacher.
prior_overlap: none

title: Multi-class Semantic Segmentation of Photovoltaic Module Defects and Features: Towards Industrial Robotic Applications
mechanism: VGG16-UNet beat ResNet50 and MobileNet encoders on the 29-class SCDD; S: VGG gives the decoder a full-resolution 64-channel skip that the ResNet stem (stride 2 + maxpool) lacks, which matters for 1 to 2 px lines.
adaptation: U-Net++ with vgg16_bn encoder, or ResNet-34 plus a light full-res stem branch feeding the last decoder node; 1-ch input, house schedule; check gridline and crack, the two thin classes.
min_experiment: Arm full-res-skip U-Net++ vs house, 5 seeds; crack IoU, relF1@2, gridline IoU; kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and gridline IoU < +0.03.
evidence: R: VGG16-UNet mean IoU 0.663 on features, 0.326 on defects, dead-cell IoU +0.129 vs prior; custom class weights. Chen 2023 (doi:10.1109/jphotov.2023.3249970) also used VGG16-UNet for crack, F1 0.875 IoU 0.782 on its own set.
prior_overlap: none: only ResNet-34/50 encoders tried; 2x input resolution (n.d.) is a different, 4x costlier change.

alt_notes.adaptation: Run their best (VGG16-UNet) under our fixed split and metrics as the label authors' reference baseline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Run once, 3 seeds, under the benchmark protocol; report all-class and robust mIoU, crack relF1@2. No score kill line.

alt_notes.adaptation: Include it as the 'prior EL baseline' in the suite, re-run on our 24-class module-grouped splits and metrics to document why published numbers differ.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Run VGG16-UNet with class weights on our folds. Baseline: house. Expected to be below the house model; it is kept for comparability, not to raise scores.

title: State-of-the-art retinal vessel segmentation with minimalistic models (W-Net)
mechanism: A tiny carefully trained U-Net nearly matches complex SOTA; a cascade (second net sees image + first prediction) reaches SOTA; most complete cross-dataset study (10 sets).
adaptation: W-Net cascade as the cheapest refinement stage: second small U-Net on [EL, 24-class softmax of the house model], trained on the frozen first stage or jointly. Compare against a 2-model ensemble to separate cascade from ensembling.
min_experiment: Arm: house + second-stage refiner, 5 seeds; baseline: 2-model house ensemble (compute-matched). Metric crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: relF1@2 gain < 0.01 vs the matched ensemble.
evidence: Minimal U-Net close to best methods; W-Net SOTA on several vessel sets with orders of magnitude fewer weights; cross-dataset performance drops a lot; self-labelling gave moderate cross-domain gain.
prior_overlap: none; refinement networks listed as never tried

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: strong simple baselines, a rigorous protocol and a mandatory unseen-domain test (E1). For scores: a W-Net style second U-Net that takes the image and the first-stage probabilities.
alt_notes.min_experiment: W-Net cascade on house vs house, 5 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2 and E1 recall. Kill if gains < 0.012.

title: SegNeXt: Rethinking Convolutional Attention Design for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Multi-scale convolutional attention built from cheap strip convolutions (k x 1, 1 x k) instead of self-attention, with a Hamburger decoder.
evidence: R: about +2.0 mIoU on ADE20K at equal or lower compute vs prior SOTA; 90.6 mIoU VOC test. In arXiv 2603.13044 SegNeXt is among the top general-purpose models on small 2D medical sets.
adaptation: MSCAN-B ImageNet weights, grey replicated, 512 px, add a full-res skip before the head; strip kernels suit long axis-aligned gridlines (recall 0.33) and long cracks along busbar directions; cheap enough for 5-fold CV.
min_experiment: Arm SegNeXt-B + full-res skip; baseline house; metrics gridline IoU/recall, crack relF1@2, mIoU_rob; kill if gridline IoU < 0.313 and crack relF1@2 < 0.881.
prior_overlap: none; only ResNet-34/50 U-Net++ tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Strip kernels align with long axis-parallel gridlines (gridline recall 0.33) and long cracks; MSCAN-B ImageNet weights, 1-ch replicated, add a full-res skip; cheap enough for 5-fold CV and ensembling.
alt_notes.min_experiment: SegNeXt-B + full-res skip at 512 vs house; metrics gridline IoU/recall, crack relF1@2, mIoU_rob; kill if gridline IoU < 0.313 and crack relF1@2 < 0.881.

title: C-RADIOv4 (Tech Report)
mechanism: Agglomerative ViT distilled from SigLIP2, DINOv3 and SAM3; any-resolution support and a ViTDet windowed mode for cheap high-resolution inference; permissive licence.
evidence: R (abstract): improves over RADIOv2.5 at same cost. Web (unverified from paper): ADE20k linear probe 55.2 / 57.0 at 512 / 1024 px.
adaptation: Backbone swap in VFM-H with no gated download; ViTDet mode at 1024 px; SO400M first.
min_experiment: C-RADIOv4-SO400M vs DINOv3-L vs SAM2 Hiera-L in the best PEFT arm; drop a backbone if E1 relF1@2 is more than 0.02 below the best.
prior_overlap: Not tested. Open.

title: ConvNeXt V2: Co-designing and Scaling ConvNets with Masked Autoencoders
mechanism: Fully convolutional masked autoencoder (sparse conv on visible patches) plus GRN layer, so ConvNets gain from masked image modeling.
adaptation: On the de-duplicated pool, 1-ch stem, 512 px random crops without rescaling: (a) continue FCMAE from ImageNet V2-Nano/Tiny; (b) from-scratch FCMAE on Pico/Nano as in the SEM paper. Mask 0.5, 32 px patches. Encoder in smp U-Net++ with a stride-2 skip, PF fine-tune.
min_experiment: Arm A continued FCMAE V2-Nano on 11.9k (~40 GPU-h) and arm B from-scratch Pico/Nano; baseline = same backbone with ImageNet weights under PF. Metrics: out-of-fold crack relF1@2 (cv5v2), E1 crack recall, inactive IoU, 2 seeds. Kill if all three below +0.01.
evidence: R: FCMAE lets ConvNeXt V2 gain from MIM on ImageNet/ADE20K; in-domain evidence comes from the SEM paper (+0.8 to +5.9 AJI+ over ImageNet on 25k greyscale images).
prior_overlap: Partial: our SparK MIM on ResNet-34 (11.9k, PF, 100% labels) was n.d. ConvNeXt V2 backbone, FCMAE recipe and from-scratch in-domain training are untested, still open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Continue FCMAE from ImageNet ConvNeXt V2-N/T on the de-duplicated pool, 1-ch stem, 512 px, mask 0.5 on 16 px patches (finer than our 32 px). Encoder into smp U-Net++ with an added stride-2 skip; PF fine-tune.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: ConvNeXt V2-T U-Net++ init from continued FCMAE, PF. Baseline: ConvNeXt V2-T ImageNet FCMAE+FT weights, PF, same steps. Metrics: out-of-fold crack relF1@2, E1 crack recall, inactive IoU, 2 seeds x 5 folds. Kill if all < +0.01.

title: CoRe-SAM3: Conditional Semantic--Visual Reconciliation for SAM3 Crack Segmentation
