mechanism: Keep SAM3's text-prompted ('crack') semantic map as the main decision path; train a 19k-param calibration plus a bounded, zero-initialised residual from native visual features to correct it.
adaptation: First a zero-shot SAM3 'crack' probe on our 54 val cells at 1008 input; if it detects cracks, train CoRe on crack only and fuse its logits with the house model, mainly for E1 half-cut / scuff cells.
min_experiment: Zero-shot SAM3 'crack' on val: relR@2 and relF1@2 vs house; kill if relR@2 < 0.5. Then CoRe + house logit fusion vs house PF on E1 crack relF1@2 (+0.03 needed).
evidence: R: 5 crack sets, native SAM3 62.34 -> CoRe 70.47 mean crack IoU, clDice 81.98 -> 89.24; corrects 34.4% of native errors, damages 0.23% of correct pixels; 3 seeds; RTX A2000.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Only if SAM3 zero-shot 'crack' fires on EL cracks (SERD probe first); train on 478 cells crack-only at 1008 px, fuse with house for other classes.
alt_notes.min_experiment: CoRe arm vs house crack, 3 seeds; crack IoU, relF1@2, E1 relF1@2; kill if crack IoU < house.

title: Sample-Centric Multi-Task Learning for Detection and Segmentation of Industrial Surface Defects
mechanism: A plug-in sample-level defect/no-defect head on the top encoder stage whose loss backpropagates only into the encoder, pushing features toward small low-contrast defects; plus per-sample Seg_Recall / Sample_mIoU metrics.
adaptation: 269 of 478 train cells lack cracks, so a cell-level crack-present head is informative; add crack and inactive presence heads on ResNet-34 layer4 of house / PF, also per 128 px tile for a local signal; report cell-level Seg_Recall in the benchmark.
evidence: R: KSDD2 DeepLabv3+ mIoU 53.2 to 58.2, Seg_Recall 72.7 to 82.7; SegNet mIoU 55.1 to 61.9; DeepLabv3 Seg_Recall dropped 71.7 to 65.5; road Crack set small gains; single runs.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + crack/inactive presence heads (cell + 128 px tile), weight 1; baseline: PF; metric: CV crack relR@2 at relP@2 >= 0.90 and cell-level Seg_Recall; kill if relR@2 gain < +0.02.
prior_overlap: none in BRIEF s5 (classification heads never tried); D27 holds Bozic stop-grad cls head, this variant sends cls gradient into the encoder.

title: STC-Net: Electroluminescence-Based Solar Cell Crack Segmentation for Power Loss Estimation
mechanism: Two fixed prior branches (Sobel gradient-magnitude pyramid and FFT radial high-pass residual pyramid) injected into the decoder of a U-Net-like crack segmenter, plus boundary-topology refinement and a crack-derived inactive-area proxy for power loss.
evidence: R: PVEL-S (840 train / 360 test polycrystalline cells): test mIoU 72.52, mDice 80.16, recall 83.18, precision 84.23. No ablation of the priors found in the text.
adaptation: Inject LoG (sigma about 1.5) instead of Sobel (Sobel fires on both flanks of a 4 px line while labels are 1 to 2 px on the ridge) and an FFT high-pass map into U-Net++ decoder stages. Use its inactive-area proxy for the severity track.
min_experiment: Arm: house + LoG and high-pass prior pyramids in decoder, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: test crack IoU, relF1@2, comp>=20 px recall. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012 and no relF1@2 gain.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Feed Sobel magnitude and a high-pass residual as extra input channels to U-Net++, with the cutoff set above finger pitch or a notch removing finger periodicity so gridlines do not light up; auxiliary head on 2 px dilated crack rather than edge labels. Reuse the inactive proxy only as a severity baseline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + 2 prior channels + aux head. Baseline: house, 5 v 5 seeds. Metrics: test crack IoU, E1 crack recall. Kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and E1 recall < +0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Cheap form: 3-channel input (EL, Sobel magnitude, high-pass residual) at 512 px. Full form: prior pyramids into U-Net++ skips, edge head target = 3 px dilated crack label to absorb 1 to 2 px jitter. Aimed at low-contrast cracks (7% are < 2% darker) and E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with priors (cheap, then full). Baseline: house, 5 seeds. Metric: test crack relF1@2, E1 crack recall. Kill if relF1@2 < +0.01 and E1 recall < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Cheap arm: Sobel magnitude and high-pass maps as extra input channels to the house U-Net++; the inactive proxy is a simpler form of the crack-bounded region prior.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with 3-channel input (EL, Sobel, high-pass); baseline: house. Metrics: CV crack relF1@2 and crack IoU. Kill if < +0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Minimal: Sobel magnitude + high-pass residual as 2 extra input channels to the house model; full: prior pyramids fused at U-Net++ decoder nodes. Source-independent contrast cue aimed at E1, where 70% of crack pixels get p < 0.001; risk of false alarms on scuff streaks and gridlines.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house + priors vs house, 5 seeds; E1 crack recall and relF1@2, test crack IoU; kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 and test crack IoU drops > 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Inject the two prior pyramids into U-Net++ decoder stages; replace Sobel with a LoG ridge prior (sigma about 1.5) because Sobel fires on both flanks of a 4 px dark line while labels sit on one ridge.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + LoG and FFT high-pass pyramids in decoder, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: test crack IoU, relF1@2, comp>=20 px recall. Kill: < +0.012 crack IoU and no relF1@2 gain.

alt_notes.adaptation: Reference only. The topology head could become an auxiliary skeleton output on U-Net++, but there is no ablation showing it helps.
alt_notes.min_experiment: None proposed until a topology-head ablation exists. At most, add a skeleton auxiliary head inside the DconnNet arm.

alt_notes.adaptation: Only EL topology paper found; no ablation of the topology module, so no evidence it helps. Cite in benchmark related work and the severity discussion.
alt_notes.min_experiment: None for scores.

alt_notes.adaptation: Same modality and size (grey, 512 px): reimplement as a benchmark entry from the paper spec (base 32 ch, depths [2,2,4,2], 120 epochs, deep supervision); edge and spectral prior injection as a cheap ablation on the house model.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house PF + Sobel and high-pass prior pyramids into decoder; baseline: house PF; CV crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if both n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Same modality and task: reimplement from the paper spec (base 32 ch, depths [2,2,4,2], 120 epochs) as a benchmark entry on our splits; its power-loss proxy informs the severity extension; its edge / spectral priors as one cheap ablation on the house model.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Bench run under the protocol vs house PF; score-arm ablation house PF + Sobel / FFT pyramid inputs, kill if 5-fold CV crack relF1@2 n.d. About 8 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Its auxiliary heads are a subset of the SBCB and distance-head arms. Its value here is as the only EL structured multi-head method. Reimplement it in the benchmark suite under our split, and reuse its inactive-area proxy only as a severity baseline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark run: STC-Net reimplementation v house under the fixed protocol. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU. No kill line; it is a suite baseline.

alt_notes.adaptation: Its auxiliary heads are a subset of the SBCB and distance arms; include in benchmark suite and reuse its proxy as a severity baseline only.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark run: STC-Net reimplemented under our protocol vs house on clean 49 crack IoU, relF1@2 and E1; no kill line (suite member).

alt_notes.adaptation: Compute the Sobel and radial high-pass maps on the 1-channel 512 px input, build small pyramids, and add them into the U-Net++ decoder skips with learned weights. The power-loss proxy is a candidate severity output.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + prior pyramids, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill: < +0.012 crack IoU and no relF1@2 gain.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark row under our protocol; for our model, replace its radial high-pass (which boosts fingers too) with the periodic notch residual.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark run under the fixed protocol (5 seeds, clean-49 + E1); as a prior arm, kill if crack IoU < +0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use only the proxy, as a second post-processing arm next to PV-Vision. Fit the percentile and dilation radius per source, because BMRK and SDLE contrast differ. Do not adopt the network: its PVEL-S binary results say nothing about our 1-2 px jittered labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Same harness as PV-Vision. Arm: dark-in-dilated-crack rule ORed with model inactive, or ANDed with p(inactive) > 0.05. Baseline PF / PF ensemble. Metric: CV and E1 inactive IoU. Kill if gain < +0.02 or precision drop > 0.05.

title: Do we really need dice? The hidden region-size biases of segmentation losses
mechanism: CE and Dice share a ground-truth matching term and differ in an implicit region-size penalty; replace it with an explicit L1 or KL term matching predicted class proportions to the target.
adaptation: CE + per-image proportion term on crack and inactive, replacing soft Dice; gives explicit control over crack predicted area (width), i.e. the precision-recall balance now set by a post-hoc logit bias.
min_experiment: Arm CE + L1 proportion term vs SUP100, 5 v 5. Kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and no relR@2 gain at relP@2 >= 0.90.
evidence: R: theory plus experiments over several losses and applications showing explicit size terms match or beat Dice (abstract; numbers not read).
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: CE + per-image proportion term on crack and inactive replacing soft Dice; gives direct control of predicted crack width instead of a post-hoc logit bias.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: CE + L1 proportion term, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012 and no relR@2 gain at relP@2 >= 0.90.

alt_notes.adaptation: Per-image crack and inactive proportion term in place of soft Dice; controls predicted crack area that today needs a val-chosen logit bias.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: CE + KL proportion term, 5 seeds. Baseline: house (CE + Dice). Metrics: crack IoU at argmax, pixel P/R balance, relF1@2. Kill: argmax crack IoU < house.

title: Rethinking the Hyperparameters for Fine-tuning
mechanism: Optimal effective lr and momentum for fine-tuning depend on source-target similarity; reference-based regularisation can fail for dissimilar datasets.
adaptation: Run the never-run grid: encoder lr {1e-4,3e-4,1e-3} x decoder lr {1e-3,3e-3} x beta1 {0.9,0.95}, on module-grouped 5-fold CV. Also warns that EL is dissimilar to ImageNet, so L2-SP / SPD may need small lambda.
evidence: Extensive transfer benchmarks (classification); momentum and effective lr matter; regularisation toward init not always helpful on dissimilar data.
min_experiment: 12 cells x 5 folds x 2 seeds vs house and PF cells. Metric: CV crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU. Kill if best cell is within CV noise of PF.
prior_overlap: none. lr fixed at 1e-3 Adam (PF 0.1x on encoder) in every run so far.

alt_notes.adaptation: Grid never run: optimizer {Adam + L2 (house), AdamW} x encoder lr {1e-3, 3e-4, 1e-4} x layer-wise lr decay {1.0, 0.7} on module-grouped 5-fold CV, 2 seeds per cell, decoder lr fixed at 1e-3.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: 12-cell grid on CV, best cell rerun 5 seeds. Baseline: house and SUP100-PF. Metric: CV crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, then test and E1. Kill: best cell within 0.012 crack relF1@2 and 0.02 inactive IoU of PF.

title: Self-Training With Noisy Student Improves ImageNet Classification
mechanism: Iterated self-training. The student is equal to or larger than the teacher, is noised (dropout, stochastic depth, RandAugment), learns from soft pseudo-labels, and then becomes the next teacher.
adaptation: Round 2 after ensemble distillation. The distilled student relabels the pool, and a larger student (U-Net++ R50 under PF, or the ViT-B hybrid) is trained with noise that does not resample labelled 1-2 px masks.
min_experiment: Round-2 student vs round-1 student (ensemble-distilled PF). Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: round 2 adds < +0.005 crack IoU and < +0.02 inactive IoU.
evidence: R: ImageNet top-1 88.4% using 300M unlabelled images, +2.0 over the prior SOTA, with large robustness gains on ImageNet-A/C/P.
prior_overlap: Partial. The SSL row used a single online round of Mean Teacher. An iterated, larger, noised student was not run. Note that ResNet-50 was worse on inactive under the house fine-tune.

title: Synth4Seg: Learning Defect Data Synthesis for Defect Segmentation using Bi-level Optimization
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
mechanism: Online Cut&Paste of defects onto labelled training images. Bi-level optimisation learns a heat map of pasting locations and weights for the augmentation sources by minimising validation loss.
evidence: MVTec products, U-Net with ResNet18, limited data. Learned locations beat random by +18.3% (Screw) and +12.2% (Capsule). Learned source weights add up to +2.6% (Tile). Poisson blending gave no gain over direct paste (local full text, Sec III-A).
adaptation: Paste crack components onto labelled train cells with full supervision, not onto pool cells, using same-source pastes only so label width matches the source's convention. Cheap version first: a rule-based location map built from per-source crack start points near busbars and cell edges and from orientation histograms on the train masks. Bi-level version: train a location net against the 54 val cells.
min_experiment: PF+crack paste onto labelled cells (rule map) vs PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: test crack IoU and relF1@2 on clean 49, the CP100 E3b decoy rate, and false crack pixels on 31 crack-free val cells. Kill if crack IoU gain < +0.012 or decoy rate > 2x PF.
prior_overlap: Partial. CP100 (crack paste, n.d., decoys 4.4x) used unlabelled pool cells, random placement, loss only on the mask and ring, and the house optimizer. Pasting onto labelled cells, learned or rule-based placement, and PF are all still open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Cheap form first: crack paste between labelled cells with a rule location map (start near busbars / edges, per-source orientation histogram; 50% of EL cracks parallel to busbars). Bi-level form only if it passes, tuned on 54 val cells.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+CPL vs PF, 5 seeds; test crack IoU and relF1@2, decoy rate, false crack px on 31 crack-free val cells. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012 or decoy rate > 2x PF.

alt_notes.adaptation: Learn placement relative to busbars, cell edges and scuffs, and weights over synthetic sources (generators in this file and D06 renderers), with module-grouped CV crack relF1@2 or F51 as the validation objective.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Learned placement vs random placement of the same synthetic cracks, on PF. Metric CV crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2. Kill: < +0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Learn crack placement relative to busbars, edges, scuffs, and weights over our synthetic sources, against module-grouped CV crack relF1@2.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Learned vs random placement of the same synthetic cracks. Metric CV and E1 relF1@2. Kill: < +0.01. About 30 GPU-h.

title: UNet 3+: A Full-Scale Connected UNet for Medical Image Segmentation (classification-guided module)
mechanism: An image-level presence classifier on the deepest features multiplies the segmentation output, removing over-segmentation in negative images.
adaptation: Two binary heads, inactive-present and crack-present, trained with BCE on mask-derived labels (42 inactive-positive train cells). Use a soft gate (p_seg x p_img) so that one missed cell does not zero its whole mask. Keep the val-chosen threshold.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + presence heads with soft gate (hard gate as a second setting). Baseline: PF. Metrics: inactive precision and IoU (CV and clean 49), E1 inactive IoU. Kill if the inactive IoU gain is < 0.02 or the inactive recall drop is > 0.03.
evidence: R: the abstract says the module reduces over-segmentation in non-organ images, on 2 datasets. The abstract page gives no numbers.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Two binary heads (inactive-present, crack-present), soft gate p_seg(inactive) x p_img(inactive); 42 positive cells so soft gate only, val-chosen threshold kept.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + presence heads, soft gate vs hard gate; baseline PF; metrics inactive precision and IoU (CV), E1 inactive IoU; kill if inactive CV IoU gain < 0.02.

title: Multiclass Boundary Refinement with Neural Cellular Automata for Remote Sensing Land Cover Segmentation
mechanism: Extends rNCA to multiclass: an NCA updates class probabilities of a frozen segmenter in log space so they stay on the simplex, with free hidden channels, correcting boundary position error cell by cell.
adaptation: Multiclass refiner over our 24-class softmax so crack, inactive, gridline and background pixels are traded jointly; train on out-of-fold maps; most useful for inactive borders and crack/inactive overlap.
min_experiment: Arm: house ensemble + multiclass NCA. Baseline: house ensemble. Metrics: inactive IoU, crack IoU, mIoU_rob, boundary IoU on 5-fold CV. Kill: inactive IoU < +0.01 and mIoU_rob < +0.005.
evidence: R: mean boundary IoU 46.63 -> 48.99 over the frozen base; +8.5 BIoU on the most irregular class (woodland).
prior_overlap: none.

title: The Treasure Beneath Multiple Annotations: An Uncertainty-Aware Edge Detector
mechanism: Model multiple annotations as a learnable per-pixel Gaussian; variance is the uncertainty; loss re-weighted toward uncertain pixels.
adaptation: Treat the 2021 and 2022 crack label versions as two annotators; sample one per iteration; learn mean and variance; read out the mean. Variance map also feeds a benchmark uncertainty view.
min_experiment: Arm = PF with UAED crack head on both label versions; baseline = PF on 2022 labels; 5 seeds + CV; metrics crack IoU (2022 labels), relF1@2. Kill if IoU drops > 0.01 with no relF1@2 gain.
evidence: R: CVPR 2023 SOTA on multi-annotator edge sets (BSDS); numbers not read.
prior_overlap: None; old labels were never used as a second annotator.

alt_notes.adaptation: Take per-pixel disagreement from the 2021 vs 2022 crack label versions. Run it as a sub-arm of the RankED test, because RankED reports the opposite weighting works better.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Sub-arm of the RankED experiment. Baseline: house at 100% labels. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Disagreement from 2021 vs 2022 crack masks on the same cells; Gaussian label on crack logit. Run as a sub-arm of the RankED test because RankED found the opposite weighting better.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Sub-arm of RankED test: house + UAED weighting, 5 seeds vs house. Kill if crack IoU and relF1@2 n.d.

title: LiNeS: Post-training Layer Scaling Prevents Forgetting and Enhances Model Merging
mechanism: Post-training edit: scale each layer's fine-tuning delta linearly with depth, shallow layers near pretrained, deep layers keep the task update.
adaptation: Zero training on house and PF checkpoints; scale encoder deltas by depth, plus the inverse ordering because our erasure sits in layer3/4; BN stats recomputed; scale chosen on val.
evidence: Reduces forgetting and improves OOD generalisation and multi-task merging in vision and NLP benchmarks (abstract; numbers not retrieved).
min_experiment: Existing checkpoints, val-chosen scale; kill if no setting beats raw by +0.005 val relF1@2.
prior_overlap: none

title: Benefit from public unlabeled data: A Frangi filtering-based pretraining network for 3D cerebrovascular segmentation
mechanism: Multi-task pretraining of the whole segmentation network on unlabeled data, with Frangi-filter-derived thin-structure maps as targets.
adaptation: Pretrain the full U-Net++ (decoder included) on the 11.9k pool, then the 159k, to regress multi-scale dark-ridge maps and the FFT periodic residual. Fine-tune with PF so the pretrained layers survive.
min_experiment: Arm: ridge-target pretraining 40k steps, then PF fine-tune, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF from ImageNet. Metric: crack IoU (CV), E1 relF1@2. Kill: < +0.012 crack IoU and < +0.02 on E1.
evidence: R: 1,510 unlabeled TOF-MRA plus 113 labelled subjects across 4 datasets; about +3% over SOTA semi- and self-supervised methods.
prior_overlap: MIM and DDeP pool pretraining were n.d.; section 5 explicitly leaves dense or thin-structure-aware objectives open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Dark-ridge filter (Frangi on inverted EL, sigma 1 to 2 px, plus black top-hat) on the de-duplicated pool; pretrain full U-Net++ R34 to regress the ridge map plus reconstruct the image; suppress busbar/finger ridges using house structural-class predictions; then house PF fine-tune.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Ridge-target pretraining on 11.9k (~20 GPU-h) then PF vs house PF and vs our MIM checkpoint; out-of-fold relF1@2 and E1 crack recall, 2 seeds; kill if relF1@2 < +0.005 and E1 recall < +0.02.

title: Masked-attention Mask Transformer for Universal Image Segmentation (Mask2Former)
mechanism: Mask classification with masked cross-attention restricted to each query's predicted region over a multi-scale pixel decoder; point-sampled mask loss.
evidence: R: SOTA on ADE20K semantic, COCO panoptic/instance at publication; authors state small-object performance is poor.
adaptation: Semantic mode, Swin-B or R50 from ADE20K weights, 512 and 1024 px, grey replicated; target inactive and region classes (splice, material, edge_dark); raise num_points and add dense CE+Dice aux for crack; keep label-safe augmentation.
min_experiment: Arm A M2F Swin-B 512; arm B + dense aux head; 5-fold CV; baseline house; metrics inactive IoU, splice/material/edge_dark IoU, mIoU_rob; kill B if mIoU_rob < house - 0.01 and inactive IoU not above house.
prior_overlap: none; mask-classification decoders listed as never tried. Also proposed as a baseline by D01/D03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Semantic mode, Swin-B or R50 from ADE20K weights, 512 and 1024 px, 1-ch replicated; target inactive and region classes (splice, material, edge_dark); raise num_points, add dense aux head and high-res conv branch for crack.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Same as GOOSE-M2F arms; arm A plain M2F vs house; metric inactive IoU, mIoU_rob, splice IoU; kill A+B if mIoU_rob < house - 0.01 and inactive not above house.

title: Clinically Applicable Segmentation of Head and Neck Anatomy for Radiotherapy (normalized surface Dice)
mechanism: Surface Dice at tolerance tau, with tau set from measured inter-observer variation, scores boundaries as correct when within tau.
adaptation: tau = 2 px from our measured annotator agreement (0.82-0.99 within 2 px); NSD@1 and @2 for crack, @2 for inactive and thin structural classes (gridline, busbar). Use as decision metric only if it separates known real effects better than strict IoU.
min_experiment: Arm: NSD@1/2/3 on OOF predictions. Baseline: strict crack IoU. Metric: paired t statistic for 5-seed ensemble vs single model (known +0.014-0.018). Kill: NSD@2 t not higher than strict IoU t.
evidence: R: introduced surface Dice with organ-specific tolerances from inter-observer variation on head and neck CT.
prior_overlap: partial: relF1@2 (tolerance F1) is already reported; NSD as decision metric and per-class tau not tested.

title: A Large-scale Evaluation of Pretraining Paradigms for the Detection of Defects in Electroluminescence Solar Cell Images
mechanism: Whole-network dense pretraining (COCO-segmentation DeepLabV3, encoder and decoder) gave the best crack IoU on the BenchmarkEL family; large OOD pretraining beat in-domain SimCLR.
adaptation: Use a full segmentation-pretrained model (ADE20K/COCO UPerNet, SegFormer or Mask2Former), average RGB first-conv weights to 1 channel, PF schedule so the pretraining is kept; avoid ResNet-50 DeepLabV3 since R50 was already worse on inactive here.
min_experiment: Arm ADE20K-pretrained UPerNet or SegFormer + PF vs house PF, 3-seed screen then 5; crack IoU, mIoU_rob, E1 crack relF1@2; kill if crack IoU < house - 0.01 and mIoU_rob not higher.
evidence: R: 642-cell labelled set (28 classes), DeepLabV3-R50; mIoU COCO 0.544, CCT 0.550, ImageNet-SimCLR 0.534, EL-SimCLR 0.517, previous SOTA 0.506; crack IoU: COCO and ImageNet-SimCLR beat all others p <= 0.0001 (block-centred IoU, Tukey HSD).
prior_overlap: Partial: foundation encoders tested as frozen probes plus one ConvNeXt-T fine-tune screen; full-network segmentation pretraining kept by PF never run. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Template for the benchmark's pretraining axis on our protocol (clean splits, tolerant crack metric, E1).
alt_notes.min_experiment: No new arm; reproduce its best pretraining under our protocol inside the benchmark (3 seeds) v house.

alt_notes.adaptation: Initialise the full DeepLabV3-R50 (encoder and decoder) from torchvision COCO weights, 1-channel by summing RGB filters, fine-tune with PF. For the benchmark, adopt block-centred per-image IoU tests.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: COCO-initialised DeepLabV3-R50 under PF. Baselines: same arch with ImageNet encoder only, and house; 5 seeds. Metric: crack and inactive IoU. Kill if crack IoU gain over the ImageNet twin < 0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: Pretrain U-Net++ encoder AND decoder on a dense EL task (UCF-EL 9.5k polygons + MultiSolSegment 585 mapped to a coarse shared class space), then PF fine-tune keeping the decoder; add their 22k unlabelled release to the pool if it is not a duplicate of the 159k.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm dense-EL-pretrained U-Net++ (encoder+decoder) + PF vs PF from ImageNet, 5 seeds, module-grouped 5-fold CV; metrics mIoU_rob and inactive IoU; kill if CV mIoU_rob gain < +0.01 and inactive gain < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Pretrain U-Net++ encoder and decoder on a dense EL task (UCF-EL 9.5k polygons + MultiSolSegment 585 mapped to a coarse 5-class space), then PF fine-tune keeping the decoder; add their 22k unlabelled release to the pool if found.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm dense EL decoder pretraining + PF vs baseline PF from ImageNet, 5 seeds, CV; metric CV mIoU_rob and inactive IoU; kill if mIoU_rob gain < +0.01 and inactive gain < +0.02. About 20 GPU-h.

title: DINOv3
mechanism: Self-supervised ViT-7B with Gram anchoring that keeps dense features clean at scale, distilled into ViT-S to H+ and ConvNeXt T to L students.
adaptation: Backbone for VFM-H: ViT-L/16 (303M) at 1024 px, or ConvNeXt-L (198M) in smp U-Net++ with a stride-2 stem under PF at 20k steps. Weights are gated (licence click), need the user's OK.
min_experiment: Arm: DINOv3 ViT-L/16 in VFM-H, and ConvNeXt-L U-Net++ PF, 20k steps. Baseline: house PF. Metric: CV crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 once. Kill: default line.
evidence: R (web, HF model cards): ViT-L/16 54.9 ADE20k (column order inferred by the search summary, check before citing); distilled family listed. Verified only via WebSearch, not Research MCP.
prior_overlap: partial: DINOv3 ConvNeXt-T under PF, 2 seeds, 4k steps, F51 crack AP: KILL (no sign of a gain). ViT-L, ConvNeXt-L, 1024 px and 20k steps untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Default VFM for the Rein, Dino U-Net and dual-branch arms: ViT-L/16 at 1024 px; gated weights need the user's OK; DINOv2-L and C-RADIOv4 are fallbacks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Backbone arm inside VFM-H vs DINOv2-L; E1 relF1@2; drop if more than 0.02 below the best backbone.

title: Rethinking Efficient Crack Segmentation with Task-Aligned Structural-Directional Modeling (RIFT)
mechanism: Treats crack segmentation as sparse structural recovery: local-evidence blocks, large directional strip kernels that aggregate continuity along orientations, and a light multi-scale decoder; 0.47 to 1.69 M parameters.
adaptation: (a) Benchmark row: RIFT-B on crack + inactive + background, 1-channel stem, 512 px, BCE-Dice. (b) Model arm: fuse RIFT crack logits with the house model (heterogeneous ensemble) or graft the directional block as a crack branch at strides 1-2 of the U-Net++ decoder. Check strip kernels against busbars and fingers, which are long straight lines.
min_experiment: Arm A RIFT-B alone; arm B PF + RIFT crack logit average; baselines PF single and PF 2-seed ensemble; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill arm B if it does not beat the 2-seed PF ensemble by +0.01 CV crack IoU or +0.03 E1 relF1@2; keep arm A as a benchmark row.
evidence: R: best or tied-best on 16 metrics across DeepCrack, CamCrack789, CrackMap, Crack500 (3 seeds); cross-dataset average 2-class mIoU 77.0 vs SCSegamba 74.6 and MixerCSeg 71.0; clDice 90.6.
prior_overlap: none. No crack-specific architecture or heterogeneous ensemble has been run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark baseline with a 24-class head. Its directional-continuity block is a candidate drop-in for the U-Net++ decoder. Its protocol (reproduced baselines plus topology-aware evaluation) is a template for the EL benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark row vs house, 3 seeds. Block-in-house arm: kill if crack relF1@2 and components found both gain < 0.012.

title: RWKV-UNet: Improving UNet with Long-Range Cooperation for Effective Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Encoder of Global-Local Spatial Perception blocks mixing convolutions with RWKV linear attention, plus a Cross-Channel Mix module for multi-scale skip fusion.
adaptation: 1-channel input, 512 px. RWKV gives global context (busbar grid, half-cut edge, scuff orientation) at linear cost, while conv branches keep 1 px crack detail. Train with both the house recipe and the PF fine-tune.
min_experiment: RWKV-UNet against house and house PF, 3 seeds, 20k steps; metric E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, test-49 crack IoU. Kill: under +0.03 E1 relF1@2, or test crack IoU worse by more than 0.01.
evidence: R: SOTA claimed on 11 datasets. In the independent U-Bench (28 2D datasets) it ranks top-1 IoU both in-domain and zero-shot.
prior_overlap: none

title: Vision Transformer Adapter for Dense Predictions
mechanism: A pretraining-free conv spatial-prior branch with injector/extractor cross-attention turns a plain ViT into a multi-scale dense backbone.
adaptation: DINOv3 ViT-B/16 or L/16 + ViT-Adapter feeding the U-Net++ decoder, plus a stride-1/2 conv stem skip for 1-2 px lines; 1-ch input replicated; PF-style schedule with layer-wise lr decay.
min_experiment: Arm: ViT-L + Adapter + U-Net++ (PF); baseline: house PF; 5-fold CV crack IoU, inactive IoU, then E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 and CV crack IoU n.d.
evidence: R: ViT-Adapter-L 60.9 box AP / 53.0 mask AP on COCO test-dev; used by DINOv2 for its segmentation evaluation (web search, not tool-verified).
prior_overlap: Foundation row: no ViT fine-tune or adapter was run. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: DINOv3 ViT-B/16 or L/16 + ViT-Adapter feeding a U-Net++ decoder plus a stride-1/2 conv stem skip; 1-ch input replicated; PF-style schedule (frozen 1k steps, 0.1x lr, layer-wise lr decay).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm ViT-Adapter-DINOv3-B + U-Net++ vs house PF on 5-fold CV crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob, then E1. Kill: E1 crack relF1@2 < +0.03 and CV crack IoU drop > 0.012. About 25 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: ViT-B DINOv2 + adapter + M2F or UPerNet at 1024 px; the conv prior gives a 1/4-res path that thin cracks and gridlines need; use if EoMT-L memory/time is a problem or ViT-B is preferred.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm ViT-B DINOv2 + ViT-Adapter + UPerNet, 5-fold CV; baseline house PF; metrics mIoU_rob, inactive IoU, E1 relF1@2; kill if all below house.

alt_notes.adaptation: ViT-B DINOv2 + adapter + M2F or UPerNet at 1024 px; the conv branch supplies the fine path thin cracks need, where EoMT at ViT-B loses most.
alt_notes.min_experiment: ViT-B DINOv2 + adapter + UPerNet vs EoMT-B and house, 5-fold; metric crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob; kill if below EoMT-B and house on all three.

title: nnWNet: Rethinking the Use of Transformers in Biomedical Image Segmentation and Calling for a Unified Evaluation Benchmark
mechanism: W-shaped network that keeps global (transformer) and local (conv) features flowing continuously across multiple resolutions (HRNet-like), integrated into the nnU-Net framework for unified benchmarking.
adaptation: Drop-in nnU-Net trainer, so it runs on our splits with the same recipe as the nnU-Net and ResEnc arms; label-safe augmentation. Keeping a full-resolution stream suits 1 to 2 px cracks.
min_experiment: nnWNet on the module-grouped folds against nnU-Net org and ResEnc M; CV-mean crack relF1@2, crack IoU and E1 relF1@2. Kill: CV-mean crack relF1@2 not above ResEnc M by 1 fold SD.
evidence: R: state of the art claimed on 2D DRIVE (retinal vessels), ISIC-2017, Kvasir-SEG and CREMI (EM membranes), and on 3D Parse2022, AMOS22, BTCV, ImageCAS, against nnU-Net and transformer baselines. Exact DRIVE/CREMI numbers not retrieved.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Run its 2D trainer on our nnU-Net dataset folder (1 channel, 512 px, 24 classes, label-safe aug, same folds). Hypothesis: the global stream separates long scuff streaks on half-cut E1 cells from local cracks while the conv stream keeps 1-2 px detail.
alt_notes.min_experiment: nnWNet 2D 5 folds v nnU-Net arm A winner and house 5-seed ensemble. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and recall, CV crack relF1@2. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 over arm A and CV crack relF1@2 not up 0.01.

title: Rethinking Transfer Learning for Industrial Inspection: DINOv3 vs. ImageNet Pretraining Across RGB and X-ray Tasks
mechanism: Controlled comparison: DINOv3-distilled ConvNeXt is no better frozen but a much better initialisation under full long fine-tuning on RGB industrial segmentation; worse on greyscale X-ray.
evidence: R (full text): Severstal frozen 62.40 vs 62.04 mIoU; full fine-tune DINOv3 ConvNeXt-T +10.29 mIoU over ImageNet ConvNeXt-T, +10.59 over R50 (Mask2Former default schedule). GDXray: ImageNet 21.32 vs 7.88 AP50 frozen, 29.74 vs 27.84 fine-tuned.
adaptation: Redo A8 properly: DINOv3 ConvNeXt-S/B in smp U-Net++ with stride-2 stem, full fine-tune (not PF), 20k steps, vs ImageNet ConvNeXt of the same size. EL is greyscale like X-ray, so expect a null; it is cheap and closes the question.
min_experiment: DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B vs ImageNet ConvNeXt-B, 3 seeds + 5-fold CV; metric CV crack IoU / relF1@2, inactive IoU; kill if DINOv3 not above ImageNet by 0.01 crack IoU.
prior_overlap: A8 tested ConvNeXt-T under PF at 4k steps on F51 AP only; full fine-tune, 20k steps, larger ConvNeXt untested. Partly open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: include ConvNeXt-T ImageNet and ConvNeXt-T DINOv3 rows under the same fine-tune for 1-ch near-IR EL; prior that general FMs are not automatically better on EL.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark row pair only; no separate arm.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: include ConvNeXt-T ImageNet and ConvNeXt-T DINOv3 rows under one fine-tune on 1-ch EL; prior that a general FM is not automatically better under greyscale modality shift.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark row pair only (already partly screened: DINOv3 ConvNeXt-T PF 4k steps, no sign); extend to full 20k schedule on folds.

title: Estimating label quality and errors in semantic segmentation data via any model
mechanism: Image label-quality score = soft-minimum of out-of-sample likelihood of each pixel's given class (cleanlab segmentation, built on confident learning doi:10.1613/jair.1.12125).
adaptation: Run cleanlab find_label_issues on the same out-of-fold softmax maps as the ensemble-ranking arm; zero extra training; standard baseline for the benchmark's label audit.
min_experiment: Arm: cleanlab ranking. Baseline: ensemble ranking (Nogueira-style). Metric: precision at 24 vs audit-flagged cells. Kill: none, kept as baseline row; drop from training arms if precision below ensemble ranking.
evidence: R: soft-min score best of 7 for detecting mislabeled images in SYNTHIA with DeepLabV3+/FPN. Nogueira 2026 measured cleanlab tau 0.17, worst on deletions.
prior_overlap: none.

title: RERN: Rich Edge Features Refinement Detection Network for Polycrystalline Solar Cell Defect Segmentation
mechanism: Edge-detection formulation of defect segmentation with bidirectional strip refinement attention (long-range horizontal and vertical context plus channel context), lightweight and pluggable; evaluated with tolerance-based ODS F-measure.
adaptation: Insert strip attention into the last two U-Net++ decoder stages; aimed at gridline (recall 0.33, long straight lines) and long cracks. Use their tolerant ODS/OIS idea as a benchmark crack metric alongside relF1@2.
min_experiment: Arm house + strip attention vs house, 5 seeds; gridline IoU/recall and crack relF1@2; kill if gridline IoU < +0.03 and crack relF1@2 not up.
evidence: R: ODS F 0.854 on their PSCDE poly-Si defect edge dataset at maxDist 0.0015; BSRA also improved other edge networks on PSCDE.
prior_overlap: none: edge-detection formulations and strip attention never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Insert BSRA (directional strip pooling) into U-Net++ decoder blocks and train crack with class-balanced edge BCE. For the benchmark, report ODS/OIS at maxDist = 2 px alongside relF1@2.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: U-Net++ + BSRA. Baseline: house, 5 seeds. Metric: relF1@2, crack components >= 20 px found. Kill if relF1@2 < +0.01.

title: Bilateral Reference for High-Resolution Dichotomous Image Segmentation (BiRefNet)
mechanism: Reconstruction module re-injects hierarchical raw image patches at each decoder stage (source reference) and uses gradient maps as target reference with auxiliary gradient supervision, for very thin high-res structures.
adaptation: Cheap: pixel-unshuffle the raw 512 px EL cell into each decoder scale of U-Net++ and add a gradient-map auxiliary loss restricted to a 3 px band around crack and gridline labels. Bench: BiRefNet as a binary crack segmenter at 512 px.
min_experiment: Arm: house PF + image re-injection + band gradient loss; baseline: house PF; CV gridline IoU and crack IoU. Kill if gridline IoU < +0.03 and crack IoU n.d.
evidence: R: abstract claims best results on four tasks (DIS, HRSOD, COD, etc.); numbers not retrieved.
prior_overlap: R5 (2x input) n.d. covers more pixels per crack, not raw-image re-injection or gradient supervision. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Pixel-unshuffle the raw 512 px EL cell into each decoder scale of U-Net++; gradient-map auxiliary loss only in a 3 px band around crack and gridline labels so it does not learn grain texture. Also run full BiRefNet as a binary crack bench entry.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house PF + image re-injection + banded gradient loss vs house PF; 5-fold CV crack relF1@2, gridline IoU; kill: gridline < +0.03 and crack n.d. About 12 GPU-h.

title: Spatially resolved electrical modelling of cracks and other inhomogeneities in crystalline silicon solar cells
mechanism: Quasi-SPICE network model of active and inactive microcracks built from EL damage maps; a cell region becomes inactive when cracks cut it off electrically from the busbars.
adaptation: Rule renderer for inactive: draw a crack curve on a train cell with crack but no inactive, compute regions isolated from every busbar along the finger direction, darken them by the source-specific inactive/active intensity ratio measured on the 42 train inactive cells (plus noise and edge blur), label inactive and crack. Gives pairs that respect 'inactive always touches a crack'. Also yields inactive-area fraction for severity bands.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + rule-rendered crack+inactive cells, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF 5 seeds. Metric: module-grouped 5-fold CV inactive IoU and BMRK inactive IoU. Kill: CV inactive IoU gain < +0.02.
evidence: R: model validated on experimental cells; 0.12% error in power-loss estimate for a complexly damaged cell. No ML or image-synthesis evidence.
prior_overlap: None; physics simulation of EL is listed as never tried.

title: Bootstrapping Semantic Segmentation with Regional Contrast (ReCo)
mechanism: Supervised pixel-level contrastive loss on a sparse set of hard negative pixels with small memory footprint.
adaptation: Projection head on the full-res decoder stage (1/4 res would erase 1-2 px cracks); class-balanced anchor sampling with per-class caps; hard negatives for crack drawn from scuff, gridline and busbar pixels.
min_experiment: Arm: ReCo loss weight 0.1 on top of the best loss/sampling arm, 3 seeds; baseline that arm; metric crack relF1@2, mIoU_rob, E1 crack recall; kill if no metric gains >= 0.01.
evidence: R: consistent gains in supervised and semi-supervised seg; strongest with very few labels (5 examples per class).
prior_overlap: none: pixel contrast never tried (MIM/DDeP pretraining is a different objective).

title: Task-specific knowledge distillation from the vision foundation model for enhanced medical image segmentation
mechanism: Fine-tune a VFM on the target task, then distil it into a small segmentation network.
adaptation: Only if a VFM-H arm helps E1: distil it into house U-Net++ R34 with soft labels on 478 labelled + 11.9k pool cells, keeping the cheap model for deployment and ensembles.
min_experiment: Arm: R34 student distilled from the best VFM-H arm. Baseline: house PF. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, clean-49 crack IoU. Kill: student keeps less than half of the teacher's E1 gain.
evidence: R: abstract fragment; medical segmentation with limited target data; numbers not read.
prior_overlap: none: distillation is listed as never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Only if a VFM-H arm wins: distil its soft logits into house U-Net++ R34 on labelled cells + 11.9k pool as transfer set.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Distilled R34 vs house PF; E1 relF1@2 and CV crack relF1@2; kill if the student keeps less than half the teacher's E1 gain.

title: TopoLoRA-SAM: Topology-Aware Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Foundation Segmenters for Thin-Structure and Cross-Domain Binary Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: LoRA in frozen SAM ViT-B plus a depthwise-separable conv adapter on the image embedding, prompt-free decoding, optional clDice.
adaptation: Use LoRA + conv adapter, drop clDice; 1024 input; multi-class head instead of binary.
evidence: R: best retina-average Dice 0.595 and overall avg Dice 0.735 vs Mask2Former 0.709; LoRA +4.2 Dice over decoder-only; conv adapter +1.2 BFScore. Absolute retina numbers are low.
min_experiment: LoRA+conv-adapter arm in the PEFT grid vs plain LoRA; crack IoU, relF1@2; kill if < plain LoRA + 0.01.
prior_overlap: Soft clDice failed here (Loss row), so the clDice part is closed; LoRA + adapter is open.

alt_notes.adaptation: SAM ViT-B/L at 1024, 24-class decoder, no clDice (soft clDice failed here), LoRA rank 16 and 32, house loss.
alt_notes.min_experiment: LoRA-SAM + conv adapter vs house PF, 5-fold CV then 3 seeds; default kill line (CV crack relF1@2 -0.005, E1 +0.03).

title: NWG-DETR: grid-line-aware wavelet-gated RT-DETR for photovoltaic electroluminescence defect detection
mechanism: Dark-contrast gating, cross-polarisation gating that attenuates repetitive grid-line artefacts, and learnable wavelet pool/unpool that keeps high-frequency defect detail.
adaptation: Take the learnable wavelet pool for the U-Net++ stem and unpool for the decoder, and the grid-line gate on the two highest-resolution skips; detector parts discarded.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + learnable wavelet pool + grid-line skip gate; baseline PF; kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.02. Only after Seg-Aliasing or HWD passes.
evidence: R: PVEL-AD mAP50 +3.77 over RT-DETR-r18, 45% fewer parameters.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace the ResNet-34 stem max-pool and first stride with Haar wavelet downsampling (keep LH/HL/HH as channels) so 1 to 2 px cracks survive the 4x stem; gate using our own predicted gridline / busbar maps.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with wavelet stem. Baseline: house, 5 v 5 seeds. Metric: crack components >= 20 px found, crack IoU. Kill if components found gain < 0.02.

title: Training Like a Medical Resident: Context-Prior Learning Toward Universal Medical Image Segmentation (Hermes)
mechanism: A universal segmentation model with learned task and modality prior tokens, trained jointly on many heterogeneous, partially labelled datasets.
adaptation: Prior tokens for the 5 BenchmarkEL sources plus UCF-EL. UCF-EL's region-style crack (crack plus inactive) then trains jointly without overwriting the thin-crack convention, and the encoder is not erased because training is joint.
min_experiment: Arm = joint BenchmarkEL + UCF-EL with dataset tokens (3 seeds) versus house PF. Metrics: crack IoU, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if all gains are < 0.012.
evidence: R: CT/MRI/PET multi-dataset universal segmentation, gains over task-specific and other universal models (abstract level).
prior_overlap: UCF-EL pretrain-then-finetune was n.d. or worse, but the fine-tune erased the encoder. Joint training with dataset priors is open

alt_notes.adaptation: Prior tokens = {5 BenchmarkEL sources, UCF-EL, MultiSolSegment}; an alternative to per-dataset channels for joint EL training.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: prior-token joint training (BenchmarkEL + UCF-EL), 5 seeds vs house PF on BenchmarkEL only; metrics clean-49 crack IoU and E1 relF1@2; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 and test IoU not up by +0.012.

title: XCT-SAM: Sequential Parameter-Efficient Domain Adaptation of SAM for Industrial XCT Defect Segmentation
mechanism: Sequential PEFT stages adapt SAM first to the general modality and then to the defect task, under severe class imbalance and scan-condition shift.
adaptation: Greyscale industrial defects, closest industrial match. Stage 1 adapter on all EL data (5 sources + UCF-EL crack/inactive region masks), stage 2 adapter on BenchmarkEL 24 classes with stage 1 frozen, to keep the broad EL features for E1.
min_experiment: Arm: two-stage PEFT on VFM-H. Baseline: single-stage VFM-H and house PF. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, CV crack relF1@2. Kill: E1 relF1@2 not +0.02 over single stage or CV drop > 0.005.
evidence: R: abstract fragment only; additive-manufacturing XCT; numbers not read.
prior_overlap: partial: UCF-EL encoder pretraining was erased by the house fine-tune (n.d.); a frozen-stage adapter keeps it, which BRIEF lists as open.

title: Dice Semimetric Losses: Optimizing the Dice Score with Soft Labels
mechanism: Dice loss that equals soft Dice on hard labels but is minimised at prediction = target for soft labels.
adaptation: Drop-in replacement for the house soft Dice in every soft-target arm (KD, SVLS, GeoLS, SoftSeg, dilated labels); run DML vs house soft Dice on the same soft targets to show whether the house loss breaks.
min_experiment: Inside the SVLS arm: SVLS+DML vs SVLS+house soft Dice, 5 v 5. Metric crack IoU; kill if DML - soft Dice < +0.012 (then the soft-Dice issue does not matter here).
evidence: R (web summary): better Dice and calibration than soft Dice with soft labels on QUBIQ, LiTS, KiTS; numbers not read.
prior_overlap: Dice on 3 classes (hard labels) n.d.; DML is identical there, so only the soft-label use is open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Drop-in replacement for the house soft Dice in every soft-target arm (KD, SVLS, GeoLS, SAUNA); paired check DML vs house soft Dice on the same soft targets.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Run inside the SVLS arm: SVLS+DML vs SVLS+house Dice, 5 seeds; metric crack IoU; kill if difference < 0.012 (then the house Dice is fine).

title: HarmonySeg: Tubular Structure Segmentation with Deep-Shallow Feature Fusion and Growth-Suppression Balanced Loss
mechanism: Vesselness map fused with image via deep mutual query and shallow query attention; growth-suppression loss: relaxed supervision outside annotated regions, reconnection pseudo-labels, spatial feature prior, mixup equivalence; built for incomplete labels.
adaptation: Use only the loss: no background penalty within 3 px of crack labels (relaxed term) plus mixup-equivalence consistency; add attention fusion of a ridge map only if the vesselness-input arm shows a signal.
min_experiment: Arm: house + relaxed term + mixup-equivalence, 5 seeds; baseline house. Metric relR@2 at matched relP@2, crack IoU. Kill: relR@2 gain < 0.01 at equal relP@2.
evidence: Hepatic vessels: GSB lifts nnU-Net Dice 60.15 -> 64.00 (terms +2.94, +1.11, +1.67, +2.01 alone); D2SD +5.1 Dice; beats DSC-Net and SR-loss nnU-Net on 3 of 4 external strata; plain concatenation of vesselness gave no notable gain.
prior_overlap: Offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) is close to the relaxed term (partly closed); mixup-equivalence and reconnection terms untested

alt_notes.adaptation: Compute a multi-scale dark-ridge Hessian map (Sato or Frangi, sigma 1 to 3 px) per cell. Feed it as a parallel stream, not by concatenation, since their ablation found concatenation useless. The relaxed-supervision term fits our missed or partial crack labels (24 of 239 audited cells were flagged).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Ridge-stream fusion vs a concat control vs house, 5 seeds. Metrics: test crack relF1@2 and E1 crack recall. Kill if it beats neither the concat control nor house by >= 0.012.

title: Improving Representation of High-frequency Components for Medical Visual Foundation Models (Frepa)
mechanism: MAE-style pretraining with high-frequency masking, low-frequency perturbation and embedding consistency so the encoder represents fine high-frequency detail; extended to Swin and ConvNets.
adaptation: Cracks are high-frequency dark lines; scuffs, source contrast and style are low-frequency. Run Frepa's ConvNeXt variant on the de-duplicated pool at 512 px 1-ch; the low-frequency perturbation doubles as source/scuff invariance for E1. PF fine-tune in U-Net++. Code reported by web search at github.com/arturia-pendragon-iris/frepa (not opened).
min_experiment: ConvNeXt Frepa pretraining on 11.9k (~40 GPU-h) + PF vs ConvNeXt ImageNet PF; out-of-fold relF1@2, E1 crack recall, inactive IoU; kill if all below +0.01.
evidence: R: 9 modalities, 32 downstream tasks; up to +15% Dice on retinal vessels over other SSL.
prior_overlap: none: our MIM used pixel targets on R34; frequency-targeted pretraining untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Cracks are high-frequency dark lines a few px wide; scuff, contrast and source effects are low-frequency. Pretrain ConvNeXt-T (and R34 as a cheap control) on the de-duplicated 11.9k pool at 512 px, 1-ch; low-frequency perturbation doubles as source / scuff invariance for E1. PF fine-tune in smp U-Net++.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: ConvNeXt-T U-Net++ from Frepa-style continued pretraining (~100 epochs, 11.9k), PF. Baseline: ConvNeXt-T ImageNet init, PF. Metrics: cv5v2 out-of-fold crack relF1@2, E1 crack recall, inactive IoU, 2 seeds. Kill if all three < +0.01.

title: Learning robust medical image segmentation from multi-source annotations (UMA-Net)
mechanism: Pixel-level annotation-uncertainty estimates weight the loss, and an image-level quality module routes each sample to a high-quality or a low-quality decoder head.
adaptation: Image quality is set from source and label-width deviation: BMRK, SDLE and the speck-level H36 labels go to the low-quality head. Pixel weights come from 5-seed disagreement. The high-quality head is used at test.
min_experiment: Arm: two-head routing by source quality, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: BMRK crack and inactive IoU, overall crack IoU. Kill if the BMRK crack IoU gain is below 0.03.
evidence: R (web abstract): on simulated JSRT lung data, +5.31% over single-annotation noise-robust methods and +1.47% over multi-source methods; tested on chest X-ray, fundus and breast DCE-MRI.
prior_overlap: none

title: Unlocking Robust Semantic Segmentation Performance via Label-only Elastic Deformations against Implicit Label Noise (NSegment+)
mechanism: Elastic deformation applied to labels only (image untouched), resampled every epoch, to model implicit boundary noise; small segments exempted.
adaptation: Invert the small-object rule: apply smooth 0.5 to 1.5 px deformation to crack and inactive labels only (sigma 4 to 8 px, p 0.5), never to structural classes. One dataloader change.
min_experiment: Arm: house + label-only jitter. Baseline: house. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if both < house + 0.005. About 6 GPU-h.
evidence: R: mIoU +2.29 Vaihingen, +2.38 LoveDA, +1.75 Cityscapes, +3.39 VOC; vs LNL methods with DeepLabV3+: +0.81 Vaihingen, +0.63 Cityscapes, beating AIO2, L2B, UCE, Compensation Learning.
prior_overlap: partial: offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) also targets shift tolerance; label-only stochastic jitter is a different regulariser and untested.

title: Diverse Weight Averaging for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
mechanism: Average weights of independent runs with different hyperparameters from a shared init; weight averaging helps most when the input distribution shifts.
adaptation: Fork 8 runs from one PF checkpoint varying lr, Dice weights, synthetic half-cut views, Skeleton Recall 0.1; average weights for one E1-robust model.
min_experiment: Arm: DiWA of 8 forks. Baseline: their output ensemble and singles. Metric: E1 relF1@2, test crack IoU. Kill: DiWA below mean single.
evidence: R: improves state of the art on DomainBed without inference overhead; bias-variance-covariance-locality decomposition.
prior_overlap: none

title: FlexiCrackNet: A Flexible Pipeline for Enhanced Crack Segmentation with General Features Transfered from SAM
mechanism: Task-specific encoder-decoder plus a frozen EdgeSAM CNN encoder used only as a generic feature extractor, fused by gated attention (IGAM); better zero-shot and robustness.
adaptation: Keep house ResNet-34 U-Net++; add a frozen side encoder (EdgeSAM or the DINOv3 ConvNeXt-T already used in the probe study) fused at each skip by a learned gate. Frozen features cannot be erased by fine-tuning, making the PF finding structural.
min_experiment: Arm: dual encoder with gated fusion; baseline: PF; 3 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, CV crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 and E1 inactive gain < +0.05 with CV crack IoU within 0.01.
evidence: R: claims SOTA, better zero-shot generalization and robustness on blurry inputs and complex backgrounds (numbers not in abstract).
prior_overlap: Section 5 fine-tuned DINOv3 ConvNeXt-T as the only encoder (2 seeds, 4k steps, F51 judged); a frozen side branch fused with the ImageNet ResNet-34 is untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: House ResNet-34 U-Net++ plus a frozen side encoder (EdgeSAM or the DINOv3 ConvNeXt-T on disk) fused at each skip through a learned gate; the frozen branch cannot be erased by fine-tuning.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + frozen side encoder with gated fusion; baseline PF; 3 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, CV crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 and E1 inactive gain < +0.05.

title: Generalizable Knowledge Distillation from Vision Foundation Models for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Two-stage KD from a VFM. Stage 1 distils domain-agnostic features into the student by query-based soft feature distillation. Stage 2 freezes those features and trains the task head, so the student keeps the VFM's out-of-domain robustness.
adaptation: Stage 1: distil DINOv2-L or DINOv3 patch features into the ResNet-34 encoder on the 11.9k pool (or the 159k pool). Stage 2: house training under PF so the distilled encoder is not erased. Target: E1 generalisation.
min_experiment: Arm: GKD-initialised R34 + PF fine-tune, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF from ImageNet. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, clean-49 crack IoU. Kill: E1 metrics within noise of PF and no test gain.
evidence: R: average gains +1.9% (foundation-to-foundation) and +10.6% (foundation-to-local) over prior KD methods on 5 domain-generalisation segmentation benchmarks.
prior_overlap: Partial. The pool feature-learning row (MIM, DDeP on R34) was n.d. VFM feature distillation is a different objective, and BRIEF lists other SSL objectives as open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Student = house R34 encoder; stage 1 feature distillation from DINOv2-L or C-RADIOv4 on the 11.9k pool; stage 2 house training, encoder frozen then PF.
alt_notes.min_experiment: GKD-initialised R34 vs house PF; E1 relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU; kill if not +0.03 E1 relF1@2.

title: Neural Network Optimization Reimagined: Decoupled Techniques for Scratch and Fine-Tuning (DualOpt)
mechanism: For fine-tuning, a per-step weight rollback toward upstream weights inside the optimizer, with rollback strength adapted per layer; evaluated on classification, detection, semantic and instance segmentation.
adaptation: Encoder-only rollback with layer3/4 rolled back hardest; second regulariser if SPD wins.
evidence: State of the art across classification, detection, semantic and instance segmentation (abstract; numbers not retrieved).
min_experiment: Arm DualOpt vs SPD vs PF, seeds 5-9. Kill if not above PF on any co-primary.
prior_overlap: Partial via PF, same as SPD.

title: PointScatter: Point Set Representation for Tubular Structure Extraction
mechanism: Split the image into scatter regions, each predicting a small point set, trained by greedy region-wise bipartite matching; points rendered as mask or centreline.
adaptation: Crack only on stride-4 features (16x16 regions); L1 point regression after matching lands at the mean of jittered labels (sub-pixel); render at source width.
min_experiment: Arm = PF + PointScatter crack head; baseline = PF; 5 seeds; metrics relF1@2, components found. Kill if relF1@2 gain < 0.01.
evidence: R: four public tubular datasets, segmentation and centreline extraction tasks.
prior_overlap: None.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack only on stride-4 features (16x16 regions); L1-regressed matched points land at the mean of jittered labels (sub-pixel); render at per-source width; other classes from the house CE head.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF encoder + PointScatter crack head vs PF; metric relF1@2 and strict IoU after per-source rendering; kill if relF1@2 +<0.01.

title: Probabilistic Modeling of Inter- and Intra-observer Variability in Medical Image Segmentation (Pionono)
mechanism: Each rater gets a learned Gaussian in latent space. A sample is fused with image features to give that rater's segmentation, trained end to end by variational inference, so it models both inter-rater style and intra-rater variability.
adaptation: Rater = source (5 Gaussians); the latent variance captures within-source jitter. Small head on top of the house decoder; use the rater mean at test.
min_experiment: Arm = house PF + Pionono head (5 seeds) versus house PF and versus the FiLM arm. Metric: crack IoU clean-49. Kill if < +0.012 or not better than the FiLM arm.
evidence: R: prostate cancer histopathology with multiple pathologists; beats STAPLE, Probabilistic U-Net and confusion-matrix models.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Rater = source (5 Gaussians); latent sampling models within-source jitter. Small head on the house decoder; use the rater mean at test.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: Pionono head on house PF, 5 seeds vs house PF; metric clean-49 crack IoU; kill if < +0.012 or if not better than the source-FiLM arm.

title: Sharpness-Aware Gradient Matching for Domain Generalization (SAGM)
mechanism: Minimise empirical risk, perturbed loss and their gap together, aligning gradient directions; better DG than SAM at equal cost.
adaptation: Drop-in replacement for SAM in the PF recipe; target E1. Run only if SAM moves E1.
evidence: Outperforms SOTA on PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita, DomainNet (classification).
min_experiment: Arm PF+SAGM vs PF+SAM vs PF, seeds 5-9. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU. Kill if not above PF+SAM on E1.
prior_overlap: none

title: Spatial Frequency Modulation for Semantic Segmentation (SFM)
mechanism: Adaptive resampling densely samples high-frequency areas before strided downsampling so they are not aliased, and multi-scale adaptive upsampling demodulates them back in the decoder.
adaptation: A 1 to 2 px crack is pure high frequency and is aliased by ResNet-34 conv1 stride 2, the maxpool and each stride-2 block. Insert ARS before conv1 stride and the layer2 downsample, MSAU in the last two U-Net++ decoder nodes; port the modules out of mmseg by hand (no install).
min_experiment: Arm house PF + SFM vs house PF; 5-fold CV crack IoU, relF1@2, crack components >= 20 px found, gridline IoU. Kill: gridline IoU < +0.03 and crack IoU n.d. About 10 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: None: 2x input (R5) added pixels but not anti-aliased sampling; no frequency-aware module was run.
evidence: R: +1.5 mIoU Mask2Former-Swin-T, +1.4 InternImage-T on ADE20K, +0.8 on Cityscapes for deformable conv.

alt_notes.adaptation: Dense resampling around cracks and finger breaks before strides; heavier follow-up to Seg-Aliasing, only if that shows a signal.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + SFM; baseline house; kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.02.

title: UAV-based pavement distress segmentation via controllable synthetic data augmentation and a lightweight selective fusion network under limited annotations
mechanism: A label generator produces multiclass structural label maps and a fine-tuned ControlNet renders spatially aligned image-mask pairs for training.
adaptation: Label generator = edited train masks (inactive from crack isolation logic, splice/gridline layouts from train statistics); ControlNet fine-tuned on 478 cells, 1-ch replicated; cracks only with ridge-snapped labels. Targets inactive and weak other classes.
min_experiment: PF + 3x synthetic (1,434 cells) vs PF. Metric mIoU_rob and module-grouped CV inactive IoU. Kill: mIoU_rob gain < +0.01 and CV inactive gain < +0.02.
evidence: R: own UAV-Road set, limited labels; mIoU 83.43 without, 87.92 with 3x synthetic augmentation.
prior_overlap: none (generative synthesis never tried)

alt_notes.adaptation: Label generator = edited train masks (inactive from crack-isolation logic, splice/gridline layouts from train stats); ControlNet on 478 cells; other classes and inactive; cracks only with snapped labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + 1,434 synthetic vs PF. Metric mIoU_rob and CV inactive IoU. Kill: mIoU_rob < +0.01 and CV inactive < +0.02. About 30 GPU-h.

title: Wavelet Convolutions for Large Receptive Fields
mechanism: Convolution applied to wavelet subbands, giving very large receptive fields with log-growing parameters, more shape bias and more robustness to corruption.
adaptation: WTConvNeXt-T (timm) encoder in U-Net++, or WTConv2d replacing the 3x3 convs in ResNet-34 layer3/4. A whole-cell receptive field should help the half-cut layout and long scuff streaks on E1.
min_experiment: Arm: WTConvNeXt-T U-Net++ under PF, 5 seeds. Baseline: ImageNet ConvNeXt-T U-Net++ under PF and the house model. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, test crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.03.
evidence: R: ImageNet-1K top-1 82.5 / 83.6 / 84.1 (T/S/B, README); better corruption robustness and shape bias.
prior_overlap: Only the DINOv3 vs ImageNet ConvNeXt-T 2-seed F51 screen was run; WTConv was never tested.

alt_notes.adaptation: WTConvNeXt-T as U-Net++ encoder or WTConv2d in ResNet-34 layer3/4; whole-cell context for half-cut layout and long scuffs on E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: WTConvNeXt-T U-Net++ under PF vs ImageNet ConvNeXt-T under PF, 5 seeds, test + E1; kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03.

title: Balanced Loss Function for Accurate Surface Defect Segmentation
mechanism: Dynamic class weighting, truncated cross-entropy that drops well-classified pixels, and label-confusion suppression that caps the very large loss at defect borders caused by ambiguous labels.
adaptation: Apply border suppression to a 1 px band each side of crack labels (half of label points sit >1 px off the ridge), truncated CE at p > 0.9 on background, dynamic weights on the 12 defect classes to help gridline / splice / edge_dark.
evidence: R: KSDD2, Severstal and an aluminium set across several CNNs, IoU +5% to +30% (abstract; single runs as far as visible). Exact thresholds not read.
min_experiment: Arm: house with 1 px border suppression + truncated CE (0.9) + dynamic class weights; baseline: house; metric: CV crack IoU and mIoU_rob; kill if both gains < +0.01.
prior_overlap: Partial: offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) also tolerates border error; truncation and dynamic class weighting untested.

title: Boxes2Pixels: Learning Defect Segmentation from Noisy SAM Masks
mechanism: Treat pseudo-masks as a noisy teacher and apply one-sided online self-correction: relax background supervision where the student is confident a defect is present, targeting teacher false negatives.
adaptation: Take only the one-sided rule for our missed crack labels (audit: issues in 24 of 239 train crack cells; E1 recall 0.17-0.21): after warm-up, drop background loss on thin confident EMA components (p>0.9) more than 2 px from any crack label; never add crack targets.
evidence: R: wind turbine blade set, binary IoU +9.71 over strongest weak baseline, binary recall +18.56 from self-correction alone.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + background-loss drop for confident thin components after 5k steps; baseline: PF; metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and CV relR@2; kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.02 and CV relP@2 falls > 0.02.
prior_overlap: none: noisy-label methods never tried; D15/D36 list the paper only for box supervision.

alt_notes.adaptation: Loss for training on FM-labelled pool half-cells: FM labellers miss thin cracks, so relax background CE where the house student is confident of crack; keep real labels for the 478 cells.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Only after a labeller passes G0: PF + labeller pseudo-labels with vs without one-sided relaxation; H36 inactive IoU and F51 crack relF1@2; kill under margin M.

alt_notes.adaptation: PVEL-AD crack boxes (needs user OK). Replace SAM with box-gated house-ensemble pseudo-masks; outside boxes hard background, inside soft with one-sided correction; own source flag for NIR poly cells.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Only if joint runs gain from extra crack data. Arm: house + PVEL-AD box-gated pseudo-masks, 30k steps, 5 seeds. Baseline: house 5-seed. Metric: clean-49 crack relR@2 and E1 crack recall. Kill if relR@2 < +0.02 and E1 recall < +0.03. ~20 GPU-h.

title: Combining partially labelled binary datasets: other-class positives as negatives
mechanism: When combining single-class datasets, positives of other classes act as negatives and a binary dataset's background is excluded from loss for classes it does not label.
evidence: +4.4% Dice over a per-class ensemble, 24% less stomach/colon confusion (2D DeepLabV3).
adaptation: For MSS and PV-Vision: their busbar/non-cell positives are negatives for crack except where their crack overlaps; their background ignored for classes they do not label.
min_experiment: Ablation inside the joint run: this masking rule vs naive background, 5 seeds each. Metric: clean-49 crack relP@2 and IoU. Kill if < +0.012 crack IoU. ~10 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: none

title: ContourDiff: Unpaired Medical Image Translation with Structural Consistency
mechanism: A diffusion model trained only on the target domain maps contour maps to target images, enforcing the contour at every sampling step, so source structure and masks are preserved under translation.
adaptation: Train on unlabelled half-cut multi pool cells (1,152) plus CSIR mono pool; contour = busbar/finger/cell-border edges plus the crack label drawn in (edge detectors miss the 7% of cracks under 2% contrast). Translate the 478 train cells into half-cut CSIR style and reuse labels; crack is forced by its own label so pairs are aligned.
min_experiment: PF + 478 translated cells vs PF, 5 seeds. Metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU. Kill: both gains < +0.02 or test crack IoU drop > 0.01.
evidence: R: CT to MRI (lumbar spine, hip-thigh); segmentation trained on translated images beats other unpaired translators on real MRI; zero-shot to unseen anatomy.
prior_overlap: Synthetic half-cut views changed geometry only; appearance translation untested. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Train on unlabelled half-cut multi and CSIR mono pool cells; contour = busbar, finger, border edges plus the crack label drawn in. Translate 478 train cells to half-cut CSIR style, keep labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + 478 translated cells vs PF. Kill: E1 relF1@2 and E1 inactive gains both < +0.02. About 36 GPU-h.

title: Depth Anything V2
mechanism: Scale up the teacher, then train students only on large sets of pseudo-labelled real images, so students learn from a consistent target instead of noisy real labels.
adaptation: Teacher = best heavy model (VFM or ensemble). Students train on 159k pseudo-labelled cells only, with no jittered GT, then get a short PF fine-tune on the 478 cells. Tests whether one consistent crack convention raises relF1@2 and E1 detection.
min_experiment: Arm pseudo-only student (+ short fine-tune) vs house PF, 3 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2 (strict IoU may fall because of per-source conventions). Kill if relF1@2 is n.d. on both sets.
evidence: R: models from 25M to 1.3B parameters; students trained on large pseudo-labelled real sets reported to give finer and more robust predictions than V1 (abstract-level claim; tables not read).
prior_overlap: Not tested; the 159k pool was never used. Open.

title: PixelUp: Zero-Shot Semantic Feature Upsampling for Fine-Grained Vision Tasks
mechanism: Zero-shot VFM-agnostic upsampler using a coarse-to-fine chain of windowed cross-attention guided by multi-scale semantic features to avoid texture artifacts of image-guided upsamplers.
adaptation: Third arm of the upsampler probe; semantic guidance should stop copying multi-crystal grain texture into crack features.
min_experiment: Within X1 probe: PixelUp-512 vs AnyUp-512 vs bilinear-1024; CV crack AP and false-positive rate on multi cells. Kill if below AnyUp.
evidence: R: average +1.2 mIoU on semantic segmentation and +0.25 delta1 on NYUv2 over prior upsamplers across VFMs.
prior_overlap: none.

title: Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation via Adaptive Equalization Learning (AEL)
mechanism: A confidence bank tracks per-class performance during training. Weak classes get a higher chance of being copy-pasted or CutMixed and of being sampled.
evidence: Cityscapes 1/32 cumulative ablation 69.1 to 74.3 mIoU, with adaptive copy-paste adding +0.85 (1/32) and +0.71 (1/16). Tail classes gain 10 to 22 IoU. These numbers come from the handbook's notes on the paper.
adaptation: Labelled stream only, since SSL was n.d. at 100%. A running per-class IoU on train batches decides which class regions (splice, gridline, edge_dark, material, inactive) are pasted between labelled cells of the same source. Crack is excluded at first because of the decoy risk.
min_experiment: PF+AEL class-aware paste vs PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: mIoU_rob and the per-class IoU of splice, gridline, edge_dark and material. Kill if mIoU_rob gain < +0.005.
prior_overlap: SSL CutMix in Mean Teacher was not class-aware and ran on the unlabelled stream (n.d.). Class-aware mixing between labelled cells has not been run.

title: StyleSPADE: Realistic Image Augmentation for Robust Infrastructure Crack Segmentation via Ensemble Learning
mechanism: Conditional generator combining SPADE mask normalisation with a style exemplar image, keeping crack geometry from the mask and background texture from the exemplar.
adaptation: Style exemplar = pool cell from a target group (half-cut CSIR, BMRK, CFVS without twin); mask = a train mask; renders every train mask in every source style. Pixel space, so 1-2 px cracks are representable.
min_experiment: PF + train masks rendered with BMRK, CFVS, half-cut CSIR exemplars vs PF. Metric weak-source CV crack IoU and E1 relF1@2. Kill: both gains < +0.02. About 20 GPU-h.
evidence: R: crack IoU 0.6376, F1 0.7586 with StyleSPADE data across Mask2Former, Swin-UPerNet, K-Net; 0.6452 with stacking ensemble.
prior_overlap: none

title: Revisiting Downsampling in Semantic Segmentation: Fighting Aliasing with Dynamic Gaussian and Gabor Frequency Filters
mechanism: Dynamic Gaussian low-pass along edge normals only, then a learnable Gabor directional band-pass that removes residual aliasing peaks concentrated along a few dominant directions; phase-error energy metric.
adaptation: EL aliasing is directionally sparse (fingers one axis, busbars the other), matching its assumption. Use the Gabor selector before stride-2 layers; use phase-error energy as a diagnostic of finger aliasing in the house encoder.
min_experiment: Arm: house + LFS (and DGK) at strides; baseline house; kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.02; only after Seg-Aliasing shows a signal.
evidence: R: consistent gains and sharper boundaries across segmentation datasets (abstract; numbers not read).
prior_overlap: none

title: Self-training for cross-centre coronary vessel segmentation in X-ray angiography using pre-contrast frame subtraction
mechanism: Self-train on a target-centre pool. Pixels found only by an independent physical cue (pre-contrast subtraction) are set to ignore, not background. The gain depends on how sensitive the teacher is.
adaptation: E1 analogue: pool = CSIR half-cut cells. Pseudo-labels come from the PF ensemble. Pixels flagged only by a ridge filter (black top-hat or Frangi tuned to the 4 px FWHM crack profile) become ignore, so cracks the teacher misses are not taught as background.
min_experiment: Arm ST-ignore vs plain target-pool self-training vs house PF, 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack recall and relF1@2. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains less than 0.03 over PF.
evidence: R: thin-vessel segmentation, ARCADE -> XCAD/XACV. XCAD macro Dice +2.7 (95% CI 2.3 to 3.2); a same-epoch fine-tuning control gave -0.6. A second round gave no gain. Starting from a 50-image model, XCAD Dice went 0.623 -> 0.745; XACV did not improve where main vessels were missed.
prior_overlap: Our Mean Teacher with the external pool set unlabelled pixels by teacher argmax and used no ignore cue. It was not aimed at E1. Open. Risk: E1 crack recall is 0.17, which is the paper's failure case.

title: When Online Adaptation Hurts: Parameter-Frozen Test-Time Ensembling for Continual Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Weights and BN stay frozen. The method averages softmax over scale and flip views after mapping each view back to native geometry; adapting the weights online was worse than this frozen ensemble.
adaptation: The flip part is already closed for us (E: +0.01 single model, 0 on the ensemble). The new part is scale views at 0.75/1.0/1.25/1.5 x D4 with logits resized back before softmax. A second arm retrains the house and PF models with label-safe 0.8 to 1.25 scale jitter so the scale views are in distribution. BMRK (downscaled ELPV, 3 px labels) is the source most likely to gain.
min_experiment: Arm A: FINAL and SUP100-PF with 32-view scale x D4 TTA. Arm B: retrain with scale jitter (5 seeds each), then the same TTA. Baselines: the same checkpoints with D4 TTA and with no TTA. Metrics: test clean-49 crack IoU, component recall >=20 px, BMRK crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if gain is < +0.01 crack IoU single model or < +0.005 on the ensemble, and E1 relF1@2 is < +0.02.
evidence: R: M&Ms cardiac MRI vendor stream, PIE 0.7786 mean Dice vs source 0.7680 vs five online CTTA methods 0.7388 to 0.7416. Saturates at 28 views. Confidence weighting, class-prior correction, CC filtering and morphology gave no gain or hurt. Qualitatively keeps thinner structures.
prior_overlap: Partial. BRIEF s5 lists flip/rot/multi-scale TTA as open, but handbook doc 18 R1 ran D4 flip+rot TTA (+0.0104 single model, -0.0001 on the ensemble). Multi-scale views and scale-jitter training were never run, so those parts are open.

title: SoMA: Singular Value Decomposed Minor Components Adaptation for Domain Generalizable Representation Learning
mechanism: LoRA initialised on the minor singular components of each pretrained weight, with generalisable blocks frozen and an annealing weight decay; keeps the major pretrained directions intact.
evidence: Top of the Rein++ DGSS comparison: 68.2 mIoU average GTAV to Cityscapes/BDD/Mapillary (Rein 64.9).
adaptation: Principled PF for ResNet-34: reshape conv kernels to (out, in*k*k), SVD, train only the bottom-r components in layer3/4, freeze stem/layer1/2; anneal weight decay. Also the DG arm for any ViT encoder from D24.
min_experiment: SoMA-ResNet34 vs PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2, test crack IoU. Kill: no gain > 0.02 over PF on either E1 metric.
prior_overlap: Partial: PF (freeze then 0.1x lr) tests the same aim, but not SVD minor-component tuning. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: A finer form of PF encoder preservation: SVD on reshaped ResNet-34 conv kernels (or a DINOv2/v3 backbone), tune minor components only.
alt_notes.min_experiment: SoMA-ResNet-34 vs PF, 3 seeds; kill if E1 inactive IoU < PF and crack unchanged.

title: Long-Tail Challenges in Electroluminescence-Based Photovoltaic Defect Detection: a Diagnostic Study
mechanism: Diagnoses that rare EL classes fail on localisation (predicted as background) and shows only cell-grid-aware copy-paste lifts tail AP.
adaptation: Paste inactive+crack pairs, splice, edge_dark, corrosion only onto labelled train cells at grid-consistent positions (between busbars, aligned with fingers, same source contrast), never onto unlabelled pool cells.
min_experiment: Arm: house + grid-aware rare-class paste. Baseline: house, 5 v 5 seeds. Metrics: test inactive IoU, mIoU_rob, splice / edge_dark IoU. Kill if inactive < +0.02 and mIoU_rob < +0.005.
evidence: R: 2,894 images, 61,331 instances, 14 classes, YOLOv11 mAP50 0.579; head AP 0.830 v tail 0.488; grid-aware paste ring_defect AP 0.145 to 0.288.
prior_overlap: Partial: crack copy-paste onto pool cells was n.d. (more decoys). Grid-aware paste on labelled cells for inactive and rare classes is untested.

title: MedDINOv3: How to adapt vision foundation models for medical image segmentation?
mechanism: Plain ViT with multi-scale token aggregation for segmentation plus multi-stage domain-adaptive DINOv3 pretraining on 3.87M CT slices.
evidence: R (abstract): matches or exceeds SOTA on four CT/MRI segmentation benchmarks.
adaptation: Use its multi-scale token aggregation as the VFM-H fusion design; run its domain-adaptive DINOv3 recipe on the 159k EL pool only if ExPLoRA shows an E1 sign (159k is 4% of their data).
min_experiment: Fusion design swap in VFM-H vs simple projection; CV crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2; kill if less than +0.01 on either.
prior_overlap: No ViT domain-adaptive pretraining was run; ResNet MIM is a different objective. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Continue DINOv3 ViT-B/16 SSL on the 11.9k pool (or the 159k pool if download approved) at 512-1024 px, then plug into the Dino U-Net harness.
alt_notes.min_experiment: EL-continued DINOv3 vs natural DINOv3 in the same Dino U-Net harness; kill if E1 crack relF1@2 gain < 0.02 and CV crack relF1@2 not better.

alt_notes.adaptation: Step 1: multi-scale aggregation + 512-768 px on DINOv3 ViT-B, no pretraining change. Step 2: the 3-stage recipe on the de-duplicated pool, stage 3 with 512-768 crops.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Step 2 vs step 1, 2 seeds, out-of-fold relF1@2 and E1 crack recall. Kill step 2 if < +0.01 and < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Step 1: multi-scale aggregation + 512 to 768 px on DINOv3 ViT-B, no pretraining change. Step 2: continued pretraining on the de-duplicated pool.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Step 2 vs step 1; kill step 2 if < +0.01 out-of-fold relF1@2 and < +0.02 E1 recall.
