title: Unsupervised and few-shot segmentation in photovoltaic electroluminescence images for defect detection via a novel enhanced iterative autoencoder
mechanism: Iterative autoencoder trained only on normal EL images reconstructs a defect-free cell; residuals give unsupervised pixel-level defect maps; few masks extend it to few-shot.
evidence: R: better pixel-level metrics than unsupervised and few-shot baselines on PV EL (numbers not in abstract).
adaptation: Bold bet for E1: train on pool half and full cells, where scuffs are common and so learned as normal; feed the residual as an input channel. Opposite failure mode to CrackCue on scuffs. Also a label-free baseline for the benchmark.
min_experiment: Arm: house + EI-AE residual channel, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: E1 crack precision and relF1@2 in scuff cells, test crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.03.
prior_overlap: none. Anomaly-detection priors are listed as never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Train on pool cells the house ensemble calls defect-free, including the 1,152 multi half-cut pool cells, and feed the residual map as a 2nd input channel; target E1 where 70% of crack pixels get p(crack) < 0.001. Scuff streaks will also be anomalous, so the supervised head must learn to reject them.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house 2-channel (EL + anomaly residual). Baseline: house, 5 v 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and recall. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Train on pool cells the house model calls crack-free, including the 1,152 multi half-cells, and feed the anomaly map as an extra input channel so E1 cracks that the model now gives p < 0.001 get a second signal.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + AE anomaly channel. Baseline: PF, 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relR@2 at matched relP@2. Kill if gain < +0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: EL-native AD baseline: train on clean cells per source; few-shot arm with the 42 inactive cells; evaluate with 2 px tolerant crack metrics.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark entry: pixel AUROC / AU-PRO / SegF1 on test and E1; no kill line.

alt_notes.adaptation: Train on clean cells per source; few-shot arm with the 42 inactive cells; EL-native AD baseline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark AD track: report pixel metrics per class on CV and E1; few-shot arm vs PF on inactive IoU with kill at < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Train on pool cells including the 1,152 multi half-cells so half-cut layout counts as normal; feed the anomaly map as an extra input channel to the house model for E1. Scuffs will also score as anomalies, so the supervised model must still reject them.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house + anomaly-map channel vs house, 5 seeds; E1 crack recall at matched test precision; kill if E1 recall gain < 0.05.

alt_notes.adaptation: Train on about 6k pool half and full cells (scuffs common there, so learned as normal); use the residual as an extra input channel; contrast with CrackCue which never sees scuffs. Also a label-free benchmark baseline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + EI-AE residual channel, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: E1 crack precision and relF1@2 in scuff cells. Kill: < +0.03 E1 relF1@2.

alt_notes.adaptation: Train on defect-free pool cells (house predicts no crack/inactive); residual map as 2nd input channel or crack/inactive proposal for E1-like cells where house gives p<0.001; EL benchmark baseline if code is obtainable.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Residual map as extra channel to house PF on cv5v2; metric out-of-fold crack relF1@2 and F51 crack recall; kill under margin M.

title: UCS: A Universal Model for Curvilinear Structure Segmentation
mechanism: Sparse adapters in a SAM encoder, an FFT high-pass prompt generator for curve-specific prompts, and a prompt-free decoder with hierarchical feature compression; tuned for cross-domain curvilinear segmentation.
adaptation: Crack-only branch fused with house multi-class output; high-pass prompts will also fire on gridlines, busbar edges and scuffs, so keep the multi-class context and check false alarms on half-cut E1 cells.
evidence: R: SOTA generalisation and open-set curvilinear segmentation across medical, engineering, natural, plant imagery (abstract).
min_experiment: UCS crack branch, 3 seeds, crack logits replace house crack logits; metric crack IoU, relF1@2, E1 relF1@2; kill if both < house + 0.012.
prior_overlap: none.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replicate the 1-channel EL image to 3 channels and upsample 512 to 1024. Fine-tune a crack-only head first, then add other classes.
alt_notes.min_experiment: UCS crack-only vs house crack-only, 2 seeds, 20k steps. Metrics: test crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2. Kill if both are below house.

title: Understanding Imbalanced Semantic Segmentation Through Neural Collapse (CeCo)
mechanism: Regularize class feature centers toward a simplex equiangular tight frame, which imbalance and context otherwise break, to improve minor-class discrimination.
adaptation: Class centers from a >=32-dim projection of the full-res decoder features (17 present classes); same plumbing as region rebalance. Could separate crack vs inactive vs scuff.
min_experiment: Arm: CeCo regularizer on best loss/sampling arm, 3 seeds; baseline that arm; metric mIoU_rob and E1 crack recall; kill if no gain >= 0.01.
evidence: R: improvements on 2D and 3D seg benchmarks; ScanNet200 test 1st place, +6.8 mIoU.
prior_overlap: none

title: BPKD: Boundary Privileged Knowledge Distillation For Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Distil edge regions and body regions with separate losses, giving edges extra spatially sensitive supervision.
adaptation: Edge mask = crack GT dilated 2 px plus inactive borders; body = rest; up-weight edge term inside the ensemble KD arm.
min_experiment: Arm: Noothout KD arm with BPKD loss. Baseline: Noothout KD arm. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill: < +0.008 crack IoU.
evidence: R: state-of-the-art KD on three segmentation benchmarks, CNN and transformer students.
prior_overlap: none

title: Constructing and Exploring Intermediate Domains in Mixed Domain Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation (MiDSS)
mechanism: Labelled data from one domain, unlabelled from several: unified copy-paste between labelled and unlabelled images creates intermediate domains, plus training-progress-aware random amplitude mixup and symmetric guidance.
adaptation: Matches our pool shape (478 labelled full cells; unlabelled mono, multi, half-cells). Paste half-cell regions (cut line, scuffs) into labelled cells and labelled crack regions into half-cells; amplitude mixup from half-cells.
min_experiment: PF + UCP + TP-RAM (pool half-cells) vs PF + MT/CutMix (BRIEF s5 config), 3 seeds. Kill if E1 crack relF1@2 gain < +0.03.
evidence: R: +13.57% Dice on Prostate over SOTA, across Prostate, Fundus, M&Ms.
prior_overlap: Partial: MT + CutMix + external pool was n.d. at 100% labels; amplitude mixup and half-cell-targeted copy-paste are new.

title: MEMO: Human-like Crisp Edge Detection Using Masked Edge Prediction
mechanism: Trains with randomly masked edge maps as an extra input. At inference it starts fully masked and reveals pixels in order of confidence, so thick confidence ridges collapse to thin lines. Uses only cross-entropy, plus synthetic pretraining.
adaptation: Add a refinement U-Net on frozen house logits, with a second input channel holding a partially revealed crack map. Progressive reveal can link crack fragments (76 to 88% of components are under 20 px). This would be the first refinement-network test on our data.
min_experiment: Arm: house + MEMO-style refinement stage, 5 seeds. Baseline: house at 100% labels. Metrics: recall of components >= 20 px, relF1@2, crack IoU. Kill if component recall gains less than 0.02 and relF1@2 is n.d.
evidence: R: better results on crispness-aware evaluations than prior methods without post-processing. Fine-tuning adds 1.2% params. Numbers not read.
prior_overlap: Refinement networks are listed as never tried. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Refinement stage on top of the house model: input EL image plus partially revealed house crack map, trained on 478 cells with random masking, no synthetic pretraining at first; LocMax reveal links crack fragments (most components under 20 px).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house logits + masked-refinement net, 5 seeds; baseline house 5-seed ensemble. Metrics components>=20px found, relF1@2, E1 relF1@2. Kill if component recall gain < 0.02 and relF1@2 n.d. About 20 GPU-h.

title: Not All Pixels are Equal: Learning Pixel Hardness for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Gradient-isolated branch learns a stable pixel hardness map by maximising hardness-weighted loss while the seg head minimises it.
adaptation: Targets thin parts (gridline, crack). On jittered crack labels hard pixels are often label noise: restrict hardness weighting to non-crack classes or to pixels within 2 px of the label.
min_experiment: Arm: hardness branch on house model, 3 seeds; baseline SUP100; metric gridline IoU and mIoU_rob, crack IoU guard; kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01.
evidence: R: +1.37 mIoU on average over popular segmentation models on Cityscapes; generalises across domains.
prior_overlap: none

title: Semantic-Aware Random Convolution and Source Matching for Domain Generalization in Medical Image Segmentation (SRCSM)
mechanism: Random convolution applied differently to each labelled region during training, plus test-time intensity mapping of target images towards the source distribution.
evidence: Beats prior DG methods in most cross-modality and cross-centre abdominal, whole-heart and prostate settings; matches the in-domain baseline in several (abstract).
adaptation: Region-wise random conv on structural classes only; at test time, histogram-match each new-module cell to the training intensity distribution, trained jointly with the randomisation.
min_experiment: PF+SRCSM vs PF, 5 seeds; metric E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: < +0.02 over GIN-IPA arm.
prior_overlap: Partial: global intensity normalisation at inference failed (BRIEF), but without training-time region randomisation. Open.

title: Widest-Path Reachability Fields for Connectivity-Preserving Slender Structure Segmentation
mechanism: A differentiable max-min (widest path) reachability objective on a domain-restricted graph sends gradient to the sparse bottleneck pixels that break connectivity. No inference overhead.
adaptation: Domain = crack label dilated by 2 px to absorb jitter, endpoints from the label skeleton, DP on GPU. An alternative solver to TRACE for the same goal, so pick one.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + WPRF (crack), 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: component recall, relF1@2, crack IoU, width. Kill as for TRACE.
evidence: R (abstract): 9 architectures, 6 datasets including cracks. Improved 87% of experiments with fixed hyperparameters, clDice +7.2 points on fragile datasets.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Domain = crack label dilated by 2 px (absorbs jitter); endpoints from the label skeleton. Same aim as TRACE with a global solver; run only if TRACE shows a gain.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + WPRF vs PF, 5 seeds. Kill if relF1@2 gain < 0.01 or width rises > 15%.

title: Dynamic Label Injection for Imbalanced Industrial Defect Segmentation
mechanism: During training, inject real defects into defect-free images by Poisson seamless cloning and cut-paste so every batch is class-balanced, replacing loss-side balancing.
adaptation: Target inactive (42 train cells), splice (never predicted), edge_dark, corrosion, not crack: clone inactive regions with their bounding crack into clean cells of the same source and mono/multi type so the inactive-touches-crack rule holds.
evidence: R: Magnetic Tile multi-class, IoU gain over balancing losses, also under weak supervision (numbers not read). Code per web search at github.com/covisionlab/dynamic-label-injection (unverified).
min_experiment: Arm: house + per-batch Poisson-cloned inactive(+crack), splice, edge_dark; baseline: house; metric: CV inactive IoU (test is decided by 3 cells) and splice IoU; kill if CV inactive IoU gain < +0.02 and splice stays 0.
prior_overlap: Crack copy-paste onto pool cells was n.d. (more decoys); inactive / rare-class injection with Poisson blending and batch balancing not tested.

title: FAST: Foreground-aware Diffusion with Accelerated Sampling Trajectory for Segmentation-oriented Anomaly Synthesis
mechanism: Mask-conditioned diffusion that adjusts anomaly-aware noise inside the foreground mask at each step (FARM) and samples in about 10 steps (AIAS), producing image-mask pairs designed for downstream segmentation.
adaptation: Train on the 478 grayscale cells with inactive and crack masks as foreground. Synthesise inactive regions (42 real train cells) on clean pool cells using real inactive and crack mask shapes, so inactive keeps touching a crack. Add to 25% of each batch.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + 2,000 FAST-synthesised inactive cells, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF 5-seed. Metrics: module-grouped 5-fold CV inactive IoU (primary), test, BMRK and E1 inactive IoU. Kill: CV inactive IoU gain under 0.02.
evidence: R: outperforms prior anomaly synthesis methods on downstream segmentation over multiple industrial benchmarks (MVTec-style); 10-step sampling.
prior_overlap: none for this mechanism. Crack copy-paste was n.d.; diffusion synthesis is listed as never tried. SARD (same group) is covered by another direction.

title: Progressive growing of patch size: Curriculum learning for accelerated and improved medical image segmentation
mechanism: Start training with small patches and grow them, scaling batch size inversely to keep FLOPs; better convergence on severe foreground imbalance, lower seed variance.
adaptation: 2D: random crops 128 (batch 128) to 256 (batch 32) to 512 (batch 8), equal steps per stage, crops anywhere on the cell; last stage long because inactive and edge_dark need whole-cell context.
min_experiment: Arm: PF with PGPS, 5 seeds. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metric: crack relF1@2, crack IoU, inactive IoU, seed std. Kill: no co-primary gain and seed std not lower.
evidence: R (abstract): +1.28% relative Dice over 15 3D tasks at equal FLOPs, better on all 15, largest on lesion tasks, lower variance. MICCAI 2024 version had code at github.com/compai-lab/2024-miccai-fischer per web search (contents not checked).
prior_overlap: BRIEF section 5: 2x resolution tested, crop curricula never. Open.

title: Scale-Aware Self-Supervised Learning for Segmentation of Small and Sparse Structures
mechanism: Add small-window cropping to the SSL augmentation pipeline so the pretext task zooms on fine sparse structures; gains appear only for small targets.
adaptation: Redo pool SSL (DINO / SimCLR style on ResNet-34 and ConvNeXt-T) with 32-96 px windows upsampled, half sampled near dark ridges (black-top-hat / Frangi response), half uniform; then house and PF fine-tune.
min_experiment: Arm scale-aware SSL init + PF vs PF and vs the existing MIM checkpoint, 5 seeds; metrics test crack IoU and crack components >= 20 px found; kill if crack IoU gain < +0.012.
evidence: R: up to +13% on seismic fault (thin line) segmentation and +5% on cell delineation under label limits; little benefit on large regions.
prior_overlap: MIM/DDeP on 11.9k pool n.d. used standard crops; a thin-structure-aware SSL objective is listed as open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Redo pool SSL on ResNet-34 with 32-96 px windows upsampled, half centred on dark ridges (black top-hat / Frangi), half uniform; house/PF fine-tune.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm scale-aware SSL ResNet-34 + PF vs baseline PF and the existing MIM checkpoint, 5 seeds; metric CV crack IoU and components >= 20 px found; kill if crack IoU gain < +0.012.

alt_notes.adaptation: 32-96 px crops resized up, half sampled near dark ridges, half uniform, in a DINO / iBOT or MIM run on ConvNeXt; score crack and inactive separately.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: ConvNeXt MIM / DINO arm with small-window crops. Baseline: same arm with standard crops. Kill if out-of-fold crack relF1@2 < +0.005.

alt_notes.adaptation: 32 to 96 px crops resized up, half centred near dark ridges, inside the LeJEPA or DINO arms; report crack and inactive separately.
alt_notes.min_experiment: LeJEPA/DINO arm with vs without small crops; kill if out-of-fold relF1@2 < +0.005.

title: Transformer-Based Annotation Bias-Aware Medical Image Segmentation (TAB)
mechanism: A transformer with one learnable query per annotator extracts preference features, so one head outputs each annotator's segmentation. A separate term models stochastic annotation error.
adaptation: One query per source in a light transformer block at the U-Net++ bottleneck; each source's images supervise only its own output. Re-implement, because the repo targets PyTorch 1.7.
min_experiment: Arm = house PF + 5 source queries (5 seeds) versus house PF. Metric: crack IoU clean-49 and per-source CV. Kill if < +0.012.
evidence: R: RIGA optic disc/cup with six annotators; beats prior annotator-bias models (abstract).
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: One query per source in a light transformer block at the U-Net++ bottleneck; each source's cells train only their query output. Re-implement the head (old PyTorch).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: TAB-style source queries on house PF, 5 seeds vs house PF; metric clean-49 crack IoU; kill if < +0.012 or not above the source-FiLM arm.

title: Fast Trainable Projection for Robust Fine-Tuning (FTP)
mechanism: Learns per-layer projection radii around pretrained weights via hyper-optimisation; AdamW plug-in.
adaptation: Encoder only, comparator for SPD.
evidence: Better OOD robustness on four vision tasks and five pretrained models; in SPD's PASCAL seg table FTP 73.79 ID / 58.45 OOD vs vanilla 66.03 / 44.00.
min_experiment: Run only if SPD wins: FTP vs SPD, seeds 5-9, same co-primaries. Kill if below SPD.
prior_overlap: Partial via PF.

title: Harmonizing output imbalance for defect segmentation on extremely-imbalanced photovoltaic module cells images
mechanism: Focal loss with separate FP and FN regulators plus a region term (DIBE), and an output imbalance index (OII) that picks the regulators so the FP/FN balance at inference hits a target; built for tiny hidden cracks at 1:2000.
adaptation: Apply to the crack channel only; compute OII on val with 2 px tolerant TP/FP/FN instead of strict pixels, and raise the FN weight because relR@2 0.866 lags relP@2 0.930.
min_experiment: Arm: house with DIBE crack term. Baseline: house, 5 v 5 seeds. Metric: test relR@2 at relP@2 >= 0.92. Kill if relR@2 gain < 0.015.
evidence: R: four architectures, four datasets of varying imbalance, outperforms CE/Dice/focal/Tversky compounds (numbers not extracted).
prior_overlap: none: focal / Tversky families listed as untested; offset-tolerant CE n.d. is a different mechanism.

alt_notes.adaptation: Closest domain (mono PV cells, tiny hidden cracks): replace soft Dice on crack with DIBE_Reg, beta > alpha to push relR@2 toward 0.90 at relP@2 >= 0.90; pick alpha/beta by OII on val instead of a post-hoc logit bias.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with DIBE_Reg (alpha 0.3, beta 0.7) on crack; baseline: house with val-chosen logit bias; metric: test/CV relR@2 at relP@2 >= 0.90; kill if gain < +0.02.

title: Strip R-CNN: Large Strip Convolution for Remote Sensing Object Detection
mechanism: Sequential orthogonal large strip convolutions aggregate context along the dominant axis of slender objects, avoiding the dilution of large square kernels.
adaptation: Add a large-strip context block (k 31 to 63) on 1/4 and 1/8 features of the house encoder; targets long axis-aligned classes (gridline, ribbons, splice, busbars) and long cracks across the cell.
min_experiment: Arm: house + strip context block, 5 seeds. Metrics: gridline IoU, splice IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: gridline IoU gain < 0.03 and mIoU_rob gain < 0.005.
evidence: DOTA-v1.0 82.75 mAP with 30M params, gains on FAIR1M, HRSC2016, DIOR (detection, not segmentation).
prior_overlap: none

title: Learning Topological Interactions for Multi-Class Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: A fully convolutional module detects pixels that violate containment or exclusion between classes and adds loss on them, trained end to end.
adaptation: Encode two rules. First, an inactive region must have a crack prediction within 5 px (an adjacency rule; 99% of train inactive regions satisfy it). Second, crack is excluded from padding and frame. Loss is applied only to violating pixels.
min_experiment: Arm: the best multi-label or gated arm + violation loss. Baseline: that arm. Metrics: inactive precision and IoU, number of inactive regions with no crack nearby. Kill if the inactive IoU gain is < 0.01.
evidence: R: validated on 2D and 3D, CT and ultrasound, private and public challenge data. The abstract page gives no numbers.
prior_overlap: none. Skeleton Recall and clDice were single-class topology losses, not cross-class constraints.

alt_notes.adaptation: EL has hard class rules: inactive regions touch a crack (99% in train), crack and inactive never lie on padding or frame_edge. Cheapest form is an inference rule: drop predicted inactive components with no predicted crack within k px. Training form: exclusion penalty between inactive / crack and padding / frame_edge.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Inference rule on existing PF checkpoints, k chosen on val (0 GPU-h); then PF + exclusion term vs PF, 5 seeds. Kill if val inactive precision gain < 0.03 or inactive recall falls > 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Exclusions: crack/inactive outside cell area. Adjacency rule (inactive region must have crack within 5 px) built as a custom violation map since TI_Loss covers containment/exclusion only.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm best of region/presence arms + violation loss; metric inactive precision and count of inactive regions without nearby crack; kill if inactive IoU gain < 0.01 over its base.

title: LoftUp: Learning a Coordinate-Based Feature Upsampler for Vision Foundation Models
mechanism: Coordinate-based cross-attention upsampler that combines the full-res image with low-res VFM features, trained on mask-based pseudo-GT features, to give sharp pixel-level features.
adaptation: Full-res path for ViT segmenters: upsample DINOv2 tokens from 1/14 to 512 px guided by the EL image, then dot with query embeddings; fine-tune the upsampler end to end on our cells since it was trained on RGB natural images.
min_experiment: Within the EoMT arm: conv refinement head vs LoftUp upsampler, 5-fold CV; metric crack relF1@2 and crack IoU; kill if LoftUp variant is below conv head on relF1@2 by any margin and not better on IoU by > 0.012.
evidence: R: outperforms prior upsamplers across dense tasks (abstract). Related arXiv 2508.21529 shows upsampled VFM features separate hairline cracks in battery micrographs with few labels. Code stated as github.com/andrehuang/loftup (not opened).
prior_overlap: none: super-resolution heads listed as open under Resolution.

title: Noisy Supervision for Correcting Misaligned Cadaster Maps Without Perfect Ground Truth Data
mechanism: A multi-resolution network predicts a dense displacement field that moves misaligned map polygons onto image evidence, trained on the noisy data itself and applied iteratively so dataset alignment improves round by round.
adaptation: Train a small U-Net (image + jittered label in, 2-channel displacement out) on synthetic jitter drawn from our measured offset distribution (48% within 1 px, 64% within 2 px) applied to high-confidence snapped labels (ARTS, strong ridges); apply to all train crack labels, two rounds; then train the house model.
min_experiment: Only if the ridge-snap arm passes. Arm: learned-alignment labels; baseline: ridge-snap arm and house. Kill if n.d. vs ridge-snap.
evidence: R: cadaster/OSM building alignment on aerial imagery (web search listing only; numbers not read).
prior_overlap: none.

title: ObjectAug: Object-level Data Augmentation for Semantic Image Segmentation
mechanism: Split the image into objects and background using the labels, transform each object, inpaint the holes, and recombine.
evidence: Abstract: clear gains on natural and medical segmentation datasets; no numbers on the arXiv page.
adaptation: Within one labelled cell: lift a crack component, inpaint its old place (a row-wise finger and grain background model, or a small inpainting net trained on crack-free train patches), and re-place it with a dihedral move inside the same cell. The labelled-background hole carries the same edit signature as the moved crack, which penalises the 'paste seam = crack' shortcut that CP100 learned. The cell keeps its own source and texture.
min_experiment: PF+ObjectAug vs PF, and paste-on-labelled+ObjectAug vs paste-on-labelled alone (Synth4Seg arm). Metrics: decoy rate and test crack relP@2. Kill if the decoy rate is not below the paste-only arm or crack relP@2 drops by more than 0.01.
prior_overlap: none. In-cell moves with inpainted negatives have not been run. CP100 is the closest and differs in where pastes go and in having no negative counterpart.

alt_notes.adaptation: Only as the move half of the GDI arm: lift a crack, inpaint with the GDI inpainter, re-place by a dihedral move in the same cell.
alt_notes.min_experiment: GDI+move vs GDI; kill if decoy rate not below GDI or crack relP@2 drop > 0.01.

title: From Reconstruction to Decision: A Post-encoder Plug-in Adapter for Curvilinear Segmentation (PEPA)
mechanism: Post-encoder adapter: target-conditioned snake upsampling to recover thin tortuous structures, plus target-adaptive differentiable thresholding with guards against trivial bias shift; about 0.26M extra params.
adaptation: Attach TCSU to the PF decoder or to a frozen foundation encoder; TADT is a learned form of our val-chosen crack logit bias, so test TCSU first with the known bias fixed.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + TCSU, val bias kept; baseline: PF + val bias; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU. Kill if gain < +0.01.
evidence: R: consistent gains on five medical and industrial benchmarks with frozen-encoder baselines; clDice gains larger than IoU gains (numbers not in abstract).
prior_overlap: Partial: val-chosen crack logit bias tested (+0.004 to +0.007 IoU); snake upsampling untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Attach the snake upsampling to the PF decoder for the crack channel; skip the thresholding half since our val-chosen crack logit bias already does that.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + snake upsampling; baseline PF + val bias; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU. Kill if < +0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Attach to the crack channel of the winning FM arm (or the house decoder); the learned threshold replaces our hand-chosen val crack logit bias.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Winning FM arm + PEPA vs same arm with val-chosen bias; crack IoU and relF1@2 on CV; kill if gain < 0.005 crack IoU.

alt_notes.adaptation: Attach to the FM decoder of the best arm, crack class only; the threshold part overlaps our val-chosen logit bias, so the test is the snake upsampler.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Best FM arm +/- PEPA upsampler, 3 seeds; crack IoU and recall on components < 20 px; kill if < +0.012 crack IoU.

alt_notes.adaptation: Attach to crack and gridline heads of the house decoder or a frozen DINOv3 pipeline; TADT replaces the fixed val-chosen crack logit bias with a per-image threshold (may help source-dependent label width).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house PF + PEPA on crack/gridline; baseline: house PF with val-chosen bias; CV crack IoU, relF1@2, gridline IoU. Kill if crack IoU and relF1@2 n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Attach to the house decoder (or a frozen DINOv3 pipeline) on crack and gridline only; adaptive threshold replaces the fixed val-chosen crack bias with a per-image threshold, relevant to the contrast spread across the 5 sources.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house PF + PEPA vs house PF; 5-fold CV crack relF1@2, crack IoU, gridline IoU; kill: relF1@2 n.d. and gridline < +0.02. About 10 GPU-h.

title: Synthetic crack generation using dynamic programming and elastic deformation to enhance segmentation of concrete and pavement defects
mechanism: Min/max cumulative-energy paths on random noise fields give 1 px crack strands. Variable-width dilation plus geometric and elastic deformation adds width, tortuosity and boundary irregularity.
evidence: 2.25M synthetic samples. Elastic deformation raised feature diversity from 0.17 to 0.31. Trained on synthetic data only: F1 up to 0.79 and mIoU above 0.80 on Cracks-200, CDLN and DeepCrack, comparable to human-annotated training (filter-based segmenter).
adaptation: Deform the skeleton first, then rasterise the label at each source's measured width (ARTS 1.5, CFVS/CSIR 1.75, BMRK 3.0, SDLE 3.25 px). Render a dark profile of about 4 px FWHM with per-source contrast, including the 7% of cracks under 2% contrast. Paste onto labelled cells with full labels, and onto pool multi half-cut cells with loss on the strand and ring only, for E1. Labels are exact, with no jitter.
min_experiment: PF+procedural strands vs PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 relF1@2 and recall@2 (half-cut scuff subset reported), test crack IoU as a guard, recall on low-contrast cracks. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02 or test crack IoU drops by more than 0.012.
prior_overlap: none. Procedural crack synthesis has not been run. Similar to the FreeCOS arm in D06.

alt_notes.adaptation: Deform skeleton, rasterise label at per-source width (ARTS 1.5, CFVS/CSIR 1.75, BMRK 3.0, SDLE 3.25 px), render ~4 px FWHM dark profile with per-source contrast incl. sub-2% contrast; onto labelled cells and pool multi half-cut cells (strand + ring loss) for E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+PROC vs PF; E1 relF1@2 and recall@2 (scuff subset), test crack IoU guard, recall of low-contrast cracks. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.02 or crack IoU drop > 0.012.

title: Benefit from public unlabeled data: A Frangi filter-based pretraining network for 3D cerebrovascular segmentation
mechanism: Pretrain on public unlabelled data with Frangi-filter-derived multi-task targets, then fine-tune.
adaptation: Bold bet: pretrain whole U-Net++ (decoder included) on the 11.9k pool to regress multi-scale dark-ridge maps plus the periodic notch residual; PF fine-tune so the pretraining survives.
min_experiment: Arm: ridge-pretrained 40k steps then PF; baseline PF from ImageNet; kill if crack IoU (CV) < +0.012 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.02. About 20 GPU-h.
evidence: R: 1,510 unlabelled TOF-MRA scans, about +3% over semi- and self-supervised methods.
prior_overlap: partial: MIM and DDeP pool pretraining n.d. (section 5), but ridge-target / thin-structure objectives are listed as open

title: A benchmark dataset for defect detection and classification in electroluminescence images of PV modules using semantic segmentation
mechanism: Weighted cross-entropy with engineered class weights (crack 100, gridline 10, inactive 10, ribbons 3, DOE-validated) to lift recall of rare thin defects.
adaptation: Leave crack to the house Dice; apply capped weights (e.g. inverse-sqrt frequency, max 10) only to weak classes gridline, splice, edge_dark, material to lift mIoU_rob without dilating cracks.
min_experiment: Arm house + weak-class CE weights vs house, 5 seeds; mIoU_rob, gridline recall, splice IoU; kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01 or crack IoU drops > 0.01.
evidence: R: 593 cells, 50 test, 24 classes; DeepLabv3+ custom weights best: crack median IoU 0.25, recall 0.86, gridline recall 0.85, defect mIoU 0.28; equal weights defects 0.04 to 0.24; low precision from dilated predictions.
prior_overlap: Dice on 12 classes (worse) and on 3 (n.d.) tested; class-weighted CE on weak classes not listed. Open.

title: SegFormer: Simple and Efficient Design for Semantic Segmentation with Transformers
mechanism: Hierarchical Mix Transformer encoder without positional encoding plus a lightweight all-MLP decoder.
evidence: R: B4 50.3 mIoU ADE20K at 64M params; B5 84.0 Cityscapes val. On EL (D01, doi:10.1109/jphotov.2024.3450009) beat U-Net/DeepLab on UCF-EL.
adaptation: MiT-B2/B5 ADE20K weights, grey replicated, 1024 px or full-res skip since output is 1/4 res; lower encoder lr; mainly a benchmark entry and heterogeneous-ensemble member.
min_experiment: Arm MiT-B2 + full-res skip, 5-fold CV; baseline house; metrics mIoU_rob, crack relF1@2, E1 crack recall; kill if all three below house.
prior_overlap: none; transformers never tried. Same arm already proposed by D01; run once.

alt_notes.adaptation: MiT-B2/B5 ADE20K weights, 1-ch replicated, 1024 px input or a full-res skip; main candidate for the heterogeneous ensemble member; benchmark entry.
alt_notes.min_experiment: SegFormer-B2 1024 px alone vs house (5-fold) and as ensemble member vs house 5-seed ensemble; metrics as in the ensemble experiment; kill alone if mIoU_rob < 0.570, as member if no metric beats noise floor.

title: Using SegFormer for Effective Semantic Cell Segmentation for Fault Detection in Photovoltaic Arrays
mechanism: SegFormer (hierarchical transformer encoder + all-MLP decoder) for EL defect segmentation; beat CNN segmenters on UCF-EL.
adaptation: MiT-B2/B3 with ADE20K weights, 1-ch stem, 512 px; add a full-res conv skip before the head because SegFormer predicts at 1/4 resolution; lower encoder lr (PF-style).
min_experiment: Arm SegFormer-B2 + full-res skip, 3-seed screen vs house; mIoU_rob, crack relF1@2, E1 crack recall; kill if all three below house.
evidence: R: UCF-EL 5 classes; pixel acc 96.24%, weighted F1 96.22%, unweighted F1 81.96%, mIoU 56.54%, above DeepLabv3, U-Net, DeepLabv3+, PAN, PSPNet, FPN.
prior_overlap: none: transformer segmenters never tried.

title: A benchmarking study of instance segmentation methods for photovoltaic cell defect detection using electroluminescence images
mechanism: Mask-classification / instance segmentation (Mask R-CNN, ConvNeXt, ConvNeXt-V2, Mask2Former via MMDetection) for EL defects.
adaptation: Mask2Former in semantic mode, Swin-T or R50 with ADE20K weights, 1-ch, 512 px; aimed at inactive (few blob regions per cell) and mIoU_rob; crack likely stays with the house model in a heterogeneous ensemble.
min_experiment: Arm Mask2Former semantic, 3 seeds vs house; inactive IoU, mIoU_rob; kill if inactive IoU < house and mIoU_rob < house - 0.01.
evidence: R: UCF-EL (crack, interconnect, contact, corrosion); ConvNeXt-V2 best: seg mAP50 0.602, seg mIoU 0.650, box mAP50 0.629. Code said public; URL not verified.
prior_overlap: none: mask-classification decoders never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Run Mask2Former and ConvNeXt-V2 UperNet as semantic baselines (mmseg) on BenchmarkEL with 1-ch replicated to 3, 512 px, house augmentation, same splits; check 1/4-res mask head on 1-2 px cracks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: Mask2Former (ConvNeXt-V2), 3 seeds, 40k iters. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, mIoU_rob. Kill as a score arm if crack IoU < house - 0.02; keep as benchmark entry regardless.

alt_notes.adaptation: Mask2Former semantic head with ConvNeXt-V2-T or Swin-T, 1-channel input replicated, 512 px, 24 classes; targets blobby inactive and rare classes where query-based masks may help.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: Mask2Former + ConvNeXt-V2-T, 40k iters. Baseline: house, 5 seeds. Metric: mIoU_rob, inactive IoU, crack IoU. Kill if mIoU_rob < 0.580 and inactive IoU < 0.449.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use its model list in our suite; treat inactive regions as instances for an instance-level AP metric alongside IoU.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark only: Mask2Former and ConvNeXt-V2 entries under our protocol (covered by #2).

alt_notes.adaptation: Convert our masks to instances by connected components (cracks merged within 3 px) to get per-crack and per-inactive-region counts, lengths, severity; a benchmark/severity lever, not a strict-IoU lever. Its UCF split has train/test leakage.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark track: Mask2Former instance model vs house semantic model, scored on crack components >=20 px found and Boundary PQ; no kill line (suite member).

alt_notes.adaptation: Cite as the existing EL benchmark and the leakage example motivating clean splits; include Mask2Former / ConvNeXt-V2 in the method suite under our protocol.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark only: run Mask2Former and ConvNeXt-V2 under the BenchmarkEL protocol and report next to house model on clean-49 and E1. ~10 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Document the flaw: UCF-EL has heavy train/test leakage (BRIEF). Add Mask2Former / ConvNeXt-V2 under our protocol as the transformer and mask-classification entry.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Mask2Former (semantic) on our folds at matched compute. Baseline: house fold ensemble. Kill for score use: inactive IoU below the house model by more than 0.02.

title: Deep-learning-based pipeline for module power prediction from electroluminescense measurements
mechanism: CNN regresses module Pmpp from module EL images, with a CAM variant giving per-cell power loss; inactive regions and cracks are the main loss drivers.
adaptation: 719 public module EL images + Pmpp from the lab family behind ELPV (our weak BMRK source). Cut into cells as a BMRK-like unlabelled pool; use module power loss as a weak bag label for the summed predicted inactive fraction (ranking loss across module pairs); use as a severity validation set for predicted inactive fraction.
min_experiment: Step 1: house model on cell crops of all 719 modules, Spearman(predicted inactive fraction, measured power loss); kill weak-supervision idea if rho < 0.3. Step 2: PF + ranking loss vs PF, CV inactive IoU and BMRK inactive IoU; kill if < +0.02. Download needs user OK.
evidence: R: 719 modules; baseline regression MAE 9.0 W (4.0%), CNN MAE 7.3 W (3.2%); dataset, code and models released.
prior_overlap: Partial: SSL with the 11.9k CSIR/ARTS pool was n.d. at 100% labels, but that pool was not BMRK-like and had no electrical labels. Weak supervision from power is untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: External task-level check of our masks. Crop ELPVPOWER cells (about 150 px) with PV-Vision preprocessing, upsample to 512, run the house / PF / ensemble models, sum the predicted inactive fraction per module and rank-correlate with measured Pmpp loss. Expect a domain gap (resolution, camera).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Ask the user before downloading ELPVPOWER (public). Metric: Spearman between predicted inactive fraction and Pmpp loss, module-grouped. Compare house vs PF vs ensemble. Kill the power track if no model reaches Spearman > 0.3. About 3 GPU-h plus a day of preprocessing.

title: Fine-tuning vision foundation model for crack segmentation in civil infrastructures (CrackSAM)
mechanism: SAM fine-tuned with adapter or LoRA for prompt-free crack semantic segmentation; strong under noise and on unseen crack sets.
adaptation: Benchmark baseline: SAM ViT-B/L adapter at 1024, 24 classes, house loss; report clean-49, E1 and per-source.
min_experiment: Adapter variant inside the TopoLoRA harness vs house PF, 5-fold CV; default kill line.
evidence: R: beat 12 segmentation models on noisy and previously unseen sets; 810 open images (road, wall); 98 citations.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Covered by the PEFT grid (LoRA / adapter arms on SAM ViT at 1024); include under its name as the canonical SAM crack baseline in the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: CrackSAM-style LoRA arm in the PEFT grid; crack IoU, relF1@2, E1 relF1@2 vs house; kill if below house on all three.

title: Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks
mechanism: Confident-learning style detection of test-set label errors; errors can flip model rankings.
adaptation: Flag val/test cells whose crack or inactive labels disagree strongly with the 5-fold OOF ensemble (CSIR_00070_r8_c4 is a known case); report rankings with and without flagged cells; no manual relabelling.
min_experiment: Arm: remove top flagged cells. Baseline: clean-49. Metric: rank change of house vs PF vs ensemble. Kill: no rank flip and |delta change| < 0.005.
evidence: R: label errors found in test sets of 10 common CV/NLP/audio datasets; rankings change on corrected subsets.
prior_overlap: partial: one noisy cell already excluded by hand; audit flagged 24 of 239 train cells, nothing systematic on test/val.

alt_notes.adaptation: After models are frozen, run label-error ranking on the 50 test and 106 E1 cells (labels only), count crack/inactive errors, report every method on original and audited labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training: audit test/E1 labels with ensemble ranking + cleanlab; re-rank the 5-seed house, PF and ensemble models. Kill: none (benchmark instrument).

alt_notes.adaptation: Rank test and E1 cells by disagreement between the OOF ensemble and the label at crack-component level. Review only the top few flags (minimal, allowed under the no-labelling rule). Publish rankings on both label sets.
alt_notes.min_experiment: OOF disagreement ranking, then rankings of house vs PF vs ensemble on original vs corrected test labels. Decision: if any pair flips, publish both leaderboards.

title: SuperADD: Training-free Class-agnostic Anomaly Segmentation (CVPR 2026 VAND 4.0 Industrial Track)
mechanism: Training-free DINOv3 memory-bank AD built for train/deploy distribution shift: overlapping patches, intensity-augmented bank, coverage-aware subsampling, iterative morphological closing.
adaptation: E1 recall prior: bank = clean pool cells incl. half-cells; overlapping 224 crops of each 512 cell; intensity augmentation spanning the 5 sources' contrast; skip closing for crack maps (widens them), keep for inactive. Fuse as an extra input channel to PF or as a logit boost inside high-AD components.
evidence: R: MVTec AD 2 segmentation F1 62.61 / 57.42 / 54.35 on public / private / private-mixed test, above SuperAD and other SOTA.
min_experiment: Offline map on F51, H36, CV folds (<3 GPU-h); kill if <30% of PF-missed crack components >=20 px recovered at 1% flagged area. If it passes: PF + AD channel vs PF, 5 seeds, CV then E1; kill E1 crack relF1@2 gain < +0.03 or CV crack IoU drop > 0.01.
prior_overlap: none in BRIEF section 5. D07 proposes a similar offline arm with AnomalyDINO / MuSc; run in the same table.

title: Exploring Intrinsic Normal Prototypes within a Single Image for Universal Anomaly Detection (INP-Former)
mechanism: Normal prototypes are extracted from the test image itself and guide a decoder to reconstruct only normal tokens; residual is the anomaly map, so no aligned external reference is needed.
adaptation: Train on clean pool cells across all sources and layouts; on E1 half-cut cells (no train references) the within-cell finger/busbar pattern serves as normality; use the map as a recall prior for inactive and crack components missed by the house model.
min_experiment: Offline: on CV folds, F51, H36, fraction of house-missed (p<0.001) crack/inactive components recovered at 1% flagged area; then logit fusion vs baseline PF ensemble; kill if < 30% recovered or fused relP@2 falls more than relR@2 rises. Under 5 GPU-h.
evidence: R: SOTA single-class, multi-class and few-shot AD on MVTec-AD, VisA, Real-IAD; some zero-shot ability. No EL evidence.
prior_overlap: none (anomaly-detection priors listed as never tried in section 5)

title: The Lovasz-Softmax Loss: A Tractable Surrogate for the Optimization of the Intersection-Over-Union Measure in Neural Networks
mechanism: Convex surrogate of the Jaccard loss via the Lovasz extension of sorted errors.
adaptation: Lovasz hinge on crack and Lovasz-softmax over present classes, computed over the whole batch (not per image) to match pooled IoU; hard labels only (cannot take soft targets). smp, the house library, ships an implementation.
min_experiment: Arm CE + Lovasz (crack + inactive) vs SUP100, 5 v 5. Kill if crack IoU < +0.012.
evidence: R: widely used IoU surrogate (1239 cites); JML paper App. E finds it equal to JML with hard labels (Cityscapes 75.53 vs 75.55).
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Lovasz hinge on crack and Lovasz-softmax over present classes, per batch (per_image False) to match pooled IoU; smp LossLovasz already in the house library; hard labels only.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: CE + Lovasz (crack, per batch), 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012.

title: AUCSeg: AUC-oriented Pixel-level Long-tail Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Pixel-level AUC (ranking) loss with a tail-class memory bank so each batch contains tail pixels.
adaptation: Threshold-free ranking suits crack (bias tuned anyway) and splice; memory bank stores small crops of splice, inactive, edge_dark, material pixels.
min_experiment: Arm: AUC loss + T-memory bank added to CE+Dice, 3 seeds; baseline SUP100; metric mIoU_rob, splice IoU, crack AP; kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01.
evidence: R: tail-class gains on Cityscapes, ADE20K, COCO-Stuff 164K.
prior_overlap: none

title: From noisy labels to intrinsic structure: A geometric-structural dual-guided framework for noise-robust medical image segmentation (GSD-Net)
mechanism: Geometric distance-aware pixel weights, structure-guided label refinement, and region swapping between image pairs for diversity.
adaptation: Distance weights from the crack distance transform down-weight the uncertain 1-2 px label edge. Region swaps pair cells from different sources. It is the most recent noise-robust baseline for the benchmark suite.
min_experiment: Arm: distance weights only (the cheapest component), 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if there is no detectable difference; run the full GSD-Net only for the benchmark.
evidence: R (web abstract): with simulated noise, +2.52% on Kvasir, +22.76% on Shenzhen, +8.87% on BU-SUC and +4.59% on BraTS2020; also tested on LIDC and MMIS-2024 with real multi-expert labels.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Invert for cracks: down-weight background pixels 1 to 2 px from crack labels (likely true crack mislabelled as background) instead of crack boundary pixels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + distance-weighted CE near crack. Baseline: house. Metric: crack IoU and relR@2. Kill if crack IoU < house + 0.005. About 6 GPU-h.

title: How Many Random Seeds? Statistical Power Analysis in Deep Reinforcement Learning Experiments
mechanism: Power analysis picks the number of seeds needed to detect a given effect with Welch t-test or bootstrap CI.
adaptation: Use our 5-seed SDs (val and OOF) to compute seeds needed for 0.01 crack IoU and 0.02 inactive IoU at power 0.8, for test-49 vs grouped CV.
min_experiment: Arm: power calculation on existing runs. Metric: seeds needed. Kill: >20 seeds on test-49 means stop using test-49 for decisions under 0.02.
evidence: R: tutorial with simulations on deep RL algorithms; Welch t-test and bootstrap CI power curves.
prior_overlap: partial: BRIEF already estimates 0.012 MDE for 5v5; formal power analysis across instruments not done.

title: MuSc: Zero-Shot Industrial Anomaly Classification and Segmentation with Mutual Scoring of the Unlabeled Images
mechanism: Training-free zero-shot segmentation: each patch is scored by its distance to patches of the other unlabelled test images, since normal patches recur and anomalies are rare.
adaptation: Transductive per E1 module and layout group (and per source in test): score each cell against the other cells of the same module; use the map to raise crack/inactive logits in components where house p < 0.001; scuff repeated across a module partly self-cancels.
min_experiment: Offline: MuSc maps on F51/H36 and pool; recall of house-missed crack components (3 px dilation) and inactive at 1% false-alarm area; then fuse with PF ensemble. Kill if recall on missed components < 30% or fused relP@2 loss exceeds relR@2 gain.
evidence: R: zero-shot SOTA on MVTec AD / VisA at publication (abstract); no EL evidence.
prior_overlap: none; anomaly-detection priors never tried. Per-module thresholds and per-panel BN failed, but those are different mechanisms.

alt_notes.adaptation: Run per E1 module group and per source/layout; scuff streaks repeated across a module partly self-cancel; output used as crack/inactive recall prior fused with the PF ensemble.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Same offline recall test as INP-Former on CV / F51 / H36 grouped by module; baseline PF ensemble; kill if < 30% of missed components recovered at 1% area or relP@2 loss exceeds relR@2 gain.

title: SAM3-Adapter: Efficient Adaptation of Segment Anything 3 for Camouflage Object Segmentation, Shadow Detection, and Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Adapter prompts injected into the frozen SAM3 encoder for low-level segmentation tasks.
evidence: R (abstract): beats SAM and SAM2 adapter variants on medical, camouflage and shadow tasks; code claimed available.
adaptation: SAM3 encoder with adapters + U-Net decoder + house R34 detail path; needs the user's OK for gated weights.
min_experiment: SAM3-Adapter side branch vs house PF; default kill line.
prior_overlap: SAM3 never tested. Open.

title: Auto-nnU-Net: Towards Automated Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Adds hyperparameter optimisation, NAS and hierarchical NAS to nnU-Net, using Regularized PriorBand (multi-fidelity, cost-aware) to trade accuracy against training cost.
adaptation: Search over lr, momentum, foreground oversampling ratio, crack/inactive loss weights, deep-supervision weights, encoder depth/width and augmentation set (default vs label-safe). Objective = CV mean of crack relF1@2 + inactive IoU on the module-grouped folds; multi-fidelity over 8 A6000.
min_experiment: One PriorBand run with a 300 GPU-h budget; evaluate the incumbent once on test-49 and E1 against the nnU-Net label-safe arm. Kill: under +0.01 CV objective over the default config.
evidence: R: improved nnU-Net on 6 of 10 Medical Segmentation Decathlon tasks and tied the other 4, at practical resource cost.
prior_overlap: none. Past loss and optimizer variations were one-at-a-time on the house recipe, never a joint search.

title: Exploring Cross-Image Pixel Contrast for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Supervised pixel-to-pixel and pixel-to-region contrast across images using class memory banks.
adaptation: Cross-source memory bank pulls BMRK / CFVS / CSIR crack embeddings together (source invariance for weak sources); full-res projection head. Run this or ReCo, not both.
min_experiment: Arm: contrast loss weight 0.1, 3 seeds; baseline SUP100; metric per-source crack IoU (BMRK) and mIoU_rob; kill if BMRK crack gain < 0.02 and mIoU_rob n.d.
evidence: R: gains on Cityscapes and other benchmarks with DeepLabV3 and HRNet (abstract level).
prior_overlap: none

title: Learning to Detect Label Errors by Making Them: A Method for Segmentation and Object Detection Datasets
mechanism: Inject typed label errors into ground truth, train an instance-segmentation network on a composite (image, label, prediction) input to find error regions.
adaptation: Inject the audit's error types (dropped crack segments, spurious lines, shifted tracing, crack/inactive swaps) into train cells; detector input = EL image + given label + OOF prediction; apply to all 532 cells.
min_experiment: Arm: learned error detector. Baseline: ensemble ranking arm. Metric: precision on held-out injected errors and at 24 audit cells. Kill: not better than ensemble ranking at 24.
evidence: R: beats task-specific baselines on simulated errors across tasks; releases 459 real Cityscapes label errors.
prior_overlap: none.

title: Multi-Task Crack Foundation Model for Engineering-Reliable Crack Representation and Topology Preservation in Civil Infrastructure (CrackGeoFM)
mechanism: Frozen visual foundation backbone with frequency-guided crack enhancement and a domain adaptation module, plus one decoder that jointly outputs mask, skeleton and uncertainty.
adaptation: Take the multi-task decoder only: skeleton head (label skeleton dilated 1 px) and aleatoric uncertainty head on the house model; skeleton output drawn at per-source width; uncertainty as a severity / review flag. 5-shot adaptation claim relevant to the E1 few-shot track.
min_experiment: Arm PF + skeleton + uncertainty heads vs PF; metric relF1@2 (CV) and E1 relF1@2; kill if relF1@2 +<0.01 and E1 relF1@2 +<0.03.
evidence: 20 crack datasets: SOTA segmentation, better topology, calibrated uncertainty, few-shot adaptation from 5 labelled images; numbers not read.
prior_overlap: partial: BRIEF 5 frozen foundation probes showed no gain, but the multi-task skeleton/uncertainty decoder was never tried

alt_notes.adaptation: Frozen DINOv3 or SAM2 encoder, 24-class mask head plus crack skeleton head plus aleatoric crack head; uncertainty feeds the severity step and benchmark calibration reporting.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + aleatoric crack head (and optionally frozen-FM variant); baseline PF; 3 seeds. Metric: crack ECE within 2 px, CV crack IoU unchanged. Kill if ECE not lower.

alt_notes.adaptation: Frozen DINOv3 or SAM2 encoder with adapter, 24-class mask head plus crack skeleton and aleatoric uncertainty heads; uncertainty output feeds the benchmark's severity and post-evaluation step.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + aleatoric crack head (and optional skeleton head); baseline: PF; 3 seeds. Metric: ECE on crack pixels within 2 px, CV crack IoU. Kill if ECE not lower or IoU drops > 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Add a skeleton head (centerline target from our 1-2 px labels) and an uncertainty head to the Dino U-Net arm; uncertainty flags E1 cells for review; skeleton output feeds crack length for severity.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Dino U-Net + skeleton + uncertainty heads vs Dino U-Net alone; crack relF1@2 on CV and E1 recall at matched precision; kill if both gains < 0.01.

title: SeaS: Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Image Generation with Separation and Sharing Fine-Tuning
mechanism: Stable Diffusion fine-tuned with an unbalanced prompt (one normal token, several anomaly tokens), decoupled anomaly alignment and normal alignment losses; masks from fused U-Net and VAE features.
adaptation: Fine-tune on rare blobby classes (splice, material, corrosion, inactive) with grey replicated to 3 channels at 512 px; do not use for 1-2 px cracks (latent 8x downsampling); generated masks checked against the house ensemble.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + SeaS samples for splice/material/corrosion, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF 5 seeds. Metric: mIoU_rob and splice IoU (0.000 now). Kill: mIoU_rob gain < +0.01 and splice still 0.
evidence: R: +12.79% IoU for supervised segmentation, +8.66% pixel AP for synthesis-based AD, on MVTec AD few-shot.
prior_overlap: None.

title: Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution (LP-FT)
mechanism: A random head distorts features during full fine-tuning; training the head first on frozen features (LP) then fine-tuning (FT) preserves them.
adaptation: PF already freezes the encoder 1k steps. Open variant: LP phase until the decoder converges (about 5k steps) then full FT at house lr, to separate LP-first from low encoder lr.
evidence: 10 shift datasets: FT +2% ID, -7% OOD vs LP; LP-FT +1% ID, +10% OOD vs FT.
min_experiment: Arm LP5k-FT(house lr) vs PF and house, seeds 5-9. Metric: E1 inactive IoU, test relF1@2. Kill if not above house on E1 inactive.
prior_overlap: Largely tested: PF is an LP-FT-like recipe (1k frozen steps plus 0.1x lr) and won E1 inactive. Only the split of LP length and post-LP lr is open.

alt_notes.adaptation: PF already does 1k frozen steps. Open variant: frozen phase until decoder converges (5k steps), then full fine-tune at the house lr (not 0.1x), to separate LP-first from low encoder lr.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: LP 5k + FT at 1e-3, 5 seeds. Baseline: SUP100-PF and house. Metric: E1 inactive IoU, layer3/4 cosine to init, test crack relF1@2. Kill: E1 inactive not above house by +0.05 (then low lr, not LP, is PF's active part).

title: Frequency-Based Matcher for Long-Tailed Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: One-to-many query matching where the number of queries matched to each class is set from class frequency, to stop oversuppression of rare classes in mask transformers; also a long-tailed seg benchmark with a dual (frequent vs rare) metric.
adaptation: In a mask classifier on our 24 classes, give inactive, splice, corrosion, material several matched queries per image; report frequent-class and rare-class mIoU separately (fits mIoU_rob vs all-class).
min_experiment: M2F arm B vs B + frequency-based matching, 5-fold CV; metric inactive IoU and mean IoU over rare classes (splice, material, edge_dark, corrosion); kill if rare-class mIoU gain < 0.02.
evidence: R: abstract only (TMM 2024); tail-class numbers not retrieved; code promised, unverified.
prior_overlap: none: long-tail losses and matching never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: report head and tail classes separately in our per-class tables. Matcher only if a Mask2Former-type decoder is adopted.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training run; adopt head/tail split reporting in the benchmark scorer and recompute existing runs.

title: Mamba-Sea: A Mamba-Based Framework With Global-to-Local Sequence Augmentation for Generalizable Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Domain generalisation via global appearance augmentation plus sequence-wise local style perturbation: resample feature mean/std inside random contiguous token sub-sequences to suppress domain-specific cues.
adaptation: Treat the 5 sources as training domains and E1 as the unseen domain. The local style perturbation is architecture-agnostic: apply it to ResNet-34 stage-1/2 feature maps over random row or column strips (half-cut scuffs are streaks), on the house PF model, at training time only.
min_experiment: House PF + strip-wise feature style resampling, 3 seeds v house PF 3 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU, test crack IoU must not drop >0.012. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 and E1 inactive IoU < +0.03.
evidence: R: first method above 90% Dice on the multi-site Prostate DG benchmark (prior SOTA 88.61%).
prior_overlap: Per-panel BN adaptation and intensity normalisation failed, but those are test-time; training-time style perturbation never tested. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Treat the 5 sources as training domains and E1 as the unseen target. Add the sequence-wise token-style perturbation to the bottleneck of Swin-UMamba or RWKV-UNet. Skip any global intensity augmentation that blurs 1 px lines.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Swin-UMamba (or RWKV-UNet) with and without sequence-wise style augmentation, 3 seeds, plus leave-one-source-out folds; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU. Kill: under +0.02 E1 relF1@2.

title: Packed-Ensembles for Efficient Uncertainty Estimation
mechanism: Grouped convolutions pack M ensemble subnetworks into one network and one forward pass while keeping deep-ensemble diversity.
adaptation: Packed U-Net++ decoder (M=4, alpha=2) on RN34; one run gives an ensemble for deployment and an uncertainty baseline for the benchmark.
min_experiment: Arm: packed U-Net++, 3 seeds. Baseline: house single and 4-seed ensemble. Metric: crack IoU, ECE. Kill: below house single.
evidence: R: matches deep ensembles on accuracy, calibration, OOD detection and shift robustness within one network's memory.
prior_overlap: none

title: SatSynth: Augmenting Image-Mask Pairs Through Diffusion Models for Aerial Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Pixel-space DDPM on the joint (image, bit-encoded label) tensor, labels as ceil(log2 K) binary channels, plus a joint super-resolution DDPM; samples added to real training data.
adaptation: 1 image channel + 5 bit channels for 24 classes; train on 256 crops at native 512 scale so cracks survive; snap crack labels to the ridge first or the joint model learns the jitter. Unconditional new layouts for all classes; best fit for mIoU_rob and inactive.
min_experiment: PF + 2,000 joint samples vs PF. Metric mIoU_rob, gridline/edge_dark/splice IoU, CV inactive IoU. Kill: mIoU_rob gain < +0.01.
evidence: R: iSAID, LoveDA, OpenEarthMap at 128 px (SR to 256); adding generated pairs gives about +1 to +1.6 IoU over real-only (read from a figure, approximate); FID 8.66 vs 17.5 DDPM on iSAID.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: 1 image channel + 5 bit channels for 24 classes; 256 crops at native scale on 478 cells; snap crack labels first; unconditional new layouts for all classes.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + 2,000 joint samples vs PF. Metric mIoU_rob, gridline/edge_dark/splice IoU, CV inactive. Kill: mIoU_rob < +0.01. About 60 GPU-h.

title: Seesaw Loss for Long-Tailed Instance Segmentation
mechanism: Per class pair, mitigate negative gradients that frequent classes put on rare classes and compensate when the rare class is wrongly predicted.
adaptation: Pixel-wise softmax version: background, ribbons, busbar suppress splice at every pixel; crack vs inactive pair benefits from compensation.
min_experiment: Arm: seesaw CE replacing CE, 3 seeds; baseline SUP100; metric mIoU_rob and splice IoU; kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01.
evidence: R: LVIS long-tailed instance segmentation, gains on rare categories (abstract level).
prior_overlap: none

title: ViT-CoMer: Vision Transformer with Convolutional Multi-scale Feature Interaction for Dense Predictions
mechanism: Bidirectional CNN-transformer fusion injecting multi-receptive-field conv features into a plain ViT, pretraining-free.
adaptation: Alternative to ViT-Adapter on DINOv3; run only the one that ports to the timm DINOv3 model with less work.
min_experiment: Same as ViT-Adapter arm; kill same.
evidence: R: ViT-CoMer-L 64.3 AP COCO val2017, 62.1 mIoU ADE20K val.
prior_overlap: none.

alt_notes.adaptation: Alternative to ViT-Adapter on DINOv3; run only whichever ports to the timm DINOv3 model with less work; same decoder and schedule.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Replace ViT-Adapter in the same arm; same baseline, metrics and kill line. About 25 GPU-h.

title: Diffusion-Based Synthetic Pretraining for Root Segmentation in Rhizotron Images
mechanism: LoRA + ControlNet + inpainting generate root images with paired masks; segmenter pretrained on synthetic then fine-tuned on real; Soft Dice against 7-annotator consensus.
adaptation: Copy the schedule: pretrain U-Net++ on generated EL pairs from the best generator, then PF fine-tune on 478 real. Its Soft Dice vs multi-annotator consensus is a template for the benchmark's crack metric using our double-annotated cells.
min_experiment: Synthetic-pretrained then PF vs PF. Metric CV crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2. Kill: both < +0.01. About 10 GPU-h once pairs exist.
evidence: R: synthetic-only Dice up to 0.60; pretrain + fine-tune 0.80; helped unseen crop species with few labels; models matched human agreement on low-ambiguity patches only.
prior_overlap: none

title: Imbalanced Medical Image Segmentation With Pixel-Dependent Noisy Labels (CLCS)
mechanism: Two-branch collaborative learning votes on pixel cleanliness with a curriculum dynamic threshold that protects minority classes, and a noise balance loss on suspected noisy pixels instead of dropping them.
adaptation: Two U-Net++ decoders on one ResNet-34 encoder; noise handling restricted to crack and inactive pixels; class-wise thresholds tuned for 0.19% crack pixels.
min_experiment: Arm: CLCS, 3 seeds on 5-fold CV. Baseline: house folds. Metric: fold-mean crack and inactive IoU. Promote if >= +0.01. About 20 GPU-h.
evidence: R: more than 3% Dice and mIoU gains on two benchmarks with different segmentation noise types (abstract).
prior_overlap: none; CPS at 5% labels was a semi-supervised use of two branches, not noisy-label selection.

title: Leveraging unlabeled SEM datasets with self-supervised learning for enhanced particle segmentation
mechanism: In-domain from-scratch ConvNeXt V2 FCMAE on 25k unlabelled greyscale SEM images, crops without rescaling to keep small details, beats ImageNet ConvNeXt V2 weights; DenseCL falls below ImageNet.
adaptation: Use their modified repo and settings (640 px crop without rescale -> 512 px for us, 32 px mask patches, 50% mask, checkpoint by val reconstruction loss) for the from-scratch arm on the EL pool; cut the 15,000-epoch schedule about 20x; Pico/Nano sizes only; 1-ch input.
min_experiment: Pico/Nano FCMAE from scratch on 11.9k (then 50k curated) vs ImageNet FCMAE weights of the same size in U-Net++ PF; out-of-fold relF1@2 and E1 crack recall, 2 seeds; kill if both < +0.01.
evidence: R (full text): +0.8 to +1.5 AJI+ low magnification, +1.9 to +5.9 high magnification over ImageNet at all 8 sizes, 10 repeats; best at Pico 8.6M; beat ImageNet with ~1,000 pretraining images on the easy task; 33 to 188 h on 80 A100s.
prior_overlap: none for this backbone/recipe; our closed run was continued MIM on ImageNet R34.

title: TopoTTA: Topology-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Tubular Structure Segmentation
mechanism: Test-time adaptation for thin structures: topological meta difference convolutions adapt without changing pretrained weights, then pseudo-break hard samples with prediction alignment restore continuity.
adaptation: Aims at E1 (half-cut, scuff). Adapt on unlabelled pool half-cells (1,152 multi half-cells), not on E1. Weak where 70% of E1 crack pixels get p < 0.001, because the pseudo-breaks need partial detection.
min_experiment: Arm: PF ensemble + TopoTTA on pool half-cells. Baseline: PF ensemble. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and recall. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03.
evidence: R (abstract): 4 scenarios, 10 datasets, average clDice +31.81% under domain shift. Code only via an anonymous link (unverified).
prior_overlap: Per-panel BN adaptation (a TTA) failed. TopoTTA uses different machinery (difference convolutions plus topology hard samples), so it is open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Adapt on the 1,152 unlabelled half-cut multi cells from the pool instead of on E1, so E1 stays a clean test. Difference convolutions may separate thin dark cracks from wider scuff streaks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: TopoTTA-style adaptation of the PF ensemble members on pool half-cuts vs the unadapted PF ensemble. Metrics: E1 crack IoU and recall, E1 inactive. Kill if E1 crack recall gains < 0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Adapt the trained PF model on unlabelled CSIR multi half-cut pool cells (same source family as E1, not E1 itself), then score E1 once.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + TopoTTA on 1,152 half-cut pool cells; baseline PF ensemble. Metric E1 crack relF1@2 and recall. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Put the difference-conv adapters in the U-Net++ decoder only. Pseudo-breaks: mask 5 to 15 px segments of predicted crack skeletons on E1 cells and align predictions on these hard samples. This targets fragmented crack predictions on scuffed half-cuts. It needs our own implementation.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: SUP100-PF + TopoTTA adapters per E1 module. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metrics: E1 component recall and relF1@2, with test crack IoU as a guard. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains < +0.02 or test crack IoU drops by 0.005.

title: BoxInst: High-Performance Instance Segmentation with Box Annotations
mechanism: Projection loss (mask max-projected on x and y must match the box) plus pairwise colour-affinity loss learn masks from boxes alone.
evidence: COCO box-only instance segmentation close to mask supervision (numbers not re-read).
adaptation: Auxiliary projection + intensity-affinity loss on the crack channel for PVEL-AD crack boxes; projection suits long thin cracks spanning the box.
min_experiment: Arm: house + PVEL-AD boxes with BoxInst loss, 5 seeds. Baseline: house 5-seed and Boxes2Pixels arm. Metric: E1 crack recall, clean-49 crack relF1@2. Kill if E1 recall < +0.03. ~15 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: none

title: Cross-Scenario Industrial Defect Detection via Domain-Robust Training and Metric-Aligned Selection
mechanism: Robust normalisation, DSU feature-statistic perturbation, progressive random convolution, small-defect loss, score calibration, and a SWAD variant with metric-aligned checkpoint selection for unseen production scenarios.
adaptation: Closest domain found (boards with surface contaminants, like scuffs). Take DSU in encoder layer1-2 and checkpoint selection on val relF1@2 rather than loss; drop detection-only parts (NWD, VFL).
min_experiment: PF + DSU vs PF, 3 seeds; kill at < +0.03 E1 crack relF1@2.
evidence: R: Track 1 score 0.564, screening 0.696 on hidden test, single RTX 4090; no ablation in abstract.
prior_overlap: none

title: Devil is in the Queries: Advancing Mask Transformers for Real-world Medical Image Segmentation and Out-of-Distribution Localization
mechanism: Object queries act as feature cluster centres; pixel-to-query similarity gives an OOD map (MaxQuery); a query-distribution loss separates targets from background at query level.
adaptation: E1 decoys: scuff streaks and half-cut layouts are OOD; use the MaxQuery map from the EoMT or M2F arm to suppress crack predictions where pixels are far from every query, or report it as an abstention score in the benchmark.
min_experiment: Inference-only filter on the trained mask classifier vs same model unfiltered; metric E1 crack relP@2 at fixed relR@2 and false-alarm px on half-cut scuff cells; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.01.
evidence: R: pancreatic and liver tumour segmentation, +5.27 DSC over nnU-Net on inliers; OOD AUROC +7.39, AUPR +14.69, FPR95 -13.79 vs previous SOTA.
prior_overlap: none: anomaly priors and OOD scoring never tried.

title: Diversified and Personalized Multi-Rater Medical Image Segmentation (D-Persona)
mechanism: Stage 1 trains a Probabilistic U-Net on multi-rater labels to build a shared latent space. Stage 2 attention heads extract expert-specific prompts for personalized masks.
adaptation: Use label versions as raters: the 2021 original and 2022 revised crack/inactive masks exist for the same cells. Train on both and output the revised-style persona, so the old labels add signal instead of being discarded.
min_experiment: Arm = two-version D-Persona-style head (3 seeds) versus house PF on revised labels only. Metric: crack IoU clean-49 and relF1@2. Kill if < +0.012.
evidence: R: NPC-170 (in-house) and LIDC-IDRI; better diversity and personalized accuracy than multi-rater baselines (abstract).
prior_overlap: label version change gave +0.05 to +0.08 crack IoU, but no run trained on both versions jointly

alt_notes.adaptation: Use label version as rater: 2021 original and 2022 revised BenchmarkEL crack / inactive masks give two raters per cell. Train on both, output the revised persona; the old masks become extra signal instead of being discarded.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: two-rater (version) model, 5 seeds, revised-persona output. Baseline: house PF on revised labels only. Metric: clean-49 crack and inactive IoU. Kill if crack IoU gain < +0.012 and inactive < +0.03.

title: Noise-Consistent Siamese-Diffusion for Medical Image Synthesis and Segmentation
mechanism: Mask-Diffusion and Image-Diffusion branches trained with a noise-consistency loss so that the mask-only sampler keeps real morphology; only the mask branch is used at sampling.
adaptation: Train-time add-on to the retrained PV-DDPM (row 2) for inactive, material and corrosion on 478 cells; the image branch uses the real cell as extra condition during training.
min_experiment: Arm: PV-DDPM + noise-consistency loss. Baseline: plain PV-DDPM at matched steps. Metric: house-ensemble inactive IoU on 200 synthetic pairs (adherence), then CV inactive IoU. Kill: adherence gain < 0.05.
evidence: R: SANet mDice +3.6, mIoU +4.4 on polyps; UNet +1.52 / +1.64 on ISIC2018.
prior_overlap: None.

title: Progressive Random Convolutions for Single Domain Generalization
mechanism: Repeated application of one small random conv block (with deformable offsets and affine) grows augmentation diversity without destroying semantics.
adaptation: Zero the deformable offsets (they move 1-2 px cracks off their labels). Run as the alternative to GIN in the same arm family.
min_experiment: PF + Pro-RandConv (no offsets) vs PF + GIN arm; keep the better on val/F51; kill if neither beats PF by +0.03 E1 relF1@2.
evidence: R: 68.88% single-source PACS (ResNet-18), 81.35% Digits (classification).
prior_overlap: none

title: Steady Progress Beats Stagnation: Mutual Aid of Foundation and Conventional Models in Mixed Domain Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: A LoRA-tuned foundation model and a conventional U-Net co-train on mixed-domain unlabelled data. The pseudo-label is a per-image weighted ensemble set by self-confidence and mutual agreement: the FM leads early, the CNN corrects its over-confident errors later, and a consensus-divergence consistency loss ties them.
adaptation: FM = SAM2 Hiera or DINOv2-B + LoRA with a mask head, which supplies context such as the half-cut layout. Conventional model = house U-Net++, which supplies thin-crack resolution. The mixed-domain unlabelled set = pool (CSIR/ARTS, mono, multi, half-cells), with labelled cells from 5 sources.
min_experiment: Arm: SynFoC pair with the CNN branch evaluated, 3 seeds. Baseline: PF house. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, clean-49 crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 and inactive IoU gain < +0.03.
evidence: R: four multi-domain medical datasets (Prostate, Fundus, M&Ms, BUSI) at few labels; Prostate Dice +10.31% over prior methods.
prior_overlap: Partial. The SSL row ran on ResNet-34 only, and BRIEF lists SSL with foundation-model teachers as open. CPS (also co-training) was run at 5% only.

title: Crucial-Diff: A Unified Diffusion Model for Crucial Image and Annotation Synthesis in Data-Scarce Scenarios
mechanism: A weakness-aware sample miner uses downstream model feedback to steer diffusion toward hard-to-detect samples, fused with a scene-agnostic feature extractor.
adaptation: Feedback = house-model per-pixel loss on generated crack/inactive; hard targets are cracks under 2% contrast, BMRK inactive, CFVS cells without a train twin, half-cut scuff cells; combine with GDI canvases.
min_experiment: Generator with loss feedback vs same generator unguided, matched count, on PF. Metric CV inactive IoU and test relR@2 on cracks < 2% contrast. Kill: < +0.01 over unguided.
evidence: R: MVTec pixel AP 83.63, F1-max 78.12; polyp mIoU 81.64, mDice 87.69.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Feedback = house per-pixel loss; hard targets = cracks under 2% contrast, BMRK inactive, CFVS without twin, scuffed half-cut cells; pair with GDI canvases.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Guided vs unguided generator at matched count. Metric CV inactive IoU, test relR@2 on low-contrast cracks. Kill: < +0.01. About 20 GPU-h.

title: Distilling Knowledge from Heterogeneous Architectures for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: KD between CNN and Transformer by projecting intermediate features into an aligned logit space, with reliability-based teacher-student knowledge mixing and evaluation.
adaptation: Transformer teacher (best from D23/D24) into the house U-Net++ RN34 student to carry global context for half-cut layout and scuff without transformer inference cost.
min_experiment: Arm: HeteroAKD student. Baseline: logit KD from the same teacher. Metric: E1 relF1@2, crack IoU. Kill: < +0.01 over logit KD.
evidence: R: beats prior KD methods on three mainstream segmentation benchmarks across heterogeneous teacher-student pairs.
prior_overlap: none

title: Frequency-Aware Feature Fusion for Dense Image Prediction (FreqFusion)
mechanism: Decoder fusion with adaptive low-pass filters inside regions, offset resampling for inconsistent features, and adaptive high-pass filters that restore boundary detail lost in downsampling.
adaptation: Replace nearest-upsample + concat in each U-Net++ decoder node with FreqFusion; the high-pass path targets 1-2 px cracks and finger interruptions.
min_experiment: Arm: house PF with FreqFusion decoder; baseline: house PF; CV crack IoU, gridline IoU. Kill if both n.d. (crack < 0.012, gridline < 0.03).
evidence: R: abstract reports gains across dense prediction tasks; numbers not retrieved.
prior_overlap: none; decoder never varied.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace nearest-upsample + concat in each U-Net++ decoder node; the high-pass path targets cracks and gridline; test as one family with SFM.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house PF + FreqFusion decoder vs house PF; 5-fold CV gridline IoU and crack relF1@2; kill: gridline IoU < +0.03 and crack IoU n.d. About 10 GPU-h.

title: GAUDA: Generative Adaptive Uncertainty-Guided Diffusion-Based Augmentation for Surgical Segmentation
mechanism: Joint LDM over compact (image, mask) latents; generation is targeted online at classes where a Bayesian segmenter's epistemic uncertainty is highest.
adaptation: Uncertainty per class from the 5-seed house ensemble; condition on class presence for inactive, splice, gridline, edge_dark, material; run offline in 3 rounds instead of online.
min_experiment: 3 rounds of uncertainty-targeted generation vs one-shot generation at matched count, on PF. Metric mIoU_rob. Kill: < +0.01.
evidence: R: +1.6 IoU CaDISv2, +1.5 IoU CholecSeg8k over comparable methods.
prior_overlap: none

title: Rethinking boundary detection in deep learning-based medical image segmentation (CTO)
mechanism: Boundary-guided decoder: fixed edge operators produce a binary boundary map that supervises a boundary-extraction module whose output is injected back into the decoder.
evidence: R (read): ISIC 2016 IoU 84.92 -> 86.60 vs Boundary loss 85.25 and Boundary DoU 85.70 on the same base; ISIC 2018 ablation BEM +0.5 IoU, BIM +0.4.
adaptation: Use only BEM/BIM on U-Net++ (no ViT stream). Sobel responses on EL fire on busbars, gridlines, cell edges and the 4 px crack ridge, independent of the jittered crack label.
min_experiment: Only if SBCB arm is positive: house + BEM/BIM vs house; gridline, edge_dark IoU, crack relF1@2; kill if mIoU_rob gain < 0.01 over the SBCB arm.
prior_overlap: none

title: U-Harmony: Enhancing Joint Training for Segmentation Models with Universal Harmonization
mechanism: Per-instance feature harmonization, then restoration layers that reinject dataset-specific statistics into the decoder. A domain-gated head infers each domain's contribution from prototypes, so no dataset ID is needed at test.
adaptation: A source-gated decoder for the case where the source is unknown or shifted (E1 half-cut CSIR, benchmark new-module track). Check whether the gate picks CSIR on E1.
min_experiment: Arm = house PF + harmonize/restore + gated head (3 seeds) versus house PF. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 and test crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.02 and test is n.d.
evidence: R: cross-institution brain lesion datasets; a secondary summary reports up to +8.4% DSC (unverified against the full paper).
prior_overlap: per-panel BN adaptation failed, but that was test-time BN statistics, not learned dataset-gated restoration

alt_notes.adaptation: Source-gated decoder for cells of unknown source (benchmark new-module track, WattCycle's future rig); compare gate-chosen source with the true source on E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: U-Harmony gated decoder, 5 seeds, no source ID at test vs source-FiLM arm with true ID and house PF; metric clean-49 crack IoU and E1 relF1@2; kill if it does not reach at least half of the source-FiLM gain.

title: A WDLoRA-Based Multimodal Generative Framework for Clinically Guided Corneal Confocal Microscopy Image Synthesis in Diabetic Neuropathy
mechanism: Foundation diffusion model fine-tuned with weight-decomposed LoRA, conditioned jointly on thin nerve-fibre masks and clinical prompts.
adaptation: Prompt = source and cell type (e.g. CSIR mono half-cut, BMRK) so every train mask can be rendered in each source style; targets weak sources (BMRK, CFVS without twin) and E1 style.
