min_experiment: PF + all train masks rendered in BMRK and CSIR half-cut styles vs PF. Metric CV BMRK inactive/crack IoU and E1 relF1@2. Kill: BMRK inactive CV gain < +0.03 and E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02.
evidence: R: grayscale corneal confocal microscopy with thin fibres; FID 5.18, SSIM 0.630; downstream segmentation +2.2%, diagnosis +2.1%.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Prompt = source and cell type so each train mask renders in every source style (BMRK, half-cut CSIR).
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + masks rendered in BMRK and half-cut CSIR styles vs PF. Kill: BMRK inactive CV < +0.03 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.02. About 30 GPU-h.

title: Deep Hierarchical Semantic Segmentation (HSSN)
mechanism: Pixel-wise multi-label classification over a class tree, with a tree-min loss that keeps child scores at or below their parent, plus hierarchy-based embedding margins.
adaptation: A 2-level tree: cell area -> feature lines (gridline, busbar, ribbon, splice), defects (crack, inactive, material, corrosion), and the rest. Add parent sigmoid channels with tree-min consistency and keep softmax leaves. Aimed at splice (never predicted) and gridline (recall 0.33).
min_experiment: Arm: house + parent channels + tree-min loss. Baseline: house. Metrics: gridline, splice and material IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill if mIoU_rob gain < 0.01 and splice stays at 0.
evidence: R: gains on Mapillary Vistas 2.0, Cityscapes, LIP and PASCAL-Person-Part across backbones. The abstract page gives no numbers.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Two-level tree: cell area -> {structural lines: gridline, busbar, ribbon, splice; defects: crack, inactive, material, corrosion}; parent sigmoid channels + tree-min, leaves stay softmax; target splice (0.000) and gridline (0.283).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house + parent channels + tree-min; baseline house; metrics gridline, splice, edge_dark IoU, mIoU_rob; kill if mIoU_rob gain < 0.01 and splice still 0.

title: Improving Semantic Segmentation via Video Propagation and Label Relaxation
mechanism: Boundary label relaxation: at boundary pixels maximise the summed probability of all classes in a small window, so small misplacements are not punished.
adaptation: Within a 3x3 window of crack label pixels the target is crack OR neighbour class (log of summed probabilities); elsewhere standard CE; tolerates 1 px jitter without widening the target.
min_experiment: Arm: relaxed CE on crack, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012 at equal relP@2.
evidence: R: Cityscapes 83.5 mIoU, robustness to boundary annotation noise and propagation artefacts.
prior_overlap: Partial: offset-tolerant CE (P14) at 10% labels used a min over shifts and was n.d.; summed-probability relaxation at 100% labels is untested.

title: Learn2Synth: Learning Optimal Data Synthesis Using Hypergradients for Brain Image Segmentation
mechanism: Learn the parameters of a synthesis or augmentation engine by hypergradients, so a segmenter trained on synthetic or augmented data is optimal on a small real labelled set that is never trained on directly.
adaptation: Engine = about 10 parametric EL augmentations (crack-region contrast, blur matching the 4 px FWHM, scuff-streak overlay, half-cut masking, per-source gamma). Outer objective = soft crack IoU on val 54 + F51 (+ H36 for half-cut). After the search, fix the parameters and run a full house training.
min_experiment: Arm: house net trained with the learned augmentation parameters, 5 seeds. Baseline: house with label-safe augmentation. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 (primary), test crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 below house + 0.02, or test crack IoU down by more than 0.012.
evidence: R: brain MRI synthetic-to-real; learned parametric and nonparametric synthesis beat hand-tuned domain randomization on synthetic and real scans (numbers not read; abstract only).
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF lists physics-based and generative synthesis as untried. Synthetic half-cut views were tried with hand-set parameters (n.d.); learned parameters are open.

title: LesionMix: A Lesion-Level Data Augmentation Method for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Lesion-level augmentation that controls lesion load distribution, shape, location and intensity, both populating and inpainting lesions.
adaptation: Unify paste (Soft-CP / CarveMix) and removal (GDI) under per-source load sampling: per cell, sample crack component count and inactive area from the train distribution of its source and add or remove to reach it.
min_experiment: Best of GDI / CarveMix / Soft-CP arms with vs without load control; kill < +0.01 on that arm's metric.
evidence: Outperforms recent Mix-based augmentations on 4 brain MR and 1 liver CT lesion datasets (abstract; no numbers read).
prior_overlap: none.

title: RaffeSDG: Random Frequency Filtering enabled Single-source Domain Generalization for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Random frequency-filter augmentation with blending of homologous samples, plus Gaussian-filter structural saliency for consistent representations across augmented views.
evidence: R: improved out-of-domain segmentation for three tissues imaged by four modalities.
adaptation: Restrict random filtering below about 1/16 px^-1 so crack bands survive; compare with GIN as the single-source DG choice for E1.
min_experiment: Run only if GIN-IPA shows a signal. Arm: house + RaffeSDG. Baseline: house + GIN. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: not better than GIN by 0.02.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Restrict random filtering to frequencies below about 1/16 px^-1 so 4 px crack bands stay intact; run only if GIN shows a signal.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + RaffeSDG augmentation, 5 seeds. Baselines: house and GIN arm. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: not better than GIN by 0.02.

title: Rethinking "Batch" in BatchNorm
mechanism: Review of BN caveats from batch choices (train vs population stats, precise BN, frozen BN in fine-tuning, domain-specific stats) and their fixes.
adaptation: Batch 8 with 5 mixed sources: test encoder BN frozen at ImageNet stats, precise-BN recompute on train before eval, and both. Required plumbing for EMA, SWAD, WiSE-FT, LiNeS arms.
evidence: Review with mitigations in visual recognition (abstract).
min_experiment: Precise BN on existing checkpoints (zero training), then frozen-BN arm vs PF seeds 5-9. Kill if val relF1@2 change < +0.005.
prior_overlap: Partial: per-panel BN adaptation at test time failed; training-time BN choices never varied.

alt_notes.adaptation: Batch 8 mixes 5 sources: test (a) encoder BN frozen at ImageNet stats, (b) precise-BN recompute on train before eval, (c) both. Needed plumbing for weight averaging arms.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: (b) free on existing checkpoints; (a) and (c) 5 seeds. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metric: test crack relF1@2, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: all within noise.

title: Segmentation Style Discovery: Application to Skin Lesion Images
mechanism: StyleSeg: M output heads plus a style classifier on (image, mask); winner-take-all Dice plus classifier-weighted Dice discovers M consistent styles without annotator IDs.
adaptation: M = 3 crack heads combined with source ID, to discover within-source annotator styles; after training pick each source's majority style head from train cells and use it at test.
min_experiment: Arm: source-FiLM + 3 style heads, 5 seeds vs source-FiLM arm alone; metric clean-49 crack IoU; kill if < +0.012 over the source-FiLM arm.
evidence: R: outperforms competing methods on four skin-lesion datasets; strong alignment of discovered styles with annotator preferences on ISIC-MultiAnnot.
prior_overlap: none

title: Towards In-context Scene Understanding (Hummingbird)
mechanism: Dense in-context prediction by nearest-neighbour retrieval from a memory of annotated patch features; pretraining with within- and across-image attention makes features suited to retrieval.
evidence: R: approaches finetuned specialists on scene understanding without modification; adapts to new tasks more efficiently than finetuning.
adaptation: Retrieval head on the house model: memory of patch features (house decoder at 1/2-1/4 res or DINOv2) from the fold's train cells, kNN label votes fused with house logits by a val-tuned weight; same-source retrieval variant to model source label conventions; targets splice (never predicted), gridline (recall 0.33), inactive.
min_experiment: cv5v2 house PF fold models with vs without kNN fusion (any-source and same-source); out-of-fold mIoU_rob and splice/gridline/inactive IoU; kill if mIoU_rob gain under margin M and no class above +0.02. No training, about 1 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: none; no nonparametric or retrieval head was ever tried.

title: Weakly Supervised Segmentation of Cracks on Solar Cells using Normalized Lp Norm
mechanism: Train a classifier with normalized-Lp pooling over activation maps so the maps become crack segmentations from image-level labels only.
adaptation: Add an image-level crack head (Lp-pooled crack logits) to the house model, trained on the 2,624 ELPV cells, the same source as our weak BMRK cells, after removing every ELPV cell present in BMRK val/test.
min_experiment: Arm: house + Lp image-level loss on ELPV. Baseline: house, 5 seeds. Metric: BMRK crack IoU (0.379 now) and overall crack IoU. Kill if BMRK crack IoU < +0.03.
evidence: R: abstract only; ResNet-50 activation-map segmentation of cracks from ELPV-type image labels; no number retrieved.
prior_overlap: none; multi-dataset training with ELPV image labels listed as untried

alt_notes.adaptation: EL-specific image-label baseline trained on ELPV labels for a weak-supervision track of the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark only: train on ELPV image labels, score crack relF1@2 on clean-49 and E1 against house model. ~2 GPU-h.

title: A Directional Connectivity Feature Enhancement Network for Pavement Crack Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
mechanism: Multi-directional enhanced convolution plus a directional-connectivity loss on neighbouring pixels for cracks.
adaptation: Port only the directional-connectivity loss to the crack head of the house model; closest-domain evidence for DconnNet-style outputs.
min_experiment: Arm = PF + directional connectivity loss on crack; baseline = PF; 5 seeds; components found, relF1@2. Kill if gain < 0.01.
evidence: R: +2.2% ODS and +1.8% mIoU on DeepCrack; +1.2 ODS, +0.9 mIoU on Crack500; six crack datasets.
prior_overlap: None.

title: Convolutional CRFs for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Fully connected CRF made local (conditional independence outside a window) so mean-field inference is a convolution; over 100x faster and all kernel parameters learnable by backprop.
evidence: R: >100x speed-up over FullCRF for inference and training (abstract). R (from rNCA table): DenseCRF on DRIVE vessels: Dice 0.761 -> 0.760, dBeta0 0.965 -> 0.712 (fewer fragments).
adaptation: Inactive arm: bilateral intensity + position kernel on the ensemble softmax so partial inactive detections expand to the uniform dark region bounded by cracks (inactive is dark, blobby, well labelled, recall 0.61). Crack arm: small spatial kernel only, as a test of whether snapping to the dark ridge helps or hurts strict IoU (labels sit off the ridge). Kernel weights fit on val / OOF; base model unchanged.
min_experiment: Arm: ConvCRF/DenseCRF on house ensemble softmax (and PF ensemble on E1). Baseline: house ensemble argmax. Metrics: inactive IoU and recall on clean-49 and OOF CV, E1 inactive IoU, crack relF1@2 as a guard. Kill: inactive IoU < +0.02 on OOF CV or crack relF1@2 drop > 0.005.
prior_overlap: none. Inference-side runs were ensemble, logit bias, BN adaptation, intensity normalisation, per-module thresholds; no CRF.

title: Deep Closing: Enhancing Topological Connectivity in Medical Tubular Segmentation
mechanism: A masked-image-modelling autoencoder trained on label masks learns a tubular shape prior and flags likely disconnections; a simple-components erosion keeps only topologically meaningful additions to the base segmentation.
adaptation: Train the shape prior on crack label masks only (no images), so all labelled crack masks can be used; apply to house predictions to close gaps between collinear fragments; guard against bridging across busbars.
min_experiment: Arm: house ensemble + Deep Closing. Baseline: house ensemble. Metrics: components found, relR@2 at fixed relP@2, crack IoU on 5-fold CV and E1. Kill: relR@2 gain < +0.01 or relP@2 drop > 0.01.
evidence: R: topology metrics improved on DRIVE, CHASE_DB1, DCA1, CREMI; transfers knowledge from external datasets (numbers not read).
prior_overlap: Partly near soft clDice and Skeleton Recall losses (BRIEF section 5), but those are training losses; a post-hoc label-only shape prior was not tested.

title: DGSAM: Domain Generalization via Individual Sharpness-Aware Minimization
mechanism: SAM can find flat total loss but sharp per-domain loss; gradual domain-wise perturbation lowers sharpness per domain at less cost than SAM.
adaptation: Domains = the 5 image sources; source-balanced batches; per-source perturbation steps. Aimed at BMRK weakness and E1 (CSIR-heavy).
evidence: Beats SOTA DG methods on several benchmarks with less overhead than SAM (abstract).
min_experiment: Arm DGSAM vs PF+SAM, seeds 5-9; metric per-source test crack IoU (BMRK) and E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if BMRK and E1 not better than PF+SAM.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Domains = the 5 image sources (ARTS, CFVS, CSIR, BMRK, SDLE); per-source perturbation steps with source-balanced batches; aims at BMRK weakness and CSIR-heavy E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + DGSAM, 5 seeds, only if plain SAM moved E1. Baseline: PF + SAM and SUP100-PF. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, BMRK crack/inactive IoU. Kill: no gain over PF + SAM.

title: Diffusion-Guided Mask-Consistent Paired Mixing for Endoscopic Image Segmentation (MCPMix)
mechanism: For each real image, a synthetic counterpart is generated under the same mask; only appearance is mixed and supervision always uses the original mask, with annealing back to real data.
adaptation: Counterparts from the UnIACorN or ContourDiff generator (half-cut CSIR style); supervision stays the real mask so generator drift adds no label noise; anneal mix strength to zero by step 20k.
min_experiment: PF + paired mixing vs PF + plain synthetic using the same counterparts. Metric E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: gain over plain synthetic < +0.01.
evidence: R: Kvasir-SEG, PICCOLO, CVC-ClinicDB, private NPC-LES, ISIC 2017; state of the art claimed, abstract gives no numbers.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Counterparts from the translation/ControlNet arms in target style; real masks keep labels clean even if the generator drifts; anneal to real by step 20k.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Paired mixing vs plain synthetic with the same counterparts on PF. Metric E1 relF1@2. Kill: < +0.01. About 6 GPU-h.

title: DPN: detail-preserving network with high resolution representation for efficient segmentation of retinal vessels
venue: Journal of Ambient Intelligence and Humanized Computing
mechanism: Stacked detail-preserving blocks with no downsampling keep full resolution throughout; about 120k parameters.
adaptation: Add a DPN-style full-res branch (8 blocks, 16-32 ch, on the 1-ch input) concatenated into the last U-Net++ decoder node; about +10% compute. Also usable as a structurally different ensemble member.
min_experiment: Arm: house PF + DPN branch; baseline: house PF; CV gridline IoU, crack IoU; also add as 6th member to the 5-seed PF ensemble. Kill if gridline IoU < +0.03, crack IoU n.d., and ensemble crack IoU < +0.005.
evidence: R: comparable accuracy on DRIVE (20 training images), CHASE_DB1, HRF; 20-160x faster than other methods on DRIVE; ~120k params.
prior_overlap: Partly R5 (2x input, n.d. on test crack IoU under house optimizer). R5 did not add a full-res path at native receptive field, did not target gridline, and did not use PF or ensemble diversity.

alt_notes.adaptation: Add a DPN-style full-resolution branch (8 blocks, 16 to 32 ch) on the 1-ch input, concatenated into the house decoder's last block, which in smp likely has no stride-1 skip.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house PF + DPN branch + raw-image pixel-unshuffle re-injection vs house PF; 5-fold CV gridline IoU, crack IoU; also as a 6th ensemble member. Kill: gridline IoU < +0.03 and crack IoU n.d.; ensemble crack IoU < +0.005. About 15 GPU-h.

title: DragOSM: Extract Building Roofs and Footprints from Aerial Images by Aligning Historical Labels
mechanism: Label alignment as iterative denoising: a model learns to move randomly Gaussian-perturbed labels back to their position, then is applied iteratively to real misaligned labels.
adaptation: Bold bet: train a small label snapper on (EL image, crack label perturbed by 1 to 3 px shifts and width changes) to recover the unperturbed label. Annotator jitter is random but the ridge is consistent, so the snapper should learn the expected label position given the image, which sits on the ridge. Apply to all train labels, retrain.
min_experiment: Gate first: on val, the snapper must move labels at least 0.3 px on average toward the dark ridge. Then arm: house on snapped labels, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill: gate fails, or crack IoU under +0.012.
evidence: R: new ReBO dataset, 179,265 buildings with OSM and corrected labels in 5,473 images; reported effective alignment (numbers not read).
prior_overlap: none

title: Edge-Boundary-Texture Loss: A Tri-Class Generalization of Weighted Binary Cross-Entropy for Enhanced Edge Detection
mechanism: Split pixels into edge, boundary (near-edge) and texture classes, each with its own supervisory weight, generalising weighted BCE.
adaptation: Crack / 1-2 px ring around the label skeleton / rest; low weight (0.2) on the ring so firing on the ridge 1 px off the drawn line is barely punished; applied to the crack channel of the 24-class CE.
min_experiment: Arm PF with EBT ring weights vs PF; metric relF1@2 and width ratio; kill if relF1@2 +<0.01 or width ratio >1.2.
evidence: Beats WBCE across several edge benchmarks with one fixed hyperparameter set; numbers not read.
prior_overlap: partial: BRIEF 5 offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) used tolerance, not near-crack down-weighting; open

title: Frequency-Adaptive Dilated Convolution for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Per-pixel dilation rate set from local frequency content; AdaKern balances low / high kernel parts; FreqSelect damps high frequency in background regions.
adaptation: Put FADC + FreqSelect in ResNet-34 layer3/4 at output stride 16. FreqSelect could learn to damp the finger frequency band away from defects.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + FADC in layer3/4, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metric: crack IoU, gridline IoU. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012.
evidence: R: gains on semantic segmentation and detection (abstract); numbers not read.
prior_overlap: none

title: ST++: Make Self-training Work Better for Semi-supervised Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Score each unlabelled image's reliability by how much saved checkpoints disagree on it. Retrain on the reliable images first. Use strong aug on unlabelled images.
adaptation: Rank pool cells by prediction agreement across the 5 seeds or checkpoints. Drop the least stable half (scuff, odd contrast, multi half-cells) before the NS or MIC arms. A cheap filter for an out-of-distribution pool.
min_experiment: NS-12k with the top-50% stable pool vs NS-12k with the full pool, 5 seeds. Metric: crack IoU and E1 relF1@2. Kill if n.d.
evidence: R: Pascal / Cityscapes SSL gains reported over plain self-training; numbers not in the abstract.
prior_overlap: Image-level selection was not used in our Mean Teacher runs (pixel thresholds only). Open, as an add-on.

title: Universal Topology Refinement for Medical Image Segmentation with Polynomial Feature Synthesis
mechanism: A model-agnostic topology refiner trained on synthetic perturbation masks generated from random orthogonal-polynomial fields, so the error distribution is not limited by a small labelled set or one network's biases.
adaptation: Generate polynomial perturbations on every crack label available (478 train, E-SCDD train cells, UCF-EL thin parts used label-only); use as the synthetic error source for the refiner in the Chen 2024 arm; compare error models.
min_experiment: Arm: refiner trained with polynomial perturbations. Baseline: house ensemble, and the morphological-error refiner. Metric: 5-fold CV components found, relF1@2, crack IoU. Kill: no gain > +0.005 relF1@2 over the house ensemble.
evidence: R: outperformed topology-driven losses and post-processing methods on medical segmentation; designed for small datasets (numbers not read).
prior_overlap: none.

title: Unified Focal loss: Generalising Dice and cross entropy-based losses to handle class imbalanced medical image segmentation
mechanism: Compound of asymmetric focal CE and asymmetric focal Tversky with three hyperparameters, generalising Dice, CE, focal and Tversky losses.
adaptation: Replace CE + Dice; asymmetry set to favour crack and inactive recall toward the relR@2 >= 0.90 target, with relP@2 watched as the width check.
min_experiment: Arm Unified Focal (paper defaults) vs SUP100, 5 v 5. Kill if relR@2 not up by 0.02 at relP@2 drop <= 0.05 and crack IoU not better.
evidence: R: imbalanced medical segmentation tasks (884 cites); numbers not read.
prior_overlap: none (focal / Tversky family untested)

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace CE + Dice; asymmetry set to favour crack and inactive recall to chase relR@2 >= 0.90; Keras code must be ported (PyTorch port on PyPI untested).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: Unified Focal at paper defaults, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Kill: relR@2 not up by 0.02 at relP@2 drop <= 0.05.

title: AnomalyDINO: Boosting Patch-based Few-Shot Anomaly Detection with DINOv2
mechanism: Training-free patch nearest-neighbour scoring on DINOv2 features against a few normal reference images.
adaptation: References = clean pool cells of the same source and layout (half-cut references from the 1,152 pool half-cells); 448 px input with ViT-S/14 and ViT-L/14; map used as an extra input channel or gating prior for inactive and for E1 recall; also the pseudo-target generator for AGSSP-EL.
min_experiment: Offline recall study as for MuSc (F51/H36), then add the map as a 2nd input channel to PF U-Net++, 5 seeds; metric inactive IoU (test, 5-fold CV) and E1 inactive IoU; kill if inactive IoU gain < +0.02 on CV.
evidence: R: one-shot MVTec-AD image AUROC 93.1 to 96.6; training-free.
prior_overlap: none; anomaly priors never tried. Frozen DINOv2-S linear probe (segmentation) is a different use.

alt_notes.adaptation: References = pool cells of the same source and layout that the house ensemble calls clean (pool contains defects, so filter the memory bank SoftPatch-style); 1,152 pool half-cells give half-cut references for E1; 448 px, ViT-S/14 and ViT-L/14; map as prior channel or logit fusion.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Offline recall test as above; baseline PF ensemble; kill if < 30% of house-missed components recovered at 1% flagged area.

title: blob loss: Instance Imbalance Aware Loss Functions for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Per GT component Dice with all other components masked, averaged over components and added to a global loss.
adaptation: Merged crack instances and inactive components; reference arm for the benchmark's loss suite.
min_experiment: Arm: house + blob Dice on crack/inactive, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: component F1 and relF1@2. Kill: no component F1 gain >= 0.02.
evidence: Five 3D tasks: F1 +5% MS lesions, +3% liver tumour, +2% microscopy vs soft Dice. In BiCC's comparison blob loss lowered precision and Dice on 4 of 5 datasets.
prior_overlap: none

title: Exploring few-shot defect segmentation in general industrial scenarios with metric learning and vision foundation models (GFDS / FM-SAM)
mechanism: Training-free few-shot defect segmentation; SAM2 run in video-tracking mode with the support image+mask as the previous frame and the query as the current frame, plus a DINO feature-matching variant refined by FastSAM.
evidence: R: 1-shot over 54 industrial defect classes, SAM2-s video mode 47.9 mIoU at 1024 px, 38.8 at 512, 23.9 at 256; FM-l 36.5 (39.3 with FastSAM); PerSAM 8.0, Matcher 5.0; meta-learning FSS ill-suited to defects.
adaptation: Upsample 512 px cells to 1024, replicate 1 channel to 3; supports = k nearest labelled train cells by DINOv2 global feature, same cell type when known; one binary pass per class (inactive, crack, splice, ribbons); labeller for the 1,152 pool multi half-cells and K-shot benchmark baseline; crack judged only by relF1@2 since the 1/4-res decoder thickens lines.
min_experiment: G0 gate: K=1/4/16 retrieved supports predict val54+F51+H36; baseline house PF 5-seed ensemble on same cells; metrics inactive IoU, crack relF1@2, splice/gridline IoU, fraction of house misses recovered; kill if below house on every class and recovers <10% of house misses on H36 inactive. If pass: PF on 478 + labeller pseudo-labelled half-cells vs PF + house-labelled half-cells, H36 inactive IoU and F51 crack relF1@2, kill under margin M.
prior_overlap: Partial: pseudo-label SSL with the house teacher was n.d. at 100% labels on the 11.9k pool; a foundation-model in-context labeller (different, possibly decorrelated errors) was never tested, and half-cell-targeted distillation was not.

title: DeSTSeg: Segmentation Guided Denoising Student-Teacher for Anomaly Detection
mechanism: Frozen teacher, denoising student trained to map corrupted normals to clean teacher features, and a segmentation head that fuses multi-level teacher-student discrepancies under synthetic-mask supervision.
adaptation: Teacher = ImageNet ResNet-34 (house encoder init); student trained on clean pool cells corrupted with dark Gaussian-profile lines (FWHM 3-5 px, 2-20% contrast) and dark blobs; seg head supervised by real crack + inactive labels (478 cells) plus synthetic masks; output a 2-class map as 6th ensemble member on crack / inactive logits.
evidence: R: MVTec AD image AUC 98.6, pixel AP 75.8, instance AP 76.4.
min_experiment: Arm: 5 PF seeds + DeSTSeg-EL member; baseline: 5 PF seeds. Metric: CV relR@2 at relP@2 >= 0.90, inactive IoU. Kill: relR@2 gain < +0.02.
prior_overlap: none; 5-seed ensembling is closed as a win but a heterogeneous AD member is listed as untested.

title: Hybrid-Segmentor: Hybrid approach for automated fine-grained crack segmentation in civil infrastructure
mechanism: Parallel CNN path for fine local features and transformer path for global crack pattern with a fused decoder, trained on a large merge of public crack datasets.
adaptation: Benchmark row with public crack weights; for our scores, init from their merged-data weights and add a 24-class head (or crack + inactive), gray to 3 channels, house loss and schedule.
min_experiment: Arm: Hybrid-Segmentor from their weights, fine-tuned; baseline: PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill as a model if CV crack IoU < PF minus 0.02; keep as benchmark row.
evidence: R: accuracy 0.971, precision 0.807, recall 0.756, F1 0.774, IoU 0.631 on their merged dataset; a third-party repo reports mIoU 67.10 vs UNet 67.39 on another dataset (web, unverified).
prior_overlap: none (no transformer segmenter tried).

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark baseline with public crack weights: initialise from their CrackVision12K weights, gray to 3 channels, crack + inactive + background head or 24-class head, fine-tune on our folds.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: Hybrid-Segmentor fine-tuned; baseline PF crack channel; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU and relF1@2. Kill as a model if CV crack IoU < PF minus 0.02; keep as benchmark row.

title: Pixel Difference Networks for Efficient Edge Detection (PiDiNet)
mechanism: Pixel difference convolutions fold classic gradient operators into conv layers, giving an accurate edge detector under 1M params trained from scratch.
adaptation: Swap the 3x3 convs in the first two ResNet-34 stages for PDC variants, or add a full-resolution PDC side branch fused into the U-Net++ decoder. Crack and gridline contrast are local intensity differences, and 7% of cracks are under 2% darker than their surroundings. Also a lightweight member of the benchmark suite.
min_experiment: Arm: house + PDC side branch, 5 seeds. Baseline: house at 100% labels. Metrics: crack recall at fixed relP@2, gridline IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if all are n.d.
evidence: R: BSDS500 ODS 0.807 at 100 FPS with under 1M params; a variant under 0.1M params runs at 200 FPS.
prior_overlap: Only the ResNet-34/50 U-Net++ backbones were tested. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: PDC side branch on the raw 1-channel EL image fused into the U-Net++ decoder at full resolution, or PDC stem convs, to boost low-contrast cracks (7% under 2% darker) and gridlines. Also the light benchmark member.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + PDC full-res branch, 5 seeds; baseline house. Metrics crack IoU, gridline IoU, relF1@2. Kill if all n.d. About 8 GPU-h.

title: Wavelet and Prototype Augmented Query-based Transformer for Pixel-level Surface Defect Detection
mechanism: Query-based mask transformer whose queries are refined by wavelet-domain cross-attention (high and low frequency) and prototype cross-attention for cluttered backgrounds.
adaptation: Benchmark arm: recent pixel-level defect method validated on cracks (CrackSeg9k) and patterned fabric (ZJU-Leaper); 1-channel stem, 24-way queries or per-class binary.
min_experiment: Benchmark run under the fixed protocol vs house; no kill line (reference row).
evidence: R: SOTA on ESDIs-SOD, CrackSeg9k, ZJU-Leaper. Code listed as github.com/yfhdm/WPFormer by a WebSearch summary, not opened.
prior_overlap: none; no mask-classification decoder was ever tried (section 5)

title: Boundary-Local Soft Supervision for Reliable Calibration in Defect Segmentation
mechanism: Boundary-gated label smoothing: local-mean soft targets only inside a morphological boundary band, hard BCE + Dice elsewhere.
adaptation: 2 px band around crack and inactive labels gets local-mean soft targets; main use is calibrated crack probabilities for decoding, ensembling and severity, not raw IoU.
min_experiment: Arm: house loss + BLSS band term, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Kill: 2 px band crack ECE on val not down 20%, or crack IoU drop > 0.012.
evidence: R: 4 defect datasets incl. DeepCrack, 20 seeds: boundary-band ECE down 28-49%, no Dice or Boundary-Dice degradation; weaker on Magnetic Tile.
prior_overlap: none

title: CrossEarth: Geospatial Vision Foundation Model for Domain Generalizable Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: VFM adapted for remote-sensing domain generalisation across location, wavelength and sensor gaps (details beyond the abstract fragment unverified).
adaptation: The sensor gap is our 5-source and E1 gap. Take its style-side data handling as EL gain, gamma, blur and vignetting jitter on VFM-H, keeping house label-safe geometry.
min_experiment: Arm: VFM-H + Rein + CrossEarth-style source jitter. Baseline: VFM-H + Rein. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, leave-one-source-out CV. Kill: not +0.02 E1 relF1@2.
evidence: R: 47 citations; abstract fragment only.
prior_overlap: partial: intensity normalisation at inference failed; training-time style jitter with a VFM untested.

title: Free Lunch of Image-mask Alignment for Anomaly Image Generation and Segmentation
mechanism: Dual-branch generator produces image and mask together with an alignment regularizer; the trained generator then supplies a generative feedback loss to the segmenter.
adaptation: Generator for inactive and material on 478 cells; its own mask branch replaces the conditioning mask as label, which can absorb label jitter; feedback loss added to PF training.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + Free Lunch samples for inactive. Baseline: row-2 PV-DDPM arm at matched sample count. Metric: CV inactive IoU. Kill: not better than row 2.
evidence: R: IoU above previous methods by 5.03 (Real-IAD), 5.68 (polyp), 16.63 (Floor Dirty). Code github.com/huan-yin/anomaly-alignment stated in abstract, not opened.
prior_overlap: None.

title: Synthetic Optical Coherence Tomography Angiographs for Detailed Retinal Vessel Segmentation Without Human Annotations
mechanism: Lightweight space-colonization simulation of thin vessel networks plus three contrast-adaptation pipelines; a model trained only on simulation segments the finest capillaries better than models trained on human annotations.
adaptation: Moonshot for crack label noise: train the crack class only on procedural/rendered cracks with exact centrelines and per-source widths, keep real labels for other classes, apply contrast adaptation (random gamma, noise, blur matched to the 5 sources); judge on detection within 2 px, not strict IoU.
min_experiment: Arm: PF with crack supervision from synthetic only. Baseline: PF with real crack labels, 5 seeds. Metric: test relF1@2 and recall@2 of low-contrast (< 2%) crack components. Kill: relF1@2 < 0.80.
evidence: R: superior segmentation on three public OCTA sets vs classical methods and human-annotation supervision (abstract; numbers not read); code, models, synthetic set public per abstract.
prior_overlap: None.

title: AIO2: Online Correction of Object Labels for Deep Learning With Incomplete Annotation in Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
mechanism: Adaptive correction trigger from the mean-teacher accuracy curve plus online object-wise label correction for missing objects.
adaptation: Add teacher-predicted crack components to labels only if p > 0.9, length >= 20 px and not inside scuff / edge_dark; targets missed cracks flagged by the audit and speck-level H36 labels.
min_experiment: Arm: house + AIO2 correction. Baseline: house. Metric: crack component recall >= 20 px and relP@2. Kill if relP@2 drops > 0.02 or recall gain < +0.02. About 8 GPU-h.
evidence: R: robust under varying building label omission on two footprint datasets; in NSegment+ comparison AIO2 gave +0.20 Vaihingen, +0.54 Cityscapes mIoU at 2x FLOPs.
prior_overlap: partial: MT pseudo-labelling was run as SSL; online object-wise completion of labelled cells was not.

title: CurvSegFlow: Time-Conditioned Flow Matching for Robust Segmentation of Curvilinear Structures in Noisy Biomedical Images
mechanism: Segmentation as time-conditioned flow matching: a U-Net with temporal embeddings integrates a learned velocity field from a noisy start to the mask, giving gradual error correction and better continuity at low SNR.
adaptation: Use as a refinement head: start the flow from house-model crack probabilities instead of noise, condition on 1-channel EL, few Euler steps; target the 7% of crack components that are < 2% darker than surroundings.
min_experiment: Arm: flow-matching refiner from house probabilities, 5 seeds. Baseline: house ensemble. Metrics: relF1@2, components found, crack IoU on 5-fold CV. Kill: relF1@2 < +0.005 after 2 days of tuning.
evidence: R: competitive or better than standard segmenters on synthetic and real microtubules, retinal vessels, corneal nerves, coronary arteries; largest gains in precision and continuity at low SNR (numbers not read).
prior_overlap: none; diffusion / flow segmenters never tried.

title: Training Beyond Convergence: Grokking nnU-Net for Glioma Segmentation in Sub-Saharan MRI
mechanism: Train far past apparent convergence (3,500 vs 200 epochs); small sub-regions improved.
adaptation: PF at 20k, 80k, 160k steps with EMA, 5 seeds; crack and inactive play the role of small sub-regions.
min_experiment: Arm: PF 80k and 160k + EMA. Baseline: SUP100-PF 20k + EMA. Metric: crack relF1@2, crack IoU, inactive IoU (test, E1). Kill: 80k not better than 20k by 0.012 relF1@2 or 0.02 inactive IoU.
evidence: R (secondary summaries, not checked in full text): tumor core / enhancing tumor Dice 86.6/86.3 to 90.1/90.2, whole tumor flat.
prior_overlap: BRIEF section 5: longer schedules never varied. Open.

title: DGSSA: Domain generalization with structural and stylistic augmentation for retinal vessel segmentation
mechanism: Structural augmentation (space-colonisation vessel trees rendered by Pix2Pix) plus stylistic augmentation (PixMix, uncertainty perturbations) for thin-vessel DG.
evidence: DeepLabv3+ MobileNetV2; DSC 78.45 DRIVE, 78.62 CHASEDB1, 72.66 HRF, 82.17 STARE (avg 77.98), better than prior DG methods.
adaptation: Use the style half: PixMix with EL-like mixing images (fractals, finger patterns, pool cells). The structure half (synthetic crack trees rendered into cells) belongs to D06.
min_experiment: PF+PixMix-EL vs PF, 5 seeds; metric E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: < +0.02.
prior_overlap: None for style mixing; crack copy-paste (n.d.) differs from rendered structures.

alt_notes.adaptation: PixMix half is cheap: mix EL cells with fractal or pool images at low weight. Structural half = synthetic branching crack masks rendered into cells (overlaps CrackSegFlow row).
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + PixMix vs PF, 3 seeds; kill at < +0.02 E1 crack relF1@2.

title: Dilated Balanced cross entropy loss for medical image segmentation
mechanism: Class-balancing CE weights computed on dilated class masks, so each class and its surrounding band share the balancing weight.
adaptation: Dilate crack by 2 px (and inactive by 2 px) for the weight computation so the jitter band is not punished as hard background; replace CE in the house loss.
min_experiment: Arm: DBCE + house Dice, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, pixel P/R. Kill: crack IoU and relF1@2 both within noise (< 0.012 / < 0.005).
evidence: Several medical datasets: beats balanced CE by a large margin; similar or better than Dice + CE.
prior_overlap: Offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) is related but changes target placement, not class balance; not the same mechanism.

title: Lesion-Aware Attention for Mammography Segmentation with Heterogeneous Supervision
mechanism: Two-branch mixed supervision: masks for base classes, image labels for more classes; a lesion-wise attentive classifier with per-class prototypes pools features only over lesion-like regions.
evidence: Consistent gains over open-vocabulary baselines on several mammography datasets; better localisation of small, low-contrast findings (qualitative).
adaptation: Prototype-attention pooling for the ELPV cell-level head so the cell label is not explained by gridlines or borders; aimed at BMRK inactive and false alarms.
min_experiment: Variant of ELPV arm: prototype-attention pooling vs plain MIL head, 5 seeds each. Metric: BMRK inactive IoU (5-fold CV), crack precision. Kill if no gain over plain MIL head by 0.03 inactive IoU. ~8 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: none

title: LogicSeg: Parsing Visual Semantics with Neural Logic Learning and Reasoning
mechanism: Class hierarchy and relations written as first-order logic rules, relaxed with fuzzy logic for training and applied at inference as matrix multiplications.
adaptation: Use the same tree as HSSN, plus the rules inactive -> defect, inactive region -> crack nearby, and padding excludes all others. This is a module on the existing U-Net++ logits.
min_experiment: Arm: house + LogicSeg rules. Baseline: house. Metrics: mIoU_rob, inactive precision. Kill if the mIoU_rob gain is < 0.01 and the inactive precision gain is < 0.03.
evidence: R: gains on four datasets with various models and backbones. The abstract page gives no numbers.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Rules: inactive -> defect; inactive region -> crack nearby; padding excludes others. Only after the tree-loss or HSSN arm shows a gain.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house + LogicSeg rule losses; baseline best tree arm; metric mIoU_rob and inactive precision; kill if gain < 0.01 over the tree arm.

title: Robust feature knowledge distillation for enhanced performance of lightweight crack segmentation models
mechanism: Logit + intermediate feature KD with mixed clean and noisy images into a 0.5 M crack segmentation student.
adaptation: 2-5 M deployment student (U-Net with MobileNetV3 or EfficientNet-B0 encoder) distilled from the 5-seed ensemble on labelled + pool cells, with EL-like noise / blur / contrast views.
min_experiment: Arm: 3 M student with ensemble KD on labelled + pool. Baseline: same 3 M student on GT only. Metric: crack relF1@2, inactive IoU on clean 49 / CV, latency. Kill: < +0.02 relF1@2 over GT-only student.
evidence: R: 62% higher mean Dice on noisy images than SOTA KD methods with a 0.5 M PoolingCrack Tiny student.
prior_overlap: none

title: SemiSAM+: Rethinking Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation in the Era of Foundation Models
mechanism: A trainable specialist generates prompts for frozen SAM-type generalists, and their masks supervise the specialist on unlabelled images.
adaptation: Inactive only (blobby, well labelled, 42 train cells). The house model proposes inactive boxes on pool cells; SAM2/SAM3 refines them; keep masks that agree with the house mask at IoU > 0.7 as extra inactive training cells. Not for thin cracks.
min_experiment: Arm house PF + SAM-refined inactive pool cells vs house PF, 5 seeds. Metric: inactive IoU on clean-49, module-grouped 5-fold CV, and E1. Kill if inactive IoU gains less than 0.03 in CV.
evidence: R: two public sets plus one in-house set; gains reported mainly with extremely scarce labels. Numbers not on the abstract page.
prior_overlap: SAM as a pseudo-label refiner was never run. Our Mean Teacher at 5% labels helped inactive (+0.11). Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: House PF predictions on pool half-cells prompt SAM2/SAM3; keep FM masks where location agrees but FM gives region extent (inactive); expected low value at 478 labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + SemiSAM+-style FM-refined pseudo-labels on pool half-cells vs PF + raw house pseudo-labels; H36 inactive IoU; kill under margin M.

title: Shape-intensity knowledge distillation for robust medical image segmentation (SIKD)
mechanism: A teacher trained on class-wise averaged training images (each labelled region set to its mean intensity) learns texture-free shape-intensity cues and distils them into a same-size student.
adaptation: Class-average EL cells over all 24 classes (removes grain, finger texture and source gain); distil into the house student; effect expected on structural classes, inactive and E1 texture shift rather than 1-2 px cracks.
min_experiment: Arm: house student + SIKD teacher distillation, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: mIoU_rob, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: mIoU_rob < +0.01 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.02.
evidence: R (web summary): improves baselines on five medical segmentation tasks and generalises better to unseen datasets.
prior_overlap: none. Distillation listed as never tried.

title: SSN: Shift Suppression Network for Endogenous Shift of Photovoltaic Defect Detection
mechanism: Background style suppression module aligns channel statistics during training to remove background style shift without target-domain data.
adaptation: Insert a BSS-style instance-statistics alignment (with style mixing across our 5 sources) into ResNet layer1-2 of the PF model, aiming at E1 contrast and scuff-streak shift.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + BSS in layer1-2. Baseline: PF, 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2; leave-one-source-out crack IoU on val folds. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03.
evidence: R: 16,323 EL images collected at three different times; SSN beats SOTA detectors under endogenous shift (detection, numbers not retrieved).
prior_overlap: Test-time per-panel BN adaptation and intensity normalisation failed; train-time style statistics suppression not tested. Open.

title: Towards Unsupervised Domain Bridging via Image Degradation in Semantic Segmentation (DiDA)
mechanism: Build continuous intermediate domains by degrading images to graded strengths, so the network learns domain-shared features, with a diffusion-encoder term that compensates semantic shift; plugs into self-training UDA.
adaptation: Source = 478 labelled cells; target = 1,152 unlabelled multi half-cut pool cells (E1-like, not E1). Degradations chosen for EL: blur, gain, noise, vignetting. Put on top of the existing Mean Teacher code.
min_experiment: Arm: MT + DiDA on the half-cut pool, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF and the existing MT-with-pool run. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU; test crack IoU must not drop more than 0.012. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain under 0.02 over PF.
evidence: R: consistent gains when added to several UDA methods on standard synthetic-to-real benchmarks (GTA/SYNTHIA to Cityscapes); exact numbers not read.
prior_overlap: Partial. Mean Teacher with the external pool was n.d. at 100% labels, but it was not aimed at E1 with target-like half-cut cells. BRIEF lists UDA aimed at E1 as open; per-panel BN adaptation (failed) is a different mechanism.

title: Data-Centric Diet: Effective Multi-center Dataset Pruning for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Per-sample importance from training dynamics on target regions (Dynamic Average Dice) for multi-centre data; gradient-norm scores fail on segmentation.
adaptation: Compute per-cell crack/inactive Dice across saved checkpoints of existing house runs, per source; low-and-flat cells are noise candidates to cross-check with ensemble ranking.
min_experiment: No training: correlate dynamics score with ensemble ranking and 24 audit cells. Kill: weaker audit agreement than ensemble ranking.
evidence: R: DAD-based pruning beats gradient-norm metrics on combined-source medical segmentation benchmarks (abstract-level evidence).
prior_overlap: none.

title: Deep Frequency Filtering for Domain Generalization
mechanism: FFT of intermediate feature maps with a learned spatial attention mask over frequencies that keeps transferable components and damps the rest.
adaptation: Insert DFF at layer2 and layer3 of ResNet-34, train with source-balanced batches over the 5 sources, and score on E1.
min_experiment: Arm: house + DFF, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: < +0.02.
evidence: R: beats prior SOTA on closed-set classification and open-set retrieval domain generalisation (abstract).
prior_overlap: none

title: Dynamic Snake Upsampling Operater and Boundary-Skeleton Weighted Loss for Tubular Structure Segmentation
mechanism: Upsampling operator that adapts its stride and picks sub-pixel samples along a serpentine path; distance-field loss weighting skeleton to boundary.
adaptation: Replace bilinear upsampling in the last two U-Net++ decoder stages; skip the boundary weighting (a 1.75 px label is all boundary).
min_experiment: Arm: snake upsampling, 5 seeds; baseline house. Metrics crack relF1@2, components found. Kill: gains < 0.01.
evidence: Plug-in gains in pixel accuracy and topology across datasets and backbones (abstract; numbers not read).
prior_overlap: none

title: Label tree semantic losses for rich multi-class medical image segmentation
mechanism: Tree-based losses (Wasserstein over a label tree, hierarchy-weighted top-level supervision) penalise confusions by tree distance.
evidence: R: consistent improvements over task baselines on whole-brain parcellation (full labels) and neurosurgical hyperspectral imaging (sparse labels).
adaptation: Same 2-level EL tree as HSSN; loss-only change so confusing gridline with busbar costs less than with background; cheaper than HSSN, run first.
min_experiment: Arm house + Wasserstein tree loss; baseline house; metrics gridline/splice/edge_dark IoU and mIoU_rob; kill if mIoU_rob gain < 0.01 and splice still 0.
prior_overlap: none; Dice-on-12-classes in section 5 is a different loss

title: Object Detection as a Positive-Unlabeled Problem
mechanism: Treats unlabelled regions as unlabelled rather than negative, using a non-negative PU risk with a class prior, so missing annotations stop teaching false negatives.
adaptation: nnPU risk on crack vs background pixels only inside the dark-ridge mask, where missing cracks can hide; standard CE elsewhere. The class prior is set per source from labelled crack density.
min_experiment: Arm: nnPU crack loss, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: relR@2, relP@2, components found. Kill if relR@2 shows no detectable difference or relP@2 drops by more than 0.02.
evidence: R (abstract): a PU loss beats the standard PN loss on PASCAL VOC and COCO across levels of missing labels. Detection, not segmentation.
prior_overlap: none

title: Revisiting Fine-Tuning Strategies for Self-supervised Medical Imaging Analysis
mechanism: Fine-tuning intermediate layers is better than end-to-end; fine-tuning the first 75% of a network beats end-to-end by up to 5.48%.
adaptation: Freeze layer4 at its pretrained weights and train the rest; reuse when MIM / DDeP or domain SSL encoders are re-tried.
evidence: Four medical downstream tasks, several fine-tuning set sizes; up to +5.48% over end-to-end.
min_experiment: Arm layer4-frozen vs PF on 5-fold CV, 2 seeds. Kill if CV inactive IoU and relF1@2 not above PF.
prior_overlap: none for permanent block freezing; MIM / DDeP + PF n.d. used full-encoder tuning.

title: SCSegamba: Lightweight Structure-Aware Vision Mamba for Crack Segmentation in Structures
mechanism: Lightweight vision Mamba (2.8M params) with gated bottleneck convolution for crack morphology and a structure-aware scanning strategy for continuity between crack pixels.
adaptation: Must-have benchmark row. Train with official code on 512 px EL, 3-class (bg, crack, inactive) and 24-class versions; gray to 3 channels; needs mamba-ssm CUDA kernels (install needs the user's OK).
min_experiment: Arm: SCSegamba 3-class and 24-class; baseline: PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU. Kill as a model if CV crack IoU < PF minus 0.02; keep as benchmark row.
evidence: R: F1 0.8390, mIoU 0.8479 on a multi-scenario dataset with 2.8M params; 104 citations. Tolerance in metrics unverified.
prior_overlap: none (no Mamba segmenter tried). Also listed in D12.

alt_notes.adaptation: Must-have benchmark entry. Official code, 1-channel stem, 512 px, crack + inactive + background and 24-class variants, house loss. Needs mamba-ssm CUDA kernels (install needs the user's OK).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: SCSegamba official recipe on our folds; baseline PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU, relF1@2, E1 relF1@2. Kill as a model if CV crack IoU < PF minus 0.02; keep as benchmark row.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use a 24-class head, 1-channel input and 512 px, under the same 20k-step protocol and metrics as house. It needs a mamba-ssm CUDA build on cv02, which needs the user's OK.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark row: SCSegamba vs house, 3 seeds, full protocol (crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive, mIoU_rob, E1). As a score arm, kill if crack relF1@2 is below house.

title: Performance uncertainty in medical image analysis: A large-scale investigation of confidence intervals
mechanism: Large-scale CI coverage study: required sample size, metric, macro vs micro aggregation and CI method all change coverage; decision tree for CI choice.
adaptation: Pick CI method and aggregation (pooled vs per-cell) per metric with their decision tree; flag inactive on test (16 cells) as below reliable coverage.
min_experiment: Arm: pooled vs per-cell aggregation on OOF house vs PF. Metric: paired-delta t. Kill: keep the higher-t aggregation; if within 10% keep pooled.
evidence: R: 24 segmentation and classification tasks, 19 models per task group; sample size for reliable CIs ranges from dozens to thousands; macro needs more cases than micro.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack IoU here is pooled over pixels (micro), and inactive is decided by 3 cells. Report both pooled and per-cell (macro) scores with the CI method the decision tree picks, and fix the aggregation in the protocol.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Compute micro and macro crack/inactive IoU and their CIs for the house seeds. Keep the aggregation with fewer seed-to-seed rank flips between house and PF.

title: Skeleton Recall Loss for Connectivity Conserving and Resource Efficient Segmentation of Thin Tubular Structures
mechanism: Soft recall loss on a tubed label skeleton. Cheap and GPU-friendly.
adaptation: Already run here. Open item: score the trained w 0.1 fresh-seed replication and add the width diagnostic. Keep it as a benchmark baseline loss.
min_experiment: Score the existing w 0.1 replication seeds against PF (E1 relF1@2, clean-49 crack IoU, width). Kill the line if the E1 relF1@2 gain does not replicate (< 0.02).
evidence: R (TopoMortar): best topology under noisy labels, but CrackTree Dice 0.32 vs 0.78 for CEDice. E: w 1.0 widened predictions and lowered test IoU while raising E1 detection. w 0.1 narrow E1 pass.
prior_overlap: Same mechanism and conditions run (Loss row). Only the replication scoring is open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Already run. Open item: score the trained w 0.1 fresh-seed replication with the width diagnostic; optionally wrap it with SCNP (SCNP paper shows SkelRecall beta0 12.45 to 5.07 with equal Dice).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Score the existing w 0.1 replication on clean-49 and E1 (0 GPU-h). Close the line if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.02 again.

title: Confidence intervals for performance estimates in brain MRI segmentation
mechanism: Measures CI width of mean Dice vs test size and spread, parametric vs bootstrap.
adaptation: Bootstrap CIs of per-cell crack IoU on val-54 and OOF-532; show readers how wide a 49-cell CI is for EL cracks.
min_experiment: Arm: bootstrap CI on val and OOF. Metric: CI width. Kill: reporting only.
evidence: R (companion ISBI 2023 doi:10.1109/isbi53787.2023.10230401): about 8 Dice points CI width for 20 test cases at SD ~0.10.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Compute the per-cell crack IoU SD on clean-49 and E1 and the CI half-width. Derive how many sealed-test cells give +/-0.01 for crack and inactive, then size the new test and E1 sets from that.
alt_notes.min_experiment: From the existing 5 house seeds: CI half-width of crack and inactive IoU on clean-49. Decision line: if the half-width > 0.02, the headline score must be OOF CV over 532 cells plus E1, not test-49 alone.

title: Application of the Hierarchical Bootstrap to Multi-Level Data in Neuroscience
mechanism: Resample the top level (subjects) then the lower level (trials) to get correct CIs on nested data.
adaptation: Resample modules then cells for E1 (106 cells from 67 modules) and the OOF pool, where cells from one module are correlated.
min_experiment: Arm: module-then-cell bootstrap. Baseline: cell bootstrap. Metric: CI width. Kill: module CI < 10% wider.
evidence: R: simulations and neuroscience data show flat bootstrap underestimates uncertainty on multi-level data.
prior_overlap: none

title: How Do Label Errors Affect Thin Crack Detection by DNNs
mechanism: Label cracks as 1 px curves with matching training and evaluation, then synthesise annotation errors: under-annotation hurts more than over-annotation; polyline approximation has modest impact.
adaptation: Benchmark: score crack as curves (relF1 on skeletons) and add a label-error robustness column (train on CV labels with synthetic 1 px jitter and 20% dropped segments). Model side: favour recall when refining labels; polyline-simplified labels are acceptable targets.
min_experiment: For the top 5 suite methods, one extra CV training on corrupted labels; report drop in CV relF1@2; no kill line (measurement).
evidence: Synthetic error study on 1 px curve labels; qualitative findings in abstract; numbers not read.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Design rule for every refinement arm: never delete crack label pixels that cannot be placed on a ridge; benchmark should report recall-oriented tolerant metrics alongside strict IoU, and can repeat the error-synthesis study on EL labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark study: add synthetic under-annotation (drop 10% of components) and 1 px jitter to train labels, train house 3 seeds each, measure crack IoU and relF1@2 drop. Kill: not a method; stop if drops are under 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Our dotted, thin-traced crack labels behave like under-annotation; train on labels dilated by 1 px (or an asymmetric soft band) and score on the original labels with a val-chosen bias.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm 1 px-dilated crack labels vs SUP100, 5 v 5. Kill if crack IoU (original labels, val bias) < +0.012 or relP@2 drop > 0.05.

alt_notes.adaptation: Our dotted, under-traced crack labels are under-annotation; train on 1 px dilated crack labels or a soft band, score on original labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: crack labels dilated by 1 px, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Kill: crack IoU on original labels < +0.012 or relP@2 drop > 0.05.

title: TransUNet: Rethinking the U-Net architecture design for medical image segmentation through the lens of transformers
mechanism: ViT encoder on CNN features for global context, plus a transformer decoder that refines learnable queries into masks (mask-classification style).
adaptation: R50-ViT hybrid encoder at 512 px (32 x 32 tokens at stride 16), 1-channel stem, PF fine-tune so ImageNet weights survive. The query decoder is the first mask-classification decoder this project would test.
min_experiment: TransUNet encoder + query decoder, PF, 3 seeds, against house PF; metrics test-49 crack IoU, inactive IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill: no metric above the house by 1 seed SD.
evidence: R: improvements over U-Net and nnU-Net-style baselines on multi-organ and tumour segmentation (abstract level). nnU-Net Revisited found transformer U-Nets below a well-configured CNN in 3D.
prior_overlap: none (BRIEF: no transformer segmenter and no mask-classification decoder tried)

title: Deep High-Resolution Representation Learning for Visual Recognition (HRNet)
mechanism: Parallel high-to-low resolution streams with repeated multi-resolution exchange keep a 1/4 stream through the whole network.
adaptation: HRNet-W18/W32 ImageNet as encoder under PF; top stream is 1/4, so add a stride-1 stem skip; 1-ch input replicated.
min_experiment: Arm: HRNet-W32 + stem skip (PF); baseline: house PF; CV crack IoU, inactive IoU, gridline IoU. Kill if all n.d.
evidence: R: shown superior on pose, segmentation, detection (Cityscapes etc.); no thin-line data.
prior_overlap: Backbone row tested ResNet-50 only; R5 partly covers resolution. HRNet itself open.

alt_notes.adaptation: HRNet-W18/W32 (timm, ImageNet) under PF plus a stride-1 stem skip; OCR head because 99% of inactive regions touch a crack, so per-cell crack-region descriptors are useful context for inactive.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm HRNet-W32-OCR vs house PF; 5-fold CV crack IoU, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob; kill: no metric above detection floor (crack 0.012) and inactive n.d. About 15 GPU-h.

title: No label left behind: a unified surface defect detection model for all supervision regimes (SuperSimpleNet)
mechanism: One discriminative model trainable in unsupervised, weak, mixed and full supervision, with feature-space synthetic anomalies plus segmentation and classification heads.
adaptation: Mixed supervision: 478 pixel-labelled cells + pool cells tagged image-level clean by the house ensemble; binary defect map (crack OR inactive OR material) used as an extra ensemble member for recall.
min_experiment: Arm PF ensemble + SuperSimpleNet member vs baseline PF ensemble; metric CV relR@2 at relP@2 >= 0.90; kill if relR@2 gain < +0.02. About 10 GPU-h.
evidence: R: SOTA across four supervision regimes on four industrial benchmarks; < 10 ms inference.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Mixed supervision: 478 pixel-labelled cells + pool cells tagged clean by the house ensemble; binary defect map (crack OR inactive OR material) as an ensemble member and as the AD-family baseline in the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Train once per supervision regime; report pixel AUROC, AU-PRO, SegF1 for crack (2 px tolerance) and inactive on test and E1; as fusion arm with PF ensemble kill if inactive IoU gain < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark baseline across supervision levels (full masks, ELPV-style image labels, mixed); for scores only its synthetic-anomaly stage as a regulariser on pool cells.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark run: train on our splits at each supervision level, report crack / inactive AP and relF1@2 on test and E1; no kill.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark baseline that can consume ELPV image labels and the unlabelled pool under the same protocol; run on 1-channel 512 px cells with crack/inactive as anomaly maps.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Run as a benchmark entry on clean-49 and E1 with mixed supervision (BenchmarkEL masks + ELPV labels). Compare to house 5-seed on crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU. No kill line; reported as a baseline. ~6 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark: binary crack and binary inactive models in all four regimes at 512 px, ELPV image labels for the weak regime. Score: borrow latent Perlin noise on labelled background as a regulariser on the U-Net++ encoder to suppress decoys (scuffs, grain boundaries).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: official code, binary crack/inactive, full and weak regimes; baseline: house; metric: crack AP, relF1@2, E1 relF1@2; benchmark row regardless; score kill if adding it as 6th ensemble member gives < +0.01 relF1@2.

title: PVEL-AD: A Large-Scale Open-World Dataset for Photovoltaic Cell Anomaly Detection
mechanism: 36,543 NIR cells, 21,044 boxes over 8 defect classes (line crack, star crack, finger interruption, black core ...), 4,148 image-level labels.
adaptation: Box-supervised auxiliary pretraining of encoder + decoder (mask projection must fill each crack box, background outside all boxes) on 1-ch images resized to 512, then PF fine-tune on our 478 so the pretraining survives.
min_experiment: Arm: 20k-step box-projection pretrain then PF. Baseline: PF, 5 v 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, test crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03 and test crack IoU flat.
evidence: R: dataset stats from Chen 2025 review; GitHub reportedly released test labels and a new download in Jan 2026 (search summary, unverified).
prior_overlap: none: PVEL-AD boxes listed as untried; UCF-EL pretraining null concerned a fine-tune that erased the encoder, PF fixes that.

title: LeJEPA: Provable and Scalable Self-Supervised Learning Without the Heuristics
mechanism: JEPA prediction loss plus SIGReg, which pushes embeddings to an isotropic Gaussian; one hyperparameter, no teacher or stop-grad, stable on ResNets and ConvNeXts, enabling in-domain pretraining on ~10k images.
adaptation: Train R34 and ConvNeXt V2-Nano from scratch on the 11.9k pool, 1-ch, 256 to 512 px with small crop scales so 1 to 2 px cracks survive; second arm adds SIGReg on per-patch features (dense variant, untested). Then U-Net++ PF fine-tune.
min_experiment: LeJEPA 400 epochs on 11.9k (~40 GPU-h per backbone) then PF vs ImageNet init of the same backbone; out-of-fold relF1@2, E1 recall, 2 seeds; kill as a model arm if below ImageNet on relF1@2 and E1 recall.
evidence: R (full text 6.3): on Galaxy10 (11k images, 400 epochs) in-domain LeJEPA on ResNet-18/34, ConvNeXt V2-Nano, LeViT beat DINOv2 ViT-S and DINOv3 ViT-S transfer, frozen and full fine-tune, 3 seeds; classification only.
prior_overlap: none: no joint-embedding or from-scratch in-domain SSL was run.

title: Lightweight transformer driven segmentation of defects in solar PV thermal imagery
mechanism: Customised SegFormer (hierarchical transformer encoder, light MLP decoder) for thermal defect segmentation on small data.
evidence: R (full text read): 277 drone IR images, 221/28/28 random split, all from 7 flights over the same 4 panels; SegFormer-B2 mIoU 0.86, custom 0.83, U-Net 0.76, DeepLabv3 0.80, Mask2Former 0.62. S: within-panel leakage, so the ranking is weak evidence.
adaptation: SegFormer-B2 encoder, 1-ch EL copied to 3 channels, 512 px, house augmentation; its 1/4-resolution output will blur 1 to 2 px cracks, so add a full-resolution refinement head (or U-Net-style skip from a stem conv) and judge on relF1@2 as well as strict IoU.
min_experiment: Arm SegFormer-B2 + full-res refinement head, AdamW 6e-5, 20k steps, 3 seeds; baseline house U-Net++ and PF; metrics test clean-49 relF1@2, crack IoU, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob; kill if relF1@2 < house minus 0.01 and mIoU_rob not above house. Keep as a benchmark row regardless.
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF 5: no transformer segmenter has been run; foundation-encoder tests were frozen probes and one ConvNeXt-T PF screen.

title: Object-Contextual Representations for Semantic Segmentation (OCR)
mechanism: Soft class-region representations are aggregated and returned to each pixel weighted by pixel-region relation.
adaptation: Inactive almost always touches a crack: an OCR head on the stride-4 decoder gives each pixel the cell's crack-region and inactive-region descriptors before the final upsample.
min_experiment: Arm: house PF + OCR head; baseline: house PF; CV inactive IoU (primary), BMRK inactive IoU. Kill if CV inactive IoU < +0.02.
evidence: R: HRNet + OCR + SegFix was 1st on Cityscapes at ECCV 2020 deadline.
prior_overlap: none.

title: Rethinking Semantic Segmentation: A Prototype View (ProtoSeg)
mechanism: Non-learnable multi-prototype classifier: several class centers per class from online clustering; pixels labelled by nearest prototype.
adaptation: Bold bet: 3-5 prototypes for crack, inactive, gridline to hold the five sources' labelling conventions and half-cut vs full-cell appearance as separate modes; 1 prototype for other classes.
min_experiment: Arm: ProtoSeg head on U-Net++ full-res features, 3 seeds; baseline SUP100; metric per-source crack IoU, E1 crack recall, mIoU_rob; kill if no gain >= 0.01 on any primary.
evidence: R: competitive or better mIoU than parametric heads on ADE20K, Cityscapes, COCO-Stuff (abstract level).
prior_overlap: none

title: Topology-aware mamba for crack segmentation in structures (CrackMamba)
mechanism: ImageNet-pretrained VMambaV2 encoder, snake-scan module that reorders crack feature sequences, and three-branch snake-conv VSS blocks in a new decoder.
adaptation: Pretrained encoder makes it the Mamba model most likely to compete at 478 images. Gray to 3 channels, 24-class decoder, house loss, PF-style reduced encoder lr.
min_experiment: Arm: CrackMamba 24-class with PF-style encoder lr; baseline: PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU, relF1@2, mIoU_rob. Kill if CV crack IoU < PF minus 0.01.
evidence: R: SOTA on CrackSeg9k and SewerCrack, competitive on CHASE_DB1 vessels (numbers not in abstract).
prior_overlap: none. Also in D12.

alt_notes.adaptation: Pretrained encoder helps at 478 cells; gray to 3 channels, 24-class decoder, house loss, PF-style encoder lr to keep pretraining.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: CrackMamba with PF-style schedule; baseline PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill as a model if CV crack IoU < PF minus 0.02; keep as benchmark row.

title: Progressive Random Convolutions for Single Domain Generalization (with RandConv, arXiv 2007.13003)
mechanism: Stacked small random convolutions (with deformable offsets and affine) as augmentation: texture and contrast diversity while keeping shape.
evidence: Outperforms SDG baselines (abstract). From GIN-IPA Table II: plain RandConv lost to GIN-IPA on all three medical tasks (e.g. prostate 57.74 vs 70.37).
adaptation: Kernel 3, at most 3 stacked layers, mixed 50/50 with the original, so cracks survive.
min_experiment: PF+RandConv vs PF+GIN-IPA, 5 seeds; E1 relF1@2. Mainly a benchmark baseline; kill if below GIN-IPA.
prior_overlap: None.

title: ResAD: A Simple Framework for Class Generalizable Anomaly Detection (and ResAD++, doi:10.1007/s11263-026-02885-1)
mechanism: Learn on residual features (feature minus few-shot normal reference features) with a hypersphere constraint, so one model detects anomalies in classes never seen in training without retraining.
adaptation: Train on train-source full cells with 4 to 8 clean same-source references; at E1, references are clean half-cut pool cells of the same module family. Map used as an E1-only prior channel; compare against the bank-based residual of WeakREST.
evidence: R: class-generalizable AD across domains; MVTec AD pixel AUROC 96.9 per leaderboard summary (WebSearch, not verified in paper).
min_experiment: Offline only: residual map on H36 and val half-cut pool cells; metric half-cut crack component recall at 1% area. Kill if below the WeakREST bank map. About 5 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: none

title: Resolving Inconsistent Semantics in Multi-Dataset Image Segmentation
mechanism: Trains one segmentation model on several datasets whose class definitions conflict, by reconciling label semantics instead of forcing one label space.
adaptation: Map UCF-EL, MultiSolSegment and PVEL-S classes onto our 24 classes with per-dataset label spaces, for joint training and for the benchmark's cross-dataset track.
min_experiment: Arm = joint training with per-dataset label spaces versus house PF. Metrics: mIoU_rob and E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01 and E1 is n.d.
evidence: R: natural-image multi-dataset segmentation (abstract level).
prior_overlap: joint multi-dataset training is open in BRIEF section 5

alt_notes.adaptation: Map UCF-EL, MultiSolSegment and PVEL-S label spaces onto our 24 classes with label-space-specific queries; use for joint training and for a cross-dataset benchmark track.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: joint training with label-space queries (needs a mask-classification decoder) vs house PF; metric E1 relF1@2 and clean-49 mIoU_rob; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03.

title: SAUGE: Taming SAM for Uncertainty-Aligned Multi-Granularity Edge Detection
mechanism: Frozen SAM with a 1.5% adapter that fuses intermediate SAM layers coarse to fine; linearly blended labels give granularity pseudo-labels.
adaptation: Frozen SAM/SAM2 encoder with multi-layer adapter fusion and crack-only head on 1-channel EL replicated to 3, aimed at E1 half-cut cells and scuff confounders.
min_experiment: Arm: SAUGE-style adapter on frozen SAM, 3 seeds; baseline PF. Metric E1 crack relF1@2 and test crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 below PF single model. About 20 GPU-h.
evidence: R: strong cross-dataset generalisation, SOTA on BSDS500, Multicue, NYUDv2 (abstract).
prior_overlap: Partial: frozen SAM2 Hiera-T linear probe showed no gain, but that was single layer, no adapter, no decoder; adapters listed as open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Frozen SAM or SAM2 encoder with a multi-layer adapter for crack, aimed at E1 (half-cut cells, scuff streaks). Granularity blending maps to label-width styles per source.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: frozen SAM + SAUGE adapter on crack, 3 seeds. Baseline: house and PF. Metric: E1 relF1@2 and crack recall. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains less than 0.03.

title: Skeleton-Guided Progressive Test-Time Adaptation for Thin Curvilinear Structures (SGP-TTA)
mechanism: Consensus Skeleton Recall builds a skeleton target from 6 aligned views and updates only the BN affine parameters (1 step per image); ProgBN moves BN statistics from source toward target by sample count.
adaptation: Drop ProgBN, because our BN-statistics TTA failed (T9, BN-HC). Keep CSR on BN affine only. Adapt continually within one E1 module and reset between modules; adapt episodically per cell on test. Skeleton dilation r=2 matches our 2 px label jitter. It extends our training-time Skeleton Recall w0.1, which was a narrow E1 pass.
min_experiment: Arm: SUP100-PF + CSR (lr chosen on F51 from 1e-4 to 1e-3, 6 views, dilation 2). Baseline: SUP100-PF without TTA. Metrics: E1 relF1@2 and component recall, with test clean-49 crack IoU as a guard. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains < +0.02, or test crack IoU or mIoU_rob drops > 0.005, or H36 crack-free false alarms rise > 2x.
evidence: R (full text): UNet at 512 px on 10 curvilinear datasets. DRIVE to STARE Dice: source 51.3, TENT 71.0, SGP 74.2. When the source model is already good (CNDS 85.56), TENT, CoTTA, SAR and EATA fall to 62 to 63 while SGP holds 85.27. Adding entropy hurt (65.22 to 62.36 retina; 59.15 to 44.98 road). Plain multi-view consistency alone was tiny (53.51 to 53.93).
prior_overlap: The ProgBN part overlaps T9 / BN-HC (per-panel and global BN statistics failed under the same conditions), so it is dropped. CSR on BN affine at test time was never run, so it is open.

title: UNet 3+: A Full-Scale Connected UNet for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Full-scale skip connections, full-scale deep supervision, and a classification-guided module that suppresses predictions in images without the target.
adaptation: Full-scale skips including a stride-1 stem; CGM as a cell-level inactive-present gate (42 train cells with inactive) to cut BMRK inactive false positives.
min_experiment: Arm: UNet 3+ decoder with stem + CGM (PF encoder); baseline: house PF; CV inactive IoU and precision, gridline IoU. Kill if inactive IoU < +0.02 and gridline n.d.
evidence: R: gains on two medical datasets (liver, spleen), fewer parameters than UNet++.
prior_overlap: none; decoder never varied.

alt_notes.adaptation: Full-scale skips including a stride-1 stem on ResNet-34; classification-guided module as an image-level inactive-present gate (42 train cells have inactive), aimed at BMRK inactive false positives.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm UNet 3+ (ResNet-34, PF) vs house PF; 5-fold CV inactive IoU and precision, gridline IoU; kill: inactive IoU n.d. and gridline < +0.03. About 10 GPU-h.

title: A2LC: Active and Automated Label Correction for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Cascaded manual plus automatic label correction: few human correction queries, an automatic stage propagates each correction to similar unqueried regions, tail-class-balanced acquisition.
adaptation: Only with user consent: 100 yes/no 'is this a crack' clicks on top flagged components from ranking arms, propagate answers by component feature similarity across all cells. Without clicks reduces to ensemble ranking.
min_experiment: Arm: 100 clicks + propagation, retrain. Baseline: ensemble-ranking arm without clicks. Metric: clean-49 crack relF1@2 and IoU. Kill: < +0.01 relF1@2 over no-click arm.
evidence: R: +27.23% over prior ALC at equal budget on Cityscapes; matches prior methods with 20% of budget; PASCAL VOC also.
prior_overlap: none; conflicts with no-manual-labelling rule unless a minimal case is accepted.

title: Localizing Data Annotation Faults in Semantic Segmentation Systems (SegFaultLoc)
mechanism: Training-free fault localisation: split masks into connected components, extract features from frozen pretrained encoders, build a semantic spectrum (class / missing faults) and a geometric spectrum (localisation / fragmentation faults), and rank components by learned suspiciousness.
adaptation: Rank train crack and inactive components across the 5 sources with DINOv2/DINOv3 features; check precision against the 24 cells the audit already flagged; set the top-ranked components to ignore or down-weight them (no hand labelling).
min_experiment: Arm: drop the top 5% of suspicious crack components (ignore index), retrain house, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: precision at 24 vs the audit list; test crack IoU and relF1@2. Kill: precision at 24 below 0.3, or crack IoU change under 0.012.
evidence: R: up to +9.2% APFD, +21.9% Precision@10%, +22.4% nDCG@10% over 7 data-quality baselines on 3 benchmarks; fixing faults it found in COCO-Stuff improved segmentation.
prior_overlap: none. The audit flagged 24 of 239 cells but nothing was fixed; automatic label refinement is listed as open.

title: Near, far: Patch-ordering enhances vision foundation models' scene understanding (NeCo)
mechanism: Dense post-pretraining that enforces consistent nearest-neighbour rankings of patch features between student and teacher via differentiable sorting; 19 GPU-h.
adaptation: Run on DINOv2-reg or DINOv3 ViT-B/L with pool cells at 448-518 px (1-ch repeated to 3) before D24's VFM fine-tune.
min_experiment: Arm: D24 DINOv3 ViT-B arm after NeCo on pool. Baseline: same arm without NeCo. Kill if E1 crack recall and out-of-fold relF1@2 both < +0.01.
evidence: R: +5.5 ADE20k and +6 Pascal in-context seg; +7.2 COCO-Things, +5.7 COCO-Stuff linear seg.
prior_overlap: None; BRIEF 5 tested only frozen linear probes and one ConvNeXt-T fine-tune screen.

alt_notes.adaptation: NeCo on DINOv2-reg / DINOv3 ViT-B with pool cells at 448 to 518 px, 1-ch repeated to 3, before the D24 VFM fine-tune.
alt_notes.min_experiment: D24 DINOv3 ViT-B arm after NeCo on pool (~20 GPU-h) vs without; kill if E1 crack recall and out-of-fold relF1@2 both < +0.01.

title: PMT: Plain Mask Transformer for Image and Video Segmentation with Frozen Vision Encoders
mechanism: Lightweight Plain Mask Decoder mimicking EoMT's last blocks runs on a frozen vision foundation model.
evidence: R: matches frozen-encoder SOTA on image benchmarks, up to 3x faster; video on par with fine-tuned methods. No small-data evidence.
adaptation: Frozen DINOv3 ViT-L (or DINOv2) at 1024 px + PMD + full-res refinement head; aimed at E1: a frozen encoder cannot overfit 478 cells from 5 sources, so half-cut/scuff cells stay nearer the pretraining distribution.
min_experiment: Arm frozen ViT-L + PMD + refinement; baseline house PF; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU; kill if E1 relF1@2 < 0.45 and E1 inactive < 0.24.
prior_overlap: Partial: frozen linear probes of small DINOv3/DINOv2 encoders showed no gain. A mask decoder on frozen ViT-L at 1024 is not the same mechanism; open but scored lower for that reason.

alt_notes.adaptation: Frozen DINOv2 (DINOv3 if OK) ViT-L + PMD + full-res head at 1024; aimed at E1, since a frozen encoder cannot overfit 478 cells from 5 sources.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PMT frozen ViT-L vs house PF; metrics E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU only; kill if E1 relF1@2 < 0.45 and E1 inactive < 0.24.

title: UnfoldCRF: Structured Mask Refinement with Image-Conditioned Latent Regions
mechanism: Refinement as unrolled damped mean-field inference in a CRF with corrected unaries, learned local pairwise terms and image-conditioned latent regions; compared against capacity-matched black-box refiners.
adaptation: Multiclass CRF refiner on the 24-class output; pairwise terms for crack/inactive borders, region terms for whole-region inactive errors. Its matched-control protocol should be used for every refiner arm in our benchmark.
min_experiment: Arm: UnfoldCRF refiner. Control: recurrent black-box refiner with the same parameters and stages. Metrics: inactive IoU, crack IoU, fraction of cells made worse on 5-fold CV. Kill: arm not better than control by >= 0.01 inactive IoU.
evidence: R: COD10K +1.0 F-beta-w over strongest matched control; images made worse 11.7% -> 8.5%; train-once over five datasets +4.2 mean delta-IoU vs +2.0 for control; +2.0 vs +0.6 on unseen mask generators.
prior_overlap: none; CRF layers not tried.

title: Faithful crack image synthesis from evolutionary pixel-level annotations via latent semantic diffusion model (LSDM)
mechanism: Latent semantic diffusion renders crack images from pixel-level annotations, and a heuristic crack-evolution step grows and branches existing annotations into richer new masks.
adaptation: Evolve skeletonised crack labels; grown cracks that isolate a region from all busbars yield new inactive masks; render with a pixel renderer or on GDI canvases rather than the latent model for 1-2 px cracks. HF demo QinLei086/LSDM stated in abstract, not opened.
min_experiment: PF + evolved masks rendered vs PF + original masks rendered by the same renderer. Metric CV inactive IoU and test crack relR@2. Kill: < +0.01 on both.
