evidence: R: crack segmentation datasets; LSDM + evolution beats traditional augmentation and other generators (no numbers in abstract).
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Evolve skeletonised crack labels; grown cracks isolating regions from busbars give new inactive masks; render with a pixel-space generator, not the latent model.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Evolved vs original masks through the same renderer. Metric CV inactive, test relR@2. Kill: < +0.01 on both. About 20 GPU-h.

title: A Unified Loss for Handling Inter-Class and Intra-Class Imbalance in Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Majority-class hard mining strength set per image by the frequency of minority classes present, plus within-class hard mining.
adaptation: Per-cell control: light majority mining on crack-free cells, heavy on cracked cells. Alternative to asymmetric margin.
min_experiment: Arm: Balance loss replacing CE, 3 seeds; baseline SUP100; metric mIoU_rob and crack recall; kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01.
evidence: R: better than common losses on 5 medical segmentation tasks with varying imbalance (abstract level).
prior_overlap: none

title: Learning Spectral-Decomposited Tokens for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Rein-like learnable tokens split by frequency band so low-frequency style and high-frequency content are tuned apart.
adaptation: Cracks are high frequency; scuff streaks and source contrast are low frequency. One arm on VFM-H replacing Rein tokens.
min_experiment: Arm: VFM-H + spectral tokens. Baseline: VFM-H + Rein. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 false alarms on scuff cells. Kill: not +0.02 E1 relF1@2.
evidence: R: 36 citations; abstract fragment only.
prior_overlap: none.

title: Rapid-Deployment Crack Measurement Based on SAM3 Semantic-Edge Response Decoding (SERD)
mechanism: SAM3's internal prompt-conditioned semantic response keeps crack evidence that its final masks suppress; calibrate it with a fixed Sobel field, training-free; also measures width/length directly.
adaptation: Use as a label-free crack prior map on E1-like half-cut cells and the 159k pool: extra input channel or soft teacher for the house model; width/length outputs feed severity.
min_experiment: Run SERD on val, F51 and H36; measure crack relR@2 at the house model's relP@2; kill if relR@2 < 0.4. Then house + SERD channel vs house PF on E1 crack recall.
evidence: R: 6 crack sets; internal response 82.66% crack-pixel recall vs 74.66% for SAM3 masks; width MAE 6.07 -> 5.55 px.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Zero-shot crack-likelihood map for EL as an E1 diagnostic (house gives p < 0.001 to 70% of E1 crack pixels), as an extra input channel, and as a severity width estimator.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training: SAM3 + SERD on val and F51; relR@2 / relP@2 for crack. Go if relR@2 >= 0.5 on F51; else close the SAM3 text-prompt route.

title: S3-TTA: Scale-Style Selection for Test-Time Augmentation in Biomedical Image Segmentation
mechanism: For each test image, choose the scale and style transform whose prediction is most consistent under further transforms, instead of averaging all views.
adaptation: Per cell, choose among scales 0.75 to 1.5 and gamma 0.8/1/1.25 by flip-consistency of the crack + inactive probability maps. This targets the per-source contrast differences (5 sources) and BMRK scale. Pure inference on existing checkpoints.
min_experiment: Arm: per-cell scale+gamma selection on FINAL. Baselines: FINAL plain and with D4 TTA. Metrics: per-source crack IoU (BMRK, CFVS, CSIR), overall crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if no source gains >= +0.02 and overall crack IoU is not up >= +0.005.
evidence: R: +3.4% over prior art on cell segmentation and +1.3% on lung segmentation.
prior_overlap: None for per-image scale/style selection. Intensity normalisation failed (BRIEF s5), but that was a fixed global mapping, not per-cell selection by consistency.

title: SoftSeg: Advantages of soft versus binary training for image segmentation
mechanism: Train on non-binarised soft labels as regression (normalised ReLU output, regression loss) instead of classification.
adaptation: Crack channel regresses a blurred crack map (soft band) while other classes stay softmax; threshold chosen on val.
min_experiment: Arm SoftSeg crack head vs SUP100, 5 v 5. Kill if crack IoU < +0.012 or relP@2 drop > 0.05.
evidence: R: Dice +2.0% (gray matter), +3.3% (MS lesions), +6.5% (brain tumour) across random splits; higher sensitivity for small objects.
prior_overlap: none

title: A Bayesian Approach to Segmentation with Noisy Labels via Spatially Correlated Distributions
mechanism: Variational inference over spatially correlated label errors via a latent Gaussian field with KMS-structured covariance (ECCD).
adaptation: Model crack labels as truth with flips correlated along the crack direction (correlation length about 10 px), covering both jitter and omission.
min_experiment: Arm: house + ECCD loss on crack. Baseline: house. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if < house + 0.008. About 10 GPU-h plus a week of code.
evidence: R: spatial correlation modelling clearly helps on several tasks; lung segmentation near clean-label level at moderate noise (abstract).
prior_overlap: none

title: AdaptDiff: Cross-Modality Domain Adaptation via Weak Conditional Semantic Diffusion for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
mechanism: Pseudo-labels on unlabelled target images train a mask-conditioned diffusion model, which renders target-style images from source masks to fine-tune the segmenter.
evidence: Seven public datasets, three modalities; improved segmentation on all unseen sets (abstract, no numbers).
adaptation: Train mask-to-image diffusion on unlabelled half-cut pool cells conditioned on house pseudo-labels of structure classes (busbars, ribbons, cut edge); render train crack/inactive masks into half-cut scuffed cells.
min_experiment: PF + 1,000 rendered half-cut cells vs PF, 5 seeds; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and recall@2 on half-cut cells. Kill: < +0.03 relF1@2.
prior_overlap: Partial: synthetic half-cut views (geometric) were n.d.; generative synthesis untested (D06 overlap).

title: Automated efficiency loss analysis by luminescence image reconstruction using generative adversarial networks
mechanism: A GAN reconstructs a defect-free luminescence image of a cell; the difference to the real image isolates defects and quantifies their efficiency loss.
adaptation: Train a masked inpainting U-Net on the 11.9k unlabelled pool cells; feed abs(EL - reconstruction) as a second input channel to the house model, as an anomaly prior that does not depend on the learned full-cell layout (target: E1, where 70% of crack pixels get p(crack) < 0.001). Scuffs will also light up, so watch precision.
min_experiment: Arm: house with 2-channel input (EL, residual); baseline: house. Metrics: E1 crack recall and relF1@2, CV crack relF1@2 as guard. Kill if E1 recall < +0.03 or CV relF1@2 drops > 0.01.
evidence: R: reconstruction-based loss analysis on luminescence images of silicon cells (companion PVSC 2021 doi:10.1109/pvsc43889.2021.9518512); numbers not retrieved.
prior_overlap: none. MIM / DDeP pretraining (n.d.) used reconstruction for features only; residual-as-input and anomaly priors are on the never-tried list.

title: Defect-Aware RGB Representation and Resolution-Efficient Deep Learning for Photovoltaic Failure Detection in Electroluminescence Images
mechanism: Local contrast enhancement then physically motivated false-colour mapping of grey ranges into 3 channels (dark crack / inactive, healthy emission, conductive paths).
evidence: R: higher ELPV classification accuracy than prior CNN results, comparable accuracy at lower resolution (classification only).
adaptation: Our ResNet-34 takes 1 channel; a 3-band per-source-percentile mapping uses the full pretrained conv1. Bands must be per source, not fixed grey values.
min_experiment: Arm: house with 3-band input, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: mIoU_rob, crack IoU, inactive IoU. Kill: < +0.01 mIoU_rob and < +0.012 crack IoU.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Per-source percentile bands (not fixed grey values) into the full 3-channel ImageNet conv1 of ResNet-34.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with 3-band input, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: mIoU_rob and crack IoU. Kill: mIoU_rob < +0.01 and crack IoU < +0.012.

title: Designing a Hybrid Neural System to Learn Real-world Crack Segmentation from Fractal-based Simulation (Cracktal / CAP-Net)
mechanism: Stochastic Koch-fractal crack simulator with exact labels. CAP-Net adds AdaIN style transfer and a pointwise-mutual-information branch with a consistency loss to bridge simulation and real data.
evidence: On SegCODEBRIM, a U-Net trained on 950 real multi-source images (F1 25.6%) did worse than a U-Net trained on simulation, which the authors attribute to inconsistent annotation styles across sources. CAP-Net adds +7% F1 over the simulation-trained U-Net. All images at 256 px.
adaptation: Our 5 sources with 5 label conventions are the same failure mode. Use fractal skeletons as a second generator alongside the dynamic-programming strands, and apply per-source intensity statistics (AdaIN-like) when rendering onto EL cells.
min_experiment: Add Cracktal skeletons as a second skeleton source in the procedural arm, 5 seeds. Metric: E1 relF1@2. Kill if not above the procedural arm alone.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Second skeleton source in the procedural arm; per-source AdaIN-style intensity statistics when rendering.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Swap fractal skeletons into the procedural arm; kill if E1 relF1@2 not above DP skeletons.

title: DriftRemover: Hybrid Energy Optimizations for Anomaly Images Synthesis and Segmentation
mechanism: Generates anomaly image and mask together from a coarse mask plus category, taking the mask from synthesis attention maps, with two modules correcting drift between synthetic and real appearance.
adaptation: Treat jittered labels as coarse guides and take the output mask from what the generator drew; latent resolution limits it to inactive and blobby classes unless run at 2x.
min_experiment: PF + 500 generated inactive cells vs PF. Metric CV inactive IoU. Kill: < +0.02.
evidence: R: MVTec pixel AP +1.3, F1-max +1.8; Floor Dirt IoU +37.2%, F-measure +25.1%.
prior_overlap: none

title: Gated-SCNN: Gated Shape CNNs for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: A full-resolution shape stream, gated by the main stream and supervised with boundaries, runs in parallel with the regular segmentation stream.
adaptation: A shape stream at 512 px gated by U-Net++ encoder features, with boundary targets as in SBCB (crack band excluded). Run only if the SBCB arm helps the thin structure classes.
min_experiment: Arm: house + shape stream. Baseline: house. Metrics: gridline and edge_dark IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill if the gain is < 0.01 mIoU_rob over the SBCB arm.
evidence: R: Cityscapes mIoU +2 and boundary F +4 over strong baselines. The abstract claims larger gains on thinner, smaller objects.
prior_overlap: none

title: Generative data-engine foundation model for universal few-shot 2D vascular image segmentation (UniVG)
mechanism: Decomposes thin structures and backgrounds and recombines them with varied morphology, then adapts the generator with a few labelled images to synthesise realistic image-label pairs.
adaptation: Recombine crack skeletons from ARTS/CFVS with CSIR half-cut canvases (GDI twins or crack-free pool cells), adapt the renderer on 478 cells; reuse the recipe, not the vascular checkpoint. Repo stated as forthcoming (github.com/XinAloha/UniVG), not verified.
min_experiment: PF + recombined crack/background pairs vs PF. Metric E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: < +0.02.
evidence: R: 11 vessel tasks across 5 modalities with 5 labelled images each; comparable to fully supervised; UniVG-58K pretraining set.
prior_overlap: CP100 pasted real crack pixels (n.d.); structure/background recombination with a learned renderer is untested. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: ARTS/CFVS crack skeletons onto CSIR half-cut canvases (inpainted twins), adapt the renderer on 478 cells.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Recombined set vs PF. Metric E1 relF1@2. Kill: < +0.02. About 15 GPU-h.

title: HRDA: Context-Aware High-Resolution Domain-Adaptive Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Multi-resolution UDA: a small high-resolution detail crop and a large low-resolution context crop, fused by a learned scale attention.
adaptation: Detail branch at native 512 (or 1024 upsampled); context branch from a 2x downsampled larger view of the module where pool images allow. Only worth running if MIC shows E1 movement.
min_experiment: MIC-E1 + HRDA vs MIC-E1, 3 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if less than +0.02.
evidence: R: GTA->CS 73.8 mIoU (+5.5 over the prior SOTA), Synthia->CS 65.8 (+4.9).
prior_overlap: A 2x input test was n.d. at 4x compute. A multi-res detail/context fusion inside UDA was not tested. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Only useful with native-resolution pool sources (about 1200 px): detail crop at native res for cracks, context crop at 512 px for layout.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark entry; score run only if native-res crops are prepared by another direction: HRDA-style dual crop vs PF, kill if test crack IoU gain < +0.012.

title: RS-MTDF: Multi-Teacher Distillation and Fusion for Remote Sensing Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: During SSL, frozen VFMs (DINOv2, CLIP) act as feature teachers. Student encoder features are aligned to theirs, and the distilled features are fused into the student decoder to bridge the labelled/unlabelled distribution gap.
adaptation: Use DINOv2-L only, since CLIP has no meaning for EL. Add a feature-alignment loss on train and pool cells to the house R34 encoder, in supervised or SSL training. A cheaper, single-stage sibling of GKD.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + DINOv2-L feature alignment loss on pool cells, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, clean-49 crack IoU. Kill: no metric beyond noise.
evidence: R: SOTA or comparable on ISPRS Potsdam, LoveDA and DeepGlobe across label ratios, with the highest IoU in most LoveDA classes.
prior_overlap: Partial. Same open slot as GKD (pool objective other than MIM/DDeP).

title: Unpaired Multi-Modal Segmentation via Knowledge Distillation
mechanism: Segment two unpaired modalities with fully shared conv kernels, modality-specific normalisation layers and a KL loss aligning per-class prediction distributions across modalities.
adaptation: Joint training of our EL cells with crack-labelled UVF cells (OpenUVF, 3000 labelled cells) and optionally UCF-EL as a second EL modality; crack + background only for the extra modality; own BN per modality; keeps the extra knowledge in shared weights instead of a pretrain that the fine-tune erases.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + joint OpenUVF batches with own BN and KL prototype loss; baseline: PF. Metrics: CV crack relF1@2 and E1 crack recall. Kill if both < +0.01. Download needs user OK.
evidence: R: cardiac and abdominal CT/MRI unpaired segmentation beats single-modality and naive joint training (numbers not read).
prior_overlap: Partial: UCF-EL encoder pretraining then house fine-tune was n.d. (encoder erased). Joint multi-dataset / cross-modality training is untested.

title: Active Learning Inspired ControlNet Guidance for Augmenting Semantic Segmentation Datasets
mechanism: Training-free guidance: gradients of active-learning scores (uncertainty, query by committee, expected model change) are added to the backward diffusion of any pretrained ControlNet.
adaptation: Query by committee = disagreement among our existing 5 house seeds; plug into the UnIACorN or pavement-style ControlNet at sampling.
min_experiment: QBC-guided vs unguided sampling from the same ControlNet, matched count, on PF. Metric as the host arm (E1 relF1@2 or mIoU_rob). Kill: < +0.01.
evidence: R: segmentation models trained on guided synthetic data outperform those trained on unguided synthetic data (abstract, no numbers).
prior_overlap: none

title: Diffusion-Based Data Augmentation and Knowledge Distillation With Generated Soft Labels for Oil Spill Segmentation Learning on Satellite SAR Images (DAKTer)
mechanism: Diffusion jointly generates images and soft-label maps, with an SNR-based factor aligning noise across the two modalities; a student segmenter learns from soft labels.
adaptation: Joint pixel-space generation of (EL, p_crack band about 4 px wide, p_inactive); soft crack labels match the jittered line; student trained on real hard + generated soft labels.
min_experiment: PF student with generated soft-label pairs vs PF. Metric test crack relF1@2 and IoU at val-chosen bias. Kill: both gains < +0.005.
evidence: R: scarce SAR oil-spill data; better than other generative augmentation methods across several segmenters (abstract gives no numbers).
prior_overlap: Offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) changed the loss on real labels; generated soft-label pairs are untested. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Joint pixel-space generation of (EL, p_crack band about 4 px, p_inactive); soft labels fit jittered cracks.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Student on real + generated soft labels vs PF. Metric test crack relF1@2 and IoU at val bias. Kill: both < +0.005. About 60 GPU-h.

title: Enhanced Mask2Former With Multi-Scale and High-Resolution for Concrete Bridge Crack Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Mask2Former plus a multi-scale RepBlock fusion module and a high-resolution wavelet-conv (WTConv + DEConv) branch with channel/spatial attention to keep fine cracks.
adaptation: In our M2F arm add a stride-1/2 conv branch from the raw EL image into the pixel decoder; same idea as doi:10.3390/electronics14142834 (local perception + aux conv, +3.2 mIoU pavement).
min_experiment: Part of M2F arm B (with dense aux head) vs arm A; metric crack relF1@2 and crack IoU; kill the branch if relF1@2 gain < 0.01.
evidence: R: bridge cracks mIoU 86.33, F1 85.07; each module alone 86.22 / 85.99 mIoU over baseline (baseline number not in abstract).
prior_overlap: none

title: Prompt and Refinement: Asymmetric Mutual Learning for Infrared Small Target Detection with Noisy Labels
mechanism: Two asymmetric learners, one prompt-driven and one refinement-driven, correct each other's noisy masks for small faint targets (abstract-level reading).
adaptation: Short faint crack components (76 to 88% under 20 px) are the closest analogue; would pair a prompt-based refiner with the house model to correct crack labels mutually. Details unread (MCP down).
min_experiment: Read the method first; if feasible, arm: mutual correction on crack labels; baseline: house; metric comp>=20px recall and relF1@2; kill if both n.d.
evidence: unverified beyond abstract fragment.
prior_overlap: partial: CPS/mutual learning was run at 5% for SSL, not for correcting labelled-set labels.

title: Enhancing recall in asphalt pavement crack segmentation using a HoughNet-extended U-Net architecture with reconstruction head
mechanism: Voting-based (HoughNet) segmentation head plus a reconstruction head to raise crack recall at similar precision.
adaptation: Swap the crack logit for a log-polar voting head; aimed at relR@2 toward the 0.90 target.
min_experiment: Arm = PF + voting crack head; baseline = PF; 5 seeds; relR@2 at relP@2 >= 0.90. Kill if relR@2 gain < 0.01.
evidence: R: Crack500 higher recall at similar precision; GAPS384 thin cracks best F1.
prior_overlap: None.

title: Geometry-aligned dual-branch detection with directional crack-aware attention for EL imaging of photovoltaic cells
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
mechanism: Directional crack-aware attention: pooling along H and W with 1-D convolutions to boost anisotropic thin structures, plus DCT high-frequency cues injected into the FPN.
adaptation: Insert strip-attention blocks into the two finest U-Net++ decoder stages; add two diagonal strip directions because our cracks are often oblique while busbars and ribbons are axis aligned and would also be amplified.
min_experiment: Arm: house + directional attention. Baseline: house, 5 v 5 seeds. Metrics: test crack IoU, components >= 20 px found. Kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and components found < +0.02.
evidence: R: PVELAD EL2021, mAP50 76.3 v YOLO11 61.5 (+14.8), recall +18.0, single seed 42.
prior_overlap: none.

title: Multi-head automated segmentation by incorporating detection head into the contextual layer neural network
mechanism: A parallel detection head gives a presence probability that gates segmentation, either soft (scale probabilities) or hard (threshold mask).
adaptation: Use it only as the soft or hard setting of the UNet 3+ presence-gate arm on inactive and crack. It does not need a separate run.
min_experiment: Run as the hard-gate setting inside the presence-head arm. Baseline: PF. Metric: inactive IoU and precision. Kill if hard gate < soft gate.
evidence: R: Dice loss 0.013 +/- 0.036 gated v 0.732 +/- 0.314 non-gated on Prostate-Anatomical-Edge-Cases (TCIA).
prior_overlap: none

title: VSR-Net: Vessel-like Structure Rehabilitation Network with Graph Clustering
mechanism: Takes a coarse vessel mask, groups broken segments into rupture clusters (curvilinear clustering), then merges them across gaps (curvilinear merging) to repair connectivity, with lower calibration error.
evidence: R: five 2D/3D medical datasets; beats prior refinement methods and lowers calibration error (abstract, no numbers on page).
adaptation: Crack channel of the ensemble only: cluster fragments, learn merges across gaps up to about 10 px along local direction; aimed at missed faint segments between detected pieces, scored by relR@2 and component recall. Implementation from paper (code not found).
min_experiment: Arm: VSR-style cluster-and-merge on ensemble crack mask. Baseline: house ensemble. Metric: relR@2 at fixed relP@2, components>=20 px found. Kill: relR@2 < +0.01.
prior_overlap: none. Skeleton Recall and clDice losses were run (training losses), not a post-hoc connectivity refiner.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply to crack components: 76-88% of crack components are < 20 px, many are pieces of one crack; merge collinear fragments; train on out-of-fold maps.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house ensemble + VSR-Net. Baseline: house ensemble. Metrics: components found, relF1@2, ECE of crack probability on 5-fold CV. Kill: components found < +0.02.

title: Why is SAM Robust to Label Noise?
mechanism: SAM's label-noise robustness comes mainly from a network-Jacobian regularisation effect and peaks with early stopping; cheaper explicit regularisers recover much of it.
adaptation: Mechanism reason for the SAM arm on jittered crack labels; if SAM helps, test the cheaper explicit regulariser at 1x cost and read earlier checkpoints.
evidence: SAM gains of tens of percent under label noise; peak before convergence (abstract).
min_experiment: Conditional on SAM: explicit-regulariser arm vs PF+SAM, seeds 5-9; kill if below PF+SAM on test relF1@2.
prior_overlap: none

title: VLMine: Long-Tail Data Mining with Vision Language Models
mechanism: Mine rare examples from an unlabelled corpus by rank-combining multiple signals (VLM keyword rarity, model uncertainty).
adaptation: Replace VLM signal (no EL knowledge) with ensemble-predicted inactive fraction, ensemble disagreement and embedding novelty vs train; mine the 159k pool for inactive-rich and half-cut scuff cells, pseudo-label only those.
min_experiment: Arm: house + 500 mined inactive-rich pseudo-labelled cells. Baseline: house 5 seeds. Metric: CV and clean-49 inactive IoU, BMRK inactive, E1 inactive. Kill: < +0.02 inactive IoU on CV folds.
evidence: R: 10-50% gains over mining baselines on ImageNet-LT, Places-LT, Waymo.
prior_overlap: Pool SSL used pool without targeted mining (n.d.). Partly open.

title: U-Mamba: Enhancing Long-range Dependency for Biomedical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Hybrid conv + Mamba (SSM) blocks in the encoder (U-Mamba Enc) or only the bottleneck (U-Mamba Bot), self-configured inside nnU-Net.
adaptation: Run U-Mamba Bot only, always with its No-Mamba control (same net, Mamba layers off), at 512 px 2D; the bottleneck is 16 x 16 tokens, so global mixing is cheap. Target the E1 context gap.
min_experiment: U-Mamba Bot against No-Mamba Base on 5 module-grouped folds; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and CV crack relF1@2. Kill: difference within fold SD.
evidence: R (original): beats CNN/Transformer baselines on abdomen CT/MR, endoscopy and microscopy. R (nnU-Net Revisited): the No-Mamba control matches U-Mamba on all 6 3D datasets, so the gains came from the residual U-Net.
prior_overlap: none here. Externally weakened by the Revisited ablation, which is why the No-Mamba control is required.

alt_notes.adaptation: Suite member: U-Mamba_Bot 2D at 512 px, same folds and label-safe aug; needs mamba-ssm CUDA kernels (install requires OK). Always paired with the No-Mamba ablation, as Revisited did.
alt_notes.min_experiment: U-Mamba_Bot v No-Mamba base, 5 folds each. Kill (for score purposes) if E1 relF1@2 difference < 0.03; keep as benchmark row regardless.

title: MixerCSeg: An Efficient Mixer Architecture for Crack Segmentation via Decoupled Mamba Attention
mechanism: A mixer encoder with CNN, Transformer and Mamba-like paths, a direction-guided edge gated convolution (DEGConv) and spatial refinement multi-level fusion (2.54M params).
adaptation: Run it as a benchmark baseline with a 24-class head at 512 px. Separately, lift DEGConv into the house decoder as a crack-edge module.
min_experiment: Benchmark row vs house, 3 seeds, full protocol. DEGConv-in-house arm: kill if crack relF1@2 gains < 0.012.
evidence: R: state of the art on several crack benchmarks at 2.05 GFLOPs (abstract). WebSearch shows it on the CVPR 2026 open-access site.
prior_overlap: None.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark entry as a 2026 crack SOTA; same adaptation as SCSegamba (1-channel stem, 512 px, 3-class and 24-class variants).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: MixerCSeg official recipe; baseline PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill as a model if CV crack IoU < PF minus 0.02; keep as benchmark row.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark row as newest crack SOTA; same training adaptation as SCSegamba (512 px, 3-class and 24-class, gray to 3 channels).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: MixerCSeg official code; baseline: PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill as a model if CV crack IoU < PF minus 0.02; keep as benchmark row.

title: A Unified Anomaly Synthesis Strategy with Gradient Ascent for Industrial Anomaly Detection and Localization (GLASS)
mechanism: Global feature-level anomaly synthesis by gradient ascent with hypersphere truncation plus local image-level synthesis, covering weak near-normal defects; a discriminator outputs the map.
adaptation: (a) Benchmark AD row trained per source on clean pool cells. (b) Auxiliary binary head on the house encoder using GAS-perturbed non-crack features as hard samples, aimed at the 7% of crack components under 2% contrast. About 150 lines of new code.
evidence: R: MVTec AD detection AUROC 99.9; SOTA on VisA, MPDD; weak-defect and woven-fabric industrial validation.
min_experiment: Arm: house + GAS aux head (weight 0.1); baseline: house. Metric: CV crack recall on components < 2% contrast, crack IoU. Kill: low-contrast recall gain < +0.05 or crack IoU drop > 0.01.
prior_overlap: none; crack copy-paste (n.d.) was image-level real-crack pasting, not feature-space synthesis.

title: SANSA: Unleashing the Hidden Semantics in SAM2 for Few-Shot Segmentation
mechanism: A light adapter makes SAM2 features semantic (not instance-tracking), then SAM2 memory attention matches support to query; supports point, box and scribble prompts.
evidence: R: SOTA on generalisation-oriented FSS benchmarks, beats generalist in-context models, faster and smaller than prior methods (natural-image benchmarks only).
adaptation: Same pipeline as GFDS SAM2 mode but semantic matching suits cracks that differ in shape between cells; optionally re-train the adapter episodically on our 478 cells (pairs sharing a class), then label pool half-cells and run the K-shot track.
min_experiment: Within G0: SANSA (off-the-shelf and EL-episodic adapter) vs GFDS SAM2 video mode vs house PF ensemble on val54+F51+H36; metric H36 inactive IoU and crack relF1@2; kill if not above SAM2 video mode and not above house on any class.
prior_overlap: none; SAM2 Hiera-T was only linear-probed frozen (no gain), never used as a matcher or labeller.

title: Contrastive Mask Fidelity: Reference-Free Auditing of Ground-Truth Masks in Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Reference-free score of how well each ground-truth mask agrees with its image, to flag coarse, incomplete or misaligned masks.
adaptation: Score all 582 + 106 crack and inactive masks; publish fidelity with the benchmark and report test scores with low-fidelity cells flagged (CSIR_00070 should rank bottom). Training: drop or down-weight the worst decile, an automatic B1 audit (24 of 239 flagged, never fixed).
min_experiment: Arm: house trained without the lowest-fidelity 10% crack masks; baseline: house. Metric crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if n.d. Audit itself is a benchmark deliverable.
evidence: R: remote-sensing segmentation datasets (abstract); numbers not read.
prior_overlap: partial: B1 manual-flag audit done, nothing fixed or removed.

alt_notes.adaptation: EL-aware judge: image-level crack classifier (train + ELPV labels); inpaint the masked crack line and measure drop in p(crack); choose per segment between human and model line; mainly to audit test labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: judge on 100 train cells with synthetic 1-2 px shifts. Baseline: ridge-darkness heuristic. Metric: fraction choosing the darkest-ridge line. Kill: < 70%.

title: AnomalyDiffusion: Few-Shot Anomaly Image Generation with Diffusion Model
mechanism: Latent diffusion with a spatial anomaly embedding (learned appearance + mask-encoded location) and adaptive attention re-weighting toward weakly generated regions for aligned anomaly image-mask pairs.
adaptation: Benchmark baseline for the synthetic-data track: train per class (crack, inactive) on train cells with grey replicated to 3 channels; report against pixel-space renderers at matched sample count.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + AnomalyDiffusion samples. Baseline: rows 1 and 2 at matched count, PF 5 seeds. Metric: E1 relF1@2 (crack), CV inactive IoU. Reported, no kill.
evidence: R: better generation authenticity and diversity on MVTec and improved downstream inspection (abstract); 192 citations. Code github.com/sjtuplayer/anomalydiffusion stated in paper, not opened.
prior_overlap: None.

title: Topologically faithful image segmentation via induced matching of persistence barcodes (Betti matching)
mechanism: Persistent-homology loss that matches predicted and label barcode features by their induced spatial correspondence, then penalises unmatched or shifted features. The efficient C++ version is arxiv:2407.04683.
adaptation: Crack class, 0-dimensional features. Compute it only on label components >= 20 px so that tiny label fragments (76 to 88% of components) are not enforced. Could raise the share of components found (0.798).
min_experiment: Arm: PF + Betti matching (crack, w 0.1, last 10k steps), 3 seeds screen then 5. Baseline: PF. Metric: component recall >= 20 px, crack IoU. Kill if component recall gain < 0.02 or crack IoU < baseline - 0.012.
evidence: R (web summary of abstract): better topology on six datasets with volumetric performance kept. TopoMortar shows a different PH loss (TopoLoss) dropping CrackTree Dice to 0.52.
prior_overlap: none. No PH loss was run here.

title: AOI-SSL: Self-Supervised Framework for Efficient Segmentation of Wire-bonded Semiconductors In Optical Inspection
mechanism: MAE pretraining in a 7k-image industrial domain (beats DINO and iBOT); hybrid conv-ViT keeps thin wires; patch-level kNN retrieval over labelled patch embeddings adapts to a new device family with tens of images.
adaptation: (b) first: kNN retrieval head on house encoder features with a memory from a few labelled half-cut cells (T3b few-shot track), fused with house logits for E1. (a) MAE on a hybrid conv-ViT only if a ConvNeXt MIM arm passes.
min_experiment: Arm: house PF ensemble + retrieval head with T3b memory. Baseline: house PF ensemble. Metric: E1 crack recall at matched precision. Kill if < +0.02.
evidence: R: FasterViT-0 MAE 60.3 mIoU vs ResNet18 U-Net++ ImageNet 52.4 (architectures differ); wire IoU 66.7 vs 43.0 for ViT-Tiny; retrieval 71.5 vs 47.5 mIoU on a single device family with a 42-image memory.
prior_overlap: None.

alt_notes.adaptation: (a) MAE on a hybrid conv-ViT on the pool, PF; (b) kNN patch-retrieval head on house encoder features with a memory from a few labelled half-cut cells, fused with house logits, as an E1 few-shot track.
alt_notes.min_experiment: (b) kNN head vs house PF ensemble on E1 crack recall at matched precision; kill if < +0.02. ~2 GPU-h.

title: Causal-Tune: Mining Causal Factors from Vision Foundation Models for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: PEFT that keeps VFM feature components linked to causal factors and suppresses spurious ones (details unverified).
adaptation: E1 failures come from spurious cues (scuff streaks, half-cut layout); one arm on VFM-H in place of Rein.
min_experiment: Arm: VFM-H + Causal-Tune. Baseline: VFM-H + Rein. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: not +0.02.
evidence: R: 5 citations; abstract fragment only.
prior_overlap: none.

title: EasyControlEdge: A Foundation-Model Fine-Tuning For Edge Detection
mechanism: Lightweight condition injection on a frozen FLUX.1-dev rectified-flow model, pixel-space weighted CE through a proxy gradient, guidance scale controls edge density at inference.
adaptation: EL replicated to 3 channels at 512 px, frozen backbone, crack-only target; guidance scale as a recall knob for E1 and the almost-all-cracks target. Gated FLUX download needs user OK. First check VAE reconstruction of GT crack maps since the 8x latent may erase 1 px cracks.
min_experiment: Step 1: crack IoU of decode(encode(GT)) vs GT on train cells; stop if < 0.8. Step 2: 1 seed on 478 cells, judged on E1 crack relF1@2 vs PF single model and PF ensemble (0.43 to 0.47). Kill if below PF single model. About 40 GPU-h.
evidence: R: BIPED with 20 training images CEval ODS 0.875 vs DiffusionEdge 0.851, GED 0.746; BSDS CEval ODS 0.807; CubiCasa walls strong at 42 images.
prior_overlap: None; generative foundation models and adapters are listed as open. Frozen linear probes of DINO/SAM do not cover this.

alt_notes.adaptation: Tile the EL image to 3 channels at 512 px and train LoRA only, on crack. The guidance scale acts as a recall knob that is not a threshold, aimed at the target relR@2 >= 0.90 at relP@2 >= 0.90 and at E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: EasyControlEdge LoRA on crack, 3 seeds. Baseline: house ensemble. Metrics: best relR@2 at relP@2 >= 0.90, E1 relF1@2. Kill if both are below the house model.

title: Balanced Learning for Domain Adaptive Semantic Segmentation (BLDA)
mechanism: Detects over- and under-predicted classes from logit distributions and aligns them to shared anchor distributions, post hoc and inside self-training.
evidence: Consistent gains on two UDA benchmarks, mostly on under-predicted classes, when added to existing methods (abstract).
adaptation: Estimate per-class logit corrections from unlabelled E1-like pool cells (half-cells); E1 cracks are under-predicted (70% p<0.001). Use post hoc first, then inside the MIC arm.
min_experiment: Post-hoc BLDA correction on PF ensemble vs val-chosen crack logit bias; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and test crack IoU. Kill: < +0.02 E1 relF1@2.
prior_overlap: Partial: a single val-chosen crack logit bias was tried; per-class target-estimated alignment was not.

title: ConformalSAM: Unlocking the Potential of Foundational Segmentation Models in Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation with Conformal Prediction
mechanism: Calibrate a foundation teacher on the labelled data with conformal prediction, and keep as pseudo-labels only the pixels whose conformal set is a single class. Later training switches to self-reliance so the student does not overfit the FM masks.
adaptation: Teacher = our ensemble or the UniMatch V2 hybrid. Per-class conformal thresholds (crack and inactive separately) from val 54 + F51 give a coverage-controlled pool pseudo-label mask in place of hand-set thresholds. An add-on to the ensemble-distillation arm.
min_experiment: Ensemble-distillation arm B with conformal masks vs the same with plain soft targets. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU, inactive IoU. Kill: < +0.005 crack IoU and < +0.01 inactive IoU.
evidence: R: beats recent SSSS methods on three standard benchmarks and helps other methods as a plug-in (numbers not retrieved).
prior_overlap: Partial. Tolerant and threshold pseudo-label variants were run under Mean Teacher. Conformal calibration with an offline teacher was not run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Teacher = PF 5-seed ensemble or the DINOv3-IML model (SEEM has no EL concepts). Per-class quantiles fitted on val 54 + F51; pseudo-label the 1,152 half-cut pool cells; class-conditional selection keeps faint crack pixels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: student trained on labelled + CP-filtered pseudo-labelled half-cut cells, 5 seeds. Baseline: the old hard / tolerant pseudo-label runs with the pool at 100%. Metrics: E1 crack recall and relF1@2. Kill: no E1 relF1@2 gain over the old pseudo-label run.

title: Distribution-aware Noisy-label Crack Segmentation
mechanism: A SAM-Adapter for cracks, guided by distribution-aware domain knowledge so that it resists omitted and mislabelled cracks in small training sets; tested on an unseen crack dataset.
adaptation: Bold bet for E1: fine-tune a SAM / SAM2 adapter on 1-channel EL replicated to 3 channels at 1024 px, with noise guidance from the house-model 5-seed ensemble. Judge on E1 half-cut cells.
min_experiment: Arm: SAM2 adapter + noise guidance, 3 seeds. Baseline: house 5-seed ensemble on E1. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < 0.47.
evidence: R (abstract): beats SOTA on two pavement crack datasets and generalises to the unseen CFD dataset.
prior_overlap: SAM2 Hiera-T was only linear-probed frozen (no sign of gain). Adapter fine-tuning with noisy-label guidance was not tried.

title: MaxStyle: Adversarial Style Composition for Robust Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Auxiliary style-augmented decoder; adversarial search over worst-case mixtures of feature styles plus noise.
evidence: Better OOD robustness on cardiac and prostate MR under corruptions, site shift and unseen sequences, in low and high data settings (abstract).
adaptation: Add an aux reconstruction decoder to U-Net++; perturb encoder feature mean/std adversarially.
min_experiment: PF+MaxStyle vs PF+GIN-IPA; E1 relF1@2; kill if < +0.02 over GIN-IPA.
prior_overlap: None.

title: OFL-SAM2: Prompt SAM2 with Online Few-shot Learner for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: A light mapping network trained on few labelled samples yields target features fused with frozen SAM2 memory attention, prompt-free, with online updates of the mapper during inference over a sequence.
evidence: R: SOTA with limited training data on three medical image segmentation datasets (3D volumes / 2D sequences).
adaptation: Bold bet: treat the cells of one module as a video so SAM2 memory and the online mapper carry what was found in earlier cells of the same module (E1 has 106 cells from 67 modules; pool cells come by module); mapper trained on the 478 cells; aimed at half-cut and scuff context shift.
min_experiment: Module-ordered OFL-SAM2 vs GFDS SAM2 video mode with fixed supports on H36 (ordered by module) and pool half-cells; metric H36 inactive IoU; kill if no gain over fixed-support SAM2.
prior_overlap: Partial: per-panel BN adaptation failed (BRIEF 5), but that is statistic adaptation of the house model, not memory-based propagation across a module.

title: Semantic-Aware Random Convolution and Source Matching for Domain Generalization in Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Different random convolutions per labelled region during training; test-time intensity mapping of target images toward source.
adaptation: Use only the training half, with the same crack/inactive exclusion as SLAug; skip test-time mapping (intensity normalisation already failed here).
min_experiment: Run only if SLAug arm passes: PF + semantic RandConv vs PF + SLAug, 3 seeds; keep the better.
evidence: R: beats prior DG methods in most cross-modality and cross-centre settings (abdominal, whole-heart, prostate), matching in-domain baseline in several.
prior_overlap: Test-time half overlaps BRIEF s5 intensity normalisation (fail); training half untested.

title: CF-Loss: Clinically-relevant feature optimised loss function for retinal multi-class vessel segmentation and vascular feature measurement
mechanism: Adds to the pixel loss a loss on downstream measurement features (vessel density, box-count fractal dimension) computed from the soft mask, so the segmentation gets the measured quantity right.
adaptation: Per-cell L1 between the soft predicted inactive fraction and GT (w 0.3) and between the soft crack density and GT (w 0.1), on top of PF. Targets the amount of inactive in BMRK and E1 cells, where the model under-calls inactive.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + feature loss, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: CV inactive IoU, per-cell inactive-fraction MAE, clean-49 crack IoU. Kill if inactive IoU gain < 0.015 and fraction MAE not reduced by >= 20%, or crack IoU drops > 0.012. About 6 GPU-h.
evidence: R (web summary, secondary): vessel density + fractal dimension loss combined with pixel loss, tested on 2 networks and 3 public datasets; numbers not retrieved.
prior_overlap: none; BRIEF section 5 losses (Dice, clDice, Skeleton Recall, offset-tolerant CE) do not include a per-image measurement loss

title: GraphMorph: Tubular Structure Extraction by Morphing Predicted Graphs
mechanism: Graph decoder predicts branch-level graph per patch; SkeletonDijkstra morphs it onto the centreline probability map; graph used to remove false positives.
adaptation: Use only as a crack false-positive filter (drop components not on predicted branches) and as crack topology for severity.
min_experiment: Arm = PF + graph decoder FP filter; baseline = PF; 3 seeds; relP@2 at fixed relR@2. Kill if relP@2 gain < 0.01.
evidence: R: centreline and segmentation tasks on several vessel and road datasets; fewer false positives.
prior_overlap: None.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use only as a crack false-positive filter on PF output (drop components not on a predicted branch), aimed at scuff/decoy false alarms on E1; graph gives crack topology for severity.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + GraphMorph filter vs PF; metric crack relP@2 at fixed relR@2 on CV and E1; kill if relP@2 +<0.01.

title: MP-Former: Mask-Piloted Transformer for Image Segmentation
mechanism: Feed noised ground-truth masks into Mask2Former's masked attention and train to reconstruct them, making masks consistent across decoder layers and speeding training.
evidence: R: +2.3 AP and +1.6 mIoU on Cityscapes (R50); matches or beats Mask2Former with half the epochs on ADE20K; no inference cost.
adaptation: For M2F on 478 cells: noise model = our known label jitter (1-2 px shifts, dilation of crack masks, random drops of small components); tests whether faster convergence helps with few images.
min_experiment: Only if M2F arm B survives: arm C = + mask-piloted training; baseline M2F arm B; metrics mIoU_rob, inactive IoU at 10k and 20k steps; kill if no gain beyond noise.
prior_overlap: none; unrelated to the offset-tolerant CE that was n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Noise model = measured label jitter (1-2 px shifts, source-specific widths); training-efficiency add-on for M2F on 478 images.
alt_notes.min_experiment: M2F arm B vs B + mask-piloted training at 10k and 20k steps; metric mIoU_rob and inactive IoU; kill if no gain > 0.01 mIoU_rob at either length.

title: SARD: Segmentation-Aware Anomaly Synthesis via Region-Constrained Diffusion with Discriminative Mask Guidance
mechanism: During reverse denoising the background is frozen and only the anomaly region is updated. A mask-guided discriminator judges both global realism and local anomaly fidelity.
evidence: Abstract: beats prior synthesis methods in segmentation accuracy on MVTec-AD and BTAD. No numbers on the arXiv page.
adaptation: With a PV-DDPM retrained on our 478 cells, insert inactive regions or crack bands into real labelled cells while every pixel outside the mask stays real. This removes the seam problem by construction for blobby classes.
min_experiment: PF + region-constrained diffusion insertions vs PF + inactive copy-paste (Soft-CP arm), 5 seeds plus CV. Metric: CV inactive IoU. Kill if not above the copy-paste arm.
prior_overlap: none

title: Towards Fewer Annotations: Active Learning via Region Impurity and Prediction Uncertainty for Domain Adaptive Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Select target regions by region impurity (class entropy in a neighbourhood) times prediction uncertainty for domain-adaptive segmentation.
adaptation: Rank the 1,152 pool half-cells (E1-like, half-cut, scuff) by RIPU score and pseudo-label the top ones with the PF ensemble; if a minimal labelling case is accepted, label 20-30 RIPU-chosen regions.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + top 300 RIPU-ranked pool half-cells pseudo-labelled. Baseline: PF variant. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU. Kill: < +0.02 E1 relF1@2.
evidence: R: 69.6 mIoU GTAV to Cityscapes with 2.2% labelled pixels vs 66.6 for LabOR. Code at github.com/BIT-DA/RIPU per search results, not opened.
prior_overlap: Synthetic half-cut views n.d.; selection of real half-cut pool cells not run. Open.

title: VasoMIM: Vascular Anatomy-Aware Masked Image Modeling for Vessel Segmentation
mechanism: MIM where an unsupervised Frangi map steers masking onto thin-structure patches (ramp 0 to 0.5, ratio 0.5) and a frozen small segmentor enforces that the reconstruction keeps the same vessels.
adaptation: Dark-ridge filter (Frangi on inverted EL, sigma 1-2 px, or black top-hat) for crack-guided masking; consistency through the frozen house U-Net++ crack / inactive logits instead of their UNeXt; on top of the Frepa or FCMAE ConvNeXt arm.
min_experiment: Arm: best ConvNeXt MIM arm + crack-guided masking + house-model consistency. Baseline: same arm with random masking. Kill if out-of-fold crack relF1@2 < +0.005 and E1 crack recall < +0.01.
evidence: R: 20,650 unlabelled angiograms, ViT-B/16 + U-Net; MAE vs scratch +18.5 Dice at 25% labels; VasoMIM over MAE only +0.35 to +1.1 Dice.
prior_overlap: None for structure-guided masking; plain MIM on R34 closed.

alt_notes.adaptation: Ridge-filter-guided masking at ratio 0.5 and consistency through frozen house crack/inactive logits, added on top of the best FCMAE/Frepa arm.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Winner of FCMAE/Frepa + guided masking vs the same without; kill if out-of-fold relF1@2 < +0.005 and E1 recall < +0.01.

title: Combining Unsupervised Domain Adaptation and Semi-Supervised Learning for Power Line and Transmission Tower Segmentation
mechanism: UDA pretraining helps the network learn thin, low-feature power lines; SSL fine-tuning follows, with dynamic co-perturbation of image and features.
adaptation: Stage 1: UDA from UCF-EL (or the 478 labelled cells) to the pool. Stage 2: SSL on the pool with combined image and feature perturbation. Closest thin-structure SSL evidence found.
min_experiment: Only after reading the full text: a 2-stage arm vs house PF, 3 seeds. Metric: crack relF1@2 on clean-49 and E1. Kill if n.d.
evidence: R: self-built + public power-line sets; beats several SSL methods; no numbers in the abstract.
prior_overlap: UCF-EL encoder pretraining was erased by the house fine-tune. UDA-then-SSL was never run. Open.

title: Focal-SAM: Focal Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Long-Tailed Classification
mechanism: Class-wise sharpness penalties, heavier on tail classes, without extra backpropagations.
adaptation: Per-class pixel losses over the 24 classes, focal weight on sharpness for inactive, crack, splice, gridline, edge_dark; run only if plain SAM helps.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + Focal-SAM, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF + SAM. Metric: inactive IoU, gridline/splice/edge_dark IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: no tail-class IoU gain >= 0.02 over PF + SAM.
evidence: R (abstract): better than ImbSAM and CC-SAM on long-tailed classification with traditional and foundation models.
prior_overlap: none; long-tail methods never tried.

title: Improving Semantic Segmentation via Decoupled Body and Edge Supervision
mechanism: Splits features into a body part (made consistent by learned flow warping) and an edge part, each with its own supervision on sampled body and edge pixels.
adaptation: Apply to inactive and the cell-structure classes (blob interiors with sharp edges). Crack stays on the normal head because it is all edge.
min_experiment: Arm: house + body/edge decoupled decoder. Baseline: house. Metrics: inactive IoU (CV), border and material IoU. Kill if the inactive CV gain is < 0.02 and mIoU_rob gain is < 0.01.
evidence: R: Cityscapes 83.7 mIoU with fine annotations only; also CamVid, KITTI, BDD.
prior_overlap: none

title: Multi-style conversion for semantic segmentation of lesions in fundus images by adversarial attacks
mechanism: A linear probe on encoder features detects dataset origin. An adversarial input perturbation toward a chosen dataset makes the frozen model segment in that dataset's annotation style, with no retraining.
adaptation: Train a source probe on the frozen house encoder, then at test take a few PGD steps that push each cell toward its own source (or toward ARTS for thin output). Measure the change in crack width and IoU.
min_experiment: Arm = PGD style steering on the existing 5-seed ensemble versus the unmodified ensemble. Metric: crack IoU clean-49. Kill if < +0.005. Under 2 GPU-h.
evidence: R: diabetic retinopathy lesion datasets with different annotation protocols; continuous style conversion shown (numbers not retrieved).
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: No retraining: probe source on frozen house encoder features, then at test push each image toward its own source (or toward ARTS for thin output) with a few PGD steps on the probe; measure crack width and IoU.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PGD style push on existing house checkpoints (5 seeds). Baseline: same checkpoints without push. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and per-source predicted width. Kill if IoU gain < +0.008 or widths do not move by >= 0.2 px.

title: Uncertainty-Masked Bernoulli Diffusion for Camouflaged Object Detection Refinement
mechanism: Estimate an uncertainty map, run Bernoulli diffusion refinement only inside uncertain regions and leave confident pixels untouched; pluggable after any encoder-decoder.
evidence: R: average gains of 5.5% MAE and 3.2% weighted F-measure across COD benchmarks with modest overhead.
adaptation: Replace their HUQNet with free 5-seed ensemble disagreement; restrict Bernoulli diffusion to a 3 px band around disagreeing crack / inactive pixels; condition on 1-ch EL and ensemble mean.
min_experiment: Arm: band-restricted Bernoulli diffusion on house ensemble. Baseline: house ensemble with val-chosen bias. Metric: crack relF1@2, IoU. Kill: relF1@2 < +0.01.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Limit refinement to the uncertain 2-4 px band around predicted cracks and inactive borders, protecting the 0.93 relP@2 already reached; uncertainty from 5-seed disagreement instead of a new network.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: masked Bernoulli diffusion refiner on the uncertain band. Baseline: house ensemble. Metrics: crack IoU, relP@2 / relR@2 on 5-fold CV. Kill: crack IoU < +0.01.

title: Topograph: An efficient Graph-Based Framework for Strictly Topology Preserving Image Segmentation
mechanism: A component graph of prediction and label finds topologically critical regions, and the loss aggregates over them. It also defines a strict homotopy metric. About 5x faster than PH losses.
adaptation: Same use as Betti matching on crack (8-connectivity, components >= 20 px). Its homotopy metric is a candidate topology score for the benchmark.
min_experiment: Same design as Betti matching. Run whichever of the two installs cleanly.
evidence: R (abstract): state-of-the-art topology on binary and multi-class datasets, up to 5x faster loss than PH methods.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack class, component (0-dim) errors only, restricted to label components >= 20 px so sub-20 px label fragments (76 to 88% of components) are not enforced. Its homotopy metric is a candidate topology score for the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + Topograph (small weight) vs PF, 5 seeds. Kill if component recall (>= 20 px) gain < 0.02 or crack IoU < PF - 0.012.

title: RankSEG-RMA: An Efficient Segmentation Algorithm via Reciprocal Moment Approximation
mechanism: Replace argmax with the decision rule that maximises expected Dice / IoU per image, now O(d) and for non-overlapping classes; the 2026 follow-up (arxiv:2609.38930, RankSEG-DEP) adds local label dependence for small low-contrast objects.
adaptation: Post-process FINAL crack probabilities per cell. It maximises per-image IoU, while our decision metric is pooled IoU, and at 100% labels a val bias adds only about +0.004, so expected gain on test is small; more useful for per-cell benchmark metrics.
min_experiment: No training: RankSEG-RMA (and DEP) vs val-chosen bias on FINAL probabilities. Kill if pooled crack IoU < bias + 0.005 and per-cell IoU not better.
evidence: R: RankSEG almost guarantees improved Dice/IoU over argmax; RMA keeps comparable performance at O(d) (LiTS RankSEG took 16.33 s vs 0.01 s argmax).
prior_overlap: Partial: logit bias tuning was run (+0.014 to +0.023 at 5%, about 0 at 100%); per-image metric-optimal decoding not run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Post-process FINAL crack probabilities per cell; compare against pooled-IoU val bias since RankSEG maximises per-image IoU.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training: RankSEG-RMA on FINAL probabilities; baseline argmax + val-chosen bias. Kill: pooled crack IoU < val-bias + 0.005.

title: SAMRefiner: Taming Segment Anything Model for Universal Mask Refinement
mechanism: Training-free refinement: mines distance-guided points, context-aware elastic boxes and Gaussian-style mask prompts from a coarse mask and feeds SAM; SAMRefiner++ adds a label-free IoU adaptation step.
adaptation: Zero-training test on predicted inactive regions (blobby, well labelled) and on BMRK cells; replicate EL to 3 channels; skip crack lines, which suit SAM poorly at 1-2 px.
min_experiment: Arm: SAMRefiner on house / PF inactive components. Baseline: unrefined masks. Metric: inactive IoU on 5-fold CV and E1 (PF). Kill: < +0.01 inactive IoU or any BMRK drop.
evidence: R: improves coarse masks from several sources for use as training labels across benchmarks (numbers not read).
prior_overlap: Frozen SAM2 Hiera-T linear probe showed no gain (BRIEF section 5); prompt-based mask refinement was not tested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Poor fit for 1 to 2 px cracks (the 2026 fracture paper found unconstrained MedSAM supervision hurts thin structures). Test only on region classes: inactive, material, edge_dark, splice, where boundaries are blobby.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house trained with SAMRefiner-refined masks for material, edge_dark, splice only, 3 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: per-class IoU and mIoU_rob. Kill: mIoU_rob under +0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Not for cracks (SAM cannot resolve 1 to 2 px lines; frozen SAM2 probe gave no signal). Refine train labels of blob classes: inactive at BMRK (IoU 0.324), material, edge_dark; keep original where SAM IoU score is low.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house trained with SAM-refined inactive/material/edge_dark labels; baseline: house. Metrics: inactive IoU (clean-49 and E1), mIoU_rob. Kill if inactive and mIoU_rob both n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Blobby classes only: inactive, material, edge_dark, border; EL replicated to 3 channels; one prompt set per connected component of the house ensemble; IoU adaptation on the unlabelled 11.9k pool. Not for 1 to 2 px cracks. Also usable as a label-refinement tool (D16).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: SAMRefiner on ensemble inactive / material components. Baseline: house ensemble (PF ensemble on E1). Metrics: inactive IoU on OOF CV and E1, material and edge_dark IoU. Kill: inactive IoU < +0.02 on OOF CV.

title: DSCformer: A Dual-Branch Network Integrating Enhanced Dynamic Snake Convolution and SegFormer for Crack Segmentation
mechanism: Dynamic snake convolution with pyramid-kernel offset prediction and bidirectional offset iteration, in a dual branch with SegFormer, plus weighted channel attention.
adaptation: Replace the last two U-Net++ decoder conv blocks with enhanced DSConv for crack-following receptive fields; encoder and other heads unchanged.
min_experiment: Arm: PF with DSConv decoder blocks; baseline: PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU and components found. Kill if IoU gain < +0.01.
evidence: R: IoU 59.22% on Crack3238 and 87.24% on FIND.
prior_overlap: none (snake / deformable convolutions are on the never-tried list).

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace the last two U-Net++ decoder conv blocks with DSConv on the crack path; keep the ResNet-34 encoder and 24-class head.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF with DSConv decoder blocks; baseline PF; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU and components >= 20 px found. Kill if IoU gain < +0.01 and components n.d.

title: Infrared Small Target Detection with Scale and Location Sensitivity (SLS loss, MSHNet)
mechanism: Scale-weighted IoU loss plus a centre-point location penalty, applied at every decoder scale via a multi-scale head.
adaptation: Scale weight per merged crack instance; drop the centre term for cracks (jitter), keep for inactive blobs; add deep supervision at each U-Net++ level.
min_experiment: Arm: house + SLS-style multi-scale scale-weighted IoU on crack, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: component recall < 20 px, relF1@2. Kill: no gain >= 0.02 component recall.
evidence: IRSTD-1K / NUDT-SIRST: plain U-Net with SLS + multi-scale head beats prior SOTA; SLS also improves other detectors.
prior_overlap: none

title: Metrics reloaded: recommendations for image analysis validation
mechanism: Problem fingerprint (target size and shape, reference quality, imbalance) drives metric choice; companion pitfalls paper doi:10.1038/s41592-023-02150-0.
adaptation: Write EL fingerprints: crack thin and noisy, inactive blob and rare, 24 classes with many absent in test; map to overlap + tolerance + per-component detection metrics; use as benchmark justification.
min_experiment: Arm: fill fingerprint for crack, inactive, structural classes. Kill: adopt only metrics it selects that we do not already report.
evidence: R: Delphi consensus framework; no empirical score gains.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Write the EL fingerprint into the spec. Crack = tubular, 1-2 px, imprecise labels, so headline tolerance F1 / clDice / component recall and keep strict IoU secondary. Inactive = blobby and reliable, so IoU plus per-cell detection. Other classes = mIoU_rob with a fixed class list.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Re-score the existing 5 house seeds and the PF ensemble with the fingerprint metrics on clean-49. Decision: keep a metric in the headline only if its seed-to-seed SD is smaller than the gap between house and ensemble.

title: Dinomaly2: A Unified Framework for Unsupervised Image Anomaly Detection
mechanism: Reconstruction on frozen DINO features with noisy bottleneck, linear attention and loose reconstruction; one model across classes, few-shot (8 normals) and RGB-IR settings.
adaptation: Supersedes D07's Dinomaly row for the benchmark: one model across 5 sources x 3 layouts; 8-shot variant with per-module-family references for E1; RGB-IR path noted for WattCycle drone IR.
evidence: R: MVTec AD / VisA I-AUROC 99.9 / 99.3 multi-class; 8-shot 98.7 / 97.4; 15 benchmarks incl. multi-view and RGB-3D / RGB-IR.
min_experiment: Benchmark AD track: train once on clean pool, report pixel AUROC, AU-PRO, crack / inactive relF1@2, cell AUROC. As a prior: same offline 30% recovery kill as SuperADD.
prior_overlap: none

title: Dinomaly: The Less Is More Philosophy in Multi-Class Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
mechanism: Normal-only feature reconstruction with a DINOv2 encoder, dropout noisy bottleneck, linear attention and loose reconstruction for a single multi-class model.
adaptation: One model across 5 sources x mono/multi/half-cut trained on clean pool cells; evaluate the map against inactive masks and crack masks dilated by 2 px; candidate prior channel for E1.
min_experiment: Train once; pixel AUROC / AU-PRO on test and F51 for inactive and crack-band; fusion with PF ensemble, kill if E1 inactive IoU gain < +0.03.
evidence: R: image AUROC 99.6 MVTec-AD, 98.7 VisA, 89.3 Real-IAD in multi-class setting.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: One model over 5 sources x mono/multi/half-cut on clean pool cells; evaluate the map against inactive and crack dilated by 2 px; prior channel for E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark AD track: train once, report pixel AUROC, AU-PRO, relF1@2 per class on CV and E1; for scores, same offline recall test as AnomalyDINO with kill at < 30% recovery.

title: DiffusionEdge: Diffusion Probabilistic Model for Crisp Edge Detection
mechanism: A latent diffusion edge detector. A pixel-level, uncertainty-aware cross-entropy is distilled into the latent space, with an adaptive Fourier filter, and it predicts crisp edges without NMS.
adaptation: Train on binary crack and gridline maps with the 1-channel EL image replicated, at 512 px. First check that the autoencoder can reconstruct the 1 px GT crack maps, a cheap test. Mainly a benchmark baseline for generative thin-structure methods.
min_experiment: Gate: autoencoder reconstruction IoU of GT crack maps, which must be >= 0.9 to proceed. Arm: DiffusionEdge on crack, 3 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: relF1@2, crack IoU. Kill at the gate or if relF1@2 is more than 0.03 below the house model.
evidence: R: on NYUDv2, ODS +30.2%, OIS +28.1% and AC +65.1% over the second best without post-processing. Trained on benchmark-sized sets of a few hundred to a thousand images.
prior_overlap: Diffusion segmenters are listed as never tried. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Train on crack + gridline binary maps, 1-channel replicated, 512 px; check VAE reconstruction of 1 px cracks first. Mainly the generative member of the benchmark suite.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: DiffusionEdge on 478 cells, 2 seeds; baseline house. Metrics relF1@2, crack IoU, AC. Kill if relF1@2 below house - 0.02. About 30 GPU-h.

title: Open data sets for assessing photovoltaic system reliability
mechanism: Review and inventory of open PV datasets across EL, IR, PL and UVF with tools and suggested practices.
adaptation: Source of OpenUVF (3000 labelled + 21,600 unlabelled UVF cell images for cracks) for the cross-modal arm, NREL field PL half-cut cell images as unlabelled half-cut context for E1, and the list of EL datasets the benchmark must check for leakage or use as external tests.
min_experiment: No training arm of its own; feeds the UMMKD arm and the benchmark external-test list. Check OpenUVF label format before any download (user OK).
evidence: R (full text read): OpenUVF 50 labelled / 100 unlabelled modules, 3000 labelled / 21,600 unlabelled cells; NREL field PL 856 half-cut cell images at 4056 x 3040; EL sets from LBNL, NREL, EPRI, Sandia, FAU, PVEL-AD, Wits, UCF, CWRU.
prior_overlap: none

title: PV-MambaSeg: Geometry-Enhanced Vision Mamba With Omni-Local Scan for Photovoltaic Cell Defect Segmentation
mechanism: Vision Mamba with omni-local multi-direction scanning plus a global-local VSS block with multi-window aggregation and channel attention for irregular, arbitrarily oriented defects.
adaptation: If code is released, train at 512 px 1-ch on our 24 classes; multi-direction scan may follow long cracks across busbars. Needs Mamba CUDA kernels (install needs user OK).
min_experiment: Arm PV-MambaSeg 3 seeds vs house; mIoU_rob and crack relF1@2; kill if both below house.
evidence: R: claims highest mIoU on two real PV defect datasets with 2.77 M params and 0.78 GFLOPs; per-dataset numbers not retrieved; code 'will be made public', not found.
prior_overlap: none: Mamba never tried.

title: Anomaly detection in IR images of PV modules using supervised contrastive learning
mechanism: Supervised contrastive training of a ResNet-34 plus kNN distance as anomaly score, evaluated as train-on-one-plant, test-on-another (unsupervised domain adaptation framing).
evidence: R: AUROC 73.3 to 96.6 % on 9 source-target combinations of 4 plants, 2.92 M IR module images, 8.5 % anomalous; at a fixed threshold 79.4 % normal and 77.1 % anomalous correct; sometimes beats a BCE classifier; insensitive to hyperparameters.
adaptation: Add a SupCon auxiliary loss on cell-pooled layer4 features (positives = same cell label crack / inactive / clean, sampled across the 5 sources) to the PF fine-tune, aimed at the E1 gap; adopt the source-to-target protocol as the model for the benchmark's unseen-module split.
min_experiment: Arm PF + SupCon aux (weight 0.1), 3 seeds; baseline PF, 3 seeds; metrics E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, test clean-49 crack IoU; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.02 or test crack IoU drops > 0.01.
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF 5 tested MIM / DDeP pool pretraining and Mean Teacher, not a supervised contrastive auxiliary loss during fine-tuning.

title: Real-time high-resolution neural network with semantic guidance for crack segmentation (HrSegNet)
mechanism: A high-resolution path kept throughout the network with a low-resolution semantic guidance branch injected into it, designed for cracks.
adaptation: Run as a crack-specific benchmark entry: 1-ch replicated, 512 px, 24 classes, our protocol and splits, no extra tuning.
min_experiment: Bench run under the protocol vs house PF; 5-fold CV crack IoU and relF1@2; as a score arm kill if CV crack IoU is below house PF minus 0.012. About 8 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: Partial overlap with R5 (more resolution, n.d.); the architecture itself never run.
evidence: R: CrackSeg9k 80.56 mIoU (B48), B16 78.43 mIoU at 182 FPS; Asphalt3k, Concrete3k.

title: Cross-Image Relational Knowledge Distillation for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Distil pixel-to-pixel and pixel-to-region relations across images using memory banks.
adaptation: Benchmark KD baseline; memory bank across cells of all 5 sources; compare with logit KD at matched GPU-h.
min_experiment: Benchmark-only: CIRKD student vs logit-KD student at matched GPU-h; metric crack IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill (for score use): below logit KD.
evidence: R: student gains on Cityscapes, CamVid, ADE20K, VOC; canonical-KD paper (2604.25530) shows it loses to plain KD at matched compute.
prior_overlap: none

title: SEiPV-Net: An Efficient Deep Learning Framework for Autonomous Multi-Defect Segmentation in Electroluminescence Images of Solar Photovoltaic Modules
mechanism: Lightweight encoder-decoder on the 24-class Pratt data; compares weighted CE, weighted squared Dice and weighted Tanimoto losses with custom vs equal class weights.
adaptation: Replace the house soft Dice on crack/inactive with weighted Tanimoto, optionally extend to weak classes; keep architecture.
min_experiment: Arm house + weighted Tanimoto vs house, 5 seeds; crack IoU, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob; kill if no metric moves beyond noise.
evidence: R: abstract only (full text unavailable): custom class weights beat equal; claims better mIoU, F1, Dice than DeepLabv3+, PSPNet, U-Net on 24 classes. Per-class numbers not retrieved.
prior_overlap: Lovasz/Jaccard metric losses listed as untested; Tanimoto is in that family. Open.

title: Supervised Anomaly Detection for Complex Industrial Images (SegAD)
mechanism: Per-region statistics of anomaly maps inside segmentation-map regions, plus an optional supervised score, feed a boosted random forest that makes the final decision.
adaptation: Per-cell features = house crack/inactive probabilities and AD scores inside structural regions (busbar, ribbon, cell body); BRF predicts cell has crack >= 20 px and inactive-fraction band, for post-evaluation / severity.
min_experiment: Arm BRF on house + AD region stats vs baseline house-ensemble max crack prob per cell; metric cell-level crack recall at 95% precision on CV and E1; kill if gain < +0.03. Under 2 GPU-h.
evidence: R: +2.1% AUROC on VAD (5,000 images, 2,000 real defects), +0.4% on VisA.
prior_overlap: none

title: A Scalable Framework for Annotating Photovoltaic Cell Defects in Electroluminescence Images
mechanism: Combine data-driven models and public datasets to produce golden-standard EL anomaly masks at reduced annotation cost.
adaptation: Human-free label refinement: ensemble predictions plus snapping to the darkest ridge propose corrected crack masks for the 24 audit-flagged train cells; accept by a fixed agreement rule.
min_experiment: Arm: house trained on refined crack masks. Baseline: house on revised masks, 5 seeds. Metric: test crack IoU on unchanged test labels, relF1@2. Kill if both < +0.012.
evidence: R: 60% annotation-cost reduction claimed on a widely used dataset (abstract only).
prior_overlap: none; label refinement listed as untried (audit flagged 24 of 239 cells, nothing fixed)

alt_notes.adaptation: Without manual labelling: take house-ensemble and PV-Vision predictions on pool cells, keep cells where both agree within 2 px, add them as down-weighted extra training targets.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + agreement-filtered pseudo masks (1:1). Baseline: house, 5 v 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, test crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use AD maps plus house ensemble disagreement to flag missing / misplaced crack and inactive labels in the 24 audited train cells and beyond, for a refined-label arm without manual labelling.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm train on AD-refined labels vs PF on current labels, 5 seeds; metric 5-fold CV crack IoU and inactive IoU; kill if CV crack IoU gain < +0.012.

title: Label fusion and training methods for reliable representation of inter-rater uncertainty
mechanism: Compares STAPLE, averaging and random per-iteration rater sampling of multi-rater labels, combined with SoftSeg (regression on soft labels). The result is better calibration with equal or better Dice.
adaptation: Where a cell has two crack label versions (2021 vs 2022, or E-SCDD re-annotations), train crack on soft averaged labels or a random version per iteration. Score on revised labels and on the union.
min_experiment: Arm: house with soft or random-version crack targets. Baseline: house on revised labels. Metric: clean-49 relF1@2 and crack IoU. Kill: relF1@2 more than 0.005 below the baseline. First count the train cells with two independent versions.
prior_overlap: none: soft-label losses and annotator modelling are listed as open in BRIEF section 5.
evidence: R: 10 splits on 2 public multi-rater datasets (spinal cord gray matter, MS lesions). SoftSeg is equal or better in Dice and better calibrated; the best fusion method was task-dependent.

title: What is the Added Value of UDA in the VFM Era?
mechanism: Measures that the UDA gain over source-only VFM fine-tuning shrinks from +8 to +2 mIoU with stronger source data, and is zero with diverse real source data.
adaptation: Use as a prior for E1. If a VFM backbone is adopted, expect target-pool UDA to add little, so run MIC on the house model first. For the benchmark, report source-only VFM fine-tuning as the E1 baseline.
min_experiment: No separate run. Read it with MIC-E1: if MIC helps the R34 house model, repeat on the VFM model; kill VFM-UDA if the gain is under +0.02 E1 relF1@2.
evidence: R: synthetic->real UDA gain +8 -> +2 mIoU with stronger source data; 0 with diverse real source; with 1/16 Cityscapes labels, synthetic UDA reaches 85 mIoU, matching full supervision.
prior_overlap: none

title: Brain Metastases Segmentation for BraTS 2026 Task 1: A Multi-Architecture Comparison
mechanism: Head-to-head region-based vs label-based training on the same model with grouped CV, plus pitfalls in region-to-label reconstruction and ensembling.
evidence: R (read): Primus region vs label: ET DSC 0.713 vs 0.710, WT 0.680 vs 0.683, RC 0.566 vs 0.531, TC 0.400 vs 0.742 from a wrong region write order. Lesion F1 unrelated to DSC ranking (ResEncL 0.452 vs Primus 0.052); probability averaging kept the weaker model's lesion F1.
adaptation: Write outer region before inner in the region head and check pixel counts vs softmax; report component-level crack recall beside IoU and check whether 5-seed averaging drops small cracks one seed finds.
min_experiment: No separate training: in the region-head run, compare write orders and per-seed vs ensemble component recall (crack components >=20 px and <20 px); flag if ensemble component recall < best single seed.
prior_overlap: none

title: Dual-Interrelated Diffusion Model for Few-Shot Anomaly Image Generation (DualAnoDiff)
mechanism: Two interrelated diffusion models generate the whole image and the anomaly part together, so the mask follows the generated defect; background and shape information reduce blur.
adaptation: Same role as AnomalyDiffusion for blobby classes and as a benchmark baseline; only if code is public.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + DualAnoDiff inactive samples. Baseline: row 2 arm. Metric: CV inactive IoU. Kill: not better than row 2; skip unless code exists by 20 Nov.
evidence: R: better diversity, realism and mask accuracy than prior methods on MVTec and better downstream detection, localization, classification (abstract).
prior_overlap: None.

title: Natural Synthetic Anomalies for Self-supervised Anomaly Detection and Localization (NSA)
mechanism: Poisson image editing blends scaled patches from other images into normal images, making natural-looking anomalies. A localiser trained on them generalises to real defects.
evidence: MVTec AD detection AUROC 97.2, best among methods without extra data. Also tested on medical images.
adaptation: Add an auxiliary head on pool cells (including the 1,152 multi half-cut cells) that predicts NSA patches made from other pool cells of the same cell type, sharing the encoder with the segmenter. The goal is a defect prior that transfers to E1. NSA patches are never labelled as background in the segmentation loss.
min_experiment: PF + NSA auxiliary head vs PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 crack recall@2 and relF1@2, with test crack IoU as a guard. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02.
prior_overlap: none. Anomaly-detection priors are listed as never tried. Pool MIM and DDeP were different objectives.

alt_notes.adaptation: Auxiliary NSA head on pool cells (incl. 1,152 multi half-cut), patches from same cell type, shared encoder with the segmenter; aim is a defect prior that transfers to E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+NSA-aux vs PF; E1 crack recall@2 and relF1@2. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.02.

title: Small Object Few-Shot Segmentation for Vision-Based Industrial Inspection (SOFS)
mechanism: FSS for small defects: no image resizing, prototype intensity downsampling of support masks, an abnormal prior map, and a mixed normal Dice loss that penalises false positives on defect-free supports.
evidence: R: outperforms FSS baselines on industrial small-defect benchmarks; also does few-shot anomaly detection.
adaptation: Run at native 512 px, episodic training on 478 cells by class, K-shot on half-cells; the mixed normal Dice idea can separately penalise crack false alarms on scuff streaks.
min_experiment: G0 entry for crack: SOFS K=16 vs house PF on H36/F51 crack relF1@2 and false-alarm rate on defect-free half-cells; kill if below house PF and no reduction of false alarms.
prior_overlap: none

title: Decoupled Single-Mask Annotation Noise Detection via Cross-Sectional Patch Self-consistency
mechanism: Training-free label-noise score: sample cross-sectional patches along a thin structure, retrieve intensity-matched neighbour patches by vector search, and score noise by mask disagreement among neighbours.
adaptation: Sample patches orthogonal to crack skeletons; retrieve similar intensity profiles from other cells and sources; flag cells where the label line is off the dark ridge compared with peers; aggregate into per-source offset and width estimates.
min_experiment: Arm: compute noise scores for train crack labels; retrain house with the top 5% patches set to ignore. Baseline: house. Metrics: correlation with the audit flags; test crack IoU and relF1@2. Kill: no enrichment of audited cells in the top decile, or crack IoU change under 0.012.
evidence: R (web summary of abstract): on coronary CT, transverse and oblique vessels had 5.1x higher error rates than axis-aligned ones; no multi-rater labels or network training needed; code stated but URL not verified.
prior_overlap: none for this mechanism. D16 / D17 cover label refinement and annotator style with other methods.

title: Few-Shot Concept Prompt Learning for Segmentation Foundation Models via Visual Grounding (FS-CPL)
mechanism: Learn a continuous concept-prompt embedding from K support image-mask pairs by mask supervision with SAM3 / Medical SAM3 frozen.
evidence: R: up to +0.62 Dice over text prompts on BUSI, HC18, TN3K, CVC-Clinic; backbone-agnostic.
adaptation: One learned prompt per EL class trained on all 478 cells (not K) turns frozen SAM3 into a cheap parametric labeller/second-opinion model for inactive and structural classes; gated weights need the user's OK.
min_experiment: Learned prompts on 478 train cells vs house PF on val54+F51; metrics inactive IoU, splice/gridline IoU, crack relF1@2; kill if below house PF on all and no decorrelated recovery of house misses (>10%).
prior_overlap: none; SAM3 prompt learning not tried.

title: From Denoising Training to Test-Time Adaptation: Enhancing Domain Generalization for Medical Image Segmentation (DeY-Net / DeTTA)
mechanism: A U-Net is trained with an auxiliary denoising decoder on the shared encoder; at test time the encoder is adapted per sample with the denoising loss.
adaptation: Add a 1-channel denoising decoder to U-Net++ during the 20k-step house training, with Gaussian plus EL-like shot noise. Then run 10-step denoising TTT per cell (test) or per module (E1) on the encoder only.
min_experiment: Arm: house + joint denoising decoder (5 seeds), with and without TTT. Baselines: the same model without TTT, and the house model. Metrics: E1 relF1@2 and inactive IoU, test clean-49 guard. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains < +0.02 or the aux head alone costs > 0.005 crack IoU.
evidence: R: domain-generalisation gains on liver segmentation benchmarks over the baseline (exact numbers not retrieved).
prior_overlap: Partial. DDeP (decoder denoising pretraining on the pool, then fine-tune) was n.d., but that discards the aux head. Joint training with test-time use of the aux loss was never run.

title: Micro-crack detection of multicrystalline solar cells featuring an improved anisotropic diffusion filter and image segmentation technique
venue: EURASIP Journal on Image and Video Processing
mechanism: Improved anisotropic diffusion smooths grain boundaries and dislocation texture while keeping crack edges in multicrystalline EL; then segmentation.
