evidence: R: classical micro-crack detection on multicrystalline EL cells (no deep baseline).
adaptation: Compute offline per cell and add the AD residual as channel 2, mainly for sp_multi cells. Also the classical non-learned baseline for the benchmark.
min_experiment: Arm: house + AD residual channel, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: test crack IoU on multi cells, relF1@2. Kill: < +0.012 crack IoU.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Offline AD-filtered residual as input channel 2, mainly for sp_multi cells; also the classical baseline in the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + AD residual channel, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: test crack IoU on sp_multi cells. Kill: < +0.012.

title: Screener: Self-supervised Pathology Segmentation in Medical CT Images
mechanism: Dense self-supervised features plus a density-based anomaly segmenter conditioned on learned masking-invariant dense features; the same pretraining also beats other SSL methods when fine-tuned supervised.
adaptation: One dense SSL run on the 159k pool gives (a) a dense-pretrained ResNet-34/ConvNeXt-T encoder for U-Net++ and (b) a label-free anomaly map; conditioning variable = cell layout/source embedding instead of position.
min_experiment: Arm dense SSL encoder + PF vs baseline PF and the MIM checkpoint, 5 seeds; metric CV crack IoU and inactive IoU; kill if crack gain < +0.012 and inactive < +0.02. About 60 GPU-h.
evidence: R: trained on > 30k unlabelled CT volumes; beats UVAS methods on four test sets (1,820 scans) and other SSL pretraining in supervised fine-tuning.
prior_overlap: Section 5 lists dense SSL objectives as not closed (MIM / DDeP only).

title: SegFix: Model-Agnostic Boundary Refinement for Segmentation
mechanism: Predict a boundary map and a direction map; replace each boundary pixel's label with that of an interior pixel along the predicted direction; applies to predictions or labels.
adaptation: Post-processing and label cleaning for blob/band classes (inactive, ribbons, border, frame_edge, edge_dark); not for 1 to 2 px cracks (no interior).
min_experiment: Arm: SegFix head trained once, applied to house predictions; baseline: house. Metric: mIoU_rob, inactive IoU. Kill if mIoU_rob gain < 0.01.
evidence: R: boundary quality gains on Cityscapes/ADE20K (known from paper; numbers not read here).
prior_overlap: none: refinement stages never tried (BRIEF).

title: Enhancing Semantic Segmentation with Continual Self-Supervised Pre-training (GLARE)
mechanism: Continual SSL for segmentation with patch-level local consistency and a regional consistency constraint, updating only lightweight adapters on a frozen SSL ViT.
adaptation: Alternative to ExPLoRA with a dense objective; regions from the structural classes (busbar, ribbon, padding, cell) predicted by the house model on pool cells.
min_experiment: Same protocol as ExPLoRA arm; kill if < +0.02 E1 relF1@2 over off-the-shelf DINOv3 in Dino U-Net.
evidence: R: consistent gains across several segmentation benchmarks in different domains with small overhead (abstract, no numbers retrieved).
prior_overlap: MIM/DDeP on ResNet-34 n.d.; dense continual SSL on a ViT foundation model is open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Regions from our structural classes (busbar / finger / cell); a cheap second choice after NeCo for a ViT arm.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: DINOv3 ViT-B VFM arm after GLARE on pool. Baseline: same arm without. Kill if E1 crack recall < +0.01.

title: Generalizable Cross-modality Medical Image Segmentation via Style Augmentation and Dual Normalization
mechanism: Separate BN for source-similar and source-dissimilar style augmentations; test-time style-distance selection of the BN path.
evidence: Outperforms DG methods on BraTS, cross-modality cardiac and abdominal (abstract).
adaptation: BN set A for label-safe augmentation, BN set B for GIN/BigAug-strong augmentation; route each cell by style distance.
min_experiment: PF+DN vs PF+GIN-IPA; E1 relF1@2; kill if < +0.02.
prior_overlap: Partial: separate BN used in SSL runs for another purpose; per-panel BN adaptation failed. Style-routed dual BN untested.

title: Normal Reference Attention and Defective Feature Perception Network for Surface Defect Detection (NDP-Net)
mechanism: Reference-based attention: features of a normal reference image repair the query's defective features; a multi-scale head segments the difference; built for textured surfaces.
adaptation: Reference-conditioned U-Net++: second input = a clean cell of the same source and layout (train) or same module (E1, if pool has it). Shared encoder, cross-attention at 1/8 and 1/16 from query to reference; decoder sees query and repaired features. Explicit 'normal here' for half-cut and scuff.
evidence: R: MVTec AD and DAGM textured defects, deployed in an industrial line; no thin-label evidence.
min_experiment: First verify E1 modules have pool cells. Arm: PF with reference branch; baseline: PF. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, CV crack IoU. Kill: E1 gain < +0.03 or CV crack IoU drop > 0.012.
prior_overlap: none

title: ShiftwiseConv: Small Convolutional Kernel with Large Kernel Effect
mechanism: Gets a large-kernel effect from multi-path shifted small kernels with sparse long-range dependencies; pure CNN that beats SLaK and UniRepLKNet.
adaptation: Use the ImageNet-pretrained SW backbone as the U-Net++ encoder with a 1-channel stem and PF fine-tune. Long sparse context may separate scuff streaks from cracks on E1 half-cut cells.
min_experiment: Arm: SW encoder U-Net++ PF, 3 then 5 seeds. Baseline: PF ResNet-34. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, test crack IoU, inactive IoU. Kill: both E1 relF1@2 and test crack IoU within noise after 3 seeds.
evidence: R: beats SLaK and UniRepLKNet in classification, segmentation and detection (ADE20K etc.; numbers not read).
prior_overlap: none. Only ResNet-34/50 encoders were tested.

title: A Transformer-Based Pavement Crack Segmentation Model with Local Perception and Auxiliary Convolution Layers
mechanism: Mask2Former plus a local perception module and auxiliary convolution layers to keep thin crack features that fade in the transformer path.
evidence: R: abstract only; numbers not retrieved (MDPI 403).
adaptation: Supports the full-res conv refinement head proposed for EoMT/M2F; local conv branch fed from the stem at full res for 1-2 px EL cracks.
min_experiment: Folded into the EoMT/M2F runs: refinement head on vs off; metric crack IoU and relF1@2; kill if gain < 0.012 crack IoU.
prior_overlap: none.

title: DINO-Mix: Distilling Foundational Knowledge with Cross-Domain CutMix for Semi-supervised Class-imbalanced Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: A frozen DINOv3 serves as an external, unbiased teacher for minority classes, which breaks the confirmation bias of inward-looking SSL. Progressive imbalance-aware CutMix forces attention to minority classes in labelled and unlabelled data.
adaptation: Minority classes = inactive, splice, gridline, edge_dark. Imbalance-aware CutMix pastes inactive regions, with their bordering cracks, into pool and train cells. DINOv3 feature similarity guides the rare classes.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + imbalance-aware CutMix + DINOv3 rare-class distillation, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: inactive IoU (clean 49, BMRK subset, E1), gridline and splice IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: inactive IoU < PF + 0.03 and mIoU_rob < PF + 0.01.
evidence: R: Synapse at 20% labels, 66.45 Dice vs 64.27 (SKCDF). AMOS at 5% labels, 62.73 vs 53.81. Low-label settings only.
prior_overlap: Partial. SKCDF-style heads were tested at 5% (worse or n.d.), and crack copy-paste onto pool cells was n.d. Inactive-focused CutMix with a DINOv3 teacher at 100% labels is untested.

title: Dual Super-Resolution Learning for Semantic Segmentation (DSRL)
mechanism: Segmentation super-resolution and single-image super-resolution streams share an encoder; a feature-affinity loss ties segmentation features to SR features.
adaptation: Label-free SR auxiliary: from 512 px input, reconstruct the native-res crop of pool cells (part is 1200 px) from decoder features with affinity on shared stride-2 features; unlabelled pool trains the SISR stream.
min_experiment: Arm: house PF + SISR aux on labelled + pool cells; baseline: house PF; CV crack relF1@2, E1 relF1@2. Kill if CV n.d. and E1 < +0.02.
evidence: R: >= 2% mIoU on Cityscapes at similar FLOPs; same mIoU at 70% FLOPs.
prior_overlap: Pool MIM and DDeP (reconstruction pretraining) were n.d.; a joint native-resolution SR auxiliary was not run, but shares the risk.

alt_notes.adaptation: Label-free SR auxiliary: reconstruct native-resolution crops (part of the pool is 1200 px) from decoder features, affinity weighted on a dilated crack + gridline band; unlabelled pool cells train the SR stream.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house PF + SR stream vs house PF; 5-fold CV crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2; kill: CV n.d. and E1 < +0.02. About 15 GPU-h.

title: MGDT: mask-guided spatial prior learning for photovoltaic fault diagnosis from infrared thermographic measurements
mechanism: An autoencoder trained on normal crops gives a reconstruction-residual anomaly mask, used as a spatial attention bias in a ViT and to weight a conditional diffusion model that synthesises minority-class samples.
evidence: R: on InfraredSolarModules, +2.53 accuracy, +3.66 macro-F1, +3.28 macro-recall, +2.97 macro-precision over the best baseline per metric.
adaptation: Train a conv AE (or patch-memory normal model) on the 11.9k unlabelled CSIR / ARTS pool; feed the residual map as a second input channel to U-Net++ (anomaly prior, never tried here); the diffusion half is a later, costlier step for inactive (42 train cells).
min_experiment: Arm PF with 2-channel input (EL + AE residual), 3 seeds; baseline PF; metrics test inactive IoU and E1 crack relR@2; kill if inactive IoU gain < 0.02 and E1 relR@2 gain < 0.03.
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF 5 lists anomaly-detection priors and diffusion synthesis as never tried.

title: Selective Masking based Self-Supervised Learning for Image Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Iterative masked reconstruction that masks the patches with highest reconstruction loss instead of random patches; helps the weakest classes most.
adaptation: Apply to the FCMAE or ridge-target arm: mask hardest-to-reconstruct EL patches (cracks, splices, gridline breaks, edges); targets weak classes gridline, splice, edge_dark as well as crack.
min_experiment: Winner arm with selective vs random masking; kill if out-of-fold relF1@2 < +0.005 and gridline/splice fold IoU < +0.02.
evidence: R: +2.9% (VOC, Cityscapes) and +2.5% (2 weed sets) over random masking and ImageNet; largest gains on lowest classes.
prior_overlap: none: our MIM used random masking.

title: Siamese network with change awareness for surface defect segmentation in complex backgrounds (CADNet)
mechanism: Formulate defect segmentation as change detection against a defect-free reference with a Siamese transformer encoder and a class-balanced contrastive loss; the distance map is skip-connected to the decoder.
adaptation: For E1: reference = defect-free pool cell retrieved by source / mono-multi / full-half-cut, or the median of other cells of the same module (E1 has module ids); feed feature distance map as extra decoder input so module-wide context cancels and cell-specific cracks remain.
evidence: R: beats semantic segmentation baselines on a synthetic LCD set and two public sets, also in semi-supervised settings (numbers not read).
min_experiment: Arm: PF + distance map to retrieved reference; baseline: PF; metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and half-cut false alarms; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03.
prior_overlap: none: reference-based inputs never tried; D39 covers normal-reference attention (NDP-Net) from the anomaly side.

title: Towards Robust Pseudo-Label Learning in Semantic Segmentation: An Encoding Perspective (ECOCSeg)
mechanism: Replace one-hot classes with error-correcting output codes and denoise labels bit by bit, so partly wrong pseudo-labels cost only some bits.
adaptation: Design bits shared across our 24 classes (dark defect, thin, structural, metal). A crack vs inactive confusion, where 20% of crack pixels sit in inactive regions, then costs one bit. Also usable with jittered GT in the supervised house model.
min_experiment: House PF with an ECOC head vs a one-hot head, 5 seeds. Metrics: crack IoU, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill if n.d.
evidence: R: plugs into existing UDA and SSL methods with gains across architectures; numbers not on the abstract page.
prior_overlap: Multi-label and structured heads are on the 'never tried' list. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Encode the 24 classes so related classes share bits (crack and inactive share a defect bit; busbar, ribbon and splice share a metallisation bit). This gives a multi-label-like head and a softer penalty for crack-versus-inactive confusion where the labels overlap.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with a 32-bit ECOC head, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: all three n.d.

title: Learning trustworthy model from noisy labels based on rough set for surface defect detection
mechanism: Treat label noise as inconsistency on suspicious regions (rough-set boundary region), redesign the loss on those pixels and add a pluggable spatially correlated Bayesian module giving a defect-discrimination confidence.
adaptation: Define the boundary region as the 1-2 px ring around crack labels plus faint crack segments (7% are < 2% darker), apply the boundary loss there; use the confidence output for the benchmark's uncertainty column.
evidence: R: abstract claims effectiveness, robustness, real-time; numbers unverified (full text not read).
min_experiment: Arm: house with rough-set boundary loss on the ring + faint segments; baseline: house; metric: CV crack IoU and relF1@2; kill if IoU gain < +0.01. Read full text first.
prior_overlap: Partial: offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) is related; Bayesian confidence module untested.

title: Rethinking Dual-Stream Super-Resolution Semantic Learning in Medical Image Segmentation (DS2F)
mechanism: Shows DSRL feature affinity is too weak for small-proportion targets; adds a shared-feature module and a target-focused proxy loss.
adaptation: Use as the DSRL variant for 0.19% crack pixels: weight SR/affinity on a dilated crack + gridline band only.
min_experiment: Second arm of the DSRL experiment; same baseline, metric and kill.
evidence: R: six public medical datasets in three scenarios; numbers not retrieved.
prior_overlap: Same as DSRL.

title: GaborNet: Gabor filters with learnable parameters in deep convolutional neural networks
mechanism: First-layer convolution filters constrained to Gabor functions whose parameters are learned by backpropagation.
adaptation: A parallel stem of 16 learnable Gabor filters (8 orientations x 2 scales, wavelength 4 to 8 px) on the 1-channel EL input, concatenated to the conv1 output.
min_experiment: Arm: house + Gabor stem, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012.
evidence: R: faster convergence and better accuracy than plain CNNs on several recognition datasets (abstract).
prior_overlap: none

title: Structure-Aware Image Segmentation with Homotopy Warping
mechanism: Warp the prediction homotopically toward the label and penalise only the critical pixels whose flip changes topology.
adaptation: A jittered but topologically equal prediction adds no extra loss, which fits our labels. Crack class only. CPU warping cost over 20k steps needs a profile first.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + warping loss (crack), 3 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metric: component recall and crack IoU. Kill if no component recall gain >= 0.02.
evidence: R (TopoMortar): CrackTree Dice 0.77 vs 0.78 CEDice. beta0 46 vs 52 under Adele, no gain in supervised training.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: A jittered but topologically equal crack prediction gets no extra loss, which suits our labels; apply to crack with CE + Dice. CPU warping per batch is the cost concern at 20k steps.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + warping loss vs PF, 5 seeds. Kill if relF1@2 gain < 0.01.

title: A new family of instance-level loss functions for improving instance-level segmentation and detection of white matter hyperintensities in routine clinical brain MRI
mechanism: Instance losses: instance segmentation, instance centre, false/missed instance rate, and proximity loss pulling predicted instances to GT instances.
adaptation: Use L_false (soft count of missed + false crack instances) and L_proximity (tolerates 1-2 px offsets) on merged crack instances.
min_experiment: Arm: house + L_false + L_proximity, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: component F1, relF1@2. Kill: no component F1 gain >= 0.02.
evidence: ADNI and WMH challenge: ensemble of two instance losses beats pixel losses on instance metrics; also helps nuclei segmentation.
prior_overlap: none

title: EfficientAD: Accurate Visual Anomaly Detection at Millisecond-Level Latencies
mechanism: Small patch description network teacher, student with hard-feature loss, plus a global autoencoder for logical anomalies; 2 ms per image.
adaptation: Benchmark baseline trained per source on clean pool cells at 512 px; PDN receptive field 33 px is near crack scale. Autoencoder branch can flag layout anomalies (missing busbar, splice) the house model never predicts (splice IoU 0.000).
evidence: R: 32 datasets from three AD collections, SOTA detection and localization at 600 img/s.
min_experiment: Benchmark row: train once, report AD metrics and splice / crack / inactive relF1@2. Optional: splice recall of AE branch on CV; kill if < 0.2 at 1% area.
prior_overlap: none

title: DRAEM: A discriminatively trained reconstruction embedding for surface anomaly detection
mechanism: Perlin-noise masks blend outside textures (DTD) into normal images. A reconstruction network plus a discriminative network is trained to segment these synthetic anomalies.
evidence: Beat prior unsupervised methods on MVTec AD by a large margin. On DAGM its localisation beats fully supervised methods (abstract). The repo is MIT-licensed and uses DTD as the anomaly source.
adaptation: For the benchmark, run it as the 'no defect labels' baseline: train on crack-free train cells, then score crack and inactive AP and relF1@2 on test and E1. For scores, replace DTD textures with dark-line and dark-blob primitives; this is a long shot.
min_experiment: DRAEM trained on crack-free train cells. Report crack and inactive AP and relF1@2 on test and E1. No kill line (benchmark baseline). Score arm: PF + DRAEM map as a second input channel vs PF, kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark no-defect-label baseline trained on crack-free train cells; for scores, swap DTD textures for dark-line and dark-blob primitives.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark run: crack / inactive AP and relF1@2 on test and E1; no kill.

title: Efficient Betti Matching Enables Topology-Aware 3D Segmentation via Persistent Homology
mechanism: Persistent-homology loss with spatially induced matching between predicted and label barcodes (Betti matching, arxiv:2211.15272), in a fast C++ implementation.
adaptation: Crack class, components only, on label components >= 20 px. Weight 1e-5 to 1e-2 chosen on val (TRACE paper notes larger weights drop Dice).
min_experiment: PF + Betti matching vs PF, 5 seeds. Kill if component recall gain < 0.02 or crack IoU < PF - 0.012.
evidence: R (abstract): large speed-up over Cubical Ripser; improved topological correctness on several datasets. R (TRACE tables): Betti matching weaker than TRACE on DeepCrack.
prior_overlap: none.

title: Segment Anything Model for Road Network Graph Extraction
mechanism: Fine-tuned SAM encoder predicts vertex and intersection masks, NMS gives vertices, a small transformer predicts edges, giving a vector graph.
adaptation: Severity, not IoU: a crack graph per cell gives crack mode (single line, dendritic, cross) and length; benchmark severity track.
min_experiment: Arm = SAM-Road style graph head on crack; baseline = skeletonised PF prediction; metric graph APLS / crack-mode accuracy vs label skeleton graph on CV. Kill if not better than skeletonised PF.
evidence: R: comparable to RNGDet++ on City-scale, 40x faster.
prior_overlap: None.

alt_notes.adaptation: Severity track only: crack graph per cell gives crack mode (single line, cross, dendritic), length and branch count; train on skeleton graphs from crack labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Graph extraction on CV folds; metric crack-mode agreement with labels-derived graphs; no score kill line (severity feature).

title: Self-supervised Pretraining of Cell Segmentation Models (DINOCell)
mechanism: Continue DINOv2 ViT-B self-distillation (DINO + iBOT) on 130k domain images with patch size cut from 14 to 8, then a light upsampling decoder.
adaptation: Patch 8 at 512 px gives 64x64 tokens, closer to crack scale; continue DINOv2 ViT-B/8 on the de-duplicated 11.9k pool, 30 epochs at 448; judge on E1 and folds.
min_experiment: Arm: continued ViT-B/8. Baseline: ViT-B/8 from DINOv2 without continuation, same decoder. Kill if E1 crack recall < +0.02.
evidence: R: LIVECell SEG 0.784, +10.42% over SAM-based models; but continued domain SSL changed little vs DINOv2 init (+6.48% on 1 of 4 sets); ~100 h on 8 L40S.
prior_overlap: None.

alt_notes.adaptation: Patch 8 at 512 px gives 64x64 tokens; continue on the de-duplicated pool; judge on E1 and folds.
alt_notes.min_experiment: ViT-B/8 continued on 11.9k vs without continuation; kill if E1 crack recall < +0.02. Only if NeCo or MedDINOv3 shows a sign.

title: Automatic Data Curation for Self-Supervised Learning: A Clustering-Based Approach
mechanism: Hierarchical k-means on embeddings plus balanced sampling across clusters yields better SSL features than uncurated pools.
adaptation: Our pool is 84% ARTS mono 5-busbar; embed cells, cluster, sample a balanced 30-50k subset across mono / multi / half-cell, CSIR / ARTS, dark-streak cells after de-duplication against test / val / E1.
min_experiment: Winning pretraining arm on curated 30k vs random 30k; same fine-tune; kill if n.d. on out-of-fold relF1@2 and E1 recall.
evidence: R: curated beats uncurated and matches manual curation on web, satellite and text data.
prior_overlap: None.

alt_notes.adaptation: Cluster embeddings of the de-duplicated 159k pool (84% ARTS mono 5-busbar) and draw a balanced 30 to 50k subset over mono/multi/half-cell, CSIR/ARTS and dark-streak cells.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Winning pretraining arm on curated 30k vs random 30k; kill if n.d. on out-of-fold relF1@2 and E1 recall.

title: Automated Defect Detection and Localization in Photovoltaic Cells Using Semantic Segmentation of Electroluminescence Images
mechanism: UCF-EL: large polygon-mask EL dataset (crack region, contact, interconnect, corrosion) with a U-Net baseline.
adaptation: Joint training: shared U-Net++ with a second 1x1 head for UCF-EL classes, loss only on each dataset's own labels, alternating batches; keeps UCF knowledge instead of the pretrain-then-erase run.
min_experiment: Arm joint training vs house, 5 seeds; crack IoU, E1 crack recall; kill if both within noise.
evidence: R: crack recall 0.82 and gridline/contact recall 0.78 (as quoted by Pratt 2023); heavy train/test leakage (BRIEF E).
prior_overlap: UCF-EL encoder pretraining with house fine-tune (erased) was n.d./worse; joint training never tried. Open.

title: Centerline Boundary Dice Loss for Vascular Segmentation (cbDice)
mechanism: clDice extended with boundary and radius-normalised skeleton terms to balance thin and thick branches.
adaptation: Crack radius is about 1 px, so on crack cbDice is close to clDice (which failed here). The only distinct use is multi-class balancing of thick inactive / ribbons against thin crack / gridline (beta 0.5 to 1 for 2D).
min_experiment: Arm: PF + cbDice over crack, gridline and inactive, 3 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: gridline and inactive IoU. Kill if neither gains 0.02.
evidence: R (full text): DRIVE 2D Dice 82.5 (best), gains under 1 point over clDice. TopCoW small-artery Dice 43.4 vs 38.5 for clDice. R (TopoMortar): CrackTree Dice 0.76, no topology gain over CEDice.
prior_overlap: Close to soft clDice (failed, same conditions) on the crack class. Untested for multi-class width balance.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack radius is about 1 px everywhere, so on crack cbDice reduces to near clDice, which failed here. Only possible use is multi-class balance between thick (inactive, ribbons) and thin (crack, gridline) classes. Belongs in the benchmark suite as a standard baseline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark baseline only: PF + cbDice on crack and gridline, 5 seeds; kill if crack IoU < PF - 0.012.

title: SegRefiner: Towards Model-Agnostic Segmentation Refinement with Discrete Diffusion Process
mechanism: Discrete diffusion over per-pixel coarse/fine states: a U-Net on image + current mask predicts the fine mask and confidence, and pixels transition coarse -> fine over T = 6 steps; trained on GT degraded by morphological perturbation.
adaptation: Fine-tune the HR model on our inactive regions and per-crack crops (1-channel EL repeated to 3); training masks from out-of-fold predictions plus morphological perturbation. Expect n.d. on cracks given the DRIVE result; mainly an inactive and benchmark baseline.
min_experiment: Arm: fine-tuned SegRefiner on house ensemble masks. Baseline: house ensemble. Metrics: inactive IoU, crack IoU on 5-fold CV. Kill: < +0.01 on both.
evidence: R: gains on BIG (semantic), COCO / LVIS (instance, APmk 47.4 reported), DIS5K; trained on LVIS then DIS5K + ThinObject-5K at 256 px. R (rNCA Table 1): on DRIVE thin vessels Dice 0.761 -> 0.760.
prior_overlap: none on our data; the DRIVE comparison in rNCA is the closest negative evidence.

alt_notes.adaptation: Retrain from scratch on OOF house predictions (not synthetic morphology), 512 native, 1-ch EL + coarse mask, separate crack and inactive refiners. Expected near null on cracks given the DRIVE result; included mainly as the standard refiner baseline for the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: SegRefiner on house ensemble. Baseline: house ensemble. Metrics: relR@2 at fixed relP@2, crack and inactive IoU. Kill: relR@2 < +0.01 and inactive IoU < +0.02.

title: Prototypical Residual Networks for Anomaly Detection and Localization (PRN)
mechanism: Multi-scale residual prototypes between anomalous and normal features plus multi-size self-attention, trained with a few real anomalies and generated seen / unseen-style anomalies.
adaptation: Supervised-AD benchmark row: 478 labelled cells as seen anomalies, binary defect target; port its anomaly generators to EL dark lines and blobs. Overlaps the WeakREST arm; run only if that arm works.
evidence: R: beats unsupervised and supervised methods on MVTec AD plus 3 more datasets.
min_experiment: Benchmark row; if used as a member, same kill as DeSTSeg (relR@2 gain < +0.02).
prior_overlap: none

title: DinoDental: Benchmarking DINOv3 as a Unified Vision Encoder for Dental Image Analysis
mechanism: Benchmark of DINOv3 as a frozen or tuned encoder on greyscale dental images with scarce labels.
adaptation: Greyscale, low-label transfer evidence; use its frozen vs tuned results to set how deep VFM-H tunes.
min_experiment: No own arm: read results, then fix VFM-H tuning depth (frozen + PEFT vs last-k blocks tuned).
evidence: R: abstract fragment only.
prior_overlap: none.

title: Structure-Aware Photovoltaic EL Anomaly Detection with Frozen DINOv2
mechanism: Frozen DINOv2 ViT-S/14 with per-patch-position prototypes of normal cells gives a structure-aware anomaly map.
adaptation: Fit position-conditioned prototypes per cell type (full, half-cut) on pool cells; use the anomaly map as an auxiliary channel or to gate low crack probabilities. Its transfer failure motivates an unseen-source test in the benchmark.
min_experiment: No training. Metric: crack pixel AUROC on F51/H36 val v house p(crack). Kill if lower than the house model.
evidence: R: AUROC 0.888, AP 0.925 on deduplicated PVEL-AD (5,143 test images) v PaDiM 0.796, PatchCore 0.791; calibration transfer to ELPV collapsed to AUROC 0.500.
prior_overlap: Frozen DINOv2-S linear probes for segmentation showed no gain; prototype anomaly scoring was not tested.

title: BerDiff: Conditional Bernoulli Diffusion Model for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Conditional diffusion with Bernoulli noise instead of Gaussian for binary masks; multiple samples give diverse plausible masks and an uncertainty view.
evidence: R: beats recent SOTA on two medical datasets of different modalities (abstract, no numbers on page).
adaptation: Base diffusion process for the UMBD arm, or a standalone crack-binary refiner conditioned on [EL, house p(crack)]; average several samples as a cheap ensemble, which may suit jittered 1 to 2 px labels.
min_experiment: Arm: BerDiff refiner on crack channel, 5 samples averaged. Baseline: house ensemble. Metric: relF1@2, crack IoU. Kill: relF1@2 < +0.01.
prior_overlap: none

title: WILDS: A Benchmark of in-the-Wild Distribution Shifts
mechanism: Splits defined by groups (hospital, camera, region). ID and OOD scores are reported separately through a standard loader and evaluator; ERM remains a strong baseline.
adaptation: Groups = module and source. Splits: ID test (seen modules), OOD-module test (E1, half-cut, scuffs), and leave-one-source-out (BMRK, SDLE). Report the worst-source score. The 11.9k/159k pool plays the role of WILDS-unlabeled (arXiv:2112.05090).
min_experiment: Re-score existing house and PF checkpoints per source and on E1. Decision: if the source-wise ranking of house vs PF differs from the pooled ranking, the worst-source score enters the headline.
prior_overlap: Partial: E1 already acts as an OOD split. Leave-one-source-out and worst-group reporting are new.
evidence: R: 10 datasets; standard training gives clearly lower OOD than ID performance on each, and existing shift methods do not close the gap.

title: Advancing automatic photovoltaic defect detection using semi-supervised semantic segmentation of electroluminescence images (PV-S3)
mechanism: Semi-supervised segmentation with a Semi Cross-Entropy loss for class imbalance.
adaptation: Run official code under our split and protocol as a benchmark baseline; test the Semi-CE loss alone inside the house model.
min_experiment: Arm: house + Semi-CE loss. Baseline: house, 5 seeds. Metric: crack and inactive IoU. Kill if both < +0.012. Separately run PV-S3 as a benchmark entry.
evidence: R: with 20% labels, +9.7 mIoU, +13.5 precision, +29.15 recall over a fully supervised SOTA on UCF-EL.
prior_overlap: SSL at 100% labels closed (n.d.); Semi-CE loss alone untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Run only as a benchmark baseline under the fixed protocol; mean teacher at 100% labels is closed for raising scores.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark run: PV-S3 code on our splits, 3 seeds, all benchmark metrics; no kill line (reference baseline).

alt_notes.adaptation: For scores, nothing new: it is the SemiCE Mean Teacher line already run here. For the benchmark, run it under our protocol (clean splits, relF1@2, E1) as the only published EL SSL baseline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark entry only: PV-S3 code on our 478-cell split + pool, 3 seeds, reported with house and PF.

title: From Claims to Evidence: A Unified Framework and Critical Analysis of CNN vs. Transformer vs. Mamba in Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: nnUZoo: one nnU-Net harness into which CNN, Transformer and Mamba networks are plugged, so only the network changes between rows; Wilcoxon tests.
adaptation: Use as the code template for the EL benchmark harness: one data folder, one augmentation (label-safe), one schedule, our folds and metrics; swap only networks (nnU-Net, ResEnc-L, MedNeXt, U-Mamba, Swin-UMamba, TransUNet, house U-Net++).
min_experiment: Harness check: reproduce house U-Net++ R34 inside the harness within 0.01 CV crack relF1@2 of the house trainer before adding other networks.
evidence: R: six datasets (microscopy, ultrasound, CT, MRI, PET); CNNs (nnU-Net, U2Net) fast and accurate; SS2D2Net ties nnU-Net with fewer params but longer training; Transformers costly.
prior_overlap: none

title: Towards Total Recall in Industrial Anomaly Detection (PatchCore)
mechanism: Coreset memory bank of mid-level patch features; nearest-neighbour distance is the anomaly score.
adaptation: Canonical AD row of the benchmark and the bank builder for the WeakREST residual arm; banks per source x layout from clean pool cells; report crack and inactive relF1@2 to show the gap to supervised.
evidence: R: MVTec AD image AUROC up to 99.6 (widely reported; 1996 citations).
min_experiment: Benchmark row, one run per source; no kill line.
prior_overlap: none

title: GP-VMxSMA: Benchmarking General-Purpose Vision Models and Specialized Architectures for 2D Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Controlled 2D comparison of general-purpose models (SegFormer-B3, SegNeXt-L, VWFormer, InternImage-T, TransNeXt-T with UPerHead) against medical architectures (U-Net, HiFormer, MISSFormer, Swin-UMamba, CENet), with a per-model LR sweep, 5-fold CV, and linear mixed-effects models for significance.
adaptation: Benchmark protocol for EL: an LR sweep per model on val, 5 module-grouped folds, and a mixed-effects model with model as a fixed effect and fold, source and cell as random effects (handles the 5 sources). Add one SegFormer or UPerNet-ConvNeXt arm as the natural-image reference.
min_experiment: Within the benchmark run, fit the mixed-effects model on per-cell crack relF1@2 for all suite methods and report the family and method effects with CIs against the house model. No kill line (protocol item).
evidence: R: on ISIC18, NeoPolyp and CAMUS, DSC estimates were tightly clustered; SegFormer mean DSC 90.7%; the family effect was significant but tiny (d = 0.04).
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Copy the mixed-effects analysis for our benchmark: fixed effect method, random effects fold, seed and source; addresses problem 5 (50-cell test noise).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Analysis only on existing and new CV results; no training.

title: How to Benchmark Vision Foundation Models for Semantic Segmentation?
mechanism: Benchmark protocol study: ViT-B, patch 16, linear decoder ranks VFMs like costlier settings; linear probing does not predict fine-tune ranking; rankings shift across datasets and domain shifts.
evidence: R (abstract): settings cut training time over 13x with representative rankings; promptable-segmentation pretraining not beneficial, MIM with abstract targets important.
adaptation: Use to (a) argue our frozen linear-probe nulls do not close fine-tune or PEFT arms, and (b) define the VFM part of the EL benchmark protocol, testing whether a linear decoder is representative for 1-2 px cracks.
min_experiment: Rank 3 VFMs with ViT-B linear-decoder fine-tune and with VFM-H; check rank agreement on CV crack relF1@2; no kill, protocol check.
prior_overlap: Not a method; informs reading of the closed probe row.

title: LUMA: Benchmarking Segmentation via a Lightweight Universal Mask Adapter
mechanism: One fixed lightweight mask-transformer head attached to any backbone (ViT, hierarchical, conv, MoE) so backbones and pretrainings can be compared under one recipe.
adaptation: Benchmark design: hold one mask head fixed and swap encoders (ResNet-34 ImageNet, ConvNeXt-T, DINOv2/DINOv3 ViT) to separate encoder from decoder effects; also a cheap way to put a mask head on the house ResNet-34.
min_experiment: LUMA head on house ResNet-34 vs house U-Net++ decoder, 5-fold; metric inactive IoU and mIoU_rob; kill if both below house by > 0.01.
evidence: R: matches EoMT at cost parity; 20 backbones, 11 pretraining schemes on ADE20K/COCO/Cityscapes; pretraining objective, not architecture, governs quality; plain ViT holds throughput Pareto front. Code stated github.com/tobna/LUMA (not opened).
prior_overlap: none

title: VM-UNet: Vision Mamba UNet for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Pure visual-state-space (Mamba) asymmetric U-Net with ImageNet-pretrained VMamba weights, built for 2D.
adaptation: 1-channel stem, 512 px, PF fine-tune. Include as the pure-SSM family member of the EL benchmark suite.
min_experiment: One run per fold in the shared benchmark protocol; compared with the house model on test-49 crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2. Kill: below house on both, then keep only as a suite baseline.
evidence: R: DSC 89.03 ISIC17, 89.71 ISIC18, 81.08 Synapse. U-Bench reports the Mamba family as weaker on fine detail.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Suite member; gray to 3 channels, 512 px, PF schedule. Patch-4 stem likely loses 1-2 px crack detail.
alt_notes.min_experiment: VM-UNet 5 folds v house PF; benchmark row; kill for score if CV crack relF1@2 < +0.01.

title: Conformal Segmentation in Industrial Surface Defect Detection with Statistical Guarantees
mechanism: Conformal risk control on a calibration split sets a pixel threshold so the expected test error rate (e.g. missed defect fraction) is bounded by a chosen risk level.
adaptation: Benchmark operating point: calibrate crack threshold on val + F51 for expected relR@2 >= 0.90 and report the precision it costs; same for inactive area fraction (severity); test whether the guarantee holds on E1 under shift.
evidence: R: Mask R-CNN on industrial defects, test error stays under the risk level across calibration/test ratios.
min_experiment: No training: calibrate on val + F51, report realised relR@2 and precision on clean-49 test and E1; kill (as a method) if realised E1 recall falls below target by > 0.1, which is itself a benchmark finding.
prior_overlap: Logit bias and per-module thresholds were tried (threshold choice); conformal guarantee is new and aimed at the benchmark, not the score.

title: Cross-Validation: What Does It Estimate and How Well Does It Do It?
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
mechanism: Naive CV CIs under-cover because fold errors are correlated; nested CV estimates the variance with near-nominal coverage.
adaptation: Use as a correction factor for naive SEs of grouped-CV deltas; full nested CV too costly for deep nets.
min_experiment: Arm: compare naive CV SE with spread of deltas across 2 groupings. Kill: ratio < 1.2 means no correction.
evidence: R: theory and simulations on linear models show naive CV intervals under-cover.
prior_overlap: none

title: Cracks in the Foundation: A Civil Infrastructure Dataset to Challenge Vision Foundation Models
mechanism: 150k-tile infrastructure defect benchmark comparing EoMT (DINOv2/DINOv3), Mask DINO, YOLO and RF-DETR under one protocol.
adaptation: Evidence that VFM mask classifiers do not fix thin-crack masks alone: keep a per-pixel crack head; in our benchmark report crack with tolerant metrics (relF1@2) beside strict IoU.
min_experiment: No separate run; its finding is tested by the EoMT arm's crack IoU vs relF1@2 gap compared with the house model.
evidence: R: tiled 1024: EoMT DINOv3 mask mAP 24.2 overall (best), crack mask mAP 4.7 (DINOv3) / 5.0 (DINOv2) vs YOLOv11-xl 8.6; authors: mask mAP plunges to single digits for cracks. Data on HF ibm-research/cif-dataset.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: add zero-shot FM rows, test centre bias (crack position within cell), possibly use as extra crack pretraining data (different modality).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark-only: report zero-shot SAM3 / SAM2 rows and a centre-bias analysis; no training needed.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark lesson: report zero-shot and in-context FM rows beside supervised rows with tolerant crack metrics; possible crack-shape pretraining data (HF ibm-research/cif-dataset), overlaps D36.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No score experiment; include FM zero-shot/in-context rows in the benchmark table.

title: Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation Meets SAM3
mechanism: Frozen SAM3 promptable concept segmentation with support and query placed side by side on one canvas and the support mask as exemplar; no training.
evidence: R: SOTA on PASCAL-5i and COCO-20i training-free; negative prompts often cause prediction collapse.
adaptation: Two 512 px cells on SAM3's 1008 px canvas (near native size); positive exemplars only; inactive and structural classes as main target; needs the user's OK for gated SAM3 weights.
min_experiment: In G0 after weights OK: FSS-SAM3 canvas vs house PF ensemble on val54+F51+H36, inactive IoU and crack relF1@2; kill if below house PF on both and below GFDS SAM2 mode.
prior_overlap: none; SAM3 never run here (D14 proposes a zero-shot text-prompt probe, different mechanism).

title: Does DINOv3 Set a New Medical Vision Standard? Benchmarking 2D and 3D Classification, Segmentation, and Registration
mechanism: Evidence paper: DINOv3 transfer across medical classification, segmentation and registration.
adaptation: Caution for VFM-H: per D14's reading, DINOv3 did not follow scaling laws in several non-natural modalities. Size (ViT-B vs ViT-L) must be measured on CV, not assumed.
min_experiment: Within the DINOv3 arm: ViT-B/16 vs ViT-L/16 on CV crack relF1@2; drop to ViT-B if L is not +0.01.
evidence: R: 47 citations; abstract fragment only.
prior_overlap: none.

title: Label Noise in Segmentation Networks: Mitigation Must Deal with Bias
mechanism: Evidence paper: segmentation nets are robust to unbiased label errors (random warp, crop) but sensitive to biased errors (constant shift), so mitigation must target bias.
adaptation: Not an arm. Frames which part of our crack IoU loss is recoverable: per-source width and any per-source constant offset (biased) vs within-source jitter (unbiased). Motivates the zero-GPU per-source offset / width diagnostics and a benchmark report of biased-error sensitivity.
min_experiment: Zero-GPU: per-source mean signed offset of label skeleton to ridge (x, y) and label width on train labels; plus per-source predicted width on CV OOF. Decision rule: proceed with style arms only if a source deviates by > 0.3 px in offset or > 0.15 px in width between prediction and label.
evidence: R: BraTS-type tumour masks; constant 5 px shift cost about 10% Dice for supervised, MT and AE models; random warps barely hurt.
prior_overlap: none

title: Mask DINO: Towards A Unified Transformer-based Framework for Object Detection and Segmentation
mechanism: DINO detector with denoising queries plus a mask branch from a high-resolution pixel embedding; unified detection and segmentation.
evidence: R: 54.5 AP COCO instance, 59.4 PQ panoptic, 60.8 mIoU ADE20K.
adaptation: Benchmark entry in semantic mode; query denoising may help few-data convergence; same 1/4-res limit for crack; could use inactive regions and crack components as instances.
min_experiment: Single benchmark run under the fixed protocol, 5-fold CV; compare with M2F; no score kill line unless it beats M2F on inactive IoU by > 0.02.
prior_overlap: none.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark entry; query denoising may help 478-image convergence; inactive as instances gives an instance-AP view.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Run once under the fixed benchmark protocol (5-fold, 1 seed per fold) vs house; no kill line, baseline only.

title: Quantifying the Limits of Segmentation Foundation Models: Modeling Challenges in Segmenting Tree-Like and Low-Contrast Objects
mechanism: Interpretable tree-likeness and textural-separability metrics predict SAM / SAM2 / HQ-SAM failures; targeted fine-tuning did not remove the failure.
adaptation: Compute both metrics per crack component on val (7% of crack components are < 2% darker than surroundings); stratify FM-arm vs house errors; define benchmark strata by contrast.
min_experiment: CPU-only: per-tercile relR@2 for house vs best FM arm on val; report, no kill needed (analysis tool).
evidence: R: synthetic controlled experiments plus real datasets; correlation of SFM performance with both metrics.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Compute both metrics per crack component on test and E1 and stratify benchmark results (7% of crack components are < 2% darker than surroundings).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Analysis only: stratified recall by separability bin for house vs FM arms.

title: Segmentation of photovoltaic module cells in uncalibrated electroluminescence images
mechanism: Ridge detection of busbars and cell borders, lens distortion and perspective correction to segment cells from uncalibrated module EL images.
evidence: R: robust cell segmentation on uncalibrated EL modules (widely used, 145 citations).
adaptation: Score side: busbar / border ridge map or half-cut cut-line location as a layout channel for E1. Benchmark side: documented cell extraction for the 159k pool and new modules.
min_experiment: Arm: house + layout ridge channel, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: E1 crack precision in half-cut cells. Kill: < +0.03 relF1@2 on E1.
prior_overlap: partial: synthetic half-cut views were n.d.; an explicit layout channel was not tested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Busbar / border ridge map as a layout channel or to locate the cut line in E1 half-cut cells; documented cell extraction for the 159k pool and new module images in the benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + ridge layout channel, 3-seed screen. Baseline: house. Metric: E1 crack false positives along cut line and relF1@2. Kill: < +0.02 E1 relF1@2.

title: CascadePSP: Toward Class-Agnostic and Very High-Resolution Segmentation via Global and Local Refinement
mechanism: A class-agnostic cascade refiner trained on perturbed masks that refines a mask globally and then locally, at any resolution.
adaptation: Inference-only test on inactive masks with the pretrained refiner (EL repeated to 3 channels); fine-tune on perturbed inactive GT if the zero-shot test is not negative.
min_experiment: Arm: CascadePSP on house / PF inactive masks. Baseline: unrefined. Metric: inactive IoU on 5-fold CV and E1. Kill: < +0.01 inactive IoU.
evidence: R: improved IoU and boundary accuracy on the BIG high-resolution set and PASCAL refinement benchmarks (numbers not read).
prior_overlap: none.

alt_notes.adaptation: Our cells are 512 px native and U-Net++ already predicts at full resolution, so its main benefit is absent; retrain on OOF masks per class only as a benchmark refinement baseline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: CascadePSP retrained on OOF crack / inactive masks. Baseline: house ensemble. Metric: relF1@2, inactive IoU. Kill: no gain > +0.01 relF1@2 and +0.02 inactive IoU.

title: Photovoltaic Defect Image Generator With Boundary Alignment Smoothing Constraint for Domain Shift Mitigation (PDIG)
mechanism: Stable Diffusion with a semantic concept embedding, a lightweight industrial style adaptor via cross-disentangled attention, and text-image dual-space constraints that place defects in given boxes.
adaptation: Box-level only; use as EL evidence that synthesis helps under a time/domain shift and as an EL generator baseline; boxes could seed crack masks only via a separate mask model.
min_experiment: No score experiment proposed; cite in the benchmark and, if code appears, run as a baseline generator for inactive at matched count vs row 2 on CV inactive IoU.
evidence: R: FID 20.90 average over 5 EL defect types vs 40.06 StyleGAN3; 200 generated images per type raised YOLOv5 mAP by 5.8 and 6.3 points on time-shifted EL group2 and group3 (ELES dataset, 16,323 images); YOLOv8 +1.8.
prior_overlap: None.

title: Continual-MAE: Adaptive Distribution Masked Autoencoders for Continual Test-Time Adaptation
mechanism: Distribution-aware masking of uncertain tokens. Predictions on masked and unmasked target views must agree, and HOG features are reconstructed at masked positions.
adaptation: Mask 16 px patches where crack or inactive uncertainty is highest. Require consistency with the unmasked prediction, and reconstruct HOG of the 1-channel EL patch through a light head on the ResNet-34 encoder (trained jointly). Adapt per E1 module.
min_experiment: Arm: house/PF + joint HOG head (5 seeds), then masked-consistency TTA per E1 module. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains < +0.02, or test crack IoU or mIoU_rob drops > 0.005.
evidence: R: state of the art on four classification and segmentation CTTA benchmarks (numbers not retrieved).
prior_overlap: Partial. MIM pretraining on the 11.9k pool was n.d., but that was pretraining followed by fine-tuning, not test-time masked consistency on target cells.

title: DGInStyle: Domain-Generalizable Semantic Segmentation with Image Diffusion Models and Stylized Semantic Control
mechanism: Style Swap (train semantic ControlNet on a source-tuned diffusion model, then swap in the general model) plus multi-resolution latent fusion, to render diverse images from source masks.
evidence: Raises several DG methods; 57.8 avg mIoU GTAV to Cityscapes/BDD/Mapillary in the Rein++ table.
adaptation: Train ControlNet on an EL-tuned diffusion model, swap to a pool-tuned model to render half-cut and scuffed styles from train masks. Overlaps D06.
min_experiment: PF + rendered set vs PF; E1 relF1@2. Kill: < +0.03.
prior_overlap: None; generative synthesis untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Fine-tune SD/ControlNet on 478 labelled + pool EL cells; multi-resolution fusion is needed for thin cracks; generate half-cut and scuff variants from edited masks. Likely shared with the generative-data direction.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Only after the CrackSegFlow-style arm shows synthetic half-cuts help: PF + DGInStyle data vs PF, 3 seeds; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03.

title: Generate Aligned Anomaly: Region-Guided Few-Shot Anomaly Image-Mask Pair Synthesis for Industrial Inspection (GAA)
mechanism: Few-shot latent-diffusion anomaly generation with localized concept decomposition, multi-round anomaly clustering, region-guided mask generation and low-quality sample filtering.
adaptation: Per-class few-shot generation for splice (never predicted), corrosion and material on train cells; clustering step can give one concept per source style; benchmark baseline next to AnomalyDiffusion and SeaS (D06).
min_experiment: Benchmark baseline: PF + GAA samples for splice/corrosion/material vs PF. Metric splice IoU (now 0.000) and mIoU_rob. Reported; drop if splice stays 0.
evidence: R: MVTec AD and LOCO; better synthesis quality and downstream localisation and classification than prior generators.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Per-class few-shot generation for splice, corrosion, material; one concept per source style.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + GAA pairs for rare classes vs PF. Metric splice IoU (now 0.000), material IoU; benchmark baseline. About 20 GPU-h.

title: JoDiffusion: Jointly Diffusing Image with Pixel-Level Annotations for Semantic Segmentation Promotion
mechanism: An annotation VAE maps masks into the image latent space and one latent diffusion model generates image and mask jointly, with a mask-optimisation step to reduce annotation noise.
adaptation: Replace text prompts with source + class-presence tokens; annotation VAE over 24 classes; 64x64 latent loses cracks, so use for other classes and inactive; recent joint baseline for the benchmark synthetic track.
min_experiment: Benchmark baseline: PF + JoDiffusion pairs vs PF. Metric mIoU_rob and per-class IoU of gridline/splice/edge_dark. Reported, no kill; drop if mIoU_rob < +0.005.
evidence: R: Pascal VOC, COCO, ADE20K gains over prior synthetic-data methods; 72.5 mIoU VOC per a web summary.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Source + class-presence tokens instead of text; annotation VAE over 24 classes; use for other classes only (latent loses cracks).
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + JoDiffusion pairs vs PF, metric mIoU_rob; benchmark baseline, reported. About 50 GPU-h.

title: A3-TTA: Adaptive Anchor Alignment Test-Time Adaptation for Image Segmentation
mechanism: Target images with compact class density act as anchors. Pseudo-labels for the others are built under anchor guidance, regularised by boundary-aware entropy and a self-adaptive EMA.
adaptation: Anchors are E1 cells whose crack/inactive feature density is close to the train prototype (likely the plain full cells). Anchor-guided pseudo-labels then go to half-cut scuff cells. Crack anchors must be class-balanced (BAPA CBA), or background dominates.
min_experiment: Arm: SUP100-PF + A3-TTA on E1 modules. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains < +0.02, or test guard drops > 0.005, or H36 crack-free false alarms rise > 2x.
evidence: R: +10.40 to +17.68 Dice over the source model on multi-domain heart and prostate segmentation plus natural images; robust in continual TTA.
prior_overlap: Partial. Pseudo-label SSL with the 11.9k pool was n.d. at 100%, but that used generic pool cells and fixed thresholds during training, not anchor-guided adaptation on target modules.

title: Domain-aligned self-supervision: CT-specialized DINOv3 enhances PET/CT tumor segmentation
mechanism: Evidence study: domain proximity and pretraining scale jointly decide whether DINOv3 pretraining helps; natural-image DINOv3 can fail to beat random init on a distant greyscale modality.
evidence: R (abstract): frozen encoders in nnU-Net, 5-fold CV on autoPET and HECKTOR; CT-pretrained DINOv3 best; natural-image DINOv3 did not beat from-scratch.
adaptation: Caution for every natural-image VFM arm on EL, and support for in-domain continued pretraining on the EL pool (ExPLoRA / MedDINOv3) over more natural-image scale.
min_experiment: Covered by the ExPLoRA arm: adapted vs original backbone on E1 relF1@2; kill if not +0.02.
prior_overlap: Not a method run here; informs the A8 null.

title: Revisiting MAE pre-training for 3D medical image segmentation
mechanism: Masked-autoencoder pretraining of an nnU-Net residual-encoder CNN on a large unlabelled pool with a configuration study, then nnU-Net fine-tuning.
adaptation: MAE-pretrain a 2D ResEnc-L on the 159k-cell unlabelled pool (13x the 11.9k used before), fine-tune with PF so the encoder is kept, label-safe aug, our folds.
min_experiment: MAE ResEnc-L (PF) v scratch ResEnc-L, 2 seeds x 5 folds. Kill if CV crack IoU < +0.01 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.03.
evidence: R: abstract reports SSL on a large clinical pool improving nnU-Net downstream segmentation (details not read).
prior_overlap: MIM on ResNet-34 with the 11.9k pool, then house and PF fine-tune: n.d. This differs in pool size, architecture and MAE recipe, so not closed.

title: SIGAN: A Novel Image Generation Method for Solar Cell Defect Segmentation and Augmentation
mechanism: GAN removes the defect while a strong identity loss keeps the background; the difference with the input segments the defect; also used to augment small defect sets.
adaptation: Generate defect-free twins of cracked train cells; use the residual (input minus twin) as an extra input channel or the twins as paired negatives to suppress decoys (scuffs, grain boundaries).
min_experiment: Arm: PF with residual channel, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF 5 seeds. Metric: test crack IoU clean 49 and E1 relF1@2. Kill: gain < +0.01 on both.
evidence: R: 90.34% F-score for crack and finger-interruption segmentation on EL-2019 (EL images).
prior_overlap: None.

title: Stochastic Segmentation Networks: Modelling Spatially Correlated Aleatoric Uncertainty
mechanism: Models logits as a low-rank multivariate Gaussian, giving spatially coherent mask samples at little extra cost.
adaptation: Replace the crack logit head with a low-rank Gaussian head. Average the samples, or pick the sample with the highest expected IoU, and use the variance as a calibrated crack uncertainty for review flags and severity.
min_experiment: Arm = house PF + SSN crack head (5 seeds) versus house PF. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, ECE. Kill if IoU < +0.012 and ECE does not improve.
evidence: R: LIDC lung nodule and BraTS; better sample diversity and quality than Probabilistic U-Net (abstract).
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Low-rank Gaussian crack head on the house decoder (base of the style-conditioned SSN); mainly calibrated crack uncertainty for severity and human-review flags.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: SSN crack head, 5 seeds vs house PF; metrics clean-49 crack IoU (mean prediction) and crack ECE; kill if IoU drops > 0.01 or ECE not better by 20%.

title: CrackUDA: Incremental Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Improved Crack Segmentation in Civil Structures
mechanism: Incremental adversarial UDA with a shared domain-invariant encoder and domain-specific decoder parameters.
evidence: +0.65 mIoU source, +2.7 mIoU target over other UDA methods on CrackSeg9K subsets and BuildCrack.
adaptation: Per-source decoder parameters for the 5 label conventions plus a half-cell pool domain; drop the adversarial part on 478 cells if unstable.
min_experiment: Per-source decoder heads vs house; metric per-source test crack IoU. Kill: < +0.01.
prior_overlap: None (source-conditional prediction never tried; D17 overlap).

title: SemiCurv: Semi-Supervised Curvilinear Structure Segmentation
mechanism: Curvilinear SSL with geometric strong augmentation, using a differentiable inverse transform to align predictions for pixel-wise consistency. An N-pair consistency loss prevents collapse to background on imbalanced thin structures.
adaptation: Apply its N-pair consistency to crack logits on pool cells, combined with the geometric transform plus inverse warp, instead of CE on hard pseudo-labels. Usable as the unlabelled loss in the ensemble-distillation or UniMatch V2 arms.
min_experiment: Ensemble-distillation arm B with an N-pair consistency term vs without. Metric: crack relF1@2 clean 49 and E1. Kill: < +0.005 relF1@2.
evidence: R: 6 curvilinear datasets including cracks; with at most 5% labels, reaches about 95% of fully supervised performance.
prior_overlap: Partial. Mean Teacher consistency with CutMix was run (n.d. at 100%). The N-pair loss and geometric inverse-warp consistency were not.

title: PointRend: Image Segmentation As Rendering
mechanism: A point head predicts labels at adaptively selected uncertain points from fine and coarse features with iterative subdivision.
adaptation: Point head on stride-1/2 features with top-k uncertain points per cell; acts as a hard-pixel sampler. Risk: the uncertain band is the 1-2 px label jitter.
min_experiment: Arm: house PF + point head; baseline: house PF; CV crack IoU, relF1@2, components >= 20 px found. Kill if all n.d.
evidence: R: gains on COCO and Cityscapes instance and semantic segmentation.
prior_overlap: none.

alt_notes.adaptation: Point head on stride-1/2 features of U-Net++, top-k uncertain points per cell; risk that the uncertain band is the 1 to 2 px label jitter, so pair it with relF1@2 scoring rather than strict IoU.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house PF + point head vs house PF; 5-fold CV crack relF1@2, gridline IoU; kill: relF1@2 n.d. and gridline < +0.02. About 10 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Keep only the uncertain-point head: an MLP over [EL intensity, stride-1/2 features, coarse logits] at the top-k ensemble-uncertain points, extra loss on those points during training; no subdivision needed at 512 px.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: U-Net++ + point head, 5 seeds. Baseline: house 5-seed. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2, gridline IoU. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012 and relF1@2 < +0.01.

title: Pseudo-SD: Pseudo Controlled Stable Diffusion for Semi-Supervised and Cross-Domain Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion on (unlabelled/target image, pseudo-label, text) triples with partial attention manipulation and structured pseudo-labels. Then generate label-controlled synthetic images in the target style and train the segmenter on them.
adaptation: Fine-tune a mask-conditioned SD on the 1,152 pool half-cells with their pseudo-labels, then render half-cut cells from labelled inactive and crack layouts. SD smears 1-2 px lines, so use the generated cells for inactive and layout context, and paste real crack pixels back.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + 2k generated half-cut cells, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: E1 inactive IoU and crack relF1@2, clean-49 non-inferiority. Kill: E1 inactive IoU < PF + 0.03 and E1 crack relF1@2 < PF + 0.02.
evidence: R: new state of the art on semi-supervised and cross-domain segmentation benchmarks when injected into current methods (numbers not retrieved).
prior_overlap: None. Generative synthesis is untested. Synthetic half-cut views made by geometry were n.d., but that is a different mechanism.

title: Deep Learning Model to Denoise Luminescence Images of Silicon Solar Cells
mechanism: Supervised deep denoiser for luminescence images of silicon cells, replacing longer exposure or better cameras.
evidence: R: PSNR +30% and SSIM +39%, better than classical denoisers.
adaptation: Targets noisy CSIR cells (one test cell wrecks 1 run in 6). Use as a second channel or test-time variant only, since 7% of crack components are under 2% darker than surroundings.
min_experiment: Arm: two-channel (raw, denoised) at train and test, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: comp>=20 px recall, crack IoU on CSIR cells. Kill: any drop in comp recall or no CSIR gain.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark robustness split (simulated low-exposure / daylight EL on test cells) and optional denoising of noisy sources such as the CSIR_00070-type cells before inference.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark use: noise-degraded copy of the test set, report each method's drop. Optional arm: denoise then house inference vs raw on CV crack relF1@2; kill if < +0.005.

alt_notes.adaptation: Second input channel or test-time variant for noisy CSIR cells; risk of erasing the 7% of crack components that are less than 2% darker than surroundings.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: test-time two-channel (raw, denoised) model. Baseline: house. Metrics: comp>=20 px recall, crack IoU on noisy CSIR cells. Kill: any drop in comp>=20 px recall or no gain on noisy CSIR cells.

title: Fine-grained crack segmentation for high-resolution images via a multiscale cascaded network
mechanism: Coarse-to-fine multiscale cascade for fine-grained cracks in high-resolution UAV images.
evidence: R: abstract only via search; numbers not read (Wiley full text unavailable off campus).
adaptation: Second stage on 2x upsampled crops around predicted crack components only, input [EL crop, upsampled crack prob]; much cheaper than the n.d. 2x global run; target width and faint ends.
min_experiment: Arm: house + crop-level 2x refiner. Baseline: house ensemble. Metric: relR@2 at fixed relP@2, crack IoU. Kill: relR@2 < +0.01.
prior_overlap: Global 2x input was n.d. at 4x compute; crop-only second stage was not run.

title: Practical Edge Detection via Robust Collaborative Learning (PEdger)
mechanism: Collaborative learning between models from different training moments and heterogeneous architectures (recurrent and not) to resist noisy labels, with no pretraining.
adaptation: An EMA teacher plus a second architecture trained on labelled data only, with crack consistency used as label denoising at 100% labels.
min_experiment: Arm: house + EMA and heterogeneous co-learning on labelled data, 5 seeds. Baseline: house at 100% labels. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if n.d.
evidence: R: better accuracy, speed and size on BSDS500 and NYUD without pretraining. Numbers not read.
prior_overlap: Partly closed: Mean Teacher at 100% with the pool was n.d., and CPS at 5% was worse. Its use for denoising labelled data at 100% is untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Supervised EMA teacher plus a second architecture on labelled cells only, consistency on the crack channel.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + EMA teacher consistency on labelled data, 5 seeds; baseline house. Kill if crack IoU n.d.

title: SARATR-X: Toward Building a Foundation Model for SAR Target Recognition
mechanism: SSL foundation model for noisy greyscale SAR on 0.18M unlabelled images, using multi-scale gradient features as masked-modeling targets so the model does not learn speckle.
adaptation: Repeat our closed R34 SparK job with multi-scale gradient / HOG targets instead of normalised pixels; gradient targets keep ridges and edges while ignoring EL sensor noise and source contrast.
min_experiment: Gradient-target MIM (~15 GPU-h) + PF vs pixel-target MIM checkpoint and house PF, 5 v 5; kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and E1 recall < +0.02.
evidence: R: competitive with or better than supervised, semi- and self-supervised methods on few-shot SAR classification and detection.
prior_overlap: Partial: same backbone and pool as our n.d. MIM; only the target changes, which was not tested.

title: A rendering-based lightweight network for segmentation of high-resolution crack images (RLCSN)
mechanism: Transformer encoder plus a super-resolution boundary-guided branch and point-wise refined rendering for thin cracks.
adaptation: Crack-domain evidence for the PointRend arm and SR boundary branch; no separate run.
min_experiment: Covered by the PointRend arm.
evidence: R: detects cracks as narrow as 0.15 mm from 3 m in UAV field tests; ablations per component.
prior_overlap: none.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack-domain variant of the PointRend arm; same test.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Same as PointRend arm; kill crack IoU < +0.012 and relF1@2 < +0.01.

title: IUR-Net: A Multi-Stage Framework for Label Refinement Tasks in Noisy Remote Sensing Samples
mechanism: Multi-stage label refinement for remote-sensing samples with image-label mismatch and inconsistent annotation quality (abstract-level).
adaptation: Candidate recipe for cleaning the 24-class structural labels drawn with different conventions per source; details unread.
min_experiment: Read method; if usable, arm: refined structural-class labels; baseline: house; metric mIoU_rob; kill if gain < 0.01.
evidence: unverified beyond abstract.
prior_overlap: none.

title: SegRCDB: Semantic Segmentation via Formula-Driven Supervised Learning
mechanism: Pretrain a segmentation network on procedurally generated images and masks (radial contours), with no real images or manual labels.
adaptation: Replace radial contours with EL-like primitives: thin dark polylines (1-4 px, branching), dark blobs attached to lines (inactive), periodic gridlines and busbars on textured grey. Pretrain the house encoder+decoder on 100k images, then PF fine-tune.
min_experiment: Arm: formula-pretrained house net + PF fine-tune, 3 then 5 seeds. Baseline: ImageNet house PF. Metrics: test crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill: both n.d. after 3 seeds.
evidence: R: higher mIoU than COCO-Stuff pretraining at equal image count when fine-tuning on ADE20k and Cityscapes.
prior_overlap: none. MIM and DDeP pool pretraining were n.d., but those are different objectives on real images. InsCore (same lab) is covered by another direction.

title: TDRPFormer: Texture-Debiased Reliable Prototype Transformer for Pixel-Level Steel Surface Defect Segmentation
mechanism: Build normal-texture prototypes from high-confidence background and subtract them from defect features, route a few reliable prototypes to mask queries, and add a continuity module for slender defects.
adaptation: Multi-crystalline grain boundaries mimic cracks: average layer2 features over confident sp_multi / sp_mono background per image and subtract a learned projection from decoder features; no query head needed.
evidence: R: best saliency metrics on ESDIs-SOD (MAE 0.0185, weighted F 0.882) and NEU-DET; no IoU on thin defects; no code.
min_experiment: Arm: house + background-prototype subtraction; baseline: house; metric: CV crack relP@2 on multi cells and material IoU; kill if multi-cell relP@2 gain < +0.02.
prior_overlap: none: mask-classification / prototype decoders never tried; D23 holds mask transformers generally.

title: Automated rock joint trace mapping using a supervised learning model trained on synthetic data generated by parametric modelling
mechanism: Parametric (discrete fracture network) synthesis of thin joint traces for segmentation. Mixed training helps when real labels are consistent; pretrain-then-fine-tune is more robust when real labels are noisy or biased.
adaptation: Design rule for any EL crack synthesizer (D06/D33): our crack labels are noisy and source-biased, so compare synthetic pretraining + real fine-tune against mixing synthetic into real batches.
min_experiment: Arm A: house pretrained on synthetic cracks then fine-tuned; Arm B: synthetic mixed at 25%. Baseline: house. Metrics: test crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill: neither arm beats house by 0.012 crack IoU or 0.02 E1 relF1@2.
evidence: R: synthetic data supports joint trace detection when real data is scarce; zero-shot from synthetic alone is limited; fine-tuning is robust to noisy labels (qualitative and quantitative, abstract only).
prior_overlap: none. Synthetic crack rendering was not tried; copy-paste is a different mechanism.

title: Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation With Cross-Consistency Training (CCT)
mechanism: Enforce agreement between the main decoder and auxiliary decoders fed perturbed encoder features on unlabelled images.
adaptation: U-Net++ with 3-6 auxiliary decoders, 11.9k pool cells as unlabelled; included mainly because it was the best mIoU on this data family in Torpey 2024.
min_experiment: Arm CCT U-Net++ vs PF, 5 seeds; metric CV mIoU_rob and inactive IoU; kill if mIoU_rob gain < +0.01.
evidence: R (via Torpey 2024): CCT mIoU 0.550 vs 0.506 previous SOTA on CSIR EL, single run.
prior_overlap: Pseudo-label SSL (Mean Teacher, CPS) n.d. at 100%; feature-perturbation consistency is a different mechanism but same SSL family, so expected gain is small.

alt_notes.adaptation: U-Net++ with 3-6 auxiliary decoders, 11.9k pool unlabelled, 100% labels; feature perturbations, not pseudo-labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm CCT U-Net++ vs baseline house, 5 seeds; metric CV mIoU_rob; kill if gain < +0.01. About 30 GPU-h.

title: Optimization for Medical Image Segmentation: Theory and Practice When Evaluating With Dice Score or Jaccard Index
mechanism: Theory and six tasks: Dice and Jaccard losses approximate each other, weighted CE has no weighting that optimises them, Tversky drifts from the optimum as weights move.
adaptation: Guides the benchmark loss axis (CE vs CE+Dice vs CE+JML vs Lovasz under one protocol) and warns that Tversky trades IoU for recall.
min_experiment: No separate run; read as design guidance for the benchmark loss baselines.
evidence: R: metric-sensitive losses beat CE-based losses on six medical tasks, across object sizes and class ratios.
prior_overlap: none

title: SemiVL: Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation with Vision-Language Guidance
mechanism: Spatially fine-tuned CLIP, a language-guided decoder, and class definitions given as text to separate confusable classes, inside UniMatch-style SSL.
adaptation: Write text definitions for gridline, splice, edge_dark, material and crack in EL terms. CLIP has little EL prior and ViT-B/16 at 512 px is coarse, so the use is mainly as a benchmark SSL baseline and a test for the weak structural classes.
min_experiment: Run the official code on our split as a benchmark arm vs UniMatch V2 and house PF, 3 seeds. Metric: mIoU_rob, gridline IoU, splice IoU. Kill as a candidate model if mIoU_rob is below house PF.
evidence: R: +13.5 mIoU on COCO with 232 labels and +6.1 on VOC with 92 labels over the prior SOTA; gains are at scarce labels.
prior_overlap: Vision-language models were never tried. Open, but the evidence is low-label only.

title: CutPaste: Self-Supervised Learning for Anomaly Detection and Localization
mechanism: Cut a patch or a thin 'scar' strip and paste it elsewhere in the same image. A classifier learns to spot the paste, and its features localise real anomalies.
evidence: Widely cited MVTec baseline (1,281 citations per the index). Numbers not re-checked this session.
adaptation: The scar variant is a thin line pasted inside the same cell, so it can serve as a cheap pretext on pool cells. In the benchmark it is the second anomaly-detection baseline next to DRAEM.
min_experiment: CutPaste trained on crack-free train cells. Report crack AP and relF1@2 on test and E1. Benchmark baseline, no kill line.
prior_overlap: none

title: Towards Real Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Via Confident Meta-Learning (CoMet)
mechanism: Model-agnostic training on uncurated data: soft confident learning down-weights low-confidence samples, meta-learning regularises updates via validation-loss covariance.
adaptation: Train pool-based AD models on the raw 11.9k (later 159k) pool, which contains defects, instead of filtering by the house ensemble (which biases banks toward cells the house model handles).
evidence: R: SOTA on MVTec AD, VIADUCT, KSDD2 with two base models; insensitive to anomalies in the training set.
min_experiment: Arm: CoMet-wrapped Dinomaly2 on raw pool; baseline: Dinomaly2 on house-clean pool. Metric: CV inactive and crack-band pixel AUROC. Kill: difference < 1 AUROC point, then keep the filtered pool.
prior_overlap: none

title: High-Precision Dichotomous Image Segmentation via Probing Diffusion Capacity (DiffDIS)
mechanism: Fine-tunes the Stable Diffusion 2.1 U-Net for one-step mask denoising with an auxiliary edge-generation task for fine-grained high-resolution segmentation.
evidence: R: SOTA on DIS5K (abstract, no numbers on page).
adaptation: Moonshot: condition SD on [EL replicated, house p(crack)] at 512 px, one step; tests whether a large generative prior recovers faint cracks; needs weight download approval.
min_experiment: Arm: DiffDIS-style refiner. Baseline: house ensemble. Metric: relR@2 at fixed relP@2. Kill: relR@2 < +0.01.
prior_overlap: none

title: Instance-Aware Test-Time Segmentation for Continual Domain Shifts (CoTICA)
mechanism: Pseudo-label thresholds adapt per class and per image from that image's own confidence distribution, and learning is re-weighted toward the classes most hurt by the shift.
adaptation: Use per-cell crack and inactive thresholds from the cell's confidence quantiles instead of a global 0.95, as the pseudo-label rule inside the SGP-TTA or A3-TTA arms. This targets the 'confident background on faint cracks' failure seen in our SSL nulls.
min_experiment: Arm: row 3 or 8 with quantile thresholds. Baseline: the same arm with a fixed threshold. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains < +0.01 over the parent arm.
evidence: R: outperforms prior CTTA and TTA methods in eight segmentation scenarios, including synthetic-to-real and long-term shifts (numbers not retrieved).
prior_overlap: None at test time. Class-aware thresholds were proposed in an earlier SSL null diagnosis but never run.

title: Vision Foundation Models in Agriculture: Toward Domain-Specific Adaptation for Weed Herbicide Trials Assessment
mechanism: Self-supervised adaptation of a general VFM on a curated domain set; gains concentrate on unseen conditions.
adaptation: Evidence to make E1 crack recall / relF1@2 the primary metric of every SSL arm, with test / folds as non-inferiority.
min_experiment: No standalone run; sets the metric for D32 arms.
evidence: R: species F1 0.91 to 0.94 standard, 0.56 to 0.66 unseen; damage 0.17 to 0.27 unseen; +5.4% F1 with 80% fewer labels.
prior_overlap: None.

title: DIP: Unsupervised Dense In-Context Post-Training of Visual Representations
mechanism: Unsupervised post-training of a pretrained ViT on automatically generated pseudo in-context tasks (diffusion model + encoder) so dense features work better for kNN / in-context segmentation.
evidence: R: beats the initial encoder and prior methods on in-context scene understanding; under 9 h on one A100.
adaptation: Post-train DINOv2-B on the 12k EL pool (1 channel replicated) and use it as the memory feature for the retrieval head and as matcher for SAM2/DINO labellers.
min_experiment: Retrieval-head experiment with DIP-post-trained DINOv2 vs plain DINOv2 memory; metric out-of-fold mIoU_rob and inactive IoU; kill if no gain over plain DINOv2 memory.
prior_overlap: Partial: MIM and DDeP pool pretraining on ResNet-34 were n.d.; DIP is a ViT with an in-context objective, not tested.

title: SEMIR: Topology-Preserving Graph Minors for Thin-Structure Segmentation
mechanism: Replace the pixel lattice with a graph minor whose contraction preserves 1-3 px structures; a GNN classifies supernodes and an exact map lifts predictions to pixels.
adaptation: Build the minor with EL ridge filters so crack px are never merged into background; GNN on house encoder features; aimed at fragmentation (components found).
min_experiment: Arm SEMIR crack classifier vs PF; metric components >=20 px found; kill if +<0.02.
evidence: TTPLA power lines, CrackSeg9k, SkyScapes lanes: matches or beats domain baselines on Dice, IoU, Boundary F1; fragmentation at least 4.6x lower than SLIC.
prior_overlap: none

title: Test-Time Coverage: Test-Conditioned Data Curation for Deployment-Aware Learning
mechanism: Select a budgeted training subset whose concept distribution matches unlabelled deployment samples.
adaptation: Simple EL descriptors (half-cut, mono/multi, busbar count, scuff, contrast) from pool and F51/H36 (not E1); select matching pool cells, pseudo-label, train.
min_experiment: Arm: 1,000 descriptor-matched pool cells pseudo-labelled. Baseline: 1,000 random pool cells, same teacher. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: no gain vs random.
evidence: R: better coverage and end-to-end driving performance than curation baselines; distant domain.
prior_overlap: Pool SSL used uniform pool; target-matched curation not run. Open.

title: TransUNet: Transformers Make Strong Encoders for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: ResNet-50 stem plus ViT encoder on the 1/16 feature map, cascaded upsampler with CNN skip connections.
adaptation: Benchmark suite: 512 px gray replicated to 3 channels, ImageNet R50-ViT-B/16 init, PF schedule, label-safe aug, same folds and metrics.
min_experiment: TransUNet (PF) 5 folds v house PF; benchmark row. For score: kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 and CV crack relF1@2 < +0.01.
evidence: R: Synapse multi-organ and ACDC gains over U-Net and attention U-Net at release; most cited 2D Transformer U-Net. Counter: Revisited shows Transformers below nnU-Net in 3D.
prior_overlap: none; no transformer segmenter tried

title: Confidence Intervals Uncovered: Are We Ready for Real-World Medical Imaging AI?
mechanism: SD of Dice approximated by a quadratic in mean Dice, so CIs can be reconstructed for papers that report none.
adaptation: Reconstruct approximate CIs for published EL segmentation numbers in the benchmark's related-work table.
min_experiment: Arm: apply fit to published EL tables. Metric: share of claimed gains inside CI. Kill: reporting only.
evidence: R: 221 MICCAI 2023 papers; >50% report no variability; median CI width 0.03, three times the median first-second gap; >60% of runners-up inside the winner's CI.
prior_overlap: none

title: Data Leakage in Visual Datasets
mechanism: Quantify leakage of evaluation images into training data via near-duplicate retrieval.
adaptation: Near-duplicate search (embedding + pixel correlation) between 11.9k/159k pool, train, val, test, E1 and across BenchmarkEL releases (same CSIR/ARTS sources), plus same-module pairs across splits, before any pool-based result enters the benchmark.
min_experiment: No training: run retrieval, report count of test/E1 cells with pool or train near-duplicates; re-score any pool-based arm without them. Kill: none (integrity check).
evidence: R: documents leakage across visual benchmarks sourced from overlapping collections (abstract-level).
prior_overlap: none; pool leakage never checked.
