title: SegDINO: An Efficient Design for Medical and Natural Image Segmentation with DINO-V3
mechanism: Frozen DINOv3 multi-level features aligned to one resolution and decoded by a light MLP head.
evidence: R (abstract): SOTA on TN3K, Kvasir-SEG, ISIC and 3 natural sets with few trainable params.
adaptation: Benchmark reference row only (frozen VFM + light head); expected to fail on 1-2 px cracks at stride 16, which documents why a detail path is needed.
min_experiment: One run under the benchmark protocol; report crack IoU, relF1@2, mIoU_rob; no kill, reference.
prior_overlap: Close to the closed frozen linear probes (DINOv3 ViT-S), but with multi-level features and ViT-L; low expected gain.

title: SegGPT: Towards Segmenting Everything In Context
mechanism: ViT-L trained as in-context colouring: given (image, mask) prompts with random colour maps it paints the query mask; multiple prompts ensembled by feature averaging.
evidence: R: strong in-domain and out-of-domain results on few-shot semantic, VOS, semantic and panoptic segmentation; no thin-structure evidence.
adaptation: Gray to 3 channels; 448 px canvas halves each cell so 1-2 px cracks vanish: use for inactive and structural classes; fixed colour per class in prompt masks; supports retrieved by source; the standard in-context row in the benchmark K-shot track.
min_experiment: In G0 and the K-shot track: SegGPT K=1/4/16 vs house PF fine-tuned on the same K cells; metrics inactive IoU, mIoU_rob classes; kill as labeller if below house PF on all classes.
prior_overlap: none

title: Boundary IoU: Improving Object-Centric Image Segmentation Evaluation
mechanism: IoU restricted to a band of width d around both contours; more sensitive to boundary quality on large objects.
adaptation: Use for inactive and large structural classes; for 1-2 px cracks Boundary IoU at d >= 2 equals mask IoU, so no use for crack.
min_experiment: Arm: Boundary IoU d=3 for inactive, gridline, busbar on OOF. Kill: never changes a ranking vs mask IoU.
evidence: R: more sensitive than mask IoU to boundary errors on large objects on COCO, LVIS, Cityscapes.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark scoring: Boundary IoU at d = 2 px for inactive and structural classes beside IoU; for crack it is close to relF1@2 and gives it a published name; Boundary PQ if an instance view is adopted.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training: rescore existing house and PF predictions on val/CV folds with Boundary IoU d = 1, 2, 3 and check rank agreement with relF1@2.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark scoring: report Boundary IoU at d = 2 px for inactive and the structural classes next to IoU. For crack it is close to our relaxed metric and gives that metric a published, citable name.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training. Recompute on existing house / PF predictions on val folds and check that model rankings stay stable across seeds.

title: U-KAN Makes Strong Backbone for Medical Image Segmentation and Generation
mechanism: Conv U-Net whose deeper stages tokenize features and process them with Kolmogorov-Arnold layers (learnable spline activations), giving higher accuracy at lower compute.
adaptation: 1-channel, 512 px. Use as the efficient-model member of the benchmark (edge deployment for WattCycle). Little expected effect on 1 px cracks, because the KAN blocks sit at low resolution.
min_experiment: One run per fold in the shared benchmark protocol; report test-49 and E1 metrics plus FLOPs/FPS against the house model. Kill: below house on crack relF1@2 by more than 0.02, then keep only for the efficiency axis.
evidence: R: better accuracy at lower compute than U-Net/UNeXt baselines on BUSI, GlaS and CVC. U-Bench ranks it in the U-Score top 10 (in-domain #8, zero-shot #3).
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Suite member, 1-channel 2D 512 px, same folds; shallow stages that carry 1-2 px crack detail are unchanged, so expected crack gain near zero.
alt_notes.min_experiment: U-KAN 5 folds v house; benchmark row only; kill for score if no CV metric +0.01.

title: A novel reconstruction-based method for unsupervised photovoltaic cell defect detection using electroluminescence images (PV-ReAD)
mechanism: EL-specific reconstruction AD with multi-layer adaptive fusion, adaptive noisy bottleneck against identity shortcut, and a global cosine focal loss.
adaptation: EL-native AD baseline for the benchmark; reimplement as Dinomaly plus their loss if no code; check whether U-PVEL-AD-seg masks are public as extra pixel labels.
min_experiment: Benchmark AD track only: train once on clean pool cells, report pixel AUROC / AU-PRO / relF1@2 per class; no kill line.
evidence: R: on new U-PVEL-AD-seg, image AUROC 95.2, pixel AUROC 99.7, AP 98.7, F1-max 93.6, AUPRO 77.8.
prior_overlap: none

title: A unified large language model-based framework for heterogeneous PV image diagnosis
mechanism: Task-aware diagnostic prompting of multimodal LLMs (zero- and few-shot) for visible, EL and IR PV images in one pipeline.
evidence: R: GPT-5.1 few-shot > 97.3 % accuracy; zero-shot 83.5 % on full ELPV, 2.8 points under a supervised CNN; open models (Qwen, CLIP) weaker on EL and IR; benchmark set of labelled PV images released.
adaptation: Benchmark: an image-level MLLM baseline (crack present / inactive present per cell) under our fixed split; deliverable: zero-label thermal triage; possible helper for the 24 audit-flagged train cells.
min_experiment: Arm open-weight VLM few-shot crack / inactive presence on F51 val cells; baseline house model image-level max probability; metric AUROC per class; kill as a scorer if AUROC < house minus 0.10 (keep as benchmark row).
prior_overlap: none.

title: Per-Pixel Classification is Not All You Need for Semantic Segmentation (MaskFormer)
mechanism: Recasts semantic segmentation as predicting a set of binary masks each with one class label.
evidence: R: outperforms per-pixel baselines when the number of classes is large.
adaptation: Guides judgement: at 24 classes (13 with test support) little gain expected overall; judge mask classifiers on inactive and rare region classes, not on crack.
min_experiment: No own run; its question is answered by the M2F/EoMT arms (per-class comparison against house).
prior_overlap: none.

title: Learning to Be a Transformer to Pinpoint Anomalies
mechanism: Shallow MLP students mimic attention-layer patch mappings of a frozen ViT on high-resolution inputs; adds defect-size-stratified evaluation metrics.
adaptation: High-resolution AD prior at native 1,200 px for pool sources that have it; and adopt size-stratified metrics in the benchmark: crack recall by component length bins (<20, 20-100, >100 px).
evidence: R: SOTA on MVTec AD, best segmentation on VisA; better robustness across defect sizes by their metrics.
min_experiment: Benchmark: add length-binned crack recall to the protocol (no GPU). Prior arm only if the WeakREST arm passes.
prior_overlap: none; 2x input resolution n.d. was for the supervised model, not an AD prior

title: Mamba as a Bridge: Where Vision Foundation Models Meet Vision Language Models for Domain-Generalized Semantic Segmentation (MFuser)
mechanism: Mamba-based fusion of VFM and VLM features with linear cost in sequence length for DGSS.
evidence: 68.20 mIoU synthetic-to-real, 71.87 real-to-real (abstract).
adaptation: Only as a modern DGSS benchmark entry on a VFM backbone; CLIP text side has no EL vocabulary.
min_experiment: Benchmark arm under leave-one-source-out; no score claim.
prior_overlap: None; VFM frozen probes only (BRIEF).

title: DatasetDM: Synthesizing Data with Perception Annotations Using Diffusion Models
mechanism: A perception decoder trained on about 100 labelled images reads diffusion-model features, so every generated image receives a dense mask.
adaptation: Needs a diffusion model fine-tuned on the EL pool; decoder trained on 478 train cells. Its labels are model predictions on generated cells, close to pseudo-labelling; mainly a canonical benchmark baseline.
min_experiment: Benchmark baseline: PF + DatasetDM pairs vs PF. Metric mIoU_rob and CV inactive IoU. Reported; drop if < +0.005.
evidence: R: state of the art synthetic training on VOC/COCO, more robust domain generalisation, with under 1% labelled images.
prior_overlap: Partly closed: pseudo-label SSL at 100% labels with the 11.9k pool was n.d., and DatasetDM labels are also model predictions; it differs only in generating the images.

title: Revealing the Semantic Selection Gap in DINOv3 through Training-Free Few-Shot Segmentation (FSSDINO)
mechanism: Training-free FSS with frozen DINOv3: class prototypes plus Gram-matrix refinement; last layer is a strong default, best intermediate layer is better but hard to select.
evidence: R: competitive with specialised FSS methods on binary, multi-class and cross-domain FSS benchmarks.
adaptation: Cheapest K-shot benchmark baseline and a layer-wise diagnostic of which DINOv3/DINOv2 layer separates EL classes; DINOv3 gated, DINOv2 fallback.
min_experiment: K-shot track row and G0 entry vs house PF fine-tuned on the same K cells; inactive IoU on H36; kill as labeller if below SAM2 video mode.
prior_overlap: Partial: frozen DINOv3/DINOv2 linear probes showed no gain over ResNet-34 in-distribution; prototype few-shot use on new contexts not tested.

title: CrossDiff: Diffusion Probabilistic Model With Cross-conditional Encoder-Decoder for Crack Segmentation
mechanism: Diffusion probabilistic crack segmenter with a cross-encoder (detail) and cross-decoder (semantics).
evidence: R: five crack sets (CFD, CrackTree200, DeepCrack, GAPs384, Rissbilder), +8.0% Dice and IoU over SOTA.
adaptation: Benchmark suite entry as the diffusion crack baseline: 1-ch input, 512 px, crack-only head or 24-class head; not a refiner.
min_experiment: Arm: CrossDiff reimplementation, 3 seeds. Baseline: house 5-seed. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill: below house on both.
prior_overlap: none

title: PVMatch: Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation for Photovoltaic Defects Using Dynamic Pseudo-Labeling and Multi-Scale Feature Consistency
mechanism: Class-aware dynamic thresholds keep rare EL defect classes in the pseudo-labels; a global-local feature consistency loss works inside masked defect regions.
adaptation: The only EL-specific SSL method found. Use it as a benchmark SSL baseline if code becomes available. The class-aware threshold could replace our fixed threshold for crack and inactive.
min_experiment: Benchmark arm only: reimplement CDT in our Mean Teacher code at 20% labels vs our Mean Teacher, 3 seeds. Metric: crack and inactive IoU. Kill if n.d.
evidence: R: real-world EL datasets, unnamed; no numbers in the abstract.
prior_overlap: Our Mean Teacher with hard/tolerant pseudo-labels was n.d. from 20% up. Class-aware thresholds were not tested, but they target the low-label regime. Mostly closed for scores.

title: Balanced Prompt Adaptation against Entropy-Induced Collapse for Test-Time Binary Segmentation (BAPA)
mechanism: The paper proves that entropy minimisation collapses imbalanced binary segmentation toward the majority class. The fix uses class-balanced high-confidence anchors with equal total loss per class and updates only the prompts.
adaptation: The VLM prompt part does not apply to our CNN. The CBA rule does: every self-training TTA arm must select crack anchors separately and give crack equal total loss weight to background.
min_experiment: Ablation inside rows 3, 8 and 9: class-balanced anchors on vs off. Kill if E1 crack recall differs by < +0.02.
evidence: R: theory of entropy-induced collapse in a shared-shift model. BAPA has the highest mean Dice across four domains and improves zero-shot Dice on all four datasets.
prior_overlap: None. Tent was dropped without a run; this paper gives the reason entropy TTA would fail on crack and a fix.

title: Generative Edge Detection with Stable Diffusion (GED)
mechanism: Fine-tunes the Stable Diffusion denoising U-Net to predict latent edge maps in one step, with granularity as a condition and a granularity regularisation.
adaptation: Same VAE-latent risk as DiffusionEdge for 1 px cracks, so the reconstruction gate comes first. Use source label style as the granularity condition.
min_experiment: Gate: SD VAE reconstruction IoU of GT crack maps >= 0.9. Arm: GED on crack, 3 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: relF1@2. Kill at the gate or if relF1@2 is below the house model.
evidence: R: BSDS ODS 0.870, OIS 0.880.
prior_overlap: Not tested. Open.

title: Test-Time Training with Masked Autoencoders
mechanism: For each test image, the MAE encoder is trained on masked-patch reconstruction for a few steps, and the task head then predicts from the updated encoder.
adaptation: Needs a ViT MAE encoder; our ResNet-34 does not fit. Only viable if D23/D24 build a ViT segmenter close to FINAL: MAE-pretrain it on the 11.9k pool, fine-tune for segmentation, then run 20-step per-cell TTT on E1.
min_experiment: Arm: ViT segmenter + per-cell MAE TTT. Baseline: the same ViT segmenter without TTT (it must be within 0.01 of FINAL on test). Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains < +0.03.
evidence: R: improves robustness on ImageNet-C and other shift benchmarks with one-sample TTT.
prior_overlap: None at test time. MIM pretraining on ResNet-34 was n.d. (BRIEF s5), but per-image TTT on a ViT was never run.

title: TOPO-Loss for continuity-preserving crack detection using deep learning
mechanism: Connectivity-oriented loss (adapted from road delineation) designed to encourage crack continuity and to accommodate imprecise annotations, combined with MSE and Dice.
adaptation: Crack class on U-Net++, as an extra term with low weight. It is the only crack-domain topology loss with code and an imprecise-label design.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + TOPO term (crack), 3 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metric: component recall, crack IoU. Kill if crack IoU < baseline - 0.012.
evidence: R: improved topology on masonry crack sets. R (TopoMortar): TOPO unstable (CREMI Dice 0.63 +- 0.22) and over-segments OOD images.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Only crack-domain topology loss with imprecise labels; reference only given its instability.
alt_notes.min_experiment: None planned; include only if the benchmark suite wants a crack-specific topology loss.

title: Dataset of damaged photovoltaic cells electroluminescence, visible and near-infrared multispectral images with performance degradation data and LLM-RAG descriptors
mechanism: Pixel-aligned EL, NIR and visible HDR images of the same cells after staged mechanical, thermal and electrical damage, with Isc / Voc per stage.
adaptation: Use abrasion / scrape stages to see how surface scuffs look in EL versus real cracks, as hard negatives for E1 scuff streaks; tiny severity check of predicted inactive fraction vs Isc drop. Test-only (one poly cell type).
min_experiment: Visual check that abrasion EL resembles E1 scuffs; if yes, paste as background-labelled negatives. Arm vs PF on E1 crack relP@2 in half-cut cells. Kill at the visual check or if relP@2 < +0.02. Download needs user OK.
evidence: R: small number of polycrystalline cells, same camera for NIR and EL gives near pixel-perfect registration; CC BY.
prior_overlap: Partial: scuff as its own class (649 px) was not learned; hard negatives from a registered external set were not tried.

title: Global-Regularized Neighborhood Regression for Efficient Zero-Shot Texture Anomaly Detection (GRNR)
mechanism: Training-free: each patch is regressed from its in-image neighbours, regularised by global normal prototypes from the same image.
adaptation: Per-cell prior for multi-crystalline texture; the periodic cell layout (fingers, busbars) makes in-image neighbours good references, including for unseen half-cut layouts. Offline only.
evidence: R: eight benchmark datasets, beats some trained methods without any training data.
min_experiment: Offline map on CV val + F51 multi cells; kill if < 30% of PF-missed crack components >=20 px recovered at 1% area.
prior_overlap: none

title: Drone-Based Daylight Electroluminescence Imaging of PV Modules
mechanism: Drone camera at 120 fps captures EL and background frame pairs under modulated bias in full daylight, giving module EL images.
evidence: R: diagnostic EL images from about 1 s of capture near 1 sun; SNR_avg 4.6.
adaptation: Moonshot route to field EL for WattCycle; our EL model would face a resolution and SNR shift like E1. Cheap proxy now: degrade test cells to drone-EL resolution and noise and measure the drop.
min_experiment: Degrade test clean-49 cells (downsample to 32 to 128 px per cell, add noise to SNR 4.6, upsample), score the house ensemble; report crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU per level. Decision aid for WattCycle hardware, no model change.
prior_overlap: Desk study ruled out drone EL by camera cost (SWIR); no measurement of required resolution was made.

title: High Quality Segmentation for Ultra High-resolution Images (CRM)
mechanism: Continuous Refinement Model: an implicit-function refiner that aligns features to the refinement target and can output at any resolution.
evidence: R: claims generalisation across the low-res training / ultra-high-res test gap (abstract, no numbers on page).
adaptation: Query at 2x or 4x output resolution to model sub-pixel crack position and source-specific width, then downsample; tests whether width / alignment error is a resolution problem.
min_experiment: Arm: CRM-style implicit refiner at 2x output. Baseline: house ensemble. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@1 and @2. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012.
prior_overlap: 2x input resolution n.d.; implicit super-resolved output not run.

title: Contour Refinement using Discrete Diffusion in Low Data Regime
mechanism: A lightweight CNN + self-attention discrete diffusion model, conditioned on a segmentation mask, iteratively denoises a sparse contour representation; built for fewer than 500 training images.
adaptation: Refine outlines of predicted inactive regions (42 train cells, labels well aligned); contours converted back to filled masks.
min_experiment: Arm: contour diffusion on PF inactive masks. Baseline: PF ensemble. Metric: inactive IoU on 5-fold CV. Kill: < +0.01.
evidence: R: beat several SOTA baselines on KVASIR, competitive on HAM10K and a smoke dataset, with < 500 training images and 3.5x faster inference.
prior_overlap: none.

alt_notes.adaptation: Inactive boundaries only; low value because inactive boundaries are already accurate (1 px shift IoU 0.94).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: contour refiner on inactive. Baseline: house ensemble. Metric: inactive IoU. Kill: < +0.02.

title: Exploring Structural Degradation in Dense Representations for Self-supervised Learning
mechanism: Longer SSL training can degrade dense-task performance. A label-free Dense representation Structure Estimator (class relevance + effective dimensionality) selects checkpoints or regularises training.
adaptation: Only useful alongside a D32 pool SSL run (159k pool, new backbone): score SSL checkpoints with DSE on pool cells and fine-tune from the DSE-chosen one, not the last.
min_experiment: Arm: PF fine-tune from the DSE-selected SSL checkpoint. Baseline: PF fine-tune from the last checkpoint. Metric: val + F51 crack AP, then test crack IoU. Kill: DSE choice no better than the last checkpoint on val.
evidence: R: degradation seen across 16 SSL methods; DSE-based model selection gives +3.0 mIoU on average at negligible cost.
prior_overlap: Partial. MIM and DDeP pool pretraining were n.d., always using the final checkpoint; checkpoint selection was not tested.

title: Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science
mechanism: A taxonomy of 8 leakage types, plus model info sheets that argue train/test independence.
adaptation: Leakage audit for EL: the same module across splits, CFVS train twins, BMRK = ELPV cells, the leaky UCF-EL split, and pool images from test modules (SSL leakage). Publish a model info sheet with each split.
min_experiment: Compare house scores on test cells with vs without a same-module or twin cell in train. E: CFVS without a twin scores 0.397 crack IoU vs 0.474 overall. Decision: if the gap is > 0.03, twins must sit inside one fold.
prior_overlap: none as an audit; the twin effect has been observed but not formalised.
evidence: R: survey of leakage across 294 papers in 17 fields; proposes model info sheets.

title: Every Component Counts: Rethinking the Measure of Success for Medical Semantic Segmentation in Multi-Instance Segmentation Tasks (CC-Metrics)
mechanism: Evaluates Dice / surface Dice per GT component on its Voronoi cell and averages, removing the large-component bias; proximity-based matching.
adaptation: Benchmark metric: per-instance crack Dice and per-instance relF1@2 on merged crack instances, plus size-stratified recall (< 20 px, >= 20 px) for test and E1.
min_experiment: Compute CC-Dice on val/F51 predictions of house vs ensemble vs PF; check rank agreement with relF1@2. Kill as a headline metric if rank correlation > 0.95 with relF1@2 (adds no information).
evidence: Whole-body PET/CT metastases: standard metrics biased to large components; CC-Metrics fixes Dice and HD sensitivity to small lesions.
prior_overlap: none

title: An Industry-Ready Deep Learning Framework for Power Loss Prediction in Half-Cut Photovoltaic Modules

title: Revisiting pre-trained remote sensing model benchmarks: resizing and normalization matters
mechanism: Mismatched input size and normalisation hide pretrained features; once matched, ImageNet stays a strong baseline.
adaptation: Benchmark rule: fine-tune each backbone at its pretraining scale and normalisation, map 1-ch EL to the backbone's 3-ch statistics, always include the ImageNet row.
min_experiment: None; protocol rule.
evidence: R: +32.28 points So2Sat, +11.16 EuroSAT from matching preprocessing.
prior_overlap: None.

title: Simple Copy-Paste is a Strong Data Augmentation Method for Instance Segmentation
mechanism: Paste object instances at random onto other images; this is a strong augmentation for instance segmentation.
evidence: Gains at every COCO data fraction; a widely used baseline (1,464 citations per the index).
adaptation: Use only as the benchmark's plain copy-paste baseline, reporting the decoy test alongside it.
min_experiment: Plain random crack copy-paste vs house model, 5 seeds, with the decoy rate reported. Benchmark row only, no kill line.
prior_overlap: Closed for scores: CP100 tested a stricter version (residual transfer) at 100% labels, n.d., with a decoy FLAG.

alt_notes.adaptation: Already tested in our variant (CP100); include only as the benchmark's plain copy-paste baseline with the decoy test reported.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark run with decoy rate; no kill.

title: An empirical investigation on the correlation between solar cell cracks and hotspots
mechanism: Classifies cracks into four modes (free, micro-crack, shaded / isolated area, breakdown) and measures which produce hot spots.
evidence: R: 12 cells; modes 1-2 no hot spot; modes 3-4 heat from 25 C to 100 C; worst at 40 to 60 % shading ratio (105 C).
adaptation: Gives a severity label computable from our masks (crack mode from predicted inactive fraction) and the EL-to-thermal mapping for the deliverable; explains why thermal cannot help strict crack IoU.
min_experiment: With E-PF masks on A3 crack modules (needs Om's open decision on inference location), Spearman between predicted inactive fraction per cell and sunlit IR cell delta T; kill the mapping claim if rho < 0.3.
prior_overlap: Desk study (doc 22) cited the abstract; no experiment run.

title: Loss Landscape Topology Reveals Why Simple Baselines are Competitive at 3D Point Cloud Segmentation Under Class Imbalance
mechanism: Systematic comparison of 11 imbalance methods vs plain CE: CE stays within 0.8-3.3 mIoU; poorly tuned specialised methods can degrade badly.
adaptation: Benchmark rule: include tuned plain CE(+Dice) as the control and report tuning budget per method; prior that loss-only fixes give small gains.
min_experiment: No training run; fold into benchmark protocol (equal tuning budget per imbalance method).
evidence: R: 3D point clouds, imbalance 641:1 and 56:1, two architectures: CE within 0.8-3.3% mIoU of specialised methods.
prior_overlap: none

title: Aerial Infrared Health Monitoring of Solar Photovoltaic Farms at Scale
mechanism: Cascade of table segmentation, oriented panel detection and anomaly detection, plus a max-minus-median sub-grid rule for hot spots with five delta-T severity bands.
evidence: R (full text read): >6,000 US farms, 2.2 to 6.5 cm GSD; table U-Net mIoU 97.9; rotated Faster R-CNN mAP@75 83.3; YOLOv5-L P@50 89.8; hot spot = >5 C above neighbours, bands up to >= 15 C. Data private.
adaptation: Blueprint for the drone thermal deliverable; the physically defined banded severity output is a template for an EL severity layer (inactive area fraction bands per cell, crack mode).
min_experiment: CPU: define EL severity bands from predicted inactive fraction per cell, check agreement with ground-truth bands on val (weighted kappa); kill the band scheme if kappa < 0.6.
prior_overlap: none.

title: From Question to Exploration: Test-Time Adaptation in Semantic Segmentation? (TTAP)
mechanism: A study of classic TTA in segmentation: BN updating brings slight gains or harm, teacher-student is stable but brings no gain on complex shifts, and long-tail imbalance breaks seg TTA even with accurate pseudo-labels. Proposes visual prompt TTA.
adaptation: Failure-mode evidence for rare classes. Use it to justify the benchmark rule that TTA is reported separately and the class-balanced selection in the self-training TTA arms.
min_experiment: Not an experiment. Cite it in the benchmark protocol; its findings are checked by the Tent/SAR/CoTTA rows.
evidence: R (abstract): BN updating slight gain or harm; teacher-student no gain over source on complex shifts; severe long-tail class imbalance problem in seg TTA.
prior_overlap: Consistent with T9 / BN-HC failure (E).

title: Solar Photovoltaic Modules Degradation: A Comparison Between Electroluminescence and Infrared Thermal Imaging
mechanism: Multimodal EL + IR detection dataset with one label scheme and weak boxes, YOLO with cross-modal fusion.
evidence: R: 359 EL and 569 IR images; no metrics in the abstract. Availability unverified.
adaptation: The only labelled EL + IR set found; if public and paired by module, it allows a cell-level mapping study (which EL defect classes have a thermal signature).
min_experiment: Locate the data; if public, count modules with both modalities and their label overlap. CPU.
prior_overlap: Not in the desk study's dataset table (A1 to A3, B, C, D, E rows).

title: Influence of irradiance and drone altitude in infrared thermography inspections of photovoltaic plants
mechanism: Controlled drone IR of 43 artificially degraded modules at 4 altitudes and 200 to 1000 W/m2 to measure which faults are thermally visible.
evidence: R: cracked modules hard to distinguish from healthy; interconnect breaks visible from 600 W/m2; PID and glass cracks no pronounced anomaly; diodes and heavy soiling 80 to >100 C even at 200 W/m2; altitude effect small. Data public (our A3, CC BY 4.0, E).
adaptation: Cross-plant test set for any thermal classifier trained on PVF-10 / ISM, and the only public place where drone IR and EL meet on the same induced faults.
min_experiment: Resume pick 1 R1 / R2 / R3b as frozen in handbook doc 22 section 11: IR screening recall by fault type on A3; CPU only.
prior_overlap: A3 downloaded and verified; sunlit arm R1 / R2 / R3b and pick3b not run (doc 22). Open.

title: Methodology for Calculating the Damaged Surface and Its Relationship with Power Loss in Photovoltaic Modules by Electroluminescence Inspection for Corrective Maintenance
mechanism: Method following IEC TS 60904-13: the per-cell percentage of Type-C crack area is mapped to module power loss; the most damaged cell dominates module performance.
adaptation: Per-cell severity = predicted inactive fraction. Module-level E1 severity = max over cells, not the mean. Use for the E1 module-level severity score (67 modules).
min_experiment: Benchmark-only: compute max-cell inactive band per E1 module from GT and predictions; report weighted kappa per model.
evidence: R: one polycrystalline module, repeated impacts, I-V after each; cell-level estimates beat substring or module level; applied to 4 field modules.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Our predicted inactive masks give the per-cell inactive area fraction directly; use to define a power-loss band metric for severity post-evaluation.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training: compute inactive-area fraction from GT and predictions on test / E1, report band agreement (e.g. 0, <5%, 5 to 20%, >20%).

title: Designing BERT for Convolutional Networks: Sparse and Hierarchical Masked Modeling (SparK)
mechanism: MIM for any CNN: sparse convolution over visible pixels and a hierarchical decoder.
adaptation: Benchmark's CNN in-domain MIM baseline row (R34 already run); the only open variant is ConvNeXt, covered by ConvNeXt V2 FCMAE.
min_experiment: None new; reuse the existing MIM100-PF runs as the benchmark row.
evidence: R: about +1.0 over contrastive and transformer MIM, up to +3.5 on detection / instance segmentation (ResNet, ConvNeXt).
prior_overlap: Closed: SparK-style MIM on ResNet-34, 11.9k pool, PF, 100% labels, n.d. (doc 11 row 25).

alt_notes.adaptation: Already run on R34 (n.d.); keep as the benchmark's CNN in-domain MIM row; only open variants are new targets (gradient, ridge) and new backbones.
alt_notes.min_experiment: None new; existing run is the benchmark row.

title: Impact of cell cracks on performance of PV modules with current cell technologies
mechanism: Correlates EL-measured crack length/count and busbar count with series resistance, shunt resistance and Pmax across full-cell PERC and half-cut TOPCon modules.
adaptation: Severity track should grade by isolated/inactive area and be layout-aware (half-cut, busbar count) rather than by crack length; E1 half-cut cells need their own severity rules.
min_experiment: No training arm: in the severity post-evaluation, compare crack-length vs isolated-area severity grades against any available power data; drop crack-length grading if it does not rank cells.
evidence: R: 230 mini-modules, 2 to 12 busbars; crack length/count not universal power-loss predictors; PERC moderate correlation at 200 W/m2 weakening at 1000 W/m2; TOPCon no meaningful correlation.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Severity design: do not score severity from crack length; use isolated / inactive area as the severity driver.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training arm; shapes the severity metric choice.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark scoring rule: do not use crack length or count as the severity target. Score isolated or inactive area per cell instead, and keep crack detection (relF1@2) as a separate safety and progression metric.
alt_notes.min_experiment: None. Design input for the severity track.

title: Panoptica -- instance-wise evaluation of 3D semantic and instance segmentation maps
mechanism: Package computing instance-wise matching, PQ and per-instance metrics from 2D/3D semantic or instance maps.
adaptation: Tooling for instance-wise crack and inactive scores in the benchmark; wrap with a 2 px tolerance matching.
min_experiment: Run on existing val predictions; confirm it reproduces our component-found metric. No training.
evidence: Software paper; no score claims.
prior_overlap: none

title: Tent: Fully Test-time Adaptation by Entropy Minimization
mechanism: Minimises prediction entropy by updating BN affine parameters while using test-batch statistics.
adaptation: Run with batch = one E1 module (or one cell), BN affine only. It is the canonical baseline and closes the thesis question that was dropped by expectation.
min_experiment: Arm: Tent on FINAL and SUP100-PF. Baseline: no TTA. Benchmark row; record whether crack recall collapses on E1 and test.
evidence: R: gains on CIFAR-C/ImageNet-C and on GTA-to-Cityscapes segmentation (numbers not retrieved). SGP-TTA reports Tent falling from 85.56 to 62.67 Dice on a thin-structure set where the source model was already good.
prior_overlap: Never run (handbook doc 20: dropped by expectation). BN-statistics adaptation (T9, BN-HC) failed, which supports a low score but does not close entropy updates.

title: AnomalyCLIP: Object-agnostic Prompt Learning for Zero-shot Anomaly Detection
mechanism: Object-agnostic normal / abnormal text prompts learned on auxiliary data give zero-shot anomaly maps for unseen objects.
adaptation: Zero-shot benchmark row only: run on EL with no EL training, report gap to supervised and to AA-CLIP trained on E-SCDD (pixel AP 0.55, D07).
evidence: R: zero-shot on many industrial and medical datasets (257 citations).
min_experiment: Benchmark row, inference only; no kill line.
prior_overlap: none

title: EL-to-IV: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of Photovoltaic Current-Voltage Curves from Electroluminescence Imaging
mechanism: A CNN maps a pair of EL images (20% and 80% Isc) to the full module I-V curve, and still works with one image.
adaptation: Benchmark reference row for 'power from EL'. We have one EL per cell and no I-V, so not usable as a method. Its 438 modules and bias levels match Sandia PV-IV-EL (likely the same data, unverified).
min_experiment: None for scores. For the benchmark, cite it as the image-level power baseline beside our mask-derived inactive-fraction proxy on Sandia PV-IV-EL.
evidence: R: 438 modules; validation accuracy about 95%; MPP and FF error < 2%; < 0.5 s per module.
prior_overlap: none

title: Matcher: Segment Anything with One Shot Using All-Purpose Feature Matching
mechanism: DINOv2 patch matching gives point prompts; SAM generates and filters masks; training-free one-shot.
evidence: R: 52.7 mIoU COCO-20i 1-shot; GFDS measured only 5.0 mIoU on industrial defects.
adaptation: Benchmark row only (K-shot track), 3-channel replicated EL, 1024 px.
min_experiment: K-shot track row vs SAM2 video mode; no labeller run unless it beats 0.2 inactive IoU on H36.
prior_overlap: none

title: The MVTec AD 2 Dataset: Advanced Scenarios for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
mechanism: Benchmark design: hidden test ground truth on an evaluation server, test splits with lighting / distribution shift, very small defects; shows SOTA below 60% AU-PRO.
adaptation: Template for the EL benchmark: hidden unseen-module test (E1-style), half-cut / new-module shift split, thresholded per-image segmentation F1 alongside AU-PRO, separate AD track.
min_experiment: No training; adopt split and metric design in the benchmark protocol.
evidence: R: 8 scenarios, >8000 high-resolution images; SOTA methods below 60% average AU-PRO.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Template for our benchmark: hidden E1-style unseen-module test, a half-cut shift split, thresholded per-image metrics, and an AD track next to the supervised track.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Not an experiment: adopt the protocol (hidden test, shift split, thresholded metrics) in the benchmark spec.

alt_notes.adaptation: Sealed EL test: hold E1 plus new labelled modules back from the public release and score them with a maintainer-held script, with the threshold fixed on dev OOF. Add an 'unseen module or cut type' split like private_mixed.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Protocol only: freeze the sealed split before any new method runs. Each method may submit once per protocol version.

title: Beyond Academic Benchmarks: Critical Analysis and Best Practices for Visual Industrial Anomaly Detection
mechanism: Fair re-evaluation of SOTA AD on real production data with practice-relevant metrics, showing academic gains often vanish in production.
adaptation: Template and harness for the benchmark AD track: fixed preprocessing, one harness for PatchCore / EfficientAD / Dinomaly2 / PRN, plant-relevant metrics (cell-level recall at fixed false-alarm rate, latency).
evidence: R: benchmarks on actual production data; public code.
min_experiment: Reuse harness to run the AD track under our split; no kill line.
prior_overlap: none

title: Evaluating Convolutional and Transformer Architectures for Photovoltaic Defect Classification via Electroluminescence Imagery
mechanism: Controlled benchmark: six backbones, identical preprocessing and training, stratified 5-fold CV, 150 runs; recommends module-grouped validation.
adaptation: Copy the protocol shape for our benchmark but with module-grouped 5-fold CV over the 532 train + val cells (fold roots exist).
min_experiment: Benchmark design item: house on module-grouped 5-fold, report fold spread; decides the smallest detectable effect.
evidence: R: 20,000 proprietary cells; ConvNeXt-T best macro-F1 93.12%.
prior_overlap: none.

alt_notes.adaptation: Copy the 'identical pipeline, all folds, mean +/- SD' reporting, with module-grouped folds and pixel metrics.
alt_notes.min_experiment: None for scores. Cite it as evidence that the EL field sees the split problem.

title: Power Loss Estimation for PV Modules with Cracked Cells
mechanism: Crack, dark and busbar masks are compressed into a VAE latent, and XGBoost predicts per-cell power loss (the pvcracks pipeline).
adaptation: Bold benchmark option: once their cell EL + I-V data is released (listed as pending), feed our masks to their power model and score segmenters by I-V agreement. Reference only until then.
min_experiment: When the data is available: per-cell dPmpp MAE using masks from the house, PF and ensemble models. Kill if the spread between models is below the model's own error.
evidence: R: per the web docs, XGBoost per-cell dPmpp; numbers not retrieved (full text fetch timed out).
prior_overlap: none

title: Benchmarking Power Loss Simulation Models for Cracked Photovoltaic Cells Using Electroluminescence Images: The Effect of Daylight and Image Resolution
mechanism: Benchmarks an analytic (bELMO) and an ML (DTU) power-loss model for cracked cells across dark lab vs daylight EL and two camera resolutions.
adaptation: Benchmark protocol: severity errors reported per severity band; daylight / low-resolution as a robustness axis for WattCycle's future drone EL.
min_experiment: No training arm; adopt the per-band reporting in the severity protocol.
evidence: R: both models good for low-loss cells, error grows for severe cracks and high-irradiance daylight; bELMO lower average error.
prior_overlap: none

alt_notes.adaptation: Design rule for our severity track: report error per severity band and per source. BMRK (downscaled ELPV) is our low-resolution case.
alt_notes.min_experiment: None. Design input: stratify severity metrics by band and by source.

title: Machine Aided Estimation of Solar Cell Crack Caused Power Loss from Electroluminescence Images
mechanism: Cell power from inactive area plus histogram moments, with busbar count as a categorical predictor, using polynomial or custom non-linear regression.
adaptation: Simplest severity regressor for our cells (inactive fraction + busbar layout), if any paired cell I-V becomes available.
min_experiment: None until paired I-V data exists.
evidence: R: linear R2 0.85; improved to R2 0.869 with max error 0.17; 2 to 5 busbar mono cells.
prior_overlap: none

title: One-shot luminescence diagnostics for field-scale photovoltaics
mechanism: Device-physics inversion converts one luminescence image into a quantitative power-loss map without multi-condition measurements.
adaptation: Design reference for a power-loss band severity output from one EL image; our cells lack calibrated intensity and electrical data, so no training use.
min_experiment: No training arm; cite in the severity protocol as the physics route for power-loss bands.
evidence: R: 300 modules, relative module-power error down to 0.5%.
prior_overlap: none

title: Quantitative Electroluminescence Imaging Analysis for Performance Estimation of PID-Influenced PV Modules
mechanism: Camera and perspective correction, then power-loss map from the log ratio of two EL images (before / after degradation or two currents).
evidence: R: about 2000 EL images and I-V curves, relative RMSE 1 to 3% against flash test.
adaptation: Single-bias data, so no score use; physics basis for converting dark / inactive area into a power-loss band, and for any future two-current capture on WattCycle's rig.
min_experiment: No training: only if two-current images become available; otherwise use as a reference for the severity metric.
prior_overlap: none

title: SolarFCD: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Solar Fault Classification in Photovoltaic Systems
mechanism: Builds a benchmark by merging public RGB and thermal sets with a unified label map, near-duplicate removal and fixed splits, then runs 16 classifiers.
evidence: R: 4,435 images, 4 merged classes, 80:10:10; best ResNet101V2 acc 86.68 %, F1 88.17.
adaptation: Benchmark hygiene for EL: unified class map and cross-release de-duplication (BenchmarkEL 2021 / 2022 / E-SCDD / UCF-EL); avoid its random split, which mixes plants.
min_experiment: CPU: perceptual-hash near-duplicate scan across EL releases, train vs test; report duplicate counts. No kill line (hygiene).
prior_overlap: none.

title: PVF-10: A high-resolution unmanned aerial vehicle thermal infrared image dataset for fine-grained photovoltaic fault classification
mechanism: Public UAV thermal dataset of module crops with 10 fault classes split by repairability, plus resampling / padding baselines.
evidence: R: 5,579 crops, 8 plants; 5 DL models OA > 83 %, best 93.32 %; later work reports DINOv3 94.67 % and JEFFNet F1 93.21. Licence and download location unverified.
adaptation: Training set for the drone deliverable's module classifier; evaluate cross-plant on A3 instead of the in-set split.
min_experiment: ResNet-34 / ConvNeXt-T trained on PVF-10 + ISM, tested on A3 module crops (healthy vs induced fault); metric AUROC per fault type; kill the train-public-deploy-at-WattCycle claim if diode / interconnect AUROC < 0.7.
prior_overlap: Desk study listed thermal-only sets (D1 to D12); nothing trained.

title: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Solar PV Panel Fault Classification
mechanism: Fuses a JEPA-pretrained ViT with an EfficientNetV2-S branch for thermal fault classification.
evidence: R: PVF-10 10-class F1 93.21, acc 94.33; ISM 12-class F1 72.60, acc 83.88; binary F1 97.53 / 94.69; 108.6 M params.
adaptation: Strong ready baseline for the thermal deliverable; not expected to help EL (frozen foundation features were n.d. on EL).
min_experiment: Run official code on PVF-10 fixed split, then test on A3 as in the PVF-10 experiment; keep it over ResNet-34 only if > 2 F1 points better cross-plant.
prior_overlap: none for thermal; foundation encoders on EL closed only for frozen probes and one ConvNeXt-T screen.

title: Computer vision tool for detection, mapping, and fault classification of photovoltaics modules in aerial IR videos
mechanism: Detects, tracks and georeferences PV modules in drone IR video and extracts per-module image stacks for classification.
evidence: R: ResNet-50 > 90 % test accuracy on 10 anomaly classes; follow-up SfM version mapped 99.3 % of 35,084 modules and extracted > 2.2 M module images (per web summary of arXiv 2204.02733).
adaptation: Module-ID map and per-module crops for WattCycle flights; lets a later EL session be matched module by module for a pre-registered EL queue.
min_experiment: Run on a public sample video, then on the first WattCycle flight; report share of modules mapped. Tooling, no kill line.
prior_overlap: Desk study idea W02 (module ID map) planned, not run.

title: KaLOS finds Consensus: A Meta-Algorithm for Evaluating Inter-Annotator Agreement in Complex Vision Tasks
mechanism: Meta-algorithm for inter-annotator agreement in vision tasks with instance correspondence, validated without circular reliance on a ground truth; argues benchmark progress is limited by label noise.
adaptation: Benchmark only: compute a KaLOS-style agreement on the doubly annotated EL cells (crack IoU 0.21-0.26 strict, 0.82-0.99 within 2 px) and report it as the label-noise ceiling next to model scores.
min_experiment: No training. Compute agreement per class and source on doubly annotated cells; decide whether a model gap smaller than the agreement spread is reported as a tie. Kill: not applicable (reporting tool).
evidence: R: proposes and validates an agreement meta-algorithm for detection and instance segmentation (abstract only).
prior_overlap: none. Annotator agreement was measured as IoU only.

title: Quantitative assessment of PV modules affected by Type-C cracks using electroluminescence imaging
mechanism: Automatic crack segmentation plus Type-C power-loss quantification across 100 field modules; power loss follows a GEV distribution.
adaptation: Prior for power-loss band edges (for example <5%, 5 to 20%, >20%) in the severity confusion matrix.
min_experiment: None. Design input.
evidence: R: 100 modules after 11 years; mean estimated loss 12.77%; modules > 20% loss unlikely.
prior_overlap: none

title: Benchmarking imaging-based inspection techniques for PV systems
mechanism: Fault-centric comparison of IR, EL, UVF, PL and emerging modalities by fault visibility and technology readiness, not by reported accuracy.
evidence: R: IR ML 94 to 98 %, EL DL up to 97.8 %, UVF crack detection > 91 % at 10 to 15x throughput; states these come from different data and protocols and are not comparable.
adaptation: Cite in the benchmark chapter as independent support that published numbers are not comparable; its fault by modality frame structures the EL-to-thermal mapping table.
min_experiment: None; citation and framing only.
prior_overlap: none.

title: Photoluminescence for Defect Detection on Full-Sized Photovoltaic Modules
mechanism: Outdoor PL on full modules, with the same defects compared across PL, IR, EL and UVF.
adaptation: Physics reference for WattCycle deployment and the benchmark's modality notes: thin cracks need EL; thermal or PL alone will not replace EL for crack segmentation.
min_experiment: No training arm.
evidence: R: 5 of 7 defect types detected well in PL; cracks only under certain conditions; interconnection failures not at all.
prior_overlap: Agrees with the BRIEF thermal desk study; nothing new to test.

title: Dataset for recognition of snail trails and hot spot failures in monocrystalline Si solar panels
mechanism: Public drone IR images of a 4-panel string with a known cell-level layout of hot spots and snail trails, plus weather readings.
evidence: R: 277 images, 336 x 256 JPG, Zenmuse XT, Cali; CC BY 4.0 (Mendeley page).
adaptation: Smoke test for the deliverable's hot-spot localiser; not a generalisation test (one string).
min_experiment: Run the max-median hot-spot rule on it and check hits against the published cell layout; CPU.
